pages.title: Docs Style Guide and Page Template
pages.content:
# Docs Style Guide and Page Template

Rules for writing and editing pages in this folder. The docs are the single source of truth for the PEPU dev kit, so accuracy outranks polish.

## Voice

- Plain, sober, friction-focused. Say what to do, then why.
- No hype words, no emoji, no marketing adjectives.
- Every page must make it easier to build or to use. If it does not, cut it.
- PEPU is a chain, not "an AI chain". Agent tooling is described as tooling that helps builders get PEPU facts right.

## Honesty about status

State plainly what is proven and what is pending. Use these labels consistently:

| Label | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Proven | Run end to end on mainnet, by a script or a person, and the page says which |
| Proven on mainnet (canary, external audit pending) | Deployed and exercised on mainnet, internally reviewed, not externally audited; the v2 paymaster carries this label |
| Built, not deployed | Code and tests exist; nothing live depends on it |
| Pending | Not built or not live yet |

Current facts to respect (re-verify before repeating as current):

- Mainnet only: chain ID `97741`. The testnet `97740` is out of scope for development. Chain ID `3409` is the dead V1 chain.
- The hosted endpoints are live and proven: bundler `https://bundler.pepeunchained.com` and paymaster service `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com`. They are the SDK defaults; keep the env var names `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` and `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` as overrides. The ERC-7677 URL always embeds a token (`https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<token>`), so there is no tokenless default; write `<token>` and never a real one. Local development defaults (`http://localhost:4337`, `http://localhost:8788`) may stay for people running their own services. Never write a tunnel URL (no ngrok, no trycloudflare) anywhere.
- The v2 paymaster `PepuSponsoredPaymasterV7` is deployed on mainnet as a canary. Use exactly: "deployed as a canary: internally reviewed 3x, external audit pending, funded in small tranches". Never say audited. The v1 paymaster is retired.
- Multicall3 is at a PEPU-specific address, never the canonical one. Give full addresses, never truncated ones, in tables meant for copying.
- Never state a feature is available if it is not live.

## Code samples use real SDK exports

- Import only symbols that exist in `@pepu-chain/sdk` and its documented subpaths: `/privy`, `/privy/react`, `/privy/wagmi`, `/privy/server`, `/session`, `/session/server`, `/session/react`, `/session/kernel`, `/aa`, `/aa/kernel`, `/aa/react`, `/aa/react-direct`, `/paymaster`, `/paymaster/server`, `/combo`, `/combo/react`, `/doctor`.
- If a symbol is not exported, do not invent it. Check `packages/sdk/src` and the exports test, or call the `pepu_sdk_exports` MCP tool.
- Prefer SDK functions over hand-rolled infrastructure. Use raw viem or JSON-RPC only where the SDK has no equivalent, and say so.
- Server-only code (Privy app secret, authorization key, claim attestation) is labeled server-only and never reads `NEXT_PUBLIC_` variables.
- Never print or embed secrets, keys or real tokens. Use obvious placeholders.
- Samples meant to compile live under `docs/snippets/` and are type-checked in CI. Pages include them and do not diverge from them.

## Page template

````markdown
# Page Title

One paragraph: what this page is for and who needs it.

> Status: proven | proven on mainnet (canary, external audit pending) | built, not deployed | pending (and what exactly was run)

## Prerequisites
## Steps or reference body
## What to expect
## Common failures
## Related
````

Rules:

- One H1 per page, title case, matching the `SUMMARY.md` entry.
- Reference pages use tables; procedures use numbered steps.
- Every failure symptom names the cause and the fix.
- Link with relative paths, for example from the docs root `[Session Keys](onboarding/session-keys.md)`.
- Add every new page to `SUMMARY.md` in the same change.
- Do not put Markdown link syntax inside `TODO` comments; the link checker reads them.

## Stubs and ownership

New pages start as stubs: a title, a one-paragraph purpose and a `TODO(Dn)` comment listing the required sections. The owner replaces the stub and removes the TODO and the status line.

| Writer | Folders |
|---|---|
| D2 | `get-started/`, `onboarding/`, `concepts/`, `privy/`, `reference/env-vars.md`, glossary, FAQ |
| D3 | `sdk/`, `recipes/`, `snippets/`, changelog |
| D4 | `mcp/`, `agent-tooling/`, `templates/`, `cli/` |
| D5 | `infra/`, `contracts/` |
| D6 | generated pages (`reference/errors.md`, `reference/endpoints.md`, `sdk/errors.md`), `llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt`, `troubleshooting.md` |

## Checks

- `node scripts/check-links.mjs` must report 0 broken links.
- `docs/llms.txt` assumes each page URL mirrors its path; D6 keeps it current.

pages.title: Pepe Unchained Developer Docs
pages.content:
# Pepe Unchained Developer Docs

Developer documentation for building on Pepe Unchained V2 (Arbitrum Orbit, mainnet chain ID `97741`). The published site is [guide.pepeunchained.com](https://guide.pepeunchained.com); the same pages live here as Markdown. You do not need to clone this repository to build on PEPU:

```bash
npx create-pepu-app@latest          # scaffold a Next.js + Privy app
npm i @pepu-chain/sdk viem          # chain definitions, contracts, ABIs, helpers
npx -y @pepu-chain/mcp              # MCP server for coding agents
```

For Claude Code, install the plugin (skills plus the MCP server):

```text
/plugin marketplace add pepu-org/pepu-devkit
/plugin install pepu-devkit@pepu
```

## The shortest path

1. [What is Pepe Unchained V2](get-started/introduction.md): the chain in one page.
2. [The Three Pillars](get-started/pillars.md): login, sessions, sponsored gas, and how they combine.
3. [Smart Account Paths](concepts/smart-account-paths.md): which setup to start from.
4. [Quickstart](get-started/quickstart-app.md): `npx create-pepu-app@latest`, fill `.env.local`, click the Privy dashboard settings, `npm run doctor`, `npm run dev`, first sponsored transaction. With an AI agent: [Build with an AI Coding Agent](get-started/ai-assisted.md).

## The nine deliverables

The dev kit is SDK-first: every other deliverable uses the SDK instead of re-implementing it.

| # | Deliverable | What it is | Docs |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | SDKs | `@pepu-chain/sdk`: chain, contracts registry, Privy, sessions, account abstraction, paymaster, combined flow, doctor | [SDK](sdk/reference.md) |
| 2 | MCP + agentic skills | `@pepu-chain/mcp` (32 tools, 6 prompts) and 12 agent skills that call the SDK and MCP | [MCP](mcp/index.md), [Skills](agent-tooling/skills.md) |
| 3 | Plugins | The `pepu-devkit` Claude Code plugin: MCP server, skills, 6 commands and a builder subagent | [Plugin](agent-tooling/plugin.md) |
| 4 | Starter templates | Six templates, from a consumer app to the full sponsored session | [Templates](templates/index.md) |
| 5 | CLI scaffolding | `create-pepu-app` scaffolds a Next.js app with a chosen template | [CLI](cli/create-pepu-app.md) |
| 6 | Developer docs | This site, one source of truth for all of the above | [Style guide](CONTRIBUTING-DOCS.md) |
| 7 | Our own bundler | The ERC-4337 bundler (Alto) for PEPU, hosted at `bundler.pepeunchained.com` | [Bundler](infra/bundler/overview.md) |
| 8 | Paymaster infrastructure | The verifying paymaster, its policy service and REST APIs, hosted at `paymaster.pepeunchained.com` | [Paymaster](infra/paymaster/overview.md) |
| 9 | Multicall3 and supporting infrastructure | Multicall3, Permit2, EntryPoints, Kernel, with every address | [Contracts](contracts/address-map.md) |

## The three pillars

1. **Google to wallet.** Sign in with Google and get an embedded wallet on PEPU. Proven live on mainnet.
2. **Session keys.** Approve once, then act with no wallet popup. Two modes: Privy session signers (proven) and Kernel on-chain session keys (proven live in a browser, 2026-10-14).
3. **Sponsored transactions.** The user pays no gas. Works end to end on mainnet through the hosted bundler and paymaster.

Their combination is the headline flow: [Google Login, Session and Sponsorship End to End](onboarding/google-session-sponsored.md). Start with [The Three Pillars](get-started/pillars.md).

## Where to start

| I want to... | Read |
|---|---|
| Understand the chain | [What is Pepe Unchained V2](get-started/introduction.md), [Network Reference](get-started/network-reference.md) |
| Get a running app and a first sponsored transaction | [Quickstart: Zero to a Sponsored Transaction in 10 Minutes](get-started/quickstart-app.md), [Template Gallery](templates/index.md) |
| Choose between a plain wallet, ZeroDev-native and Privy Smart Wallets | [Smart Account Paths](concepts/smart-account-paths.md) |
| Get a paymaster project (claim, deposit, keys) | [Register, Deposit and Claim a v2 Project](infra/paymaster/v2-register-deposit-claim.md) |
| Look up a term (UserOperation, bundler, paymaster, Kernel) | [Glossary](reference/glossary.md) |
| Build with an AI agent | [Build with an AI Coding Agent](get-started/ai-assisted.md), [MCP](mcp/index.md) |
| Configure Privy | [Dashboard Settings](privy/dashboard-settings.md), [Privy Setup](onboarding/privy-setup.md) |
| Avoid a wallet popup per action | [Session Keys](onboarding/session-keys.md) |
| Understand gas sponsorship | [Sponsored Transactions](onboarding/sponsored-transactions.md), [Paymaster](infra/paymaster/overview.md) |
| Use the SDK | [SDK](sdk/reference.md) |
| Look up an address | [Address Map](contracts/address-map.md), [Deployed Contracts](contracts/deployed-contracts.md), [The Multicall3 Trap](contracts/multicall3.md) |
| Deploy and verify a contract | [Deploy & Verify a Contract](contracts/deployment.md) |
| Copy a pattern | [Recipes](recipes/read-a-contract.md) |
| Look up an env var or error | [Environment Variables](reference/env-vars.md), [Error Reference](reference/errors.md) |
| Fix a problem | [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md) |

The full navigation is in [`SUMMARY.md`](SUMMARY.md). Machine-readable index: [`llms.txt`](llms.txt).

## Hosted bundler and paymaster

The hosted endpoints are live and proven: bundler `https://bundler.pepeunchained.com` and paymaster service `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com`. They are the SDK defaults; `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` and `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` override them. The ERC-7677 URL always embeds a token (`https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<token>`). The v2 paymaster is deployed as a canary: internally reviewed 3x, external audit pending, funded in small tranches. Operators who want to run their own can use the source in [`services/bundler`](../services/bundler) and [`services/paymaster`](../services/paymaster).

## Maintainer notes

This folder syncs to GitBook through bi-directional Git Sync: merging Markdown to the synced branch publishes it, and edits made in GitBook's editor are committed back here.

- **`SUMMARY.md` is load-bearing.** GitBook builds the table of contents from it, so add every new page there in the same change that adds the file.
- **`llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt`** follow the llmstxt.org format and are generated by `node scripts/gen-docs.mjs` (CI runs it with `--check`). They assume each page's published URL mirrors its path here. The same script generates `reference/errors.md`, `reference/endpoints.md` and `sdk/errors.md`; do not edit those by hand. `node scripts/check-docs-parity.mjs` keeps counts, names and addresses on the pages equal to the code.
- **Voice.** Plain, sober, friction-focused. No hype words, no emoji. Never state a feature as available if it is not live; say plainly that it is in progress. The test for every page: does it make it easier to build or to use?
- **Facts that change often.** Re-check before repeating as current: hosted endpoint status (live), the v2 paymaster canary (external audit pending), Privy behavior (allowed-origin port rule, `eoaOnly`, server-side `eth_sendTransaction` not supporting chain 97741), Multicall3 (deployed at a PEPU-specific address, never the canonical one), Permit2 (canonical address), and testnet `97740` (out of scope for development).
- **Flip these together** when the hosted endpoint status changes: [`onboarding/sponsored-transactions.md`](onboarding/sponsored-transactions.md), [`onboarding/smart-accounts.md`](onboarding/smart-accounts.md), [`onboarding/privy-embedded-wallets.md`](onboarding/privy-embedded-wallets.md), [`onboarding/privy-setup.md`](onboarding/privy-setup.md), [`get-started/introduction.md`](get-started/introduction.md), [`contracts/deployed-contracts.md`](contracts/deployed-contracts.md), [`troubleshooting.md`](troubleshooting.md) and `llms.txt`.
- **Not written yet, deliberately:** a Stylus page, a grants and ecosystem section, and Remix or thirdweb deep-dives. Add them to `SUMMARY.md` only when they exist.
- **Writing pages.** Read [`CONTRIBUTING-DOCS.md`](CONTRIBUTING-DOCS.md) first. No page should contain a stub marker; `check-docs-parity.mjs` fails on one.

pages.title: AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md in Templates
pages.content:
# AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md in Templates

Every app scaffolded from a PEPU template carries an agent kit: instructions and editor configs that point a coding agent at the SDK and the MCP server. This page lists what is in the kit, which part of `AGENTS.md` is hand-written and which is generated, and how the kit is kept in sync. Read it if you work with an agent inside a scaffolded app, or if you maintain a template.

> Status: built and tested. `templates/scripts/check-agent-kit.mjs` fails when any template drifts from the shared kit. The plugin route for Claude Code is recommended. Templates no longer ship a `.mcp.json`.

## Prerequisites

- An app from [create-pepu-app](../cli/create-pepu-app.md). Pass `--skip-agent-files` to leave the kit out.
- An agent client that reads `AGENTS.md` (Cursor, VS Code Copilot and others) or `CLAUDE.md` (Claude Code).

## What is in the kit

| File | Who reads it | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `AGENTS.md` | Most agents | The template's instructions: how to build and run, which SDK functions the template uses, design rules, plus the generated "PEPU dev kit: agent wiring" block. |
| `CLAUDE.md` | Claude Code | One line, `@AGENTS.md`, which imports `AGENTS.md` so both agents read the same text. |
| `.cursor/mcp.json` | Cursor | Declares the `pepu` MCP server under the `mcpServers` key, with `"type": "stdio"`. |
| `.vscode/mcp.json` | VS Code | Declares the `pepu` MCP server under the top-level key `servers`, with `"type": "stdio"`. |
| `.claude/settings.json` | Claude Code | Declares the `pepu` marketplace from `pepu-org/pepu-devkit` and enables `pepu-devkit@pepu`, so Claude Code offers the plugin when you open the project. |

The editor configs all run the same command, `npx -y @pepu-chain/mcp`. See [Install per Client](../mcp/install.md) for the exact shapes and the environment variables.

`.claude/settings.json` carries exactly this:

```json
{
  "extraKnownMarketplaces": {
    "pepu": { "source": { "source": "github", "repo": "pepu-org/pepu-devkit" } }
  },
  "enabledPlugins": { "pepu-devkit@pepu": true }
}
```

What the plugin then gives you is described in [Claude Code Plugin](plugin.md). You still see Claude Code's trust prompt.

## Per-template section versus generated block

`AGENTS.md` has two parts.

1. **Per-template section (hand-written, above the markers).** Build and run commands, the table of SDK functions the template uses and where, the template's own rules (for example, game-app keeps `tap()` non-payable and never grants an unscoped signer; sponsored-demo never labels a send gasless unless a paymaster paid it), the design notes and what the template deliberately does not do. Edit this freely.
2. **Generated block (between the markers).** Everything between `<!-- BEGIN:pepu-agent-kit -->` and `<!-- END:pepu-agent-kit -->` is generated. Do not edit it by hand: the next sync overwrites it and the check fails.

The generated block says:

| Section | Content |
|---|---|
| Header | Template name, title and features (login, session, sponsor). "Use the kit; do not hand-roll what it already provides." |
| Chain facts | Chain `97741`, mainnet only, no testnet switch. RPC, pepuscan, native token PEPU with 18 decimals. Multicall3 at the PEPU-specific `0x9CE19273Ae9c24437DFF512E8DFCAed4E4B001bd`, never the canonical address. Get everything from the SDK (`pepuMainnet`, `explorerLinks`, `getPepuAddresses`). |
| Use the SDK | The SDK subpaths this template should import from, chosen by its features, then a table of every subpath and what it is for. |
| Use the MCP tools | The `pepu` server, the 32 tools grouped by purpose, the 6 prompts and the resources. `pepu_chain_info` is called first. |
| Skills and the plugin | The plugin install commands (`/plugin marketplace add pepu-org/pepu-devkit`, `/plugin install pepu-devkit@pepu`). |
| Environment | The template's required and optional env vars, its Privy dashboard settings and extra steps, and `npm run doctor`. |
| Never print secrets | Do not print, log, echo, commit or paste `PRIVY_APP_SECRET`, `PRIVY_AUTHORIZATION_KEY`, any private key or credential-bearing URL. Do not read `.env*` into the conversation: use `npm run doctor`, which prints no values. Only `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` values are safe to show. |

The per-template values come from `packages/create-pepu-app/src/templates.json` (name, title, features, env, Privy dashboard ids, extra steps).

## Sync and check scripts

The shared source is `templates/_agent`: the editor configs, `.claude/settings.json`, `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.base.md` (the generated block's template).

```bash
# After editing anything in templates/_agent or templates.json:
node templates/scripts/sync-agent-kit.mjs     # copies the verbatim files, renders the block into every template's AGENTS.md
node templates/scripts/check-agent-kit.mjs    # fails (exit 1) on any drift
```

`check-agent-kit.mjs` fails when a kit file is missing or does not parse, a kit file differs from `templates/_agent`, the generated block in a template's `AGENTS.md` is missing or stale, or a template lacks the `doctor` npm script or `scripts/doctor.mjs`.

The design system has the same pattern (`sync-design.mjs` and `check-design.mjs`). See `templates/BRAND.md`.

## What to expect

- The agent knows to call `pepu_chain_info` first, to use SDK functions, and to run `npm run doctor` instead of reading `.env.local`.
- With `--skip-agent-files`, none of these files are in the app and the agent has only what you give it.

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `check-agent-kit.mjs` reports a stale block | Someone edited the generated block, or `templates.json` or `_agent` changed | Run `node templates/scripts/sync-agent-kit.mjs`, and make hand edits above the markers only. |
| VS Code ignores the MCP config | The file uses `mcpServers` instead of `servers` | Use the shape in `.vscode/mcp.json` shown in [Install per Client](../mcp/install.md). |
| Claude Code does not offer the plugin | The folder is not trusted, or `.claude/settings.json` was removed | Trust the folder, or install by hand with the two `/plugin` commands. |
| The agent reads `.env.local` | It ignored the rules | Point it at the "Never print secrets" section and run `npm run doctor` yourself. |

## Related

- [Claude Code Plugin](plugin.md)
- [Skills Catalog](skills.md)
- [Install per Client](../mcp/install.md)
- [create-pepu-app CLI](../cli/create-pepu-app.md)
- [Template Gallery](../templates/index.md)

pages.content:
# Agent Tooling: MCP Server and Skills

This is the hub for the PEPU agent tooling: infrastructure that helps coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code and similar) build on Pepe Unchained and get PEPU's specific facts right. It is not a claim that PEPU is "an AI chain". It is not one. AI is a feature builders add to their own products. This tooling exists so an agent, or a person using one, does not guess a chain ID, invent an address or use the canonical Multicall3 address that has no code here (see [The Multicall3 Trap](../contracts/multicall3.md)).

> Status: built and tested. The MCP server, 12 skills, 6 plugin commands and the builder subagent all exist on main. The hosted bundler (`https://bundler.pepeunchained.com`) and paymaster service (`https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com`) are live and are the defaults; sponsorship needs a project token in the paymaster URL (`PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL`). The v2 paymaster is Proven on mainnet as a canary (external audit pending).

## The pieces

| Piece | What it is | Page |
|---|---|---|
| `pepu` MCP server | `@pepu-chain/mcp`: 32 tools, 6 prompts and 5 resources for chain facts, probes, explainers, scaffolding, env and Privy checks, session policies and SDK snippets | [MCP Server Overview](../mcp/index.md), [Install per Client](../mcp/install.md), [Tool Reference](../mcp/tools.md) |
| Skills | 12 `SKILL.md` playbooks, each built on `@pepu-chain/sdk` and the MCP tools | [Skills Catalog](skills.md) |
| Claude Code plugin | `pepu-devkit`: the MCP server, the 12 skills, 6 slash commands and the `pepu-builder` subagent in one install | [Claude Code Plugin](plugin.md) |
| Template agent kit | `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` and editor configs shipped in every scaffolded app | [AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md in Templates](agents-md.md) |

## Quick start

In Claude Code, install the plugin (recommended):

```text
/plugin marketplace add pepu-org/pepu-devkit
/plugin install pepu-devkit@pepu
```

Or add only the MCP server with `claude mcp add pepu -- npx -y @pepu-chain/mcp`. Cursor, VS Code and other clients are covered in [Install per Client](../mcp/install.md).

## How they fit together

- The SDK (`@pepu-chain/sdk`) holds the functions. Skills and tools tell the agent to wire them, not to hand-roll infrastructure.
- The MCP server answers live questions: what is deployed, is sponsorship available, what does this error mean, which env var is missing.
- Skills carry the method: the order of steps, the dashboard settings, the safety rules and the pitfalls.
- Each skill tells the agent to call `pepu_chain_info` or the relevant probe first, so a fact that changed since the skill was written is caught by a live check.

The same line applies to everything here: it makes building on PEPU easier, or it does not belong.

## Related

- [Build with an AI Coding Agent in 3 Minutes](../get-started/ai-assisted.md)
- [create-pepu-app CLI](../cli/create-pepu-app.md)
- [SDK Overview and Reference](../sdk/reference.md)

pages.title: Claude Code Plugin
pages.content:
# Claude Code Plugin

The `pepu-devkit` plugin bundles everything the kit gives a coding agent into one Claude Code install: the `pepu` MCP server, the 12 skills, 6 slash commands and the `pepu-builder` subagent. This page covers installing it, what each command does, what loads, and the trust prompt you will see.

> Status: built and tested, version 0.4.1. The plugin manifest, marketplace manifest, commands and subagent are checked against the real MCP tools and SDK exports by `scripts/check-plugin.mjs`. Commands that touch sponsorship use the hosted bundler and paymaster service by default and need a project token for the paymaster URL (`PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL`).

## Prerequisites

- Claude Code with plugin support.
- Node.js 18 or newer, because the plugin starts the MCP server with `npx`.
- Optional: `PEPU_RPC_URL`, `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` and `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` exported in your shell. The plugin forwards them to the server and uses an empty value when they are unset.

## Install

Plugin (recommended):

```text
/plugin marketplace add pepu-org/pepu-devkit
/plugin install pepu-devkit@pepu
```

The first command registers the marketplace named `pepu` from the GitHub repository `pepu-org/pepu-devkit`. The second installs the plugin `pepu-devkit` from it.

If you only want the MCP server, use the fallback instead: `claude mcp add pepu -- npx -y @pepu-chain/mcp`. See [Install per Client](../mcp/install.md).

Apps scaffolded with [create-pepu-app](../cli/create-pepu-app.md) carry a `.claude/settings.json` that declares the `pepu` marketplace and enables `pepu-devkit@pepu`, so Claude Code offers the plugin the first time you open the project. See [AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md in Templates](agents-md.md).

## What loads

| Part | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| MCP server `pepu` | 1 server, 32 tools, 6 prompts, 5 resources | Started with `npx -y @pepu-chain/mcp@^0.2`. Environment: `PEPU_RPC_URL`, `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL`, `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL`. See [Tool Reference](../mcp/tools.md). |
| Skills | 12 | Listed in the [Skills Catalog](skills.md). |
| Commands | 6 | Below. |
| Subagent | 1 | `pepu-builder`, below. |

Inside Claude Code, the plugin's MCP tools are named `mcp__plugin_pepu-devkit_pepu__<tool>`, for example `mcp__plugin_pepu-devkit_pepu__pepu_chain_info`. Each command and the subagent list exactly the tools they may call.

## The trust prompt

A plugin runs code and can start a server on your machine, so Claude Code asks before it enables one. Expect:

1. A prompt to trust the marketplace or the folder when you add it, and to confirm the plugin install.
2. An approval for the plugin's MCP server the first time it starts. It runs `npx` with the package above.
3. Permission prompts for tool calls according to your normal rules. Read-only tools are annotated as such. The two write tools, `pepu_scaffold_app` and `pepu_generate_authorization_key`, are the ones that ask first.

Read the manifest before you trust it: it is `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` in the repository. Exact prompt wording belongs to Claude Code and can change.

## Commands

All six commands call the SDK through the MCP snippets. None hand-writes chain, Privy, session or sponsorship code.

| Command | Argument | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `/pepu-new-app` | `[app name or idea]` | Lists templates, picks one by pillar and says why (default `consumer-app`), scaffolds to an absolute directory with `pepu_scaffold_app` (or the CLI with `--yes --no-install --no-git --json`), installs, runs `pepu_check_env` and `pepu_check_privy_config`, reports sponsorship status for sponsorship templates, then typechecks and builds. Follows the `pepu-build-dapp` skill. |
| `/pepu-add-login` | `[login methods, default google and email]` | Adds Google login and a Privy embedded wallet to the current Next.js app: `PepuPrivyProvider` or `PepuPrivyWagmiProvider` with `WalletGate`, and `createEnsureWalletRoute()`. Adds env placeholders, checks the dashboard (allowed origin with port, Google on, embedded wallets on). Follows `pepu-onboarding-privy`. |
| `/pepu-add-session` | `<contract address> <function signatures, e.g. tap()>` | Adds Privy session keys: builds the policy with `pepu_session_policy` (Privy mode), generates the authorization key with `pepu_generate_authorization_key` and asks you to register the public key and paste the quorum id, then applies the session routes and hooks. The consent screen says the user pays gas. Follows `pepu-session-keys`. |
| `/pepu-add-sponsorship` | `[transport: privy-smart-wallets or direct]` | Runs `pepu_sponsorship_status` first and reports the answer exactly, then wires `useSponsoredSend` or `useDirectSponsoredSend` (browser) or `sendSponsored` (server). Prefers the Privy Smart Wallets transport for browser code because a paymaster URL embeds a credential. Only says a send was sponsored when `result.paymaster` is set. Follows `pepu-sponsored-transactions`. |
| `/pepu-add-sponsored-session` | `<contract address> <function signatures>` | Adds the combination: Kernel scope from `pepu_session_policy`, `createSponsoredSessionRoutes` with its five route files and a `useSponsoredSession` component. Warns that `createMemoryStore()` is dev only and sizes spend caps above the gas reservation. For a new project prefer `/pepu-new-app` with `sponsored-session-app`. Follows `pepu-sponsored-session`. |
| `/pepu-doctor` | `[template name, optional]` | Readiness check: `pepu_check_env`, `npm run doctor` if defined, `pepu_check_privy_config`, `pepu_sponsorship_status` for sponsorship templates and `pepu_health_check`. Ends with a table of check, status and fix, applies the fixes it can, and lists exactly what only you can do. Never reads secret values. |

## The pepu-builder subagent

`pepu-builder` builds and extends PEPU apps end to end and asks you only for what only you have. Claude Code delegates to it for any task that creates or changes a PEPU app, a contract deployment or a PEPU chain integration.

How it works:

1. Scaffold first, never from a blank folder.
2. Ask the tools, not memory: `pepu_chain_info`, `pepu_sponsorship_status`, `pepu_check_env`, `pepu_check_privy_config`, `pepu_sdk_snippet`, `pepu_sdk_exports`.
3. Load the matching skill and obey its never-hand-roll list.
4. Verify before saying done: env check, Privy check, typecheck, build, then prove the pillar works.
5. On failure, `pepu_explain_error` with the exact text, then `pepu_known_gotchas`.

What only you can do, and it will name each precisely: paste the Privy App ID and App Secret, register the authorization public key in the Privy dashboard, add the allowed origin, supply bundler and paymaster URLs, and fund wallets.

It never prints, logs or commits secrets, never calls a transaction free unless a paymaster paid it, and says which session mode it built. It finishes with a report of what it built, which SDK functions it uses, what was verified and what you still have to do. Its tools are Claude Code's file and shell tools (Read, Write, Edit, Glob, Grep, Bash) plus an explicit allow-list of all 32 PEPU MCP tools that includes both write tools. The list is in `agents/pepu-builder.md`.

## Versions and checks

The plugin version, the marketplace version and the MCP server's declared range move together. From a checkout:

```bash
node scripts/check-versions.mjs   # plugin.json, marketplace.json and packages/mcp/server.json in lock-step; prints SDK, MCP, CLI and plugin versions
node scripts/check-plugin.mjs     # validates skills, commands, agents, tool names, SDK imports and manifest counts
```

`check-plugin.mjs --write` regenerates the counts in the manifest descriptions.

## What to expect

- After install, `/mcp` shows the plugin's `pepu` server, and the six commands appear when you type `/pepu`.
- Without a project token for the paymaster URL, the sponsorship commands still set up the code and leave `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` as a marked placeholder (`https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<token>`; the bundler defaults to the hosted one). They do not claim sponsorship works.

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `/plugin marketplace add` fails | No network, or the repository is not reachable | Check access to `github.com/pepu-org/pepu-devkit`, or use the `claude mcp add` fallback. |
| The MCP server does not start | Node older than 18 or `npx` not on PATH | Install Node 18+. |
| Sponsorship tools say "not configured" | The environment cleared a default, or the paymaster URL has no project token | Export `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` (`https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<token>`) and, for your own bundler, `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` before launching Claude Code. |
| A command asks for something and stops | It needs a value only you have | Provide the Privy App ID or secret, or complete the named dashboard step, then continue. |

## Related

- [Skills Catalog](skills.md)
- [AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md in Templates](agents-md.md)
- [Install per Client](../mcp/install.md)
- [Build with an AI Coding Agent in 3 Minutes](../get-started/ai-assisted.md)

pages.title: Skills Catalog
pages.content:
# Skills Catalog

The 12 PEPU skills: what each one does, when it triggers, the chain facts they all share, how they use the SDK and the MCP tools instead of hand-rolled code, and the rules for writing a new one. Read it to know which skill an agent will load, or before adding one.

> Status: built and tested. The skills ship in the `pepu-devkit` plugin and are also served by the MCP server as `pepu://skills/{name}`. The pillar skills describe flows that are Proven on mainnet; the paymaster v2 skill describes a contract that is Proven on mainnet as a canary (deployed as a canary: internally reviewed 3x, external audit pending, funded in small tranches).

## Prerequisites

- The skills are installed through the [Claude Code plugin](plugin.md), or read one on demand through the `pepu://skills/{name}` MCP resource.
- For method, not just text: the [MCP server](../mcp/index.md) connected, because every skill tells the agent to call its tools.

## The 12 skills

| Skill | What it does | Use it for |
|---|---|---|
| `pepu-build-dapp` | The entry point from zero to a running app. Scaffolds with `create-pepu-app` or the MCP tools `pepu_list_templates` and `pepu_scaffold_app`, picks the template by pillar, fills and checks env and Privy config, runs the app and hands off to the pillar skills. | Building, starting, scaffolding or extending a PEPU app. |
| `pepu-sdk` | A cheat sheet for `@pepu-chain/sdk`: the subpath map, "if you want X, import Y", which entries are server-only, client-only or ESM-only, and the rule against reimplementing what it ships. | Before writing any PEPU infrastructure code by hand, or to pick the right import. |
| `pepu-chain-setup` | Configures viem, wagmi, Hardhat and Foundry for chain `97741` with the SDK instead of a hand-written chain object. Carries the traps: PEPU-specific Multicall3, the huge-looking gas price, the 2,000-block `eth_getLogs` cap, no WebSocket RPC. | Adding PEPU to any project, setting up a client, batching reads. |
| `pepu-onboarding-privy` | Google (and email) login with a server-provisioned Privy embedded wallet, built from the SDK provider, `WalletGate`, `createEnsureWalletRoute` and `requireUser`. Gives the Privy dashboard fields and the troubleshooting for login hangs and a missing wallet. Pillar: Google to wallet. | Sign-in, wallets, protecting an API route by user. |
| `pepu-session-keys` | Privy session signers on a plain embedded wallet, so an app acts for the user with no popup per action. The scope is enforced off-chain by Privy and the user pays gas. Includes the three safety rules. Pillar: session keys. | "No wallet popup" actions with the user paying gas. |
| `pepu-sponsored-transactions` | Gasless transactions with a Kernel v3.1 smart account, an EntryPoint v0.7 bundler and an ERC-7677 paymaster. Covers both transports (Privy Smart Wallets or direct URLs). Sponsorship status is live-checked, never assumed. Pillar: sponsored transactions. | Gasless, paymaster, bundler or UserOperation work. |
| `pepu-sponsored-session` | The combination: Google login, one owner signature that grants an on-chain Kernel session key, then actions with no popup and no user gas. The scope is enforced on-chain. Includes the five routes and the production `SessionStore` warning. | The full flow, matching the `sponsored-session-app` template. |
| `pepu-smart-accounts` | Account mechanics: the two-address model (embedded EOA owner plus Kernel smart account), counterfactual addresses and when a smart account is the right choice. Deliberately slim. | Computing or inspecting a smart account, explaining owner versus smart account. |
| `pepu-paymaster-projects` | The v2 tiered model: claim a project keyed by Privy app id, deposit PEPU one-way, set targets and daily limits. Deployed as a canary: internally reviewed 3x, external audit pending, funded in small tranches. Advise small deposits. | Preparing, reviewing or scripting the v2 workflow, and answering tier questions honestly. |
| `pepu-deploy-contract` | Deploys and verifies a Solidity contract on mainnet with Foundry (primary) or Hardhat. Detects the `foundry-zksync` binary shadowing `forge` before it produces a wrong deployment. | Deploying or verifying a contract on PEPU. |
| `pepu-token-and-nft` | Deploys and uses an ERC-20 or ERC-721 on PEPU, and explains what "getting listed" actually means: the PepuSwap list and the kit's own token list are separate and neither is automatic. | Creating a token or NFT collection, or interacting with one. |
| `pepu-debug-transaction` | Diagnoses a failed, stuck, denied or expensive transaction, UserOperation or Privy, paymaster or session error. Starts with `pepu_explain_tx`, `pepu_explain_error` and `pepu_known_gotchas`. | Reverts, transactions that never land, denied sponsored sends, session 409s. |

The three pillar skills (`pepu-onboarding-privy`, `pepu-session-keys`, `pepu-sponsored-transactions`) and their combination (`pepu-sponsored-session`) match the pillars in [The Three Pillars and How They Combine](../get-started/pillars.md).

## Shared chain facts

Every skill carries two shared files in its own `reference/` folder, so a skill is self-contained when installed alone:

- `reference/chain-facts.md` is generated from the built SDK (chains, endpoints, the contract registry). It states chain `97741`, mainnet only, the default RPC and explorer, the PEPU-specific Multicall3, the full registry table with deployed or pending status, the gas explanation, the endpoint-resolution order and a "where to look things up" table.
- `reference/rules.md` is hand-written: "use the SDK, call the MCP tools, never hand-roll". It holds the order of work, a table of what never to write by hand and the SDK function to use instead, the hard rules and the MCP tool contract.

The hard rules every skill repeats:

| Rule | Detail |
|---|---|
| Mainnet only | Chain `97741`. Do not add the testnet to a chain list. |
| Never print secrets | `PRIVY_APP_SECRET`, `PRIVY_AUTHORIZATION_KEY`, paymaster URLs and session private keys. Report key names and presence only. |
| Sponsorship wording follows the live answer | Call `pepu_sponsorship_status` or `checkSponsorship()`. The hosted bundler and paymaster service are live and are the defaults, but the ERC-7677 URL needs a project token, so the app brings a project. |
| Say which session mode | Privy session mode is enforced off-chain and the user pays gas. Kernel session mode is enforced on-chain. |
| v2 is a canary | Never call the v2 paymaster audited. Deposits are one-way; advise small deposits. The v1 paymaster is retired: never deposit to it. |
| Never call a transaction free or gasless | Unless a paymaster actually paid it. |
| Always a scoped session policy | Never an empty `policyIds`. |
| No server-side `eth_sendTransaction` on 97741 | Privy rejects it. Sign with `eth_signTransaction` and broadcast; the SDK does this. |

## How skills use the SDK and MCP

A skill follows one pattern: ask the tools, wire the SDK, verify.

1. Ground the facts with `pepu_chain_info` or the matching probe (`pepu_sponsorship_status`, `pepu_check_contract_deployed`).
2. Take canonical code from `pepu_sdk_snippet` and confirm names with `pepu_sdk_exports`. Import from the documented subpaths only.
3. Check `pepu_check_env` and `pepu_check_privy_config` before debugging application code.
4. Verify with the project's typecheck and build, then prove the pillar works (sign in, grant, act, send).
5. On failure, `pepu_explain_error` with the exact text, then `pepu_known_gotchas`.

Each `SKILL.md` has the same sections: When to use, Chain facts, SDK functions to use, MCP tools to call first, Steps, Verify, Pitfalls and Never hand-roll (the pillar skills add their safety rules).

If the SDK lacks something, the skill says so, writes the smallest local code and marks it `// TODO(sdk): ...`.

## Authoring rules for a new skill

1. Create `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` with frontmatter `name` equal to the directory name and a non-empty `description` that says when to use it.
2. Use the uniform sections above, in that order.
3. Name only SDK functions that exist, and only MCP tools that are registered. Import paths must exist in the SDK exports map.
4. Do not copy chain facts into the skill. Link to `reference/chain-facts.md`, which is generated.
5. State Proven, Built, not deployed or Pending plainly, using the labels in the docs style guide.
6. Run the sync and the check:

```bash
pnpm --filter @pepu-chain/sdk build        # the scripts read the built SDK
node scripts/sync-skill-shared.mjs         # regenerate chain-facts.md and copy shared files into every skill
node scripts/check-plugin.mjs              # validate skills, commands, agents, tool names, SDK imports and counts
```

`check-plugin.mjs` fails if a skill's name does not match its directory, a named `pepu_*` tool is not registered, an imported SDK symbol is not exported, a count in the manifest descriptions is wrong, or the shared files are stale. `node scripts/sync-skill-shared.mjs --check` is the CI form of the sync.

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| The agent does not load a skill | The plugin is not installed or enabled | Install it ([Claude Code Plugin](plugin.md)), or ask the agent to read `pepu://skills/<name>`. |
| `check-plugin.mjs` reports stale shared files | The SDK registry changed | Rebuild the SDK and run `node scripts/sync-skill-shared.mjs`. |
| `check-plugin.mjs` reports an unknown tool or export | A skill names something that does not exist | Fix the name against `pepu_sdk_exports` or the tool registry. |

## Related

- [Claude Code Plugin](plugin.md)
- [MCP Server Overview](../mcp/index.md)
- [SDK Overview and Reference](../sdk/reference.md)
- [Agent Tooling hub](mcp-and-skills.md)

pages.title: create-pepu-app CLI
pages.content:
# create-pepu-app CLI

`create-pepu-app` scaffolds a PEPU starter template into a new folder: it copies the template, vendors the SDK, writes `.env.local`, adds the agent kit, optionally installs dependencies and runs `git init`, then prints what is left for you to do. This page is the reference for its prompts, flags, `--json` output, env prefill and the vendored-SDK behaviour.

> Status: built and tested (version 0.1.3, on npm). The scaffold, `--json` output and doctor wiring have tests in `packages/create-pepu-app/test`. The default is the npm SDK, with a vendored fallback when npm cannot be reached. Run it with `npx create-pepu-app@latest`. The templates it ships scaffold `@pepu-chain/sdk@^0.2.2`.

## Prerequisites

- Node.js 18 or newer.
- A package manager: npm, pnpm, yarn or bun. The CLI detects the one that launched it.
- A target folder that does not exist or is empty.

## Usage

```bash
npx create-pepu-app                       # interactive
npx create-pepu-app my-app --yes          # defaults, no prompts
npm create pepu-app@latest my-app -- --pm pnpm
npx create-pepu-app my-app --template token-gated-app --yes
npx create-pepu-app --list                # show the templates
npx create-pepu-app my-app --template sponsored-session-app --yes --no-install --no-git --json
```

Agents can do the same through the MCP tool `pepu_scaffold_app`, which runs this CLI with `--yes --json`. See [Tool Reference](../mcp/tools.md#pepu_scaffold_app).

## Flags

```text
create-pepu-app [directory] [options]
```

| Flag | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `directory` (positional) | prompted, or `./pepu-app` with `--yes` | Where to create the project. Only one is accepted. A path such as `./apps/my-app` works; the package name is derived from the last segment. |
| `-t`, `--template <name>` | `consumer-app` | The template to scaffold. Passing it skips the template question. |
| `-y`, `--yes` | off | Skip prompts and accept defaults. Installs and runs `git init` unless you pass `--no-install` or `--no-git`. |
| `--pm <manager>` | auto-detected | `npm`, `pnpm`, `yarn` or `bun`. Detected from `npm_config_user_agent`, falling back to `npm`. |
| `--install` / `--no-install` | ask, or install | Install dependencies after scaffolding, or skip. |
| `--git` / `--no-git` | ask, or `git init` | Run `git init`, or skip. It is also skipped when the folder is already inside a git repository or git is missing. |
| `--sdk <mode>` | `npm` | How the app depends on `@pepu-chain/sdk`: `vendor` or `npm`. See [Vendored SDK versus npm](#vendored-sdk-versus-npm). |
| `--skip-agent-files` | off | Leave out the agent kit: `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/mcp.json`, `.vscode/mcp.json` and `.claude/settings.json`. See [AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md in Templates](../agent-tooling/agents-md.md). |
| `--json` | off | Print exactly one JSON document on stdout. Implies `--yes`. For agents and scripts. |
| `--list` | off | Print the templates and exit. With `--json`, as JSON. |
| `-h`, `--help` | | Show usage. |
| `-v`, `--version` | | Show the CLI version. |

Parsing rules: an unknown flag, a missing value (`--template` with nothing after it), an invalid `--pm` or `--sdk` value, or a second positional argument is an error.

## Interactive flow

The prompts run only when stdin is a terminal and neither `--yes` nor `--json` is set. Each question is skipped when its flag was given. With no terminal (CI, piped input) the CLI behaves as if `--yes` were passed instead of waiting for an answer.

1. **Which template?** An arrow-key list. Each row shows the template title and its features (sign-in + embedded wallet, session keys, sponsored gas), and the description appears on the highlighted row. Default `consumer-app`.
2. **Project name.** Defaults to the directory's name, or `pepu-app`. The package name is a slug of it.
3. **Package manager.** `npm`, `pnpm`, `yarn` or `bun`, with the detected one marked.
4. **Install dependencies?** Yes by default.
5. **Initialize a git repository?** Yes by default.

Then the CLI copies the template, rewrites `package.json`, vendors the SDK, writes `.env.local`, adds the agent files, installs and runs `git init` as chosen, and shows numbered next steps.

Cancelling at any prompt exits with code 1 and creates nothing.

## What the scaffold does

1. Copies `templates/<name>` into the target folder and restores dotfiles.
2. Sets the `package.json` `name` to a slug of the project name and rewrites the `@pepu-chain/sdk` dependency (`workspace:*`) to the SDK spec.
3. Vendors the SDK into `vendor/pepu-sdk` when in vendor mode.
4. Generates `.env.local` from `.env.example`.
5. Applies the agent kit (kept, filled in from the shared kit, or dropped with `--skip-agent-files`).
6. Installs dependencies and runs `git init` when chosen.
7. Computes the next steps from the template's requirements and the actual contents of `.env.local`.

## Env prefill and next steps

`.env.local` keeps every comment and line of `.env.example` and is prefixed with a header that states the network: Pepe Unchained V2, mainnet, chain `97741`, currency PEPU, the public RPC and the explorer. The SDK already knows these, so no network variable needs setting by hand.

Secrets are never prefilled. `PRIVY_APP_SECRET`, `PRIVY_AUTHORIZATION_KEY`, `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` and `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` stay blank (any variable whose name matches `SECRET`, `AUTHORIZATION_KEY`, `API_KEY`, `PAYMASTER_URL` or `BUNDLER_URL` is treated as a credential). Values that a template's `.env.example` already carries as a public default stay as they are, for example the `WPEPU` address in `token-gated-app` and the paymaster contract address in `sponsored-demo`. If `.env.local` already exists it is not overwritten.

The next steps come from the SDK doctor's `TEMPLATE_REQUIREMENTS` and the Privy requirements table, checked against the real `.env.local`:

1. `cd <dir>`
2. The install command, when you skipped the install or it failed.
3. The env vars still blank, by name. Secrets stay server-side and out of git.
4. "Set at least one of A or B" for any-of groups (token-gated-app needs one gate token address).
5. The Privy dashboard settings the template needs, from `PEPU_PRIVY_REQUIREMENTS`.
6. The template's extra steps, with `{run:<script>}` expanded to your package manager's command (for example generating the authorization key for `game-app`, or deploying the contract for `nft-mint`).
7. The doctor command, if the template defines `doctor`.
8. The dev command.

The app runs and shows a setup screen even before you add a Privy App ID.

### Doctor

Every template has an `npm run doctor` script. It loads `.env.local` and runs `checkPepuEnv` from `@pepu-chain/sdk/doctor` for that template. It prints one line per required key (`ok` or `FAIL` plus the fix), never a value, and exits 1 when any required key is missing or malformed. The same check is available to agents as `pepu_check_env` and, for the dashboard, `pepu_check_privy_config`. See [Privy Env Vars and Verification](../privy/env-and-checks.md).

## JSON output

`--json` prints one document to stdout and sends everything else (including the package manager's install output) to stderr. Key names only, never values.

Success:

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `ok` | `true` | |
| `path` | string | Absolute path of the new project. |
| `targetDir` | string | Same as `path`. |
| `template` | string | Template name. |
| `title` | string | Template title. |
| `features` | array of `login`, `session`, `sponsor` | What the template demonstrates (display tags). The SDK doctor's `pillars` are separate. |
| `packageManager` | string | The one used for printed commands and the install. |
| `sdk` | object | `{ mode: "vendor" or "npm", spec?: string, fellBackToVendor: boolean }`. |
| `installed` | boolean | Whether the install ran and succeeded. |
| `gitInitialized` | boolean | Whether `git init` ran. |
| `envFile` | string, optional | `.env.local`, when generated. |
| `requiredEnv` | array | `{ key, secret, missing }` for each required variable. `missing` is true when the scaffold left it blank. |
| `missingEnv` | array of strings | The keys still to set. |
| `privyDashboard` | array | `{ id, label, fix }` for each Privy dashboard setting needed. |
| `nextSteps` | array of strings | The same steps the human output prints. |
| `agentFiles` | array of strings | Agent kit files present in the project. |
| `warnings` | array of strings | For example a failed install, a skipped `git init`, an SDK fallback. |

An example for a no-install scaffold (abridged):

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "path": "/home/me/my-app",
  "template": "game-app",
  "features": ["login", "session"],
  "packageManager": "pnpm",
  "sdk": { "mode": "npm", "spec": "^0.2.2", "fellBackToVendor": false },
  "installed": false,
  "gitInitialized": false,
  "envFile": ".env.local",
  "requiredEnv": [
    { "key": "NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_APP_ID", "secret": false, "missing": true },
    { "key": "PRIVY_APP_SECRET", "secret": true, "missing": true }
  ],
  "missingEnv": ["NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_APP_ID", "PRIVY_APP_SECRET"],
  "nextSteps": ["cd my-app", "pnpm install", "..."],
  "warnings": []
}
```

Failure (also exit code 1):

```json
{ "ok": false, "error": "Unknown template \"foo\".", "templates": ["consumer-app", "..."] }
```

`error` is always present. `templates` is added for an unknown template. Argument errors and an existing non-empty directory also come back this way.

`--list --json` prints `{ "ok": true, "templates": [...] }`, where each entry is the registry record (name, title, description, features, required and optional env, Privy dashboard ids, extra steps, `hasContracts`, difficulty, `recommendedFor`).

## Vendored SDK versus npm

By default the scaffold depends on `@pepu-chain/sdk` from npm. If the registry has no such package (or npm is offline), the CLI bundles a copy of the SDK instead. This is the vendored-SDK note:

| Mode | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--sdk npm` (default) | Writes `^<version>` from the registry. The CLI checks the registry with `npm view @pepu-chain/sdk version` (15 second timeout). If the SDK is not published, or npm is offline, it falls back to the vendored copy, says so as a warning, and reports `fellBackToVendor: true`. |
| `--sdk vendor` | Copies the bundled SDK into `vendor/pepu-sdk` in your project and rewrites the dependency to `file:./vendor/pepu-sdk`. The vendor folder is part of your project: commit it. |

If the CLI cannot find a bundled SDK, it warns that a dependency install may fail until the SDK is published or vendored.

To move a vendored project to npm later, change the `@pepu-chain/sdk` dependency to a registry range and delete `vendor/pepu-sdk`.

## Exit codes

| Code | When |
|---|---|
| 0 | Scaffold completed (even if the install or `git init` produced a warning), or `--help`, `--version`, `--list`. |
| 1 | Bad arguments, unknown template, target directory exists and is not empty, a prompt was cancelled, or an unexpected error. With `--json` the error is printed as `{ ok: false, error }` first. |

A failed install does not fail the scaffold: the project is created, a warning is recorded and the next steps tell you to run the install command yourself.

## What to expect

- The scaffold takes seconds; the install dominates.
- You end up with a folder that runs with `dev` and shows a setup screen listing exactly what is still missing.
- For sponsorship templates the CLI does not invent endpoints. It points you to the hosted bundler (`https://bundler.pepeunchained.com`, the default for `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL`) and tells you to set `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` to `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<token>` with your own project token (local defaults for your own services are `http://localhost:4337` and `http://localhost:8788`).

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `"<dir>" already exists and isn't empty.` | The target has files in it | Choose a new directory or empty it. The CLI never overwrites. |
| `Unknown template "<name>".` | Typo or a removed template | Run `npx create-pepu-app --list` and pass one of those names. |
| `--sdk requires "vendor" or "npm"` | Missing or wrong value | Pass `--sdk vendor` or `--sdk npm`. |
| Warning: `--sdk npm` fell back to the vendored copy | You are offline, or the registry check failed | Nothing to fix. Pass `--sdk vendor` to skip the registry check. |
| Warning: dependency install failed | Network, registry or package manager error | Run the printed install command in the project to see the error. |
| Warning: skipped git init | git is not installed, or the folder is already inside a repository | Nothing to fix, or run `git init` yourself. |
| Login fails after the first run | The Privy allowed origin does not match the port | Use the exact origin including the port (`http://localhost:3000`). See [Privy Setup Walkthrough](../onboarding/privy-setup.md). |

## Related

- [Template Gallery](../templates/index.md)
- [Quickstart: Zero to a Sponsored Transaction in 10 Minutes](../get-started/quickstart-app.md)
- [AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md in Templates](../agent-tooling/agents-md.md)
- [Environment Variables](../reference/env-vars.md)

pages.title: Architecture: Who Calls What
pages.content:
# Architecture: Who Calls What

One page showing the browser, your Next.js route handlers, Privy, the RPC, the bundler, the paymaster and the EntryPoint, and which credential each hop uses. Use it to find which package owns a hop and where a failure comes from.

> Status: the plain and Privy-session paths are proven on mainnet. The sponsored path is proven on mainnet through the hosted bundler (`https://bundler.pepeunchained.com`) and paymaster service (`https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com`), with the v2 paymaster deployed as a canary (internally reviewed 3x, external audit pending). The full combination of Google login, a Kernel session key and sponsorship is proven live in a browser on mainnet (2026-10-14) against the hosted bundler and v2 paymaster.

## Components

```
                       ┌────────────────────────── your app ───────────────────────────┐
 browser ──────────────► Next.js route handlers (SDK server entries) ──► PEPU RPC (Conduit)
 PepuPrivyProvider            │        │                │
 hooks (SDK react)            │        │                └──► bundler (ERC-4337 v0.7) ─► EntryPoint ─► Kernel account
        │                     │        └──► paymaster (ERC-7677 policy service) ─► signs, pays from deposit
        └──► Privy (login, wallets, signing, policies)
```

| Component | Role | Credential used |
|---|---|---|
| Browser | Login, owner signatures, UI | Privy access token (bearer) to your server |
| Route handlers | Verify the token, provision wallets, hold session keys, call services | `PRIVY_APP_SECRET`, `PRIVY_AUTHORIZATION_KEY`, session private key, paymaster URL |
| Privy | Users, embedded wallets, policy engine, signing | App ID (public), app secret, authorization key |
| PEPU RPC | Chain reads and raw transaction broadcast | None (public), or an authenticated URL via `PEPU_RPC_URL` |
| Bundler | Accepts UserOperations, submits through EntryPoint | `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` (private network or credential) |
| Paymaster | Approves sponsorship, pays gas | App key embedded in `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL`; Privy access token for the free tier (v2) |
| EntryPoint v0.7 `0x0000000071727De22E5E9d8BAf0edAc6f37da032` | Validates and executes UserOperations | None |

## Sequences

### Plain transaction (embedded wallet, user pays gas)

1. Browser: `PepuPrivyWagmiProvider`, wagmi `useSendTransaction` on the pinned embedded wallet.
2. Privy's confirmation modal; the wallet signs; the transaction is broadcast to the PEPU RPC.
3. Bundler, paymaster and your server are not involved.

### Privy session action (user pays gas)

1. Browser: `useSessionAct` posts to your action route with `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (`usePepuAuthFetch`).
2. Server: `createSessionActionRoute` verifies the token, finds the delegated wallet, re-checks the call against the scope.
3. Server to Privy: `eth_signTransaction` with `PRIVY_AUTHORIZATION_KEY`. Privy's policy engine evaluates the policy.
4. Server to RPC: `signAndBroadcast` sends the raw transaction (Privy's server-side `eth_sendTransaction` rejects chain 97741).

### Sponsored UserOperation (Privy Smart Wallets or direct)

1. Browser: `useSponsoredSend` (Privy Smart Wallets) or `useDirectSponsoredSend` (own bundler and paymaster) sends from the Kernel account (owner: embedded wallet).
2. Client to paymaster: `pm_getPaymasterStubData`, then bundler gas estimation, then `pm_getPaymasterData` (the second call is the authorization; stub data is unauthenticated by spec).
3. Owner signs the UserOperation; client sends `eth_sendUserOperation` to the bundler.
4. Bundler submits `handleOps` to the EntryPoint; the EntryPoint validates the account and the paymaster signature, executes, and charges the paymaster's deposit.

### Sponsored session action (the combination)

1. Browser: `useSponsoredSession.act()` posts to `/api/session/act`.
2. Server: `createSponsoredSessionRoutes` checks the live session, `assertCallsInScope`, takes the per-user lock.
3. Server: `loadKernelSessionAccount` rebuilds the account from the approval and the session key; `createPepuSponsoredClient` and `sendSponsored` send one UserOperation through the bundler with the paymaster.
4. EntryPoint: the Kernel account's validation runs the call policy and timestamp policy on-chain. Out of scope fails here.

## Package and subpath owning each hop

| Hop | Owner |
|---|---|
| Provider, wallet gate, hooks for auth | `@pepu-chain/sdk/privy/react`, `/privy/wagmi` |
| Token verification, ensure wallet, `requireUser` | `/privy/server` |
| Session policy, grant, act, revoke (Privy) | `/session`, `/session/server`, `/session/react` |
| Kernel policies, owner approval, session account | `/session/kernel` |
| Kernel account, sponsored client, probes | `/aa`, `/aa/kernel`, `/aa/react`, `/aa/react-direct` |
| Five session routes and browser flow | `/combo`, `/combo/react` |
| v2 project helpers, REST client | `/paymaster`, `/paymaster/server` |
| Endpoint resolution | root (`resolvePepuEndpoints`, `PEPU_HOSTED` in `src/endpoints.ts`) |
| Readiness checks | `/doctor` |

## Local development versus hosted

| | Local development | Hosted |
|---|---|---|
| Bundler | `http://localhost:4337` (`services/bundler`) | `https://bundler.pepeunchained.com` (SDK default for `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL`) |
| Paymaster | `http://localhost:8788/v2/paymaster/<token>` (`services/paymaster/policy-service`) | `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<token>` in `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL`; the token is always part of the URL, so there is no tokenless default (the SDK default is the base `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com`) |
| App | `http://localhost:3000` (must match Privy Allowed origins) | Your production origin, also in Allowed origins |

The hosted URLs live in one place, `PEPU_HOSTED` in `packages/sdk/src/endpoints.ts` (`bundlerUrl`, `paymasterBaseUrl`, and `paymasterUrl: null`), and the SDK, MCP server and docs read it. See [Infrastructure Map](../infra/overview.md).

## Common failures

| Symptom | Hop | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 401 from your route | Browser to server | Secret belongs to another app, or no token; see [Privy Env Vars](../privy/env-and-checks.md) |
| `BUNDLER_UNREACHABLE` | Server to bundler | Fix `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` |
| `PAYMASTER_*` | Server to paymaster | [Error Reference](../reference/errors.md) |
| UserOperation reverts at validation | Kernel account | Call outside session scope, or expired |

## Related

- [The Three Pillars](../get-started/pillars.md)
- [Trust and Security Model](trust-and-security.md)
- [Google Login, Session and Sponsorship End to End](../onboarding/google-session-sponsored.md)

pages.title: Smart Account Paths: Plain Wallet, ZeroDev-Native or Privy Smart Wallets
Trust and Security Model
pages.content:
# Trust and Security Model

States precisely what each mechanism protects against and who is trusted, so builders do not overclaim. Covers off-chain versus on-chain enforcement, secret handling and the session store. Read it before telling users what a session or sponsorship guarantees.

> Status: describes the mechanisms proven on mainnet. The v2 paymaster is deployed as a canary: internally reviewed 3x, external audit pending, funded in small tranches. Keep deposits small. The v1 paymaster is retired.

## Privy session signers (off-chain)

- Scope (one contract, listed functions, zero value, expiry) is enforced by Privy's backend policy engine on each signing request. You trust Privy and your policy configuration.
- It cannot bound gas; the user pays it.
- The authorization key lets your server request signatures for any wallet that granted its quorum, within each policy. A policy must always be attached; the SDK refuses to build an unscoped one.
- Revocation: `removeSigners` from the browser is the real revoke.
- Show `SESSION_TRUST_NOTICE["privy-offchain"]` on the consent screen.

## Kernel session keys (on-chain)

- Scope is enforced by the call policy v0.0.4 and timestamp policy contracts during UserOperation validation. It holds even if your backend is compromised.
- A leaked session key can act within the permission until expiry: the listed targets, selectors, value limit, validity window.
- The owner key never leaves Privy and the browser. The approval holds no secret.
- Revocation deletes the server key at once; the on-chain grant lapses at expiry (uninstalling is an owner-signed call a destination-allowlisted paymaster should not sponsor). Keep sessions short.
- Show `SESSION_TRUST_NOTICE["kernel-onchain"]`.

## Paymaster

- **Signer:** the paymaster contract trusts any signature from its authorized signer, so the signer key is a hot wallet for the deposit. Keep the deposit small and monitored.
- **Policy service:** signs only if the destination allowlist, per-user, per-app and global caps pass. The allowlist limits what sponsorship money can pay for; it does not protect the user's account.
- **Project deposits (v2, canary):** deposits only, no withdrawals by anyone. `projectId = keccak256(bytes(appId))`. Ownership is Privy-verified: verify the app secret, get an EIP-712 attestation, call `claimProject`. The claim sets the owner only; the owner then calls `setTargets`, `setDailyLimit` and `setSenderDailyLimit`. Re-claims, and the first claim of a project that already holds funds, are timelocked 48 hours and can be cancelled (the owner once per new owner). A project must have a per-wallet limit. Pausing is the exit. Free tier: 100 PEPU per user per day and 50 PEPU per hour (enforced by the service), verified Privy users from PEPU's own Privy app only, no chain-wide ceiling. Not externally audited.
- **A paymaster URL is a credential.** It embeds a token. A project client token (`ppt_`) is publishable but works only from the project's allowed origins (`project_origin_not_allowed` otherwise); a project server key (`ppk_`) is secret and belongs in a backend. A third-party app's own Privy token does not unlock the free tier.

## Secrets: where each may live

| Secret | May live | Never |
|---|---|---|
| `PRIVY_APP_SECRET` | Server env | `NEXT_PUBLIC_`, client code, git, logs |
| `PRIVY_AUTHORIZATION_KEY` | Server env | Same; a production signing key |
| Session private key | Server session store, encrypted at rest in production | Browser, logs |
| `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL`, `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` | Server env | Browser unless you accept exposing the credential |
| Policy service signer, bundler executor keys | Operator's secret store | Repo |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_APP_ID`, quorum id | Public by design | n/a |

The SDK's server entries (`/privy/server`, `/session/server`, `/combo`, `/paymaster/server`) call `assertServerOnly` and refuse to load in a browser bundle. Server-only code never reads `NEXT_PUBLIC_` secrets. Doctor and MCP check tools report presence and length, never values. `requestClaimAttestation` sends your Privy app secret to the PEPU service for one request: use a dedicated app and rotate afterwards.

## Session store options

| Store | Durability | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `createMemoryStore()` | Lost on restart, not shared across instances, key in plaintext memory | Development and tests only |
| Your `SessionStore` on a database or KV | Durable | Production, with `sessionPrivateKey` encrypted at rest (KMS or envelope key) and an atomic or distributed `tryLock` |

## Threat table

| Threat | Privy mode | Kernel mode |
|---|---|---|
| Compromised app server | Can sign within each policy via the authorization key | Can act within the on-chain permission until expiry |
| Compromised Privy | Total over wallets | Cannot exceed the owner-signed permission, but controls the owner key |
| Leaked authorization key | Within policies, for all granting users | n/a |
| Leaked session key | n/a | Within scope until expiry |
| Out-of-scope call | Denied by Privy's engine | Fails EntryPoint validation |
| Gas drain of user | Possible: user pays | Sponsored; bounded by paymaster caps |
| Paymaster budget drain | n/a | Bounded by allowlist and caps |

Everything the SDK server boundary enforces: user id only from a verified token, owner address from Privy's records, calls re-checked against scope before signing, per-user lock and rate limit, approval bound to this account and permission id. For Kernel mode these are fail-fast checks; the chain is the real enforcement.

## Related

- [Session Keys](../onboarding/session-keys.md)
- [Sponsored Transactions](../onboarding/sponsored-transactions.md)
- [Sponsorship Tiers](../onboarding/sponsorship-tiers.md)
- [Authorization Keys](../privy/authorization-keys.md)
- [Audits and Verification Status](../contracts/audits.md)

pages.title: Address Map
pages.content:
# Address Map

Every contract address in the SDK registry for Pepe Unchained V2 mainnet (chain `97741`), verified live on chain, with a source and a do-not-substitute note for each. Use this as the one table to copy from. In code, read the registry instead of pasting: `getContract`, `listContracts`, `getPepuAddresses` (an array of rows; `getPepuAddressMap` returns the same rows keyed by name) and `isDeployed` from `@pepu-chain/sdk`.

> Status: **verified**. Every address below returned non-empty bytecode from `eth_getCode` when `pnpm --filter @pepu-chain/sdk live-check` was run on **2026-10-14** (read-only). The registry's own `verifiedAt` stamps are 2026-10-02 for the older entries and 2026-10-14 for the v2 paymaster. Mainnet only; testnet (97740) is out of scope. `paymasterV2` is deployed as a canary: internally reviewed 3x, external audit pending, funded in small tranches. The v1 paymaster is retired.

## Verification method

1. Run `pnpm --filter @pepu-chain/sdk live-check` from the repository root. It calls `eth_getCode` on each registry address and prints the byte count; it also confirms the canonical Multicall3 address has no code.
2. By hand, `cast code <address> --rpc-url https://rpc-pepu-v2-mainnet-0.t.conduit.xyz`, or the MCP tool `pepu_check_contract_deployed`.
3. Code present is not proof of function. Several entries were also exercised (see the notes).

Result on 2026-10-14: all 16 deployed entries `OK`, none pending, canonical Multicall3 `empty (expected)`.

## Core infrastructure

| Name | Address | Bytes | Source | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CREATE2 deterministic deployer (`create2Factory`) | `0x4e59b44847b379578588920cA78FbF26c0B4956C` | 69 | Canonical Nick's-method deployer | Used to deploy Multicall3 and Permit2. See [CREATE2 and Deterministic Deployment](create2-and-deterministic-deployment.md) |
| Multicall3 (`multicall3`) | `0x9CE19273Ae9c24437DFF512E8DFCAed4E4B001bd` | 3808 | PEPU-specific deployment from `mds1/multicall3` source via CREATE2, zero salt | **Not the canonical address.** `0xcA11bde05977b3631167028862bE2a173976CA11` has no code here and never can. See [The Multicall3 Trap](multicall3.md) |
| Permit2 (`permit2`) | `0x000000000022D473030F116dDEE9F6B43aC78BA3` | 9152 | Canonical Uniswap Permit2, deployed by PEPU via CREATE2 | Canonical address. Not PepuSwap's copy. See [Permit2](permit2.md) |

## ERC-4337 and Kernel (ZeroDev Conduit Marketplace integration)

| Name | Address | Bytes | Source | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| EntryPoint v0.6 (`entryPoint06`) | `0x5FF137D4b0FDCD49DcA30c7CF57E578a026d2789` | 23689 | ZeroDev, at the canonical v0.6 address | Served by the bundler; not used by Kernel v3.1 |
| EntryPoint v0.7 (`entryPoint07`) | `0x0000000071727De22E5E9d8BAf0edAc6f37da032` | 16035 | ZeroDev, at the canonical v0.7 address | The version Kernel v3.x, the paymaster and Privy target |
| Kernel v3 factory (`kernelFactory`) | `0xaac5D4240AF87249B3f71BC8E4A2cae074A3E419` | 989 | ZeroDev | Account factory; `getAddress` gives the counterfactual address |
| Kernel MetaFactory (`kernelMetaFactory`) | `0xd703aaE79538628d27099B8c4f621bE4CCd142d5` | 1871 | ZeroDev | |
| Kernel v3.1 implementation (`kernelImplementation`) | `0xbAC849bB641841b44E965fb01A4Bf5F074F84B4d` | 22784 | ZeroDev | What `kernelFactory.implementation()` resolves to; same address ZeroDev uses on every chain with this version |
| Kernel ECDSA validator (`ecdsaValidator`) | `0x845ADb2C711129d4f3966735eD98a9F09fC4cE57` | 1819 | ZeroDev | Default validator: an ECDSA key (for example a Privy embedded wallet) authorises the account |
| Kernel ECDSA signer module (`kernelEcdsaSignerModule`) | `0x6A6F069E2a08c2468e7724Ab3250CdBFBA14D4FF` | 1609 | ZeroDev | Signer in permission-validator session keys |
| Call policy v0.0.4 (`kernelCallPolicyV004`) | `0x9a52283276A0ec8740DF50bF01B28A80D880eaf2` | 6539 | ZeroDev | Scopes a session key to targets and selectors. **Use v0.0.4, not v0.0.5**: v0.0.5 is not deployed on PEPU, so the SDK pins `CallPolicyVersion.V0_0_4` |
| Timestamp policy (`kernelTimestampPolicy`) | `0xB9f8f524bE6EcD8C945b1b87f9ae5C192FdCE20F` | 1441 | ZeroDev | Bounds a session key to a validity window |

## Paymaster and demo

| Name | Address | Bytes | Source | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Paymaster v2 (`paymaster` and `paymasterV2`, same contract) | `0xdb28528C9399C33c9A0297E8A62F39145acbC30D` | 23722 | This project: `PepuSponsoredPaymasterV7` | **Deployed as a canary** (about block 10537341): internally reviewed 3x, external audit pending, funded in small tranches. Owner and manager are separate addresses (`0x5966…4A1` and `0x063A…aBb0`). Free pool seeded with 300 PEPU. Proven with a project-sponsored operation through the hosted bundler and paymaster. Keep deposits small. See [Paymaster Overview](../infra/paymaster/overview.md) |
| Paymaster v1 (`paymasterV1`) | `0x2B6FED323bFA24f0475f4e1Dd3C7F6Cc1f3ae8B0` | 8842 | This project: `PepuVerifyingPaymasterV7` | **Retired.** It was funded, and its EntryPoint deposit has been withdrawn (0), so it cannot sponsor anything. The bytecode still exists. Never deposit to it. Kept for history |
| TapScore (`tapScore`) | `0x261eA5971B93237a56990206A46Bc80318e4d078` | 587 | This project: demo contract | `tap()` with no arguments, non-payable. Used by the `game-app` and `sponsored-demo` templates |

## PepuSwap (third party)

PepuSwap is not in `pepuContracts`; it has its own registry (`getPepuSwapContract`, `listPepuSwapContracts`). Its addresses, including the **non-canonical** multicall and Permit2 that must not replace the ones above, are on [PepuSwap Addresses](pepuswap.md).

## Canonical versus PEPU-specific

| Contract | Canonical address used on PEPU? |
|---|---|
| CREATE2 deployer | Yes |
| Permit2 | Yes |
| EntryPoint v0.6 and v0.7 | Yes |
| Multicall3 | **No.** PEPU-specific at `0x9CE19273…01bd` |
| Kernel contracts | ZeroDev's standard addresses for these versions (no canonical-address trick; use the registry) |
| Paymaster, TapScore | Project-specific |

## Do-not-substitute checklist

- Never use `0xcA11bde05977b3631167028862bE2a173976CA11` as Multicall3 on PEPU. `assertNotCanonicalMulticall3` throws `MULTICALL3_CANONICAL_ADDRESS`.
- Never use PepuSwap's `0xB461…8b4B` as Permit2 or its `0x927a…383B` as Multicall3.
- Never use call policy v0.0.5.
- Never write an address for `paymasterV2` until it is announced.

## Related

- [Deployed Contracts Reference](deployed-contracts.md)
- [EntryPoints and Kernel](entrypoints-and-kernel.md)

pages.title: Audits and Verification Status
pages.content:
# Audits and Verification Status

What has and has not been reviewed, tested or verified for each PEPU contract. **There has been no external audit of any PEPU-authored contract.** The only reviews are three internal, AI-assisted reviews of the v2 paymaster, produced with the [pashov](https://github.com/pashov/skills) `solidity-auditor` methodology. They are not third-party audits, carry no assurance from an independent firm and cannot prove the absence of vulnerabilities. Read this before depositing into or depending on any of these contracts.

> Status: v2 paymaster **deployed as a canary: internally reviewed 3x, external audit pending, funded in small tranches**. v1 paymaster **retired** (deposit withdrawn), tested, never externally audited. Third-party contracts (ZeroDev Kernel and EntryPoints, Permit2, Multicall3) are upstream code deployed unmodified; PEPU has not audited them.

## Per-contract table

| Contract | Address | Source verified | Tests | Audit status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Paymaster v1 `PepuVerifyingPaymasterV7` | `0x2B6FED323bFA24f0475f4e1Dd3C7F6Cc1f3ae8B0` | Deployed, now retired; byte-for-byte hash cross-check with the policy service (frozen golden vector) | 18 Foundry tests (17 security tests plus the cross-check) | **None external.** Retired: its EntryPoint deposit was withdrawn and it cannot sponsor anything. A fork of Pimlico's singleton paymaster with ERC-20 mode removed. Not covered by the 2026-10 internal reviews, which target v2 |
| Paymaster v2 `PepuSponsoredPaymasterV7` | `0xdb28528C9399C33c9A0297E8A62F39145acbC30D` | Deployed on mainnet as a canary (2026-10-14) | 195 Foundry tests (18 v1, 177 v2: unit, fuzz, 6 invariants, a real-EntryPoint v0.7 harness, reentrancy, cross-language vectors, review-3 regressions; also at 2,000 fuzz runs) and 328 policy-service tests; one project-sponsored operation proven on mainnet through the hosted URLs | **Three internal reviews, external audit pending.** Funded in small tranches. Do not deposit large amounts before an external audit |
| Multicall3 | `0x9CE19273Ae9c24437DFF512E8DFCAed4E4B001bd` | Verified on pepuscan; built from canonical `mds1/multicall3` source with canonical settings | Confirmed working with viem's `multicall()` | Upstream code, no PEPU changes. No PEPU audit |
| Permit2 | `0x000000000022D473030F116dDEE9F6B43aC78BA3` | Exact upstream creation bytecode; address reproduced independently by `prove-address.sh` | `DOMAIN_SEPARATOR()` call checked | Upstream code, no PEPU changes. No PEPU audit |
| EntryPoint v0.6 and v0.7, Kernel v3.1, validator, signer, call and timestamp policies | see [Address Map](address-map.md) | ZeroDev deployments through Conduit Marketplace | `eth_getCode` live check; Kernel flows exercised on mainnet | ZeroDev's own audits apply to upstream code; PEPU did not review them. Call policy v0.0.4 is used because v0.0.5 is not deployed |
| TapScore | `0x261eA5971B93237a56990206A46Bc80318e4d078` | Verified on pepuscan | Used by templates and demos | A demo contract. Not for value |
| CREATE2 deployer | `0x4e59b44847b379578588920cA78FbF26c0B4956C` | Standard deployer, 69 bytes | n/a | Widely used upstream |

"Verified source" means the source is published on pepuscan or reproducible from the repository; it does not mean audited. The registry check `pnpm --filter @pepu-chain/sdk live-check` confirms bytecode exists (last run 2026-10-03); it proves nothing about correctness.

## The three internal reviews of v2

All three live in `services/paymaster/audits/`. The findings are reproduced as written there; each file begins with a fix-status table.

1. **`2026-10-internal-review.md`** reviewed commit `dafc259` (contract, EntryPoint interaction, deploy script, signing service). It built a harness on the real EntryPoint v0.7 sources because the existing solvency tests used a mock. 118 tests passed at baseline. 0 Critical, 0 High, 2 Medium, 5 Low, 8 Info.
2. **`2026-10-delta-review.md`** (2026-10-02) reviewed the later deposit-only and attested-claim changes (`f55527f..c354508`) that the first review did not cover. 1 Medium, 4 Low, plus cheap leads, all fixed afterwards. Baseline 165 Foundry and 235 vitest tests passing; 171 and 246 after the fixes.
3. **`2026-10-review-3.md`** (2026-10-09) reviewed commit `4882bd3` with three parallel auditors (economics and accounting; access control and governance; ERC-4337 conformance and the signer service), all on the real EntryPoint v0.7. 0 Critical, 0 High, 3 Medium, 6 Low, plus Info items and leads. The Medium and Low findings and three Info items were fixed afterwards; the rest are documented.

### Fix status: first review

| ID | Severity | Finding | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| M-1 | Medium | Unexecuted approvals count as outstanding; the public client token could lock a project's budget | Mitigated: reservation caps (2 per wallet, 5% per IP, 25% total), per-IP rate limit, 60 s window, replace-on-retry. Residual: many-address attacker can saturate the client-token pool |
| M-2 | Medium | Manager or owner can extract funds indirectly (add signer plus own bundler) | Fixed, claims restated: additions timelocked, on-chain fee cap, separate manager role at deploy. Residual: gas quantities not capped on chain; an already-authorised signer plus bundler can burn daily limits |
| L-1 | Low | Daily counter refund skipped for stale-day operations | Fixed: context records the bucket the reservation landed in |
| L-2 | Low | Allowlist checks calldata shape, not account type | Mitigated: optional per-project codehash pin. Residual documented |
| L-3 | Low | `tx.origin` gate banned by ERC-7562; `address(0)` allowlist divergence | Documented: v2 supported only behind a self-run bundler with safe mode off |
| L-4 | Low | Service signs any user gas fields | Fixed: gas and fee bounds in the service plus an on-chain fee cap |
