| L-5 | Low | Post-op overhead floor 14,000 below the attacker-forceable 14.5k | Fixed: floor 18,000, deploy default 20,000 |
| I-1 | Info | Dead 64-byte signature branch | Fixed |
| I-2 | Info | Renounce and manager footguns | Unchanged, documented |
| I-3 | Info | Owner = manager = deployer defaults; script key handling | Partly fixed: owner and manager separated in the script; the `eval` of `.env` and `--private-key` flag unchanged (use a keystore or hardware wallet) |
| I-4 | Info | Free pool has no outflow ceiling | Unchanged (decision) |
| I-5 | Info | `validAfter = now` has no clock-skew tolerance | Fixed: 5 s skew |
| I-6 | Info | Manager could `unlockStake` | Fixed: owner only |
| I-7 | Info | `ECDSA.recover` reverts on malformed signatures | Fixed: signature failure, not a revert |
| I-8 | Info | Worst-case penalty charged unconditionally | Unchanged, documented |

The first review predates the deposit-only change, so its findings about withdrawals, the withdraw-delay-derived timelock and registrant-namespaced ids describe a design that no longer exists.

### Fix status: delta review

| # | Severity | Finding | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (M1) | Medium | A signer-chosen mode bit disabled the `tx.origin` bundler gate | Fixed: mode byte must be exactly `0x02`; gate always enforced |
| 2 (L1) | Low | A stranger could exhaust the verify limiter and lock out the owner | Fixed: failure budget keyed on (app id, SIWE address), charged only when Privy rejects |
| 3 (L2) | Low | Attestation did not bind targets and limits | Fixed: claim sets only the owner; owner configures afterwards |
| 4 (L3) | Low | Pending re-claim survived a voluntary transfer and revived when a signer was re-added | Fixed |
| 5 (L4) | Low | Credentials issued to the previous owner kept working | Fixed: revoked on owner change (`project_owner_changed`) |
| Lead | Cheap | Spoofable per-IP limits via leftmost `X-Forwarded-For` | Fixed: rightmost-by-hops |
| Lead | Cheap | App id case handling | Documented, no code change |
| I-6, I-8, I-5 | Info | No cap on attestation deadline; no upper bound on delay; tautological asserts | Fixed |
| I-2 | Info | Claim attestor and sponsorship signer share one signer set | Documented (needs a separate role; does not fit the contract size) |
| I-1, I-3, I-4, I-7 | Info | Stranded `keccak256("")` deposits, self re-claim, derived deposit, signer status unchecked | Documented only |
| Lead | | Privy cross-app check | **Open**: needs a live two-app test before launch |
| Lead | | First claim immediate for funded unclaimed projects | **Fixed in review 3 (M-1)**: pending for the admin delay, cancellable |

### Fix status: review 3

| ID | Severity | Finding | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| M-1 | Medium | A funded, unclaimed project has no pause defence (a compromised manager can claim and drain it after the 48 h bundler/signer timelock) | Fixed: the first claim of a funded project is pending for `adminChangeDelay`, signer-bound, cancellable by the contract owner or manager; sponsor fee caps cannot exceed the immutable default. Residual: after a renounce with a rogue manager nobody can cancel |
| M-2 | Medium | A hostile owner can veto a recovery re-claim forever | Fixed: one veto per (project, new owner); the second attested re-claim by the same new owner is final and survives an ownership transfer |
| M-3 | Medium | Unthrottled denials write a SQLite audit row each; ERC-7677 junk tokens dodge the limiter | Fixed: unknown credentials are not persisted, per-IP limiters before the body is read, 30-day audit retention |
| L-1 | Low | Projects get no per-wallet limit after a claim | Fixed: a project with no per-wallet limit fails closed on chain and in the service |
| L-2 | Low | A manager can re-lock the owner's unlocked stake for 136 years | Fixed: `addStake` is owner-only, delay at most 30 days |
| L-3 | Low | Removing `address(0)` as a bundler is irreversible | Fixed: `address(0)` can be re-proposed as a bundler |
| L-4 | Low | Replacing an approval for the same nonce undercounts signed exposure | Fixed: the larger reservation stays until the old one expires |
| L-5 | Low | `allowAccountDeployment=false` not enforced on `/v2/sponsor` | Fixed: enforced in the engine |
| L-6 | Low | Real worst-case postOp was 16.2k to 18.1k gas against the 18,000 floor | Fixed: overhead snapshotted at validation; worst case 13,918 |
| Info | | B5 expiries, C-L1 appId binding, A7 free-tier validation, openapi 400/413 | Fixed |
| Info | | C-L2 log rescans, A4 overcharge, A5 midnight gap, A6 immutable fee cap, A8 stranded funds, free-pool sybil cost, B leads, ERC-7562 bundler conformance | Documented in the spec (section 16.3), not fixed |

## Known gaps

- **No external audit** of the immutable v2 contract that will hold third-party money, and none of v1.
- **No fork test** against the PEPU chain's real EntryPoint v0.7 and Nitro gas schedule. The harness uses vendored sources on a local EVM, so the 18,000-gas post-op floor has not been re-measured on PEPU.
- **No Alto canary** for the v2 `tx.origin` gate and storage access.
- No automatic on-chain reconciliation for v1; the v2 reconciler is untested against a live deployment.
- The review lens was AI-only (one sequential reviewer for the first two reviews, three parallel reviewers for the third): no independent human review.
- Contract size margin is 854 bytes, and only because the contract is compiled with 8,000 optimizer runs (25,115 bytes at 1,000,000); any change needs a re-check.

## How to report an issue

Do not open a public issue for a vulnerability. Follow [SECURITY.md](../../SECURITY.md): email contact@pepeunchained.com with a description, reproduction steps, the affected package or file and whether it touches deployed contracts. The policy covers this repository's code (the paymaster contracts and services live here too; if in doubt, send it); it does not cover the chain, Conduit, pepuscan or third-party contracts such as Kernel.

## Related

- [Paymaster v2 Spec Summary](paymaster-v2-spec.md)
- [PepuSponsoredPaymasterV7 Contract](../infra/paymaster/contracts.md)
- [Address Map](address-map.md)
- [Trust and Security Model](../concepts/trust-and-security.md)

pages.title: CREATE2 and Deterministic Deployment
pages.content:
# CREATE2 and Deterministic Deployment

How PEPU's deterministic deployer was used to put Multicall3 and Permit2 on chain, what salt and init code each used, and how to reproduce the addresses. Read it if you want to deploy your own contract at a predictable address or verify the proofs.

> Status: **proven**. The deployer has 69 bytes of code on mainnet (checked 2026-10-03), and both deployments below landed from it and are verified.

## The deployer

| | |
|---|---|
| Address | `0x4e59b44847b379578588920cA78FbF26c0B4956C` |
| What it is | The standard "Nick's method" deterministic deployer, at the same address as on every chain that has it |
| Registry key | `create2Factory` |
| Calling convention | Send a transaction **to** the deployer whose data is `salt (32 bytes) ‖ initCode`. It runs `CREATE2` and the new contract's address is not returned (compute it) |
| Address formula | `address = last 20 bytes of keccak256(0xff ‖ deployer ‖ salt ‖ keccak256(initCode))` |

Anything deployed through it with the same salt and init code lands at the same address on any chain that has the deployer. The Alto bundler also uses it to deploy its own simulation contracts.

## What was deployed this way

| Contract | Salt | Init code | Address | Transaction |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Multicall3 (PEPU-specific) | all zeros | `contracts/multicall3/initcode.hex`, from `mds1/multicall3` source, solc 0.8.12, optimizer 10,000,000 runs | `0x9CE19273Ae9c24437DFF512E8DFCAed4E4B001bd` (`contracts/multicall3/predicted.txt`) | `0xf9d8f45010e2a2020871af9a677d134e9b43e039a0a73c09bcd22d1825f99241`, block 10521048 |
| Permit2 (canonical) | `0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000d3af2663da51c10215000000` (`contracts/permit2/salt.txt`) | `contracts/permit2/initcode.hex`, the exact upstream creation bytecode | `0x000000000022D473030F116dDEE9F6B43aC78BA3` (`contracts/permit2/predicted.txt`) | `0xbb0a23420f47dd4dbb524d96f46115011a66fc88bbdf0963cd24a50feb6f7c93`, block 10521367 |

Permit2 reproduces its **canonical** address because that address was itself produced by CREATE2 with Uniswap's salt. Multicall3's canonical address was not produced by CREATE2 (it came from a plain `CREATE` by a burn key through a pre-signed 1,000,000-gas transaction), so no salt can reproduce it, and that transaction cannot run on this chain. PEPU's Multicall3 is therefore at a different, but reproducible, address. See [The Multicall3 Trap](multicall3.md).

## Reproduce an address

With upstream Foundry (not `foundry-zksync`, which can shadow `forge` and `cast` on `PATH`; check `forge --version`):

```bash
cast create2 \
  --deployer 0x4e59b44847b379578588920cA78FbF26c0B4956C \
  --salt 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000d3af2663da51c10215000000 \
  --init-code "$(cat contracts/permit2/initcode.hex)"
# expect 0x000000000022D473030F116dDEE9F6B43aC78BA3
```

By hand: `keccak256(0xff ++ deployer ++ salt ++ keccak256(initcode))`, take the last 40 hex characters. `contracts/permit2/prove-address.sh` does both and prints `RESULT: MATCH`.

Check on chain, read-only:

```bash
cast code 0x000000000022D473030F116dDEE9F6B43aC78BA3 --rpc-url https://rpc-pepu-v2-mainnet-0.t.conduit.xyz
```

## Deploy your own contract deterministically

1. Compile and keep the creation bytecode (`initcode`).
2. Pick a salt and compute the predicted address as above.
3. Check the predicted address has no code.
4. Send a transaction to `0x4e59…956C` with data `salt ‖ initCode`. Set an explicit gas limit: Arbitrum Nitro charges differently from L1, and a bytecode that fits in 1,000,000 gas elsewhere can need far more here (Multicall3 needed about 14.3 million for the plain-`CREATE` route; the CREATE2 deploy used 874,693).
5. Re-check `eth_getCode` at the predicted address.

## Scripts

| Script | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `deploy/deploy-multicall3.sh` | Deploys Multicall3. Idempotent: exits if code already exists at the predicted address |
| `deploy/verify-multicall3.sh` | Verification checks |
| `contracts/permit2/deploy-permit2.sh` | Rebuilds, compares the creation bytecode to `initcode.hex`, refuses to broadcast on drift, deploys |
| `contracts/permit2/prove-address.sh` | Independent address computation, read-only |
| `contracts/permit2/compute-domain-separator.sh`, `estimate-gas.sh` | Domain and gas checks |
| `deploy/deploy-tapscore.sh`, `deploy/fund-paymaster.sh`, `deploy/allow-bundler.sh` | TapScore deploy and paymaster operations (not CREATE2) |

These read private keys and the RPC key from gitignored env files. Do not paste keys anywhere.

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Computed address does not match | Different init code (compiler version, optimizer runs, constructor args or line endings) | Reproduce the exact build settings; `forge build --force` and compare to `initcode.hex` |
| Deployment transaction succeeds but no code at the address | Wrong salt or init code, or the call reverted inside the deployer (it returns no data) | Recompute; raise the gas limit |
| Out of gas on a plain `CREATE` replay | Nitro needs far more gas than the replayed transaction allows | Use CREATE2 through the deployer instead |
| `forge` behaves oddly | `foundry-zksync` first on `PATH` | Use upstream Foundry |

## Related

- [Address Map](address-map.md)
- [The Multicall3 Trap](multicall3.md)
- [Permit2](permit2.md)
- [Deploy and Verify a Contract](deployment.md)

pages.title: Deployed Contracts Reference
pages.content:
# Deployed Contracts Reference

The complete, current answer to "does standard contract X exist on Pepe Unchained V2, and where." Every address below is on **mainnet (chain `97741`)** unless stated otherwise — see [Network Reference](../get-started/network-reference.md#testnet-out-of-scope-today) for why testnet isn't covered here.

Check this page, not a canonical-address list you already have memorized, before hardcoding anything for PEPU. Multicall3 is live at an unusual address, and the paymaster contracts have caveats attached — read the notes, not just the address column.

## Core infrastructure

| Contract | Address | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| CREATE2 deterministic deployer | `0x4e59b44847b379578588920cA78FbF26c0B4956C` | **Deployed**, canonical address | Standard "Nick's method" deterministic deployer. Multicall3 and Permit2 were deployed through it. See [CREATE2 and Deterministic Deployment](create2-and-deterministic-deployment.md). |
| Multicall3 | `0x9CE19273Ae9c24437DFF512E8DFCAed4E4B001bd` | **Deployed — NOT at the canonical address** | Read [The Multicall3 Trap](multicall3.md) before using this. The canonical address (`0xcA11bde05977b3631167028862bE2a173976CA11`) is structurally unreachable on this chain. This deployment was built from canonical `mds1/multicall3` source (solc `0.8.12`, optimizer `10,000,000` runs), deployed via the CREATE2 deterministic deployer above with a zero salt, verified on pepuscan, and confirmed working with viem's `multicall()`. Receipt: transaction `0xf9d8f450…99241` in block 10521048. |
| Permit2 | `0x000000000022D473030F116dDEE9F6B43aC78BA3` (canonical) | **Deployed**, canonical address | Deployed via ordinary CREATE2 at the canonical address (9,152 bytes of live bytecode confirmed via `eth_getCode`). Deployment proof and receipt: [Permit2](permit2.md) and `contracts/permit2/`. |

## ERC-4337 / smart accounts (mainnet only)

Deployed by ZeroDev's one-click Conduit Marketplace integration, plus a project-deployed paymaster canary. All bytecode was re-verified with `eth_getCode` on 2026-10-14. The complete table with byte counts and sources is the [Address Map](address-map.md); the roles are explained on [EntryPoints and Kernel](entrypoints-and-kernel.md).

| Contract | Address | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| EntryPoint v0.6 | `0x5FF137D4b0FDCD49DcA30c7CF57E578a026d2789` | **Deployed**, canonical address | |
| EntryPoint v0.7 | `0x0000000071727De22E5E9d8BAf0edAc6f37da032` | **Deployed**, canonical address | The version Kernel v3.x, the paymaster, the bundler and Privy target |
| Kernel v3 account factory | `0xaac5D4240AF87249B3f71BC8E4A2cae074A3E419` | **Deployed** | The smart-account factory Privy lists as a selectable option |
| Kernel MetaFactory | `0xd703aaE79538628d27099B8c4f621bE4CCd142d5` | **Deployed** | |
| Kernel v3.1 implementation | `0xbAC849bB641841b44E965fb01A4Bf5F074F84B4d` | **Deployed** | What the factory resolves to |
| Kernel ECDSA validator | `0x845ADb2C711129d4f3966735eD98a9F09fC4cE57` | **Deployed** | Default root validator |
| Kernel ECDSA signer module | `0x6A6F069E2a08c2468e7724Ab3250CdBFBA14D4FF` | **Deployed** | Signer in session-key permissions |
| Call policy v0.0.4 | `0x9a52283276A0ec8740DF50bF01B28A80D880eaf2` | **Deployed** | Pinned; v0.0.5 is not deployed on PEPU |
| Timestamp policy | `0xB9f8f524bE6EcD8C945b1b87f9ae5C192FdCE20F` | **Deployed** | Session-key validity window |
| Paymaster v2 (`PepuSponsoredPaymasterV7`) | `0xdb28528C9399C33c9A0297E8A62F39145acbC30D` | **Deployed as a canary** | This project's own contract: internally reviewed 3x, external audit pending, funded in small tranches. In the registry as `paymaster` and `paymasterV2`. Free pool seeded with 300 PEPU. Sponsorship through it is **proven** with a project-sponsored operation through the hosted URLs. Keep deposits small. See [Paymaster v2 Spec Summary](paymaster-v2-spec.md) |
| Paymaster v1 (`PepuVerifyingPaymasterV7`) | `0x2B6FED323bFA24f0475f4e1Dd3C7F6Cc1f3ae8B0` | **Retired** | Its EntryPoint deposit has been withdrawn (0), so it cannot sponsor anything. The bytecode still exists. Never deposit to it. In the registry as `paymasterV1` with `retired: true`. History: it was staked and funded, and sponsored a real operation through the hosted URLs before retirement |

**Hosting is live.** The bundler is at `https://bundler.pepeunchained.com` (`PEPU_BUNDLER_URL`) and the paymaster policy service at `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com`; the ERC-7677 URL always embeds a token (`https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<token>`). A fresh Kernel account holding 0 PEPU transacted on mainnet through both with the v2 canary paying the gas (the paymaster paid 5.00 PEPU including account deployment). The v2 paymaster is a canary with external audit pending. See [Infrastructure Map](../infra/overview.md) and [Sponsored Transactions](../onboarding/sponsored-transactions.md).

## Demo / reference contracts

| Contract | Address | What it's for |
|---|---|---|
| TapScore | `0x261eA5971B93237a56990206A46Bc80318e4d078` | Minimal gameplay contract (`tap()`, no args, non-payable) used by the `game-app` template to demonstrate a scoped session signer calling one function repeatedly with no wallet popups, and by the `sponsored-demo` template as its sponsored call. Verified on pepuscan. See [Session Keys](../onboarding/session-keys.md) and [Sponsored Transactions](../onboarding/sponsored-transactions.md). |

## Non-canonical addresses used by ecosystem apps — don't reuse these as generic infrastructure

Some first-party PEPU apps deployed their own small, purpose-built contracts that are easy to mistake for general infrastructure because of their name. They are **not** Multicall3- or Permit2-compatible and are not a substitute for the canonical registry above — they're sized for one app's own needs.

| Contract | Address | Belongs to | Why it's not a substitute |
|---|---|---|---|
| PepuSwap "multicall" | `0x927af2a6B76d2d8206d93004463F8C122701383B` | PepuSwap (the native DEX, a Uniswap V3 fork) | A small, non-canonical router-adjacent contract, not Multicall3-compatible. Don't wire it into a generic multicall config. |
| PepuSwap Permit2 | `0xB461c05f76d7f919FF7A3Df2B0D2593F56538b4B` | PepuSwap | PepuSwap's own Permit2 deployment, not the canonical Permit2. If a library assumes canonical Permit2 (most `permit2-sdk`-style tooling does), pointing it at this address will not behave the same way. |

## Tokens

| Token | Address | Chain | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| WPEPU (Wrapped Pepe Unchained) | `0xF9Cf4A16d26979b929Be7176bAc4e7084975FCB8` | Mainnet | Cross-verified across docs, Blockscout, PepuSwap's deployment config, an `eth_getCode` check, and Blockscout's contract-verification match against the `WETH9` source. See [`@pepu-chain/sdk`'s token list](../sdk/core.md#contract-and-dex-registries) — deliberately minimal. |
| USDT (Tether USD) | `0x06f69A40C33C5A4Cd038BBE1DA689D4D636Ec448` | Mainnet | 6 decimals. Discovered as the non-WPEPU side of PepuSwap's WPEPU/USDT pool, then confirmed directly with live `name()`, `symbol()` and `decimals()` reads. Do not format it with 18 decimals. |
| USDC (USD Coin) | `0x20fB684Bfc1aBAaD3AceC5712f2Aa30bd494dF74` | Mainnet | 6 decimals. One of the tokens PepuSwap trades. Verified read-only on 2026-10-03: `eth_getCode` returns code, and `name()`, `symbol()` and `decimals()` read as "USD Coin", "USDC" and 6. Do not format it with 18 decimals. |
| WETH (Wrapped Ether) | `0x7CCC51754216C04D4Bb1210630cCA16e5430Aa70` | Mainnet | 18 decimals. One of the tokens PepuSwap trades. Verified read-only on 2026-10-03: `eth_getCode` returns code, and `name()`, `symbol()` and `decimals()` read as "Wrapped Ether", "WETH" and 18. |

Last live check: `pnpm --filter @pepu-chain/sdk live-check`, 2026-10-14 (all 16 registry entries have code; none pending).

## Where this table comes from

Every address above is also encoded in [`@pepu-chain/sdk`'s contract registry](../sdk/core.md#contract-and-dex-registries) (`getContract`, `listContracts`, `isDeployed`), which is the machine-readable version of this page — use it in code instead of copy-pasting addresses out of Markdown. A `"pending"` registry entry has no `.address` field at all, so code that reads the registry can't accidentally treat an undeployed contract as real.

If you find infrastructure not listed here that you believe is genuinely deployed and verified on PEPU, treat it as unconfirmed until you've checked it directly (`eth_getCode`, or `pepu_verify_contract_status` if you have the [PEPU MCP server](../agent-tooling/mcp-and-skills.md) connected) — don't propagate an address you can't independently verify.

pages.title: Deploy & Verify a Contract
pages.content:
# Deploy & Verify a Contract

This page takes you from nothing to a deployed, verified contract on Pepe Unchained V2 **mainnet**. Foundry is the primary path below; a complete Hardhat path follows it for anyone who prefers that toolchain. Both are real, complete, and independently sufficient — pick one.

If you haven't already, skim [V1 vs V2](../get-started/v1-vs-v2.md) first: the chain ID and RPC URL below are for the current chain (V2). An older, dead chain shares the project name and gets confused with this one constantly.

**Looking for the fastest path to a running app instead of a bare contract?** See [Quickstart: Zero to a Sponsored Transaction in 10 Minutes](../get-started/quickstart-app.md) — it scaffolds a Next.js app with sign-in and a wallet, no Solidity required. This page is for when you specifically want to write and deploy a contract.

## Why mainnet, not testnet

Testnet (chain `97740`) has no public faucet, no indexed explorer, and none of the infrastructure on this page deployed to it — see [Network Reference](../get-started/network-reference.md#testnet-out-of-scope-today). It is out of scope for development today. Mainnet is the actual "try it" chain: a deployment costs a fraction of a cent, so use a dedicated development key with minimal funds and deploy there directly. Everything below targets mainnet only.

## What you'll need

- A wallet with a private key you control (use a dedicated development key with minimal funds — never a key holding meaningful value).
- Either [Foundry](https://getfoundry.sh) or Node.js 18+ with a package manager, depending on which path you follow.
- A small amount of PEPU to pay gas (see "Get funds" below).

## Network parameters

| Parameter | Value |
|---|---|
| Chain ID | `97741` |
| RPC URL | `https://rpc-pepu-v2-mainnet-0.t.conduit.xyz` |
| Currency | PEPU (18 decimals) |
| Explorer | `https://pepuscan.com` |

Full parameters, an "Add to Wallet" JSON snippet, and the complete deployed-contracts reference are on [Network Reference](../get-started/network-reference.md).

## Get funds

Buy PEPU on an exchange, or bridge existing PEPU from Ethereum L1 via [pepubridge.com](https://pepubridge.com). Gas on this chain is a fraction of a cent per transaction (see the gas note on [Network Reference](../get-started/network-reference.md)), so a very small amount funds a long testing session.

## The contract

Both paths below deploy the same minimal contract. Save it as `src/Counter.sol` (Foundry) or `contracts/Counter.sol` (Hardhat):

```solidity
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
pragma solidity ^0.8.24;

contract Counter {
    uint256 public count;

    function increment() external {
        count += 1;
    }
}
```

---

## Path 1: Foundry (primary)

### Install and confirm your toolchain

```bash
curl -L https://foundry.paradigm.xyz | bash
foundryup
```

This has been verified working against Pepe Unchained mainnet on upstream Foundry `v1.5.1-stable`.

> **Check which `forge` you're running before you go further.** If [`foundry-zksync`](https://github.com/matter-labs/foundry-zksync) is installed on the same machine, the `forge` binary on your `PATH` may resolve to the zkSync fork instead of upstream Foundry. The zkSync fork compiles and deploys differently and is the wrong tool for an Arbitrum Orbit chain like this one. Run:
>
> ```bash
> forge --version
> ```
>
> The zkSync fork announces itself in the version string (it will mention `zksync`). If you see that, reinstall or switch to upstream Foundry via `foundryup` before continuing.

Confirm the RPC is reachable and returns the chain ID you expect:

```bash
cast chain-id --rpc-url https://rpc-pepu-v2-mainnet-0.t.conduit.xyz
# 97741
```

### Set up the project

```bash
forge init pepu-quickstart
cd pepu-quickstart
```

`forge init` scaffolds its own default `src/Counter.sol`. Replace it with the contract from [above](#the-contract) so the rest of this walkthrough matches exactly.

Add an RPC alias to `foundry.toml`:

```toml
[profile.default]
src = "src"
out = "out"
libs = ["lib"]

[rpc_endpoints]
pepu_mainnet = "https://rpc-pepu-v2-mainnet-0.t.conduit.xyz"
```

### Build

```bash
forge build
```

### Deploy

Set your development private key as an environment variable (never commit it):

```bash
export PRIVATE_KEY=0xyourdevelopmentprivatekey
```

```bash
forge create src/Counter.sol:Counter \
  --rpc-url pepu_mainnet \
  --private-key $PRIVATE_KEY \
  --broadcast
```

Foundry estimates gas automatically — you don't need to override gas price to work around PEPU's ~12,500 gwei-equivalent base fee; that's a real, expected value, not something to fight (see [Troubleshooting](../troubleshooting.md)). Note the deployed contract address `forge create` prints — you'll need it to verify.

### Verify

Verify against pepuscan directly, using Foundry's Blockscout verifier:

```bash
forge verify-contract \
  --rpc-url https://rpc-pepu-v2-mainnet-0.t.conduit.xyz \
  --verifier blockscout \
  --verifier-url https://pepuscan.com/api \
  <DEPLOYED_ADDRESS> \
  src/Counter.sol:Counter
```

This is Blockscout's own documented Foundry verification pattern (`--verifier blockscout` pointed at a self-hosted instance's `/api` path), confirmed working against pepuscan. Most self-hosted Blockscout instances, pepuscan included, don't require an API key for this.

Don't just trust the CLI's exit code — confirm the verification actually landed:

```bash
curl -s "https://pepuscan.com/api/v2/smart-contracts/<DEPLOYED_ADDRESS>" | grep -o '"is_verified":[a-z]*'
```

If you have the `pepu` MCP server connected, `pepu_verify_contract_status` does this same check and also distinguishes "unverified contract" from "not a contract at all" — see [Agent Tooling](../agent-tooling/mcp-and-skills.md).

Conduit's Sourcify-compatible service (`--verifier sourcify --verifier-url https://contracts.conduit.xyz`) is a documented fallback if the Blockscout route doesn't pick up the verification for some reason — but Blockscout against pepuscan is the confirmed, primary path.

### View it

Open `https://pepuscan.com/address/<DEPLOYED_ADDRESS>`. You should see the contract, its verified source, and a "Read/Write Contract" tab once pepuscan.com picks up the verification.

---

## Path 2: Hardhat (alternative)

Foundry is primary for PEPU work, but Hardhat is a fully documented alternative — use it if the project already standardized on Hardhat, or if Foundry genuinely isn't available on the machine.

### Install

```bash
mkdir pepu-quickstart && cd pepu-quickstart
npm init -y
npm install --save-dev hardhat @nomicfoundation/hardhat-toolbox dotenv
npx hardhat init
```

Choose "Create a TypeScript project" (or JavaScript, adjusting file extensions below) when prompted.

### Configure

Create a `.env` file:

```
DEPLOYER_PRIVATE_KEY=0xyourdevelopmentprivatekey
```

Replace `hardhat.config.ts` with:

```ts
import type { HardhatUserConfig } from "hardhat/config";
import "@nomicfoundation/hardhat-toolbox";
import "dotenv/config";

const DEPLOYER_PRIVATE_KEY = process.env.DEPLOYER_PRIVATE_KEY;

const config: HardhatUserConfig = {
  solidity: "0.8.24",
  networks: {
    pepuMainnet: {
      url: "https://rpc-pepu-v2-mainnet-0.t.conduit.xyz",
      chainId: 97741,
      accounts: DEPLOYER_PRIVATE_KEY ? [DEPLOYER_PRIVATE_KEY] : [],
    },
  },
  sourcify: {
    enabled: true,
    apiUrl: "https://contracts.conduit.xyz",
    browserUrl: "https://pepuscan.com",
  },
};

export default config;
```

The `sourcify` block is the fastest way to get one-command verification working on Hardhat 2 + `hardhat-toolbox` today (it runs against Conduit's Sourcify-compatible service). If your project has moved to **Hardhat 3**, its newer `@nomicfoundation/hardhat-verify` plugin has first-class Blockscout support instead — configure a `verify.blockscout` block and run `npx hardhat verify blockscout --network pepuMainnet <address>` for the same pepuscan-verified result the Foundry path above gets directly. Either produces a verified contract on pepuscan; they're two different plugins' paths to it, not competing sources of truth.

### Write the contract and compile

Save the contract from [above](#the-contract) as `contracts/Counter.sol`, then:

```bash
npx hardhat compile
```

### Deploy

Create `scripts/deploy.ts`:

```ts
import { ethers } from "hardhat";

async function main() {
  const Counter = await ethers.getContractFactory("Counter");
  const counter = await Counter.deploy();
  await counter.waitForDeployment();
  console.log("Counter deployed to:", await counter.getAddress());
}

main().catch((error) => {
  console.error(error);
  process.exitCode = 1;
});
```

```bash
npx hardhat run scripts/deploy.ts --network pepuMainnet
```

### Verify

With the `sourcify` block above in place, Hardhat's standard verify command runs against Conduit's Sourcify-compatible service:

```bash
npx hardhat verify --network pepuMainnet <DEPLOYED_ADDRESS>
```

### View it

Same as the Foundry path: `https://pepuscan.com/address/<DEPLOYED_ADDRESS>`.

---

## Next steps

- [Address Map](address-map.md) and [Deployed Contracts Reference](deployed-contracts.md) — the full table of what's live on this chain, with verification links.
- [CREATE2 and Deterministic Deployment](create2-and-deterministic-deployment.md): deploy to a predictable address through the live deployer, as Multicall3 and Permit2 were.
- [The Multicall3 Trap](multicall3.md) — Multicall3 is deployed here now, but not at the address your tooling probably assumes.
- [`@pepu-chain/sdk` Reference](../sdk/reference.md) — import chain definitions and the contract registry instead of hand-rolling them.
- [Recipes](../recipes/read-a-contract.md) — short, copy-pasteable patterns for reading and writing contracts once one is deployed.
- [Social Login & Embedded Wallets (Privy)](../onboarding/privy-embedded-wallets.md) — wiring up user-facing wallets instead of a raw private key.

pages.title: EntryPoints and Kernel
pages.content:
# EntryPoints and Kernel

The ERC-4337 contracts on PEPU mainnet: EntryPoint v0.6 and v0.7, the ZeroDev Kernel v3.1 account stack (factory, meta-factory, implementation, ECDSA validator and signer) and the session-key policies, with the ABIs the SDK ships. Read it to know which address does what and which versions to pin.

> Status: **deployed and verified**. All addresses below returned bytecode from `eth_getCode` on 2026-10-14 (`pnpm --filter @pepu-chain/sdk live-check`). They were deployed by ZeroDev's one-click Conduit Marketplace integration; mainnet only. Sponsored operations and session keys have run on them on mainnet (see [Infrastructure Map](../infra/overview.md)).

## EntryPoints

| Version | Address | Bytes | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| v0.7 | `0x0000000071727De22E5E9d8BAf0edAc6f37da032` | 16035 | Kernel v3.x, the PEPU paymaster, Privy's smart-wallet integration. Use this one |
| v0.6 | `0x5FF137D4b0FDCD49DcA30c7CF57E578a026d2789` | 23689 | Deployed and served by the bundler; nothing in the dev kit targets it |

Both are at the canonical addresses. The paymaster, the bundler and the policy service all use v0.7. The SDK ships `entryPointV07Abi` (from `@pepu-chain/sdk`); the paymaster deposit is read through it (`getPaymasterDeposit` in `@pepu-chain/sdk/aa`).

## Kernel account stack

| Component | Address | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Kernel v3 factory | `0xaac5D4240AF87249B3f71BC8E4A2cae074A3E419` | Creates accounts; `getAddress(...)` returns the counterfactual address, so never re-implement the CREATE2 hash |
| Kernel MetaFactory | `0xd703aaE79538628d27099B8c4f621bE4CCd142d5` | Factory of factories |
| Kernel v3.1 implementation | `0xbAC849bB641841b44E965fb01A4Bf5F074F84B4d` | What the factory's `implementation()` resolves to; accounts are proxies to it |
| Kernel ECDSA validator | `0x845ADb2C711129d4f3966735eD98a9F09fC4cE57` | Default root validator: one ECDSA key (for example a Privy embedded wallet) authorises the account |
| Kernel ECDSA signer module | `0x6A6F069E2a08c2468e7724Ab3250CdBFBA14D4FF` | Signer used inside permission-validator session keys |

The SDK pins Kernel v3.1 (`KERNEL_VERSION` in `@pepu-chain/sdk/aa/kernel`). Accounts are deployed on the user's first UserOperation (the operation carries `factory` and `factoryData`), which is why a first transaction costs about 12 PEPU worst case against about 3 PEPU afterwards.

## Session-key policies

| Policy | Address | What it enforces |
|---|---|---|
| Call policy **v0.0.4** | `0x9a52283276A0ec8740DF50bF01B28A80D880eaf2` | Only the listed targets and selectors, with a native value no larger than the limit (default 0) |
| Timestamp policy | `0xB9f8f524bE6EcD8C945b1b87f9ae5C192FdCE20F` | The permission is invalid outside `validAfter` to `validUntil` |

**Why v0.0.4, not v0.0.5.** ZeroDev's call policy v0.0.5 is not deployed on PEPU. The SDK pins `CallPolicyVersion.V0_0_4` and exports the address as `CALL_POLICY_V0_0_4_ADDRESS` (and `TIMESTAMP_POLICY_ADDRESS`) from `@pepu-chain/sdk/session/kernel`. An out-of-scope UserOperation is rejected by the EntryPoint itself, whoever relays it. Do not configure a newer policy version or a client default that selects v0.0.5; it will point at an address with no code. See [Session Keys](../onboarding/session-keys.md).

## ABIs in the SDK

| Export | Covers |
|---|---|
| `entryPointV07Abi` | EntryPoint v0.7 |
| `kernelFactoryAbi`, `kernelEcdsaValidatorAbi` | Kernel factory and validator. `KERNEL_V3_1_IMPLEMENTATION_ADDRESS` and `ERC7579_MODULE_TYPE` are exported alongside |
| `multicall3Abi`, `permit2Abi` | The two infrastructure contracts, [Multicall3](multicall3.md) and [Permit2](permit2.md) |
| `pepuSponsoredPaymasterV2Abi` (from `/paymaster`) | The v2 paymaster |

Registry access: `getContract(97741, "entryPoint07")`, `getContract(97741, "kernelFactory")` and so on; `isDeployed` narrows the type so a pending entry can never be read as an address. Names: `entryPoint06`, `entryPoint07`, `kernelFactory`, `kernelMetaFactory`, `kernelImplementation`, `ecdsaValidator`, `kernelEcdsaSignerModule`, `kernelCallPolicyV004`, `kernelTimestampPolicy`.

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Session key setup reverts or the policy has no code | A client defaulted to call policy v0.0.5 | Pin v0.0.4 |
| Counterfactual address differs from the deployed one | Different Kernel version, validator or index | Use the factory's `getAddress` with the SDK's pinned version |
| Operation rejected during account creation | Wrong factory or init data | Build the account with `toPepuKernelAccount` / `getKernelAddress` from `@pepu-chain/sdk/aa/kernel` |
| Bundler says EntryPoint unsupported | Sent v0.6 | Use v0.7 |

## Related

- [Address Map](address-map.md)
- [/aa](../sdk/aa.md), [/session/kernel](../sdk/session-kernel.md)
- [Smart Accounts](../onboarding/smart-accounts.md)
- [Bundler Overview](../infra/bundler/overview.md)

pages.title: The Multicall3 Trap
pages.content:
# The Multicall3 Trap

This is the single most important gotcha on Pepe Unchained V2. Read it before you wire up any tooling that reads multiple contracts at once — viem's `multicall()`, wagmi's `useReadContracts`, or anything built on top of either.

## The short version

**Multicall3 is deployed on PEPU mainnet — but not at the address almost every EVM tool assumes.**

| | |
|---|---|
| Canonical Multicall3 address (works on nearly every other EVM chain) | `0xcA11bde05977b3631167028862bE2a173976CA11` — **has no code on PEPU. It is permanently unreachable here — see why below.** |
| PEPU's actual Multicall3 address | `0x9CE19273Ae9c24437DFF512E8DFCAed4E4B001bd` — deployed, verified on pepuscan, confirmed working with viem's `multicall()`. |

If your chain configuration doesn't explicitly set this address, or if a library you're using hardcodes the canonical one, batched reads will either throw a confusing "no code at this address" error or silently fail — not something an unfamiliar developer will trace back to "wrong Multicall3 address" quickly.

## Why the canonical address is unreachable here — not just unused

Other canonical contracts could be recovered on PEPU because they were deployed through CREATE2: the deterministic deployer is live, so the same source deployed the same way reproduces the canonical address (that is how Permit2 was deployed; see [Permit2](permit2.md)). Multicall3 is different.

Multicall3's canonical deployment on other chains was **not** done via CREATE2. It used a plain `CREATE` from a specific burn EOA, via a **pre-signed transaction with a hardcoded 1,000,000 gas limit**. That transaction is replayed, unmodified, on every new chain to get Multicall3 at the same address everywhere.

Arbitrum Nitro chains — including PEPU — need roughly **14.3 million gas** to deploy the same Multicall3 bytecode. The pre-signed transaction's fixed 1,000,000 gas limit means it **cannot execute here**, on this chain, ever, using that original signed transaction. There is no version of "just run the deploy script again" that fixes this — the transaction that would recreate the canonical address doesn't have enough gas headroom for this chain's execution costs, and it can't be re-signed with a higher limit without changing its hash (and therefore its resulting address).

The only way to get Multicall3 at the canonical address on PEPU would be for Conduit to add it as a **predeploy** at genesis — something only the chain operator can do, and not something that helps a chain that has already launched.

## What PEPU did instead

A PEPU-specific Multicall3 was deployed:

1. Built from the canonical [`mds1/multicall3`](https://github.com/mds1/multicall3) source, compiled with solc `0.8.12`, optimizer runs set to `10,000,000` — matching the canonical build as closely as possible so the bytecode's behavior is identical.
2. Deployed via the CREATE2 deterministic deployer (`0x4e59b44847b379578588920cA78FbF26c0B4956C`) with a zero salt, which is why the resulting address (`0x9CE19273Ae9c24437DFF512E8DFCAed4E4B001bd`) is reproducible from the same inputs, just not equal to the canonical one (different deployment method → different resulting address, by construction).
3. Verified on pepuscan.
4. Confirmed working end-to-end with viem's `multicall()` action against it.

It behaves exactly like Multicall3 everywhere else — it's simply at a different address, and every tool that talks to it needs to be told that explicitly.

## Deployment receipt and verification

| | |
|---|---|
| Address | `0x9CE19273Ae9c24437DFF512E8DFCAed4E4B001bd` (in the SDK registry as `multicall3`) |
| Deployer contract | CREATE2 deterministic deployer `0x4e59b44847b379578588920cA78FbF26c0B4956C`, salt all zeros |
| Transaction | `0xf9d8f45010e2a2020871af9a677d134e9b43e039a0a73c09bcd22d1825f99241` |
| Block | 10521048 (`0xa089d8`), the `blockCreated` used in the chain definition |
| Gas used | 874,693 (`0xd58c5`) |
| Runtime size | 3,808 bytes, checked with `eth_getCode` by `pnpm --filter @pepu-chain/sdk live-check` on 2026-10-03 |
| Source | `contracts/multicall3/src/Multicall3.sol`, solc 0.8.12, optimizer 10,000,000 runs (`contracts/multicall3/foundry.toml`) |
| Receipt and script | `deploy/multicall3-receipt.json`, `deploy/deploy-multicall3.sh`, `deploy/verify-multicall3.sh` |

The same live check confirms the canonical `0xcA11bde0…CA11` has no code. See [CREATE2 and Deterministic Deployment](create2-and-deterministic-deployment.md) for reproducing the address.

## What to do about it

**If you're using `@pepu-chain/sdk`:** nothing extra — `pepuMainnet.contracts.multicall3` is already set to the correct address. `getPublicClient(pepuMainnet)` and any wagmi config built from `pepuChains` pick it up automatically, and viem's `multicall()` action just works. See [`@pepu-chain/sdk` Reference](../sdk/reference.md).

**If you're hand-rolling a chain definition**, set the address explicitly rather than relying on a default:

```ts
import { defineChain } from "viem";

export const pepuMainnet = defineChain({
  id: 97741,
  name: "Pepe Unchained V2",
  nativeCurrency: { name: "Pepe Unchained", symbol: "PEPU", decimals: 18 },
  rpcUrls: { default: { http: ["https://rpc-pepu-v2-mainnet-0.t.conduit.xyz"] } },
  contracts: {
    multicall3: {
      address: "0x9CE19273Ae9c24437DFF512E8DFCAed4E4B001bd",
      blockCreated: 10521048,
    },
  },
});
```

**Never substitute the canonical `0xcA11bde0…` address for PEPU.** It has no code here — any call against it returns empty data, and viem/wagmi's batching will fail for every read routed through it.

**If you omit `contracts.multicall3` entirely**, viem and wagmi fall back to individual per-call requests instead of batching. This is safe — you lose batching performance, not correctness — but it's strictly worse than setting the correct address above, since PEPU does have a working Multicall3 today.

## Don't confuse it with PepuSwap's "multicall"

PepuSwap (PEPU's native DEX, a Uniswap V3 fork) deployed its own small, non-canonical multicall-named contract at `0x927af2a6B76d2d8206d93004463F8C122701383B`. It is **not** Multicall3-compatible — it's a router-adjacent contract sized for PepuSwap's own needs, not general-purpose batching. Don't point generic tooling at it. See [Deployed Contracts Reference](deployed-contracts.md) for the full list of these app-specific, easy-to-confuse addresses.

## Recipe

Once your chain definition has the right address, batching reads is exactly the same code you'd write on any chain with Multicall3 — see [Batch Reads with Multicall3](../recipes/batch-reads-with-multicall3.md) for a copy-pasteable example.

pages.title: Paymaster v2 Spec Summary
pages.content:
# Paymaster v2 Spec Summary

A readable summary of the tiered gas-sponsorship specification (`services/paymaster/SPONSORSHIP-SPEC.md`): model, invariants, trust model, decisions and open items. The full spec is the source of truth; this page is the map. Read it to understand what v2 promises and what it does not.

> Status: **proven on mainnet (canary, external audit pending).** Deployed at `0xdb28528C9399C33c9A0297E8A62F39145acbC30D` on 2026-10-14: internally reviewed 3x, external audit pending, funded in small tranches. The contract has unit, fuzz and invariant tests (195 Foundry tests, 328 policy-service tests) and three internal AI-assisted reviews ([Audits and Verification Status](audits.md)). A project-sponsored operation from a fresh Kernel account holding 0 PEPU has run through the hosted bundler and paymaster. The v1 paymaster is retired. The numbers below are the spec's design numbers; the live per-user free allowance is 100 PEPU per day and 50 PEPU per hour, enforced by the policy service.

## Model

| Tier | Funded by | Who draws | Bound |
|---|---|---|---|
| Free tier | The chain: a free pool anyone can fund | **Verified Privy users only** | Live: 100 PEPU per user per day and 50 PEPU per hour (service). Spec design numbers: 50 PEPU per day, 40 PEPU max per operation. On-chain per-wallet backstop, the pool balance. **No chain-wide ceiling** |
| Project tier | A project, funded by anyone depositing on chain | **Any wallet** the project sponsors | Project balance, daily limit, per-wallet limit, destination allowlist, gas-price cap |

Per operation, atomically and never split: the project pays if it can; otherwise the free tier, only for a verified Privy account with allowance; otherwise denied. The free tier never pays for non-Privy wallets, even when a project is empty.

One contract is both paymaster and vault. All PEPU sits in its EntryPoint deposit and an internal ledger records each sponsor's share (`sponsorId` 0 is the free pool; otherwise `keccak256(bytes(appId))`). Validation deducts the full `maxCost` from the sponsor; `postOp` refunds `maxCost - charge` to that same sponsor.

## Decisions

| | Decision |
|---|---|
| Deposits | **One-way.** Anyone deposits into any project (claimed or not) or the free pool; **nothing can withdraw**, not project owners, the contract owner or the manager. The only outflow is gas settlement |
| Project identity | `projectId = keccak256(bytes(appId))`: one canonical project per Privy app, case-sensitive |
| Ownership | Privy-verified. The policy service checks the Privy app secret, issues an EIP-712 attestation, the developer calls `claimProject`. **The claim sets only the owner**; the owner then calls `setTargets`, `setDailyLimit`, `setSenderDailyLimit` (all three are required: a project with no per-wallet limit is rejected on chain). An **empty** project is claimed immediately; a project that **already holds funds** is pending for the admin delay (cancellable by the contract owner or manager) |
| Re-claim | Of an owned project: timelocked at least 48 hours, announced on chain, cancellable by the current owner **once per new owner** (a second attested re-claim by the same new owner is final), void if the attesting signer was removed, lapses 30 days after it becomes executable |
| Exit | **Pausing is the exit**, instant. Funds cannot leave |
| Contract owner | The deployer by default; `Ownable2Step`, renounce supported. Nothing a project needs depends on the owner |
| Free tier numbers | 50 PEPU per user per day, 40 PEPU per operation |
| Surplus | Unused prepay returns to the exact sponsor that was charged; unattributable residue (and donations) can only go to the free pool, never to the owner |
| Governance | Signer and bundler **additions** wait an immutable `adminChangeDelay` (at least 48 hours, at most 30 days); removals instant; manager separate from owner |
| Gas-price cap | On-chain per-sponsor cap on `maxFeePerGas` (deploy default 40,000 gwei; a sponsor can only tighten it) plus service bounds |
| Bundler gate | Unconditional on-chain `tx.origin` allowlist; mode byte must be exactly `0x02` |
| Credentials | Server key `ppk_` (secret, any wallet) or client token `ppt_` (publishable, origin-bound) |
| Stranded funds | Accepted: an abandoned project's money stays locked, no escape hatch |

## Differences from v1

| | v1 | v2 |
|---|---|---|
| Caps | Off-chain only | Off-chain plus on-chain allowlist, limits and fee cap per sponsor |
| Accounting | One shared deposit | Per-sponsor ledger, actual-cost settlement and refunds |
| Who funds | One operator | Anyone, per project, plus a free pool |
| Onboarding | Manual registration | Self-serve claim |
| Mode byte | `0x00` | `0x02` only (sponsor id in the signed data) |
| Bundler gate | None | Required allowlisted bundler |

## Invariants (all tested)

- Ledgers sum to `totalLiabilities`, and `totalLiabilities` is at most the EntryPoint deposit; balances never underflow.
- **No function of any role moves ledger funds out of the EntryPoint deposit**; the contract never calls `entryPoint.withdrawTo` (a test scans the bytecode). Only stake, a separate balance, can be withdrawn by the owner.
- The deposit plus gas paid to the beneficiary equals everything ever deposited, over random sequences of claims, deposits, donations, pauses, stake moves and operations.
- On the real EntryPoint v0.7 sources, the ledger charge is at least the EntryPoint's true debit for every operation, including the worst-case slot-restoring attack at the overhead floor (post-op overhead floor 18,000 gas, deployed 20,000; measured worst case 13,918 gas with cold state, after the overhead is snapshotted at validation).
- Day counters track charges exactly; one sponsor's operation never moves another sponsor's ledger.

## Trust model

- The policy signer is the **ownership gatekeeper** for projects as well as the sponsorship signer (one shared signer set). A compromised signer can claim an **empty unclaimed** project immediately, claim a funded one after the admin delay unless the contract owner or manager cancels it (or the signer is removed), or start a re-claim of an owned one, but can never withdraw funds. Its spending is bounded on chain: only claimed sponsors, only allowlisted targets, only within the daily and per-wallet limits, only paid to an allowlisted bundler, at no more than the fee cap. The free pool's worst case is its balance, because a signer can invent wallets.
- A hot manager cannot quickly add itself as signer and bundler: additions are timelocked, so projects that watch `AdminChangeProposed` can pause first.
- Re-claims and the first claim of a funded project are visible, timelocked, cancellable and die with a removed signer; credentials follow the on-chain owner and are revoked on change. The owner can veto a re-claim once per new owner, so a hostile owner cannot block recovery forever.
- The `tx.origin` gate means v2 works only behind a bundler with safe mode off and an allowlisted executor, which is how the hosted PEPU bundler runs; a conformant public-mempool bundler rejects it.
- Honest residuals: free-tier sybil (N Privy accounts get N times the per-user free allowance a day, bounded by the pool balance), a many-address attacker holding up to 25% of a client token's reservation pool, no audit of an immutable contract that holds third-party money, destination decoding is Kernel-only, runtime size 23,722 of 24,576 bytes (only with 8,000 optimizer runs for this contract).

## Open items

- **External audit** is pending; the canary is funded in small tranches until it is done. A fork test against the real PEPU EntryPoint and Nitro gas schedule is also still open.
- Whether to add a dormant-balance path to the free pool (stranded funds).
- Separate claim-attestation key (does not fit in the remaining contract size; needs a refactor).
- Guardian address for owner key loss; multiple Privy apps for the free tier; stablecoin deposits; free-pool funding policy; orphaned prepay after a post-op revert; Privy cross-app check needing a live two-app test.
- Contract size margin (854 bytes at 8,000 optimizer runs; a project-ownership registry contract is the prepared contingency, `SPONSORSHIP-SPEC.md` 16.2).

## Full detail

- Full spec: `services/paymaster/SPONSORSHIP-SPEC.md` (sections: model, architecture, contract, accounting, free tier, sybil resistance, invariants, claims, API, threat model T1 to T22, migration, decisions D1 to D22, open questions, and review 3 in section 16).
- Contract reference: [PepuSponsoredPaymasterV7 Contract](../infra/paymaster/contracts.md).
- API: [REST API v2](../infra/paymaster/rest-api-v2.md). Procedure: [Register, Deposit and Claim a v2 Project](../infra/paymaster/v2-register-deposit-claim.md).
- User-facing model: [Sponsorship Tiers](../onboarding/sponsorship-tiers.md).

## Related

- [Audits and Verification Status](audits.md)
- [Paymaster Overview](../infra/paymaster/overview.md)
- [Address Map](address-map.md)

pages.title: PepuSwap Addresses
pages.content:
# PepuSwap Addresses

PepuSwap is PEPU's main DEX, operated by a third party (0sum.io): a white-labelled Uniswap V3 fork. Several of its contracts sit at non-canonical addresses, and two of them (a multicall and a Permit2) are easy to mistake for general infrastructure. This page lists them and the do-not-substitute rules.

> Status: addresses are in the SDK's PepuSwap registry (`getPepuSwapContract`, `listPepuSwapContracts`) and were cross-checked by the registry authors (factory getters, pool reads, `eth_call` simulation). They are third-party contracts: PEPU does not operate them and they are outside this repository's security policy. They were **not** part of the 2026-10-03 `live-check` run, which covers `pepuContracts` only. Re-verify with `pepu_check_contract_deployed` before relying on one. Mainnet only.

## Address table

| Registry key | Name | Address | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `v3Factory` | UniswapV3Factory | `0x5984B8BF2d4dB9C0aCB1d7924762e4474D80C807` | Verified on pepuscan; other PepuSwap contracts' `factory()` all return it |
| `swapRouter02` | SwapRouter02 | `0x150c3F0f16C3D9EB34351d7af9c961FeDc97A0fb` | `factory()` and `WETH9()` resolve to the factory and WPEPU |
| `universalRouter` | UniversalRouter | `0x0dE72b751b77d3c74fB96C5fAd0320Cd8d133d36` | No public getters; verified by simulating `execute` |
| `positionManager` | NonfungiblePositionManager | `0xe2060CbdE18b5e765c86e5Cd6EE68AF209a9faa7` | LP NFTs list as "Launchpad V3 Positions NFT" / UNI-V3-POS |
| `quoterV2` | QuoterV2 | `0xd647b2D80b48e93613Aa6982b85f8909578b4829` | Quote with `eth_call` or `simulateContract` only; never send a real transaction |
| `tickLens` | TickLens | `0x4EB8aA84c066f9bf210eAfE33B30AE49BfafD9a6` | Stateless; verified with a live `getPopulatedTicksInWord` |
| `v3Migrator` | V3Migrator | `0xFE406d6c3fc0BB3a6D195b089eFADfc8658206D5` | No dedicated ABI in the SDK |
| `v3Staker` | V3Staker | `0x0a875d1C72cb4e1CD61401c3C49f85Df45071f83` | Uniswap LP incentive staking, unrelated to "stake PEPU". No dedicated ABI in the SDK |
| `multicallNonCanonical` | UniswapInterfaceMulticall | `0x927af2a6B76d2d8206d93004463F8C122701383B` | **Not Multicall3** |
| `permit2NonCanonical` | PepuSwap Permit2 | `0xB461c05f76d7f919FF7A3Df2B0D2593F56538b4B` | **Not the canonical Permit2** |

Tokens it trades (also in `@pepu-chain/sdk` tokens): WPEPU `0xF9Cf4A16d26979b929Be7176bAc4e7084975FCB8` (18 decimals), USDT `0x06f69A40C33C5A4Cd038BBE1DA689D4D636Ec448` (6 decimals), USDC `0x20fB684Bfc1aBAaD3AceC5712f2Aa30bd494dF74` (6), WETH `0x7CCC51754216C04D4Bb1210630cCA16e5430Aa70` (18). Get PepuSwap's token list from `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0sum-io/tokens/refs/heads/main/pepu-mainnet2.json` rather than hardcoding more.

## Do-not-substitute table

| If you want | Use | Never use |
|---|---|---|
| Batched reads (Multicall3 `aggregate3`) | `0x9CE19273Ae9c24437DFF512E8DFCAed4E4B001bd` ([Multicall3](multicall3.md)) | PepuSwap's `0x927a…383B` (a Multicall2-style contract with a different function set), and not `0xcA11…CA11`, which has no code |
| Permit2 for your own contracts and libraries | `0x000000000022D473030F116dDEE9F6B43aC78BA3` ([Permit2](permit2.md)) | PepuSwap's `0xB461…8b4B` |
| Integrating with PepuSwap's UI or routers | PepuSwap's own addresses above | The canonical Permit2 (its frontend overrides `PERMIT2_ADDRESS` for chain 97741) |

The two Permit2 deployments respond to `DOMAIN_SEPARATOR()` with different values, so signatures are not interchangeable. The SDK ships separate ABIs (`pepuSwapMulticallAbi`, `pepuSwapPermit2Abi`) so the confusion is visible in types.

## Using the registry

```ts
import { getPepuSwapContract, listPepuSwapContracts } from "@pepu-chain/sdk";

const router = getPepuSwapContract(97741, "swapRouter02");
const all = listPepuSwapContracts(97741);
```

Other PepuSwap ABIs shipped: router, quoter, position manager, V3 factory, V3 pool, tick lens and universal router.

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Batched calls to `0x927a…` revert or return the wrong shape | It is not Multicall3 | Use PEPU's Multicall3 |
| Permit2 signature rejected by PepuSwap | Signed for the canonical domain | Sign against PepuSwap's Permit2 domain |
| Quoter call spends gas | Sent as a transaction | Use `eth_call` or `simulateContract` |

## Related

- [Address Map](address-map.md)
- [Deployed Contracts Reference](deployed-contracts.md)
- [The Multicall3 Trap](multicall3.md)
- [Permit2](permit2.md)

pages.title: Permit2
pages.content:
# Permit2

Uniswap's Permit2 is deployed on PEPU mainnet at its canonical address. This page gives the address and the deployment proof, the EIP-712 domain, typed-data examples with the SDK builders, and how it differs from PepuSwap's separate Permit2. Read it before signing a Permit2 permit or pointing a library at a Permit2 address.

> Status: **proven**. `eth_getCode` returns 9,152 bytes (checked 2026-10-03 with `pnpm --filter @pepu-chain/sdk live-check`), and a `DOMAIN_SEPARATOR()` call succeeded when it was first verified on 2026-09-24. It was deployed by PEPU, not by Uniswap.

## Address and deployment proof

| | |
|---|---|
| Address | `0x000000000022D473030F116dDEE9F6B43aC78BA3` (canonical) |
| Deployer | CREATE2 deterministic deployer `0x4e59b44847b379578588920cA78FbF26c0B4956C` |
| Salt | `0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000d3af2663da51c10215000000` (Uniswap's upstream salt) |
| Transaction | `0xbb0a23420f47dd4dbb524d96f46115011a66fc88bbdf0963cd24a50feb6f7c93` |
| Block | 10521367 (`0xa08b17`) |
| Gas used | 2,025,730 (`0x1ee902`) |
| Runtime size | 9,152 bytes, matching Permit2's known bytecode size |
| Evidence in the repo | `contracts/permit2/` (`initcode.hex`, `salt.txt`, `predicted.txt`, `permit2-receipt.json`, `prove-address.sh`, `deploy-permit2.sh`, `compute-domain-separator.sh`) |

Why it works: Permit2's canonical address is a CREATE2 address, so the exact upstream creation bytecode plus the upstream salt through the live deployer reproduces it. `prove-address.sh` recomputes the address independently with `cast create2` and by hand from `keccak256(0xff ++ deployer ++ salt ++ keccak256(initcode))`. Compare [Multicall3](multicall3.md), which could not be recovered at its canonical address. How to reproduce: [CREATE2 and Deterministic Deployment](create2-and-deterministic-deployment.md).

## Domain and typed data

The EIP-712 domain is `{ name: "Permit2", chainId: 97741, verifyingContract: <the address above> }`. There is no `version`. `permit2Domain()` builds it:

```ts
import { permit2Domain, getPermit2 } from "@pepu-chain/sdk";

const domain = permit2Domain(); // { name: "Permit2", chainId: 97741, verifyingContract }
const { address } = getPermit2();
```

The registry ABI (`permit2Abi`) covers `DOMAIN_SEPARATOR`, `allowance`, `approve`, `nonceBitmap` and `invalidateNonces`.

## Examples

AllowanceTransfer `PermitSingle`:

```ts
import { buildPermitSingleTypedData, readPermit2Allowance } from "@pepu-chain/sdk";

const { nonce } = await readPermit2Allowance(publicClient, { owner, token, spender });

const typed = buildPermitSingleTypedData({
  token,
  amount: 1_000_000n,
  expiration: Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000) + 3600,
  nonce,
  spender,
  sigDeadline: BigInt(Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000) + 600),
});
const signature = await walletClient.signTypedData({ account, ...typed });
```

SignatureTransfer `PermitTransferFrom`:

```ts
import { buildPermitTransferFromTypedData } from "@pepu-chain/sdk";

const typed = buildPermitTransferFromTypedData({
  token,
  amount: 1_000_000n,
  spender,
  nonce: 0n, // a fresh unordered nonce; check nonceBitmap
  deadline: BigInt(Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000) + 600),
});
const signature = await walletClient.signTypedData({ account, ...typed });
```

The user still needs a normal ERC-20 `approve` of the token to Permit2 once. See [Sign a Permit2 Permit](../recipes/permit2-permit.md).

## Versus PepuSwap's Permit2

PepuSwap deployed its own Permit2 at `0xB461c05f76d7f919FF7A3Df2B0D2593F56538b4B` and its frontend overrides the address for chain 97741. The two have different EIP-712 domains (`DOMAIN_SEPARATOR()` returns different values), so a signature for one is invalid on the other. Libraries that assume canonical Permit2 will not work against PepuSwap's copy, and PepuSwap's UI will not honour approvals made to the canonical one. Use the canonical address for your own contracts and PepuSwap's only when integrating with PepuSwap itself. See [PepuSwap Addresses](pepuswap.md).

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `InvalidSigner` or signature rejected | Signed against the wrong domain (PepuSwap's Permit2, or wrong chain id) | Use `permit2Domain()`; confirm the verifying contract |
| `InvalidNonce` | Reused or stale nonce | Read `allowance` (AllowanceTransfer) or `nonceBitmap` (SignatureTransfer) |
| Transfer reverts after a valid permit | The token was never approved to Permit2 | Send the one-time ERC-20 `approve` |
| `SignatureExpired` | `sigDeadline` or `deadline` passed | Re-sign with a later deadline |

## Related

- [Address Map](address-map.md)
- [CREATE2 and Deterministic Deployment](create2-and-deterministic-deployment.md)
- [Sign a Permit2 Permit](../recipes/permit2-permit.md)
- [PepuSwap Addresses](pepuswap.md)

pages.title: Build with an AI Coding Agent in 3 Minutes
pages.content:
# Build with an AI Coding Agent in 3 Minutes

The fastest path for agent users: install the MCP server, the plugin and the skills, then scaffold and verify an app without leaving the agent. The agent does the code and config; you provide the Privy credentials. This page is the short path; detail is in the agent-tooling and MCP sections.

> Status: the MCP server (`@pepu-chain/mcp` 0.2.5: 32 tools, 6 prompts), 12 skills, 6 commands and the builder subagent (plugin 0.4.1) exist and are tested. Gas sponsorship uses PEPU's hosted bundler and paymaster and needs a funded project of yours.

## Use it with an AI agent: the fast path (Claude Code)

Three steps, about three minutes of your time.

1. Install the plugin (once):

   ```text
   /plugin marketplace add pepu-org/pepu-devkit
   /plugin install pepu-devkit@pepu
   ```

2. In an empty folder, run the command with your idea:

   ```text
   /pepu-new-app a tap game where players pay no gas and approve once
   ```

3. Answer the agent when it asks for the few things only you have (below), then run what it tells you: `npm run dev`.

What `/pepu-new-app` does, in order:

| Step | What the agent does | Tool |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Lists the templates and picks one by what you described, saying why in one line. For the idea above: `sponsored-session-app` | `pepu_list_templates` |
| 2 | Scaffolds the app into a new folder (the same as `npx create-pepu-app`), then installs dependencies | `pepu_scaffold_app` |
| 3 | Reads `.env.local`, fills what it can, and asks you for the rest by name without echoing secrets | `pepu_check_env` |
| 4 | Checks your Privy dashboard for the dev origin and tells you which rows to change | `pepu_check_privy_config` |
| 5 | For a sponsored template, checks the hosted bundler and paymaster live and says what is missing (your project's key) | `pepu_sponsorship_status` |
| 6 | Runs typecheck and build and ends with the three commands to run | |

What only you do:

1. Create the Privy app at [dashboard.privy.io](https://dashboard.privy.io) and give the agent the App ID and App Secret (or paste them into `.env.local` yourself).
2. Click the dashboard settings the agent lists: Allowed origins `http://localhost:3000`, Google on, embedded wallets on, and Smart Wallets only if it picked `sponsored-demo`. The exact clicks are in [Dashboard Settings](../privy/dashboard-settings.md).
3. For a sponsored template, get a paymaster project with its key. Ask: "Walk me through claiming and funding a paymaster project for my Privy app." The agent encodes the transactions with `pepu_prepare_project_tx`; you sign them with the owner wallet and run the SIWE and attestation script, which needs your wallet and your Privy secret. See [Register, Deposit and Claim a v2 Project](../infra/paymaster/v2-register-deposit-claim.md).
4. Run `npm run doctor`, then `npm run dev`, and click through the flow. When it looks right, the agent can re-run `/pepu-doctor` for a readiness report.

Other clients (Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf, Claude Desktop, Cline) get the MCP server only, no slash commands: use the first prompt below. The rest of this page is the manual route.

## Prerequisites

- Node.js 18.17 or newer and an MCP-capable agent client.
- A Privy account (you create the app and copy two values).

## 1. Install the MCP server

Every client takes the same stdio server:

```bash
npx -y @pepu-chain/mcp
```

Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf, Claude Desktop and Cline each have their own config file shape. The shared entry is:

```json
{ "mcpServers": { "pepu": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@pepu-chain/mcp"] } } }
```

Exact per-client steps: [Install per Client](../mcp/install.md). Scaffolded templates already ship a `.mcp.json`. No API key is needed. Optional env: `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL`, `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL`, `PEPU_RPC_URL`.

## 2. Claude Code plugin

```text
/plugin marketplace add pepu-org/pepu-devkit
/plugin install pepu-devkit@pepu
```

It adds the MCP server, 12 skills, a builder subagent and six commands:

| Command | Does |
|---|---|
| `/pepu-new-app` | Scaffolds an app, choosing the template by pillar |
| `/pepu-add-login` | Google login and an embedded wallet |
| `/pepu-add-session` | Privy session keys |
| `/pepu-add-sponsorship` | Sponsored transactions, after a live availability check |
| `/pepu-add-sponsored-session` | The full combination |
| `/pepu-doctor` | Env, Privy dashboard and sponsorship readiness |

See [Claude Code Plugin](../agent-tooling/plugin.md) and [Skills Catalog](../agent-tooling/skills.md).

## What the agent does unattended, and what needs you

| Agent can | Needs a human |
|---|---|
| Scaffold the app (`pepu_scaffold_app`) | Create the Privy app at dashboard.privy.io |
| Write SDK code, routes and hooks | Copy the App ID and App Secret into `.env.local` (or paste them to the agent; the tools never echo secrets) |
| Generate the authorization key into `.env.local` without printing it | Register the public key and create the key quorum in the Privy dashboard |
| Check env keys, Privy config, sponsorship status | Set Allowed origins, enable Google, enable embedded wallets |
| Run `npm run doctor`, typecheck, build | Provide the paymaster project key for sponsored templates (`PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL`; the bundler defaults to the hosted one) |
| Explain a failed transaction or error | Click through the browser flow and approve Privy prompts |

## A first prompt

```text
Create a PEPU app that has Google login and a wallet. Use the pepu MCP tools and the
pepu-build-dapp skill. Scaffold it in ./my-app with the consumer-app template, tell me
exactly which Privy dashboard settings I must change, then run npm run doctor and
pepu_check_privy_config with origin http://localhost:3000 and report what is left.
```

For no-popup, no-gas, ask for the `sponsored-session-app` template and say you will supply a paymaster project token (the bundler URL defaults to the hosted one).

## What to expect

The agent lists the template choice with one line of reasoning, scaffolds, reports missing env keys by name, and finishes with a doctor report. Fields Privy does not expose come back `unknown`, not failed.

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Tools not listed | MCP not registered or the client not restarted | [Install per Client](../mcp/install.md) |
| Doctor: `PRIVY_APP_SECRET` missing | You have not provided it | Add it to `.env.local`, restart dev |
| Agent claims sponsorship is live | Skipped the live check | Run `pepu_sponsorship_status` |

## Related

- [MCP Server Overview](../mcp/index.md)
- [MCP and Skills overview](../agent-tooling/mcp-and-skills.md)
- [Quickstart: Zero to a Sponsored Transaction in 10 Minutes](quickstart-app.md)
- [Smart Account Paths](../concepts/smart-account-paths.md)
- [AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md in Templates](../agent-tooling/agents-md.md)

pages.title: What is Pepe Unchained V2
pages.content:
# What is Pepe Unchained V2

Pepe Unchained V2 is an Arbitrum Orbit (Nitro) chain, operated by Conduit, settling to Ethereum L1. It is a standard EVM chain — if you already know how to deploy and verify a Solidity contract on any Arbitrum Orbit chain, you already know how to do it here. Nothing about the execution environment is bespoke.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Mainnet chain ID** | `97741` |
| **Testnet chain ID** | `97740` (out of scope for development: no faucet, no indexed explorer, no deployed infrastructure) |
| **Stack** | Arbitrum Orbit / Nitro, ArbOS 51 |
| **Settles to** | Ethereum L1 (AnyTrust/Optimium DA — see [Network Properties](network-properties.md)) |
| **Native gas token** | PEPU, 18 decimals |
| **Operator** | Conduit |

Full copy-pasteable RPC URLs, explorers, and currency details are on the [Network Reference](network-reference.md) page. The deeper architectural picture — DA mode, precompiles, and an honest read of the chain's current L2BEAT rating — is on [Network Properties](network-properties.md).

Terms used on this page: [EntryPoint](../reference/glossary.md), [bundler](../reference/glossary.md), [paymaster](../reference/glossary.md), [Kernel](../reference/glossary.md), [session key](../reference/glossary.md), [project](../reference/glossary.md), [free tier](../reference/glossary.md). All are defined in the [Glossary](../reference/glossary.md).

## There is an old chain. This is not it.

If you've found a chain ID `3409`, an OP Stack reference, or a Celestia data-availability mention anywhere claiming to be "Pepe Unchained," that's the legacy V1 chain. It is dead. See [V1 vs V2](v1-vs-v2.md) before you configure anything.

## What you can build on today

The goal is a consumer app deployed quickly, without a founder spending weeks learning the chain. Three pillars have been proven on mainnet; see [The Three Pillars](pillars.md).

| Pillar | What a builder can use today |
|---|---|
| Google login to an embedded wallet | Yes. [Embedded Wallets](../onboarding/privy-embedded-wallets.md), [Privy Setup](../onboarding/privy-setup.md). |
| Session keys, no popup per action | Privy mode: yes, the user pays gas. Kernel on-chain mode: proven live in a browser on mainnet (2026-10-14), uses the hosted bundler and a funded project. [Session Keys](../onboarding/session-keys.md). |
| Sponsored transactions | Proven end to end through the **hosted** bundler and paymaster; you bring a funded project. [Sponsored Transactions](../onboarding/sponsored-transactions.md). |
| All three combined | Proven live in a browser on mainnet (2026-10-14). [End to End](../onboarding/google-session-sponsored.md). |

A tiered sponsorship model (a daily free allowance for PEPU's own apps plus project deposits) is live on mainnet, deployed as a canary: internally reviewed 3x, external audit pending, funded in small tranches; see [Sponsorship Tiers](../onboarding/sponsorship-tiers.md).

## Endpoints at a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| RPC | `https://rpc-pepu-v2-mainnet-0.t.conduit.xyz` |
| Explorer | `https://pepuscan.com` |
| Bundler | `https://bundler.pepeunchained.com` (SDK default; `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` overrides; local `http://localhost:4337`) |
| Paymaster | `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com`; ERC-7677 URL `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<token>` (`PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` overrides; local `http://localhost:8788`) |

Full list: [Network Reference](network-reference.md) and [Endpoints](../reference/endpoints.md).

## What this section covers

This is the developer-facing documentation for building on Pepe Unchained V2: network parameters, contract deployment, verification, wallet and account onboarding (Privy setup, session signers, sponsored transactions, smart accounts), an SDK reference, copy-pasteable recipes, and agent tooling (an MCP server and coding-agent skills). It assumes you already know Solidity and standard EVM tooling (Hardhat, Foundry) — it does not re-teach those tools, only how they apply here.

If you want a running app (and, with a funded project, a sponsored transaction) in about ten minutes, go to [Quickstart: Zero to a Sponsored Transaction in 10 Minutes](quickstart-app.md). If you specifically want to deploy a Solidity contract, go to [Deploy & Verify a Contract](../contracts/deployment.md).

## Scope decisions

Two things are deliberately not part of the dev kit today:

- **No Telegram Mini App template.** Telegram restricts Mini Apps to the TON blockchain, so a PEPU Mini App template would not be accepted there. It is excluded, not postponed.
- **Global Wallet (a cross-app wallet) is deferred.** Each app provisions its own Privy embedded wallet. A shared wallet that follows a user between apps is not built.

pages.title: Network Properties
pages.content:
# Network Properties

This page states plainly what kind of chain Pepe Unchained V2 is, including the parts that are trade-offs rather than selling points. Serious builders check third-party risk assessments before shipping to a chain regardless of what any docs page says — better they read it here first than find it independently and wonder why it wasn't mentioned.

## Stack

Pepe Unchained V2 runs on **Arbitrum Orbit**, using the **Nitro** execution stack, on **ArbOS 51**, operated by Conduit. It settles to Ethereum L1. This is a standard, largely unmodified Orbit deployment — see [Deploy & Verify a Contract](../contracts/deployment.md) for confirmation that ordinary Hardhat/Foundry tooling works against it without special handling.

## Data availability: AnyTrust, 1-of-1 committee

The chain runs in **AnyTrust** mode (sometimes referred to as Optimium), not full Rollup mode. The distinction matters:

- A full Rollup posts all transaction data to Ethereum L1, so anyone can reconstruct chain state from L1 data alone.
- An AnyTrust chain instead relies on a **Data Availability Committee (DAC)**: a set of parties who attest that they're holding the data off-chain. As long as enough committee members are honest and available, the data stays retrievable; if they aren't, data availability isn't guaranteed by L1 alone.

Pepe Unchained's DAC currently has **one member (1-of-1)**. There is no redundancy: data availability depends on that single party. This is a meaningfully weaker trust assumption than either a full Rollup or an AnyTrust chain with a larger, more distributed committee.

## Newer EVM features live on this chain

- **EIP-7702 is live.** EOAs can delegate execution to contract code without a full smart-account migration.
- **The P256 precompile is live at `0x100`.** This makes secp256r1 signature verification (as used by passkeys) cheap to do on-chain — a building block for passkey-based authentication, though it is only one piece of that puzzle. See [Social Login & Embedded Wallets](../onboarding/privy-embedded-wallets.md) for what's actually wired up today versus what still depends on infrastructure that isn't publicly hosted yet.
- **An ERC-4337 EntryPoint (v0.6 and v0.7), a ZeroDev Kernel v3 smart-account factory, and a funded, staked paymaster are deployed on mainnet.** Smart accounts are genuinely possible here now, and gas sponsorship has been proven end to end on mainnet — but it isn't usable by an application yet, because the bundler and paymaster policy service that served it aren't publicly hosted. See [Sponsored Transactions](../onboarding/sponsored-transactions.md) and [Smart Accounts](../onboarding/smart-accounts.md) for the complete picture of what this does and doesn't unlock.

## L2BEAT assessment

[L2BEAT's "Pepe Unchained" page](https://l2beat.com/scaling/projects/pepeunchained) exists, but it is not an assessment of this chain. It covers the **archived V1 chain — chain ID `3409`, an Optimium on the OP Stack** — and carries L2BEAT's own banner stating the project is archived and no longer maintained, having migrated from OP Stack to Orbit. Its stage rating and critical-severity findings (including things like an unenforced upgrade delay and non-permissionless fraud proofs) describe that dead chain, not V2. If you land on that page while researching Pepe Unchained, read it as V1 history — see [V1 vs V2](v1-vs-v2.md) — not as current risk information.

**V2 (chain ID `97741`) has no independent L2BEAT assessment or equivalent third-party risk rating at this time.** No separate L2BEAT page tracks the Orbit chain. That absence is stated here as a fact, not a reassurance — it means the centralization properties described above (the 1-of-1 data availability committee in particular) haven't been independently rated by L2BEAT or a comparable third party, in either direction. Judge V2 on its own documented properties, not on V1's findings and not on the assumption that "no rating" implies a good one.

## What this means practically

None of the above prevents you from deploying and using standard EVM contracts today — the execution environment works as documented in [Deploy & Verify a Contract](../contracts/deployment.md). It does mean you should factor the chain's current centralization and maturity profile into any decision that assumes L1-grade trust guarantees (for example, holding significant value in a bridge or contract that assumes fully trustless exit paths).

pages.title: Network Reference
pages.content:
# Network Reference

Copy-pasteable network parameters for Pepe Unchained V2. If you landed here from a search engine or an AI assistant and haven't confirmed you're looking at V2 (not the dead V1 chain, ID `3409`), read [V1 vs V2](v1-vs-v2.md) first.

## Mainnet

Build here. Every guide in this docs set targets mainnet by default — see "Testnet: out of scope today" below for why.

| Parameter | Value |
|---|---|
| Chain ID | `97741` (`0x17dcd`) |
| Network name | Pepe Unchained V2 |
| RPC URL | `https://rpc-pepu-v2-mainnet-0.t.conduit.xyz` |
| Currency symbol | PEPU (18 decimals) |
| Block explorer | `https://pepuscan.com` (Blockscout, fully indexed) |
| Contract verification | `https://pepuscan.com/api` (Blockscout verifier — see [Deploy & Verify a Contract](../contracts/deployment.md)) |

### Authenticated RPC

The RPC URL above is public and rate-limited, and gates `debug_*`/`trace_*` methods (`-32401`). Conduit also issues an **authenticated RPC URL** in the form `https://rpc-pepu-v2-mainnet-0.t.conduit.xyz/<API_KEY>` for anyone with a Conduit API key. The authenticated endpoint exposes `debug_traceCall` and `eth_simulateV1` in addition to standard JSON-RPC — useful for local simulation, safer contract-verification tooling, and anything that needs to trace a call before submitting it. There is no public self-serve signup for a key documented here; if you need one, ask whoever operates your Conduit relationship.

## Testnet: out of scope today

Testnet (chain `97740`) is a real, live chain, but there is nothing to build against on it today:

| Parameter | Value |
|---|---|
| Chain ID | `97740` (`0x17dcc`) |
| Network name | Pepe Unchained V2 Testnet |
| RPC URL | `https://rpc-pepu-v2-testnet-vn4qxxp9og.t.conduit.xyz` |
| Currency symbol | PEPU (18 decimals) |
| Block explorer | **None indexed.** `explorer-pepu-v2-testnet-vn4qxxp9og.t.conduit.xyz` is Conduit's default, non-Blockscout UI, which self-reports no indexer — it can show a single block or transaction by hash and nothing else. No `pepuscan.com`-equivalent Blockscout instance is registered for chain `97740` (confirmed against Blockscout's own public chain registry). |
| Faucet | **None exists.** There is no documented, self-serve way to obtain testnet PEPU. |
| Contracts | **None of the infrastructure on this page is deployed on testnet** — no Multicall3, no Permit2, no ERC-4337 EntryPoint, no Kernel smart-account factory. Everything below this section is mainnet-only unless stated otherwise. |

**Route everyone to mainnet.** With no faucet, no indexed explorer, and no deployed infrastructure, testnet cannot support a real development workflow today — and it doesn't need to: a transaction on PEPU mainnet costs a fraction of a cent. Every quickstart, recipe, and template in this docs set defaults to mainnet for exactly this reason. If testnet gains a faucet and an indexed explorer later, this page will say so plainly — until then, don't spend time trying to make testnet work.

## Sponsorship endpoints

Gas sponsorship needs a bundler and a paymaster. PEPU hosts both, and the SDK uses them by default.

| Service | Variable (override) | Local development default | Hosted (default) |
