|---|---|---|---|
| Bundler (ERC-4337, EntryPoint v0.7) | `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` | `http://localhost:4337` | `https://bundler.pepeunchained.com` |
| Paymaster (ERC-7677) | `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` | `http://localhost:8788/paymaster/<your-app-key>` | `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com`; ERC-7677 URL `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<token>` (always embeds a token) |

See [Endpoints](../reference/endpoints.md) and [Infrastructure Map](../infra/overview.md).

## Add to your wallet

Paste this into a `wallet_addEthereumChain` call, or enter the fields manually under your wallet's "Add Network" screen.

```json
{
  "chainId": "0x17dcd",
  "chainName": "Pepe Unchained V2",
  "nativeCurrency": { "name": "Pepe Unchained", "symbol": "PEPU", "decimals": 18 },
  "rpcUrls": ["https://rpc-pepu-v2-mainnet-0.t.conduit.xyz"],
  "blockExplorerUrls": ["https://pepuscan.com"]
}
```

There is no reason to add testnet to a wallet today — see "Testnet: out of scope today" above.

## Which standard contracts are deployed

This used to be the table that saved you a debugging session by warning you that almost nothing was here. That's no longer the whole story: **Multicall3 and the ERC-4337/smart-account stack are now live on mainnet** — but at addresses and with caveats that still trip up tooling built for a "default" EVM chain. Read this table before you hardcode anything.

The full table, with deployment notes, verification links, and the reasoning behind each gap, lives on [Deployed Contracts Reference](../contracts/deployed-contracts.md). Summary:

| Contract | Canonical address (other chains) | Status on Pepe Unchained V2 mainnet |
|---|---|---|
| CREATE2 deterministic deployer | `0x4e59b44847b379578588920cA78FbF26c0B4956C` | **Deployed**, at the canonical address. This is what makes everything else on this table possible. |
| Multicall3 | `0xcA11bde05977b3631167028862bE2a173976CA11` | **Deployed — but NOT at the canonical address.** See [The Multicall3 Trap](../contracts/multicall3.md) before you wire this up; the canonical address is permanently unreachable on this chain and PEPU's deployment lives somewhere else. |
| Permit2 | `0x000000000022D473030F116dDEE9F6B43aC78BA3` | **Deployed**, at the canonical address. |
| ERC-4337 EntryPoint v0.6 | `0x5FF137D4b0FDCD49DcA30c7CF57E578a026d2789` | **Deployed**, at the canonical address. |
| ERC-4337 EntryPoint v0.7 | `0x0000000071727De22E5E9d8BAf0edAc6f37da032` | **Deployed**, at the canonical address. |
| Kernel v3 account factory + MetaFactory + ECDSA validator | (ZeroDev, versioned) | **Deployed.** See [Smart Accounts](../onboarding/smart-accounts.md) and the full reference table for addresses. |
| Sponsored paymaster v2 | `0xdb28528C9399C33c9A0297E8A62F39145acbC30D` (project-specific, not canonical) | **Deployed as a canary** (2026-10-14): internally reviewed 3x, external audit pending, funded in small tranches. Sponsorship is proven on mainnet through the hosted endpoints. The v1 paymaster `0x2B6FED323bFA24f0475f4e1Dd3C7F6Cc1f3ae8B0` is retired and cannot sponsor. |

**A deployed EntryPoint is not gas sponsorship, and gas sponsorship needs a bundler and a paymaster service on top.** Sponsorship is proven end to end on mainnet: a zero-balance smart account transacted, paid for by the paymaster above, through PEPU's hosted bundler and ERC-7677 policy service. An app uses those by default and overrides them with `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` and `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL`; see [Endpoints](../reference/endpoints.md). See [Sponsored Transactions](../onboarding/sponsored-transactions.md), [Smart Accounts](../onboarding/smart-accounts.md) and [Social Login & Embedded Wallets](../onboarding/privy-embedded-wallets.md) for what that does and doesn't unlock today.

A practical consequence of the gaps that remain: some ecosystem dApps on Pepe Unchained (for example, the native DEX) use their **own non-canonical** Multicall/Permit2 addresses, sized for their own needs — these are not general-purpose substitutes. Don't assume any Multicall or Permit2 address you find referenced by an app on this chain is the canonical one, or compatible with the standard ABI; check it against the [Deployed Contracts Reference](../contracts/deployed-contracts.md), or read it directly from that app's own deployment config.

## A note on gas

The native gas token is PEPU, priced far below ETH, so gwei-denominated gas prices here are not comparable to Ethereum mainnet or most L2s. Expect a base fee around **12,500 gwei-equivalent** — this is a low-value-token artifact, not a sign the chain is expensive or congested, and not a misconfigured RPC. A simple transfer still costs a fraction of a cent in practice. Don't set gas price limits in your tooling based on habits formed on ETH-denominated chains, and don't "fix" the number by hardcoding a lower gas price — your transactions will just get stuck. See [Troubleshooting](../troubleshooting.md) if this is the reason you landed here.

pages.title: The Three Pillars and How They Combine
pages.content:
# The Three Pillars and How They Combine

The PEPU dev kit is built around three capabilities that make an app feel like a normal consumer app: Google login to a wallet, session keys, and sponsored transactions. This page defines each pillar, says what is proven, and gives the decision table for choosing a combination. Read it first; every other page in Onboarding, Privy and the SDK section hangs off it.

> Status: Pillars 1 and 2 (Privy mode) are proven on mainnet and usable today. Pillar 3 and the combination are proven on mainnet (the combination live in a browser on 2026-10-14, against the hosted bundler and v2 paymaster), through the hosted bundler (`https://bundler.pepeunchained.com`) and paymaster (`https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com`), which you use with a funded project. The v2 tiered paymaster is deployed as a canary: internally reviewed 3x, external audit pending, funded in small tranches.

Terms used on this page: [UserOperation](../reference/glossary.md), [bundler](../reference/glossary.md), [paymaster](../reference/glossary.md), [EntryPoint](../reference/glossary.md), [Kernel](../reference/glossary.md), [session key](../reference/glossary.md), [project](../reference/glossary.md), [free tier](../reference/glossary.md). All are defined in the [Glossary](../reference/glossary.md).

## Prerequisites

- Mainnet only: chain ID `97741`. Testnet `97740` is out of scope.
- A Privy app (App ID and App Secret). See [Privy Configuration Overview](../privy/index.md).
- For pillar 3 and the combination: a bundler and a paymaster. Write them as `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` and `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL`. Local development defaults are `http://localhost:4337` and `http://localhost:8788`. See [Infrastructure Map](../infra/overview.md).

## The pillars

### Pillar 1: Google login to an embedded wallet

| | |
|---|---|
| What it gives | A user clicks "Sign in with Google" and gets a self-custodial Privy embedded wallet on chain 97741. No seed phrase, no extension. |
| What it needs | A Privy app with Google enabled, the exact origin (with port) in Allowed origins, embedded wallets on for Ethereum, and `PRIVY_APP_SECRET` on the server for the ensure-wallet route. No bundler, no paymaster. |
| SDK | `/privy` (config, requirements), `/privy/react` (`PepuPrivyProvider`, `WalletGate`, `useEmbeddedWallet`), `/privy/wagmi` (`PepuPrivyWagmiProvider`), `/privy/server` (`createEnsureWalletRoute`, `requireUser`) |
| Template | `consumer-app` |
| Status | **Proven.** A real Google login on a real Privy app created an embedded wallet through the server-side ensure route, on mainnet. |
| Page | [Social Login and Embedded Wallets (Privy)](../onboarding/privy-embedded-wallets.md) |

### Pillar 2: Session keys, with no popup per transaction

There are two modes. They differ in who enforces the limits and in who pays gas.

| | Privy session signers | Kernel on-chain session keys |
|---|---|---|
| Account | The plain embedded EOA | A ZeroDev Kernel v3.1 smart account owned by the embedded wallet |
| Who signs actions | Privy, on your server's request (`eth_signTransaction`), then your server broadcasts | A session key your server holds, signing UserOperations |
| Where the scope is enforced | Privy's backend policy engine (off-chain) | Call policy and timestamp policy contracts, during UserOperation validation (on-chain) |
| What you trust | Privy's policy engine and your policy configuration | The chain. A compromised server can only do what the permission allows until it expires |
| Who pays gas | The user, from the embedded wallet | Whoever sponsors it: pair it with a paymaster (the combination) |
| Needs | An authorization key and a key quorum in the Privy dashboard | A bundler, a paymaster and a session store. No authorization key |
| SDK | `/session` (policy), `/session/server` (routes), `/session/react` (hooks) | `/session/kernel` (policies, approve, load), plus `/combo` for the routes |
| Template | `game-app` | `sponsored-session-app` |
| Status | **Proven** end to end on mainnet with a real Privy app. | **Proven** on mainnet by script (with scope refusals proven) and live in a browser (2026-10-14). Uses the hosted bundler and a funded project. |
| Page | [Session Keys: No Popup Per Transaction](../onboarding/session-keys.md) | [Session Keys: No Popup Per Transaction](../onboarding/session-keys.md), [Sponsored Session](../onboarding/sponsored-session.md) |

### Pillar 3: Sponsored transactions

| | |
|---|---|
| What it gives | The user pays no gas. A Kernel smart account holding 0 PEPU sends a transaction and a paymaster pays. |
| Who pays | The paymaster contract, from its own EntryPoint deposit, after an off-chain policy service approves the UserOperation. Today that is the v2 paymaster `0xdb28528C9399C33c9A0297E8A62F39145acbC30D` (a canary), paid from your project's deposit or, for PEPU's own apps, the free tier. The v1 paymaster is retired. |
| What it needs | A bundler (ERC-4337, EntryPoint v0.7), a paymaster (ERC-7677), and your contract on the paymaster's allowlist. |
| SDK | `/aa` (probes, errors), `/aa/kernel` (`toPepuKernelAccount`, `createPepuSponsoredClient`, `sendSponsored`), `/aa/react` (`useSponsoredSend`, `usePepuSmartAccount`, `usePepuSponsorship`), `/aa/react-direct` (`useDirectSponsoredSend`, `useDirectSmartAccount`), `/paymaster` (v2 project helpers) |
| Template | `sponsored-demo` |
| Status | **Proven** end to end on mainnet through the hosted bundler and paymaster (a project-sponsored operation from a fresh 0 PEPU account). The v2 tiered paymaster is **proven on mainnet (canary, external audit pending)**. |
| Page | [Sponsored Transactions](../onboarding/sponsored-transactions.md) |

### The combination: Google login, one signature, no popups, no user gas

Sign in with Google (pillar 1), approve one scoped session with one owner signature (the Kernel mode of pillar 2), and every later action is a sponsored UserOperation (pillar 3). The limits live on-chain in the user's smart account.

| | |
|---|---|
| SDK | `/combo` (`createSponsoredSessionRoutes`), `/combo/react` (`useSponsoredSession`), on top of `/session/kernel`, `/aa/kernel`, `/privy/*` |
| Template | `sponsored-session-app` |
| Status | **Proven** on mainnet live in a browser (2026-10-14, against the hosted bundler and v2 paymaster: Google sign-in, one Privy signature, sponsored taps with no popup, revoke) and by script (`npm run prove-session`, and the SDK's own `prove-session`): one owner signature, then two sponsored UserOperations signed by the session key, from an account holding 0 PEPU. A different function on the allowed contract, and an expired grant, are refused. |
| Page | [Google Login, Session and Sponsorship End to End](../onboarding/google-session-sponsored.md) |

## Decision table

| I want | Choose | Dashboard needs | Template |
|---|---|---|---|
| Login and a wallet, user pays gas, user approves each send | Pillar 1 only | Allowed origins, login methods, embedded wallets | `consumer-app` |
| Popup-free actions, user pays gas, simplest setup, no bundler | Privy session signers | Pillar 1 plus an authorization key and key quorum | `game-app` |
| Gasless sends, user still signs each one | Sponsored transactions, `privy-smart-wallets` transport | Pillar 1 plus Smart Wallets: Kernel, chain 97741, bundler URL, paymaster URL | `sponsored-demo` |
| Gasless sends, URLs kept in your env, no Privy Smart Wallets | Sponsored transactions, `direct` transport | Pillar 1 only | none (use `useDirectSponsoredSend` from `/aa/react-direct`) |
| No popup and no gas, limits enforced on-chain | The combination | Pillar 1 only. Smart Wallets and authorization keys are not needed | `sponsored-session-app` |

Not sure which smart-account setup you need? [Smart Account Paths](../concepts/smart-account-paths.md) compares the plain wallet, the ZeroDev-native path (the SDK builds the Kernel account) and Privy Smart Wallets (Privy builds it) side by side, with a "pick this if" list.

Two choices inside the sponsorship rows:

- **`privy-smart-wallets` versus `direct`.** With `privy-smart-wallets`, Privy's smart-wallet client calls the bundler and paymaster URLs you entered in the dashboard (`https://bundler.pepeunchained.com` and `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<project token>`). A paymaster URL embeds a token, so entering it in the dashboard stores a credential there, and the free tier is not reachable from it. With `direct`, the SDK builds the Kernel account itself and your env supplies the URLs. `direct` is what the combination uses. See [Sponsored Transactions](../onboarding/sponsored-transactions.md).
- **Privy session versus Kernel session.** Choose Privy mode when users pay their own gas and you accept that Privy's policy engine enforces the scope. Choose Kernel mode when you want the chain to enforce it, which in practice means you also sponsor gas. A Kernel session does not use Privy session signers, so no authorization key is involved.

## What to expect

- Pillar 1 works today with nothing but a Privy app.
- Pillar 2 in Privy mode works today. The user pays gas, a fraction of a cent.
- Gas sponsorship needs a claimed and funded project (the free tier is only for PEPU's own Privy app). Do not tell users a transaction is "gasless" until you have configured and tested one. Use `usePepuSponsorship` or the `pepu_sponsorship_status` MCP tool to check live.

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Login fails or the iframe is blocked | The origin, including the port, is not in Allowed origins | [Dashboard Settings](../privy/dashboard-settings.md) |
| "Creating your wallet..." never ends | Privy's client-side creation hangs when the dashboard setting is off | Use `WalletGate` and `createEnsureWalletRoute`; see Pillar 1 page |
| Session grant returns 401 "No valid authorization keys" | Key quorum mismatch (Privy mode) | [Authorization Keys and Key Quorums](../privy/authorization-keys.md) |
| Sponsored send denied | Destination not allowlisted, cap hit, or no deposit | [Sponsored Transactions](../onboarding/sponsored-transactions.md) |
| A page spins on "Setting up your smart wallet..." | Smart Wallets not configured for chain 97741 (Privy transport only) | [Dashboard Settings](../privy/dashboard-settings.md) |

## Related

- [Smart Account Paths: which one to use](../concepts/smart-account-paths.md)
- [Architecture: Who Calls What](../concepts/architecture.md)
- [Trust and Security Model](../concepts/trust-and-security.md)
- [Quickstart: Zero to a Sponsored Transaction in 10 Minutes](quickstart-app.md)
- [Template Gallery](../templates/index.md)
- [SDK Overview and Reference](../sdk/reference.md)

pages.title: Quickstart: Zero to a Sponsored Transaction in 10 Minutes
pages.content:
# Quickstart: Zero to a Sponsored Transaction in 10 Minutes

Copy-paste path from nothing to a running Next.js app on Pepe Unchained V2 that sends a real transaction whose gas someone else pays. You choose a template, scaffold it, fill two Privy values, click through the Privy dashboard once, get a paymaster project (for the sponsored templates), run `npm run doctor`, run the app and send. If you only want login and a wallet, the first six steps are the whole job and take about five minutes. To let an AI agent do it, see [Build with an AI Coding Agent](ai-assisted.md). To deploy only a Solidity contract, see [Deploy and Verify a Contract](../contracts/deployment.md).

> Status: proven. The CLI (`create-pepu-app` 0.1.3), the templates and the SDK (`@pepu-chain/sdk` 0.2.2) are on npm. The two sponsored templates use the hosted [bundler](../reference/glossary.md) (`https://bundler.pepeunchained.com`) and [paymaster](../reference/glossary.md) (`https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com`); they need a [project](../reference/glossary.md) of yours (claim, deposit, token), because the [free tier](../reference/glossary.md) is only for PEPU's own Privy app. The v2 paymaster is deployed as a canary: internally reviewed 3x, external audit pending, funded in small tranches, so keep deposits small.

## Prerequisites

- Node.js 18.17 or newer and npm. You do not clone this repository.
- A Privy account (free): [dashboard.privy.io](https://dashboard.privy.io).
- For a sponsored template only: a wallet holding a little PEPU (for the one-time project setup and the deposit). Buy PEPU on an exchange or bridge via [pepubridge.com](https://pepubridge.com). A transaction costs a fraction of a cent.

## 1. Pick a template

Answer one question: **who pays gas, and does the user approve each action?**

| You want | Template | Smart account path | Extra setup |
|---|---|---|---|
| Login, a wallet, a real PEPU send. Users pay gas | `consumer-app` (default) | none (plain wallet) | none |
| Unlock content by holding a token or NFT | `token-gated-app` | none | a gate token address |
| An NFT mint page | `nft-mint` | none | deploy the contract |
| Popup-free play, user pays gas, limits enforced by Privy | `game-app` | none (Privy session signers) | authorization key, key quorum, a deployed contract |
| One gasless button, client only | `sponsored-demo` | Privy Smart Wallets | Smart Wallets in the dashboard, a project **client** token |
| One signature, then no popups and no user gas, limits enforced on-chain | `sponsored-session-app` | ZeroDev-native | a project **server** key |

Not sure? Take `consumer-app` to see login work, or `sponsored-session-app` for the full experience. The difference between the two smart-account paths is explained in [Smart Account Paths](../concepts/smart-account-paths.md); the template list with more detail is the [Template Gallery](../templates/index.md).

## 2. Scaffold

```bash
npx create-pepu-app@latest my-app --template sponsored-session-app
cd my-app
```

Swap the template name for the one you picked. With no `--template` it asks. The CLI copies the template, creates `.env.local` from `.env.example`, adds `.mcp.json` and agent files, installs dependencies and prints the next steps. If it did not install, run `npm install`. Flags (`--yes`, `--pm`, `--no-install`, `--json`) are in [create-pepu-app CLI](../cli/create-pepu-app.md).

## 3. Get your Privy values

1. Open [dashboard.privy.io](https://dashboard.privy.io), create an app, and open Settings, Basics.
2. Copy the **App ID** and create an **App Secret**.
3. Put them in `.env.local`:

```
NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_APP_ID=<your App ID>
PRIVY_APP_SECRET=<your App Secret>
```

The App ID is public. The secret is server only: never prefix it `NEXT_PUBLIC_`, never commit it.

## 4. Click through the Privy dashboard

Four settings decide whether login works. Do them now; the exact menu paths and failure symptoms are in [Dashboard Settings, Field by Field](../privy/dashboard-settings.md).

| # | Setting | Value |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Allowed origins (Configuration, App settings) | `http://localhost:3000`, with the port. Add your production origin later |
| 2 | Login methods (User management, Authentication) | Enable Google and email |
| 3 | Embedded wallets (Wallets) | On for Ethereum, create wallets on login |
| 4 | Smart Wallets (Wallets, Smart wallets) | **Only for `sponsored-demo`**: provider Kernel v3.1, chain 97741, bundler `https://bundler.pepeunchained.com`, paymaster URL from step 5. Every other template: leave it alone |

Port 3000 must be free. If it is taken, Next.js silently starts on 3001 and login fails with errors that never mention the port. Free 3000 rather than working around it.

## 5. Get a paymaster project (sponsored templates only)

Skip this step for `consumer-app`, `token-gated-app`, `nft-mint` and `game-app`.

A sponsored transaction is paid from a project budget that you own. Getting one is claim, configure, deposit, register; it takes a script about two minutes. Follow [Register, Deposit and Claim a v2 Project](../infra/paymaster/v2-register-deposit-claim.md): it has the SDK code, the runnable recipe ([Deposit and Claim a Paymaster Project](../recipes/v2-deposit-and-claim.md)), and an MCP and agent route for the parts a tool can encode. At the end you hold two credentials, shown once:

| Credential | Looks like | Use it in |
|---|---|---|
| Server key | `ppk_...` (secret) | `sponsored-session-app`: `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL=https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<server key>` in `.env.local` |
| Client token | `ppt_...` (publishable, works only from your allowed origins) | `sponsored-demo`: the paymaster URL in the Privy dashboard (step 4, row 4) |

Make sure your project's targets include the contract the template calls: both sponsored templates call `TapScore` (`0x261eA5971B93237a56990206A46Bc80318e4d078`), and the per-wallet daily limit must be above about 21 PEPU, with a project balance of at least about 25 PEPU, or a new user's first action (which deploys their account) is denied.

For `sponsored-session-app` your `.env.local` now also has:

```
PEPU_BUNDLER_URL=https://bundler.pepeunchained.com
PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL=https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<server key>
```

Never commit it. Template-specific variables are in [Environment Variables](../reference/env-vars.md).

## 6. Run the doctor

```bash
npm run doctor
```

It checks `.env.local` against your template, the chain RPC, the bundler and paymaster, and your Privy dashboard settings (including that `http://localhost:3000` is an allowed origin). It never prints values. **Success looks like** lines starting `ok` and a final `ok   no failing checks`:

```text
ok   privy.app-id: Privy app id format looks right.
ok   chain.rpc: RPC reachable, chainId 97741.
ok   sponsorship.bundler: Bundler reachable and reports supported entry points.
ok   sponsorship.paymaster: Paymaster endpoint reachable.
ok   privy.allowed-origins: The page origin (including the port) is in Allowed origins: http://localhost:3000 is allowed.
ok   privy.embedded-wallets: Embedded wallets are enabled for Ethereum ...
ok   no failing checks
```

| Line | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `FAIL` | Fix it before you run the app; the message names the variable or setting |
| `WARN ... could not be verified` | Privy's public config did not report that setting. Not a failure: check the dashboard row by hand |
| `skip` | The check does not apply to this template, or you passed `--offline` |

Running on another port: `PEPU_APP_ORIGIN=http://localhost:3001 npm run doctor`, after adding that origin in the dashboard.

## 7. Run the app and send your first sponsored transaction

```bash
npm run dev
```

Open `http://localhost:3000` and check the terminal says port 3000. Then:

| Template | Click | You should see |
|---|---|---|
| `consumer-app` | Sign in, send a small PEPU amount (the wallet needs PEPU) | Your address and balance, then a transaction link. Gas is not sponsored; a permanent notice says so |
| `sponsored-session-app` | Sign in with Google, **Start session**, **Approve**, sign once in Privy, then **Tap** | No popup on Tap. After a few seconds an evidence panel shows a pepuscan link, the sender (your smart account, not your wallet), "Gas paid by paymaster" and a cost. The smart account holds 0 PEPU |
| `sponsored-demo` | Sign in, **Sponsor a tap** | The Kernel smart account (0 PEPU), a transaction link, and the paymaster's EntryPoint deposit dropping. That drop, not the hash, is the proof |

Wallet creation shows "Setting up your wallet..." for a moment on first login. A brand-new account's first sponsored operation also deploys the account, so it takes longer and costs more than the next one.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Login fails, iframe blocked, OAuth 403 | Origin or port missing from Allowed origins | Step 4, row 1 |
| Setup screen on load | A required env key is missing | Run `npm run doctor`, set the key, restart `npm run dev` |
| `/api/wallet/ensure` returns 500 | `PRIVY_APP_SECRET` unset, or the dev server was not restarted | Set it and restart |
| No "Continue with Google" button | Google is off in the dashboard | Step 4, row 2 |
| Page spins on "Setting up your smart wallet..." | `sponsored-demo` without Smart Wallets for chain 97741 | Step 4, row 4 |
| `project_origin_not_allowed` | A client token with no allowed origins, or a client token used from a server | Set allowed origins on the project, or use the server key from the server |
| `PAYMASTER_DESTINATION_NOT_ALLOWED` | The project's targets do not include `TapScore` | Run the `configure` step again with the contract |
| `trailing-hour spend ... would exceed cap` after the first tap | The per-wallet limit is below the first-operation reservation | Raise the per-wallet limit above about 21 PEPU |
| Privy refuses a send you can afford | Its conservative gas estimate at PEPU's roughly 12,500 gwei base fee | See [Troubleshooting](../troubleshooting.md) |

## Next steps

- [Smart Account Paths](../concepts/smart-account-paths.md): why the two sponsored templates differ and which to ship
- [The Three Pillars](pillars.md)
- [Session Keys](../onboarding/session-keys.md) and [Sponsored Transactions](../onboarding/sponsored-transactions.md)
- [Template Gallery](../templates/index.md)
- [Recipes](../recipes/read-a-contract.md)
- [SDK Overview and Reference](../sdk/reference.md)
- [Build with an AI Coding Agent](ai-assisted.md)

pages.title: V1 vs V2: Which Chain Are You On
pages.content:
# V1 vs V2: Which Chain Are You On

**Short answer: if you are building today, you are building on V2 — chain ID `97741` (mainnet) / `97740` (testnet), Arbitrum Orbit. There is an older chain, V1 — chain ID `3409`, OP Stack — and it is dead. Do not configure your tools against chain ID `3409`.**

This page exists because search results, older third-party chain listings, and cached AI answers still surface V1 details under the name "Pepe Unchained." Getting this wrong costs real time: a wrong chain ID means your wallet, RPC, and deploy scripts silently point at a chain that no longer accepts new activity.

## The two chains

| | V1 (legacy, dead) | V2 (current) |
|---|---|---|
| Chain ID | `3409` | `97741` (mainnet), `97740` (testnet) |
| Stack | OP Stack / Optimium | Arbitrum Orbit / Nitro |
| Data availability | Custom Gas Token setup via Celestia-adjacent configuration | AnyTrust/Optimium, 1-of-1 committee — see [Network Properties](network-properties.md) |
| Status | **Dead.** Legacy migration/claims portal closed **2026-01-31, 23:59 UTC**. No new deployments, no supported RPC. | **Live.** This is the chain the rest of these docs cover. |
| RPC | Not documented here — do not use | `https://rpc-pepu-v2-mainnet-0.t.conduit.xyz` (mainnet), `https://rpc-pepu-v2-testnet-vn4qxxp9og.t.conduit.xyz` (testnet) |

The migration from V1 to V2 happened because Conduit deprecated the Custom Gas Token feature V1 depended on. V2 is a separate chain, not an upgrade in place — different chain ID, different stack, different RPC, no shared state.

## Where the confusion comes from

- **Third-party chain-list and SDK pages have been observed showing incorrect V2 testnet data** — including a wrong chain ID and a wrong gas-token currency for testnet `97740`. Always verify against this page or a direct `eth_chainId` call against the RPC URLs above rather than trusting a third-party listing.
- Generic "Pepe Unchained" search results and some cached AI answers may still describe the V1 chain's architecture (OP Stack, Celestia-style DA) as if it were current. If you see chain ID `3409` mentioned anywhere in the same breath as architectural claims about Pepe Unchained, that content is describing the dead chain.
- A separate, unrelated chain called "Pepe Chain Mainnet" also exists on some chain-list sites under a different chain ID. It is not related to Pepe Unchained at all — don't confuse the two by name alone.

## What to do

- Configure your wallet, Hardhat/Foundry, and any chain-definition objects against chain ID `97741` (mainnet) or `97740` (testnet) only. See [Network Reference](network-reference.md) for the full, copy-pasteable parameters.
- If you're citing an architectural fact about "Pepe Unchained" from a source you didn't get from this docs set, check whether it's talking about chain `3409` before you rely on it.

pages.title: Bundler JSON-RPC API
pages.content:
# Bundler JSON-RPC API

Method-by-method reference for the PEPU bundler (Alto, ERC-4337 EntryPoint v0.7, chain `97741`). Read this when you are calling the bundler without the SDK, debugging a failing UserOperation or writing your own client. Most apps do not call these methods by hand: viem's bundler client, Privy's smart-wallet client and the SDK (`@pepu-chain/sdk/aa`) do it for you.

> Status: **proven** on mainnet for estimate, send, get-by-hash and get-receipt, including through the hosted endpoint `https://bundler.pepeunchained.com`. `eth_supportedEntryPoints` and `eth_chainId` responses below were captured read-only from a local bundler on 2026-10-03. The other examples show the response shape and use values from the 2026-09-24 proof-of-life run; they are abridged. Write `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` in your config, or rely on the SDK default (the hosted URL). The local development default is `http://localhost:4337`.

## Endpoint and transport

| | |
|---|---|
| URL | `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` (browser-exposed variant `NEXT_PUBLIC_PEPU_BUNDLER_URL`). Hosted default `https://bundler.pepeunchained.com`. Local default `http://localhost:4337`. |
| Method | `POST`, `Content-Type: application/json`, JSON-RPC 2.0 body |
| Auth | None at the Alto layer. The hosted deployment sits behind a proxy that may add its own |
| CORS | Enabled; any `Origin` is reflected, `OPTIONS` preflights return 204. See [Bundler Overview](overview.md#cors-and-the-proxy-policy) |
| Batching | Not covered by this page; send one request per call |
| Rate limits | Applied at the proxy if at all; Alto itself has none. Do not rely on them |

The SDK resolves the URL for you (explicit option, then the env variables, then the hosted default, `https://bundler.pepeunchained.com`). Never hard-code a tunnel URL.

Quantities are `0x`-prefixed hex strings, as in all Ethereum JSON-RPC. A v0.7 UserOperation is sent in its **unpacked** form:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `sender` | address | The Kernel smart account |
| `nonce` | hex quantity | EntryPoint nonce (key and sequence packed) |
| `factory`, `factoryData` | address, hex | Only when the account is not yet deployed |
| `callData` | hex | A Kernel `execute(bytes32,bytes)` call |
| `callGasLimit`, `verificationGasLimit`, `preVerificationGas` | hex quantity | |
| `maxFeePerGas`, `maxPriorityFeePerGas` | hex quantity | PEPU's base fee is about 12,500 gwei; this is normal |
| `paymaster`, `paymasterVerificationGasLimit`, `paymasterPostOpGasLimit`, `paymasterData` | | Only for sponsored operations; from the [paymaster](../paymaster/erc7677.md) |
| `signature` | hex | The account's signature (or a dummy of the right length when estimating) |

## Supported methods

| Method | Supported | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `eth_chainId` | Yes | Returns `0x17dcd` (97741) |
| `eth_supportedEntryPoints` | Yes | v0.7 first, then v0.6 |
| `eth_estimateUserOperationGas` | Yes | Proven on mainnet |
| `eth_sendUserOperation` | Yes | Proven on mainnet; needs `safe-mode: false` (known Alto 0.0.21 bug) |
| `eth_getUserOperationByHash` | Yes | `null` if unknown |
| `eth_getUserOperationReceipt` | Yes | `null` until included |
| `pimlico_getUserOperationGasPrice` | Implemented in Alto 0.0.21 | Not exercised against the PEPU bundler during this documentation pass. `probeBundler` reports whether a given deployment answers it |
| `pimlico_getUserOperationStatus` | Implemented in Alto 0.0.21 | Same caveat |
| `zd_getUserOperationGasPrice` | Not an Alto method | `probeBundler` checks for it because ZeroDev's client prefers it; expect "method not found" |
| `debug_bundler_*` | Disabled | `enable-debug-endpoints` is `false` |

## eth_chainId

Request:

```json
{ "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": "eth_chainId", "params": [] }
```

Response (captured 2026-10-03):

```json
{ "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "result": "0x17dcd" }
```

`0x17dcd` is 97741. Any other value means you are pointed at the wrong network.

## eth_supportedEntryPoints

Request:

```json
{ "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": "eth_supportedEntryPoints", "params": [] }
```

Response (captured 2026-10-03):

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 1,
  "result": [
    "0x0000000071727De22E5E9d8BAf0edAc6f37da032",
    "0x5FF137D4b0FDCD49DcA30c7CF57E578a026d2789"
  ]
}
```

Use the first entry (EntryPoint v0.7) for Kernel v3.x. The addresses are documented in [EntryPoints and Kernel](../../contracts/entrypoints-and-kernel.md).

## eth_estimateUserOperationGas

Params: `[userOperation, entryPoint]`, optionally a third argument of state overrides. Pass a dummy-but-well-formed `signature` (the right length for your account) so signature validation does not fail the simulation. For a **sponsored** operation, attach the paymaster fields from `pm_getPaymasterStubData` first. Estimating without them makes EntryPoint demand the sender's own prefund and fail with `AA21 didn't pay prefund` for a zero-balance account.

Request (abridged):

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 1,
  "method": "eth_estimateUserOperationGas",
  "params": [
    {
      "sender": "0xA43CDA364c524551640206A5A22906dBD989F373",
      "nonce": "0x0",
      "factory": "0xaac5D4240AF87249B3f71BC8E4A2cae074A3E419",
      "factoryData": "0x…",
      "callData": "0x…",
      "callGasLimit": "0x0",
      "verificationGasLimit": "0x0",
      "preVerificationGas": "0x0",
      "maxFeePerGas": "0x…",
      "maxPriorityFeePerGas": "0x…",
      "signature": "0x…"
    },
    "0x0000000071727De22E5E9d8BAf0edAc6f37da032"
  ]
}
```

Response (values from the 2026-09-24 run: an account-deploying operation):

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 1,
  "result": {
    "preVerificationGas": "0xc769",
    "verificationGasLimit": "0x51e44",
    "callGasLimit": "0x3fc3"
  }
}
```

When the request carried paymaster fields, the result also includes `paymasterVerificationGasLimit` and `paymasterPostOpGasLimit`. The deployed Kernel follow-up operation estimated `preVerificationGas` `0xbbd8` and `verificationGasLimit` `0x1573d`.

`preVerificationGas` is large because PEPU is a Nitro chain: it includes the L1 data fee component (`chain-type: arbitrum`).

## eth_sendUserOperation

Params: `[userOperation, entryPoint]`, with real gas limits and a real signature (and paymaster fields for a sponsored operation). Returns the **userOpHash** (not a transaction hash).

Request: same shape as above, with the estimated gas limits filled in.

Response:

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 1,
  "result": "0xc20a1c642b0b61d4c545de2ec5d333b37440ff8a0b0ec9307b8e64cfe3c6e0f8"
}
```

(That hash is the first operation of the 2026-09-24 proof of life.) The operation is queued, bundled on the next bundling pass (about `block-time`, 5 seconds) and submitted by the executor. Poll for the receipt.

If the call fails with HTTP 500 and `Encoded error signature "0x99410554" not found on ABI`, `safe-mode` is on. See [Bundler Overview](overview.md#safe-mode-is-off-known-alto-0021-bug).

## eth_getUserOperationByHash

Params: `[userOpHash]`.

```json
{ "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": "eth_getUserOperationByHash", "params": ["0xc20a1c642b0b61d4c545de2ec5d333b37440ff8a0b0ec9307b8e64cfe3c6e0f8"] }
```

Response when the operation is included:

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 1,
  "result": {
    "userOperation": { "sender": "0xA43CDA364c524551640206A5A22906dBD989F373", "…": "…" },
    "entryPoint": "0x0000000071727De22E5E9d8BAf0edAc6f37da032",
    "blockNumber": "0xa08cc7",
    "blockHash": "0x…",
    "transactionHash": "0x8232872612eb500033faf8ef605f7c14f4fef556defdbb4d7c67c1731d0b00d3"
  }
}
```

`result` is `null` when the operation is unknown or not yet mined.

## eth_getUserOperationReceipt

Params: `[userOpHash]`. Returns `null` until the operation is included, so poll (every 2 to 5 seconds, with a timeout).

Response (abridged, same operation; `actualGasCost` is 7.725575 PEPU, `actualGasUsed` is 309,023):

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 1,
  "result": {
    "userOpHash": "0xc20a1c642b0b61d4c545de2ec5d333b37440ff8a0b0ec9307b8e64cfe3c6e0f8",
    "entryPoint": "0x0000000071727De22E5E9d8BAf0edAc6f37da032",
    "sender": "0xA43CDA364c524551640206A5A22906dBD989F373",
    "nonce": "0x0",
    "actualGasCost": "0x6b36c187d8a37000",
    "actualGasUsed": "0x4b71f",
    "success": true,
    "logs": [],
    "receipt": { "transactionHash": "0x8232872612eb500033faf8ef605f7c14f4fef556defdbb4d7c67c1731d0b00d3", "blockNumber": "0xa08cc7", "status": "0x1" }
  }
}
```

`success: false` means the call inside the operation reverted (see `reason`) even though the transaction itself succeeded. For a sponsored operation the response includes `paymaster`. The SDK helpers `userOpEventFromReceipt` and `userOpEventsFromReceipt` (from `@pepu-chain/sdk/aa`) decode the `UserOperationEvent` from the transaction receipt.

## pimlico_getUserOperationGasPrice

Alto implements this method; it returns three tiers of fee suggestion. The SDK probe checks for it. Treat it as optional: if a deployment does not answer, read `eth_gasPrice`/fee history from the chain RPC instead.

```json
{ "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": "pimlico_getUserOperationGasPrice", "params": [] }
```

Response shape:

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 1,
  "result": {
    "slow":     { "maxFeePerGas": "0x…", "maxPriorityFeePerGas": "0x…" },
    "standard": { "maxFeePerGas": "0x…", "maxPriorityFeePerGas": "0x…" },
    "fast":     { "maxFeePerGas": "0x…", "maxPriorityFeePerGas": "0x…" }
  }
}
```

Not verified against the PEPU bundler: this shape comes from Alto 0.0.21's source, not a live call.

## Error codes

Errors follow ERC-7769 and use the standard JSON-RPC envelope `{ "error": { "code", "message", "data" } }`. Alto 0.0.21 defines:

| Code | Meaning | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `-32601` | Method not found | You called a method this deployment does not serve (for example a `debug_` method) |
| `-32602` | Invalid fields | A field is missing, mistyped or the wrong width. Check the unpacked v0.7 shape above |
| `-32500` | Rejected in account validation (`validateUserOp`) | The sender or its validator rejected the operation. An `AAxx` code is in the message: `AA21` prefund not paid, `AA23` reverted, `AA25` invalid nonce, `AA33` paymaster reverted |
| `-32501` | Rejected by the paymaster | Sponsorship was refused or the paymaster data is invalid. `AA33`, `AA34` (bad signature) and `AA31` (paymaster deposit too low) all surface here or as `-32508` |
| `-32502` | Opcode validation | Banned opcode or storage access. Only raised with `safe-mode: true` |
| `-32503` | Expires shortly | The paymaster approval (`validUntil`) is about to lapse. Request fresh paymaster data and retry |
| `-32504` | Reputation | A throttled or banned entity |
| `-32505` | Insufficient stake | A staked entity is required |
| `-32506`, `-32507` | Unsupported aggregator, invalid signature | |
| `-32508` | Paymaster deposit too low | Fund the paymaster's EntryPoint deposit |
| `-32521` | Execution reverted | The operation's call failed in simulation |

Failures that are not JSON-RPC errors: an HTTP 500 with a raw message (the safe-mode bug above) and a browser `Failed to fetch` (CORS off, or the endpoint is down). The Privy-side symptom of a bundler error is usually opaque; call the bundler directly with `curl` to see the real message.

## Using the SDK instead

```ts
import { probeBundler } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/aa";
import { createPepuSponsoredClient, sendSponsored } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/aa/kernel";
```

`createPepuSponsoredClient` and `sendSponsored` build the Kernel account, estimate, request paymaster data and send, so you only deal with raw JSON-RPC when debugging. See [/aa](../../sdk/aa.md).

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `AA21 didn't pay prefund` on estimate | Estimated without paymaster fields on a zero-balance sender | Attach stub paymaster fields first, or fund the sender |
| `AA33 reverted` on send | The paymaster rejected the operation: expired `validUntil`, or the bundler executor is not allowlisted (v2) | Re-request paymaster data; for v2 use the PEPU bundler |
| `AA25 invalid account nonce` | A pending operation from the same sender holds the nonce | Wait for the receipt, or use the next nonce |
| `null` receipt forever | The executor is out of PEPU, or the operation was dropped | Check executor balance and the bundler log. See [Operating the Bundler](operating.md) |
| 500 with `0x99410554` | `safe-mode` is on | Turn it off and restart |

## Related

- [Bundler Overview](overview.md)
- [Operating the Bundler](operating.md)
- [ERC-7677 Methods](../paymaster/erc7677.md)
- [Endpoints reference](../../reference/endpoints.md)

pages.title: Operating the Bundler
pages.content:
# Operating the Bundler

Runbook for anyone running the PEPU Alto bundler: locally for development, or as a hosted service. The source is `services/bundler` in the repository. Read [Bundler Overview](overview.md) first for what the service is and why it is configured the way it is.

> Status: **proven**. PEPU runs this bundler as the hosted service at `https://bundler.pepeunchained.com`, and it has carried real mainnet operations, including a sponsored one through the hosted URL. **Built, not run:** `docker-compose.yml` was written from verified image facts but has never been executed (no Docker daemon was available when it was authored). The hosted instance runs behind nginx and pm2 (see the hosting kit in `deploy/`). Treat "Hosting readiness" as the requirements for any hosted deployment, including your own.

## Prerequisites

- Node.js (verified with v24.4.1).
- A PEPU mainnet RPC URL. The Conduit URL embeds an API key, so the whole URL is a secret.
- A **fresh executor key** (an EOA used only by the bundler) with a small PEPU float. Never reuse a deploy key or a key that holds meaningful funds.

## Run it locally

From `services/bundler`:

```bash
cp .env.example .env
# edit .env: set ALTO_RPC_URL and ALTO_EXECUTOR_PRIVATE_KEYS

npm install
npm start          # alto run --config alto.config.json, listens on :4337
```

Confirm it is alive:

```bash
npm run healthcheck
```

or by hand:

```bash
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4337 \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"eth_chainId","params":[]}'
# {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":"0x17dcd"}
```

Alto reads its config **once at startup**; there is no hot reload. After any change to `alto.config.json` or `.env`, restart the process and confirm the new process started after the file changed.

### Configuration files

| File | Contents | Committed |
|---|---|---|
| `alto.config.json` | EntryPoints, chain type, safe mode, CORS, ports and so on. No secrets | Yes |
| `.env` | `ALTO_RPC_URL`, `ALTO_EXECUTOR_PRIVATE_KEYS` | **No**, never |
| `alto.config.unsafe-diagnostic.json` | Same shape on port 4338, for running a second isolated instance to compare behavior | Yes |

Alto's CLI maps every `ALTO_`-prefixed environment variable onto the matching `--kebab-case` flag. That is how the RPC URL and keys reach it without being written into the committed config or passed as arguments (which would leak into process listings). Never put either in `alto.config.json`.

| Variable | What it is |
|---|---|
| `ALTO_RPC_URL` | PEPU mainnet RPC URL (secret: embeds the API key) |
| `ALTO_EXECUTOR_PRIVATE_KEYS` | Comma-separated executor private key(s) (secret) |
| `ALTO_UTILITY_PRIVATE_KEY` | Refills executors below the minimum balance. Deliberately unset; `refilling-wallets` is `false` |
| `ALTO_LOG_LEVEL` | Optional override of `log-level` (default `info`) |

## Docker (built, not run)

`services/bundler/docker-compose.yml` runs `ghcr.io/pimlicolabs/alto:v1.2.8`, mounts `alto.config.json` read-only, reads secrets from `.env`, publishes `4337:4337` and has a Node-based `eth_chainId` health check. Two disclosed caveats:

- The `v1.2.8` image corresponds to `@pimlico/alto@0.0.20`, one release behind the `0.0.21` that the npm path pins. Track the Alto repository for a newer image tag before relying on the container.
- It has never been run. Prove it with `npm run healthcheck` equivalents and a real `scripts/estimate-kernel-userop.mjs --send` before trusting it.

Bind to `127.0.0.1:4337:4337` if the host is internet-facing and you want only the proxy to reach Alto.

## Hosting readiness

What a hosted deployment needs (PEPU publishes `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` as `https://bundler.pepeunchained.com`; use this list for your own):

| Requirement | Detail |
|---|---|
| Containerised service | Docker or compose (or an equivalent platform) with a restart policy, instead of a foreground `npm start`. Prove `docker-compose.yml` first |
| Reverse proxy in front | Fixed hostname, TLS, `Origin` filtering (Alto reflects any origin), rate limiting and request size limits. Alto should not be reachable except through it |
| Fresh executor key, small float | A key created for this service only, funded with a bounded amount and topped up on a schedule. See the next section |
| Secrets management | RPC URL and executor key in a secrets manager or the host's protected environment, never in the repository. Plan key rotation |
| More than one executor | Production should use several executor keys so one in-flight bundle does not block the next. Only one exists today |
| Monitoring and alerting | Alert on health-check failure, executor balance, process exit and error rate. Ship the JSON logs somewhere searchable |
| Stable URL | Tunnels change URL on restart and break every Privy Dashboard that has the old URL pasted in |
| Safe-mode decision | Off because of the Alto 0.0.21 bug. Re-test on each Alto release. Do not expose the RPC to untrusted submitters while off without the proxy controls above |

## Executor funding

- The executor EOA signs and submits every `handleOps` transaction and pays gas up front, then is reimbursed per operation from each payer's EntryPoint deposit (the sender's own, or the paymaster's).
- **If it runs dry, `eth_sendUserOperation` is still accepted but bundles never land.** Estimation does not need executor funds, so the bundler keeps looking healthy to clients. This is the most common silent failure.
- Real operations observed on mainnet cost 3 to 8 PEPU in gas each. Keep the float small on purpose (it is a hot key) but large enough for hours of runway.
- Top up with any normal PEPU transfer to the executor address, or `node scripts/fund-address.mjs`.
- A smart account that sends **without** a paymaster must hold enough PEPU to pay its own prefund. That is a per-account concern, not something the bundler can fix.

## Monitoring

`npm run healthcheck` (`scripts/healthcheck.js`) runs four independent checks and exits `0` if all pass, `1` otherwise:

1. **Bundler responding**: `eth_chainId` against the bundler's port, and it must be `0x17dcd`.
2. **Chain RPC reachable**: `eth_blockNumber` straight against `ALTO_RPC_URL`, so an RPC outage can be told apart from a bundler outage.
3. **EntryPoints reachable**: `eth_supportedEntryPoints` must list both v0.6 and v0.7.
4. **Executor funded**: every executor address derived from `ALTO_EXECUTOR_PRIVATE_KEYS` must hold at least `ALTO_HEALTHCHECK_MIN_EXECUTOR_BALANCE_PEPU` (default 500). Only the address is ever printed.

Wire it into the supervisor, a container health check or an uptime checker. Alert on:

- Any health-check failure, especially executor balance.
- Alto process exit.
- A sustained rise in `eth_sendUserOperation` errors, especially the `0x99410554` signature (it means safe mode was switched back on).

Client-side, `probeBundler` (SDK) and `pepu_bundler_health` (MCP) give an external view without needing server access.

When the bundler is down, every UserOperation flow stops: nothing can be estimated or submitted. Receiving funds and reading balances still work, because they go straight to the chain RPC.

## Verify a change

1. Restart the process.
2. `npm run healthcheck`.
3. `node scripts/estimate-kernel-userop.mjs` confirms gas estimation.
4. `node scripts/estimate-kernel-userop.mjs --send` confirms a real operation lands. It costs a few PEPU of real gas and is the only proof that sending works: estimation succeeding is not enough (that is how the safe-mode bug hid).

## Known gaps

- Single executor key, no utility wallet (refilling is off).
- `safe-mode: false` as a tracked workaround for the Alto 0.0.21 bug.
- `docker-compose.yml` unexecuted, and its image is one Alto release behind the npm package.
- `arbitrum-base-fee-multiplier` (150) and `block-time` (5000 ms) are reasonable defaults, not load-tested against PEPU.
- No rate limiting or origin allowlist at the Alto layer.
- This service never sponsors gas. Do not describe it as gasless.

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Healthcheck: executor below threshold | Float is low | Top up the executor address |
| Healthcheck: wrong chain | `ALTO_RPC_URL` points at another network | Use the mainnet RPC |
| 500 with `0x99410554` | Safe mode on | Set `safe-mode` to `false` and restart |
| Browser `Failed to fetch` | CORS off, or an old process is still serving the port | Enable CORS, restart, verify the new process is the one listening |
| Config edit ignored | Alto does not hot reload | Restart |

## Related

- [Bundler Overview](overview.md)
- [Bundler JSON-RPC API](api.md)
- [Paymaster Overview](../paymaster/overview.md)
- [Infrastructure Map](../overview.md)

pages.title: Bundler Overview
pages.content:
# Bundler Overview

The PEPU bundler is an ERC-4337 bundler for Pepe Unchained V2 mainnet (chain ID `97741`), hosted by PEPU at `https://bundler.pepeunchained.com` and also runnable on your own machine. It runs Pimlico's open-source [Alto](https://github.com/pimlicolabs/alto) (`@pimlico/alto@0.0.21`) and takes UserOperations from Kernel smart accounts, wraps them into `handleOps` transactions and submits them to the chain. Read this page to know what the bundler does, which EntryPoints it supports, how it is configured and what its limits are.

> Status: **proven**. The hosted bundler at `https://bundler.pepeunchained.com` (the SDK default for `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL`) carried a real sponsored operation on mainnet: a fresh Kernel account holding 0 PEPU, paid for by the v2 canary paymaster, with the bundler and paymaster both reached through their hosted URLs. Earlier UserOperations landed on 2026-09-24 from a development machine. Running your own bundler remains possible (see [Operating the Bundler](operating.md)); point your app at `http://localhost:4337` or your own URL.

## What it does

- Accepts the ERC-4337 JSON-RPC methods an app needs: estimate gas, send, look up by hash, get the receipt. See [Bundler JSON-RPC API](api.md).
- Simulates each UserOperation against the real EntryPoint, then bundles accepted operations and submits them from one **executor** EOA.
- The executor fronts gas for the whole bundle and is reimbursed by each operation's payer out of its EntryPoint deposit: the sender's own deposit, or the [paymaster](../paymaster/overview.md)'s when the operation is sponsored.
- **It is a bundler, not gas sponsorship.** On its own it never pays gas for anyone. Sponsorship comes from the paymaster contract and its policy service.

## What it is not

- It does not gossip to a public mempool. It receives operations directly from your app or from Privy's smart-wallet client.
- It does not hold user funds. The only key it holds is the executor key, which should carry a small float (see [Operating the Bundler](operating.md)).

## EntryPoints and chain type

| Setting | Value | Why |
|---|---|---|
| EntryPoint v0.7 | `0x0000000071727De22E5E9d8BAf0edAc6f37da032` | The version Kernel v3.x, the PEPU paymaster and Privy's smart-wallet integration target. Every verification used v0.7. |
| EntryPoint v0.6 | `0x5FF137D4b0FDCD49DcA30c7CF57E578a026d2789` | Also served. Deployed on mainnet. |
| Chain type | `arbitrum` | PEPU is an Arbitrum Orbit (Nitro) chain. This makes Alto price UserOperations for Nitro's two-part fee: L2 execution gas plus a separate L1 data fee. Do not remove it. |
| `arbitrum-base-fee-multiplier` | `150` (a 1.5x safety margin on the L2 base fee) | Starting default, not load-tested against PEPU fee swings. |
| Chain ID | `97741` (`0x17dcd`) | Mainnet only. |
| Multicall3 | `0x9CE19273Ae9c24437DFF512E8DFCAed4E4B001bd` | PEPU's own deployment, used by Alto for batched reads during simulation. See [The Multicall3 Trap](../../contracts/multicall3.md). |
| CREATE2 deployer | `0x4e59b44847b379578588920ca78fbf26c0b4956c` | Alto uses it to deploy its own simulation contracts the first time it runs against a chain (`deploy-simulations-contract: true`). |

A live read-only call against a running local bundler on 2026-10-03 returned both EntryPoints from `eth_supportedEntryPoints` and `0x17dcd` from `eth_chainId` (full responses in [Bundler JSON-RPC API](api.md)).

## Safe mode is off (known Alto 0.0.21 bug)

`safe-mode` is `false` in the committed configuration. With it on, `eth_sendUserOperation` fails for every operation, valid or not, with an HTTP 500 and the error `Encoded error signature "0x99410554" not found on ABI`. The selector is EntryPoint v0.7's own `DelegateAndRevert(bool,bytes)` error. Alto's Node-side decoder for its simulation contract has no error definitions in its ABI, so it throws on the wrapper that every simulation returns. This was traced to the exact code in the installed version, reproduced, and confirmed still present on Alto's `main` branch on 2026-09-24. `0.0.21` is the latest npm release, so there is nothing newer to upgrade to.

What safe mode off means:

- Alto still validates signature, nonce, prefund and gas. What is skipped is the ERC-7562 storage-access and opcode tracer, which protects a **shared public mempool** from operations crafted to behave differently at inclusion time.
- That is acceptable only with the controls around it. It matters more now that the RPC is public, which is why the hosted deployment sits behind a reverse proxy (see below and [Operating the Bundler](operating.md)).
- The v2 paymaster contract depends on this setting: it gates payment on `tx.origin` being an allowlisted bundler, and `ORIGIN` is banned under ERC-7562, so a conformant public-mempool bundler would reject its operations. See [Paymaster v2 Spec Summary](../../contracts/paymaster-v2-spec.md).
- Re-test and re-enable safe mode when Alto publishes a release past `0.0.21`.

## The paymaster bundler allowlist

The v2 paymaster only pays out to allowlisted bundler executor addresses. A third-party bundler would see operations that pass simulation but fail at inclusion. In practice: sponsored operations must go through the PEPU bundler (or one whose executor has been added to the paymaster's allowlist). v1 does not have this restriction. See [PepuSponsoredPaymasterV7 Contract](../paymaster/contracts.md).

## CORS and the proxy policy

Browsers call the bundler directly (Privy's smart-wallet client sends `eth_estimateUserOperationGas` from the user's browser), so CORS has to work.

- `enable-cors` is `true`. In Alto 0.0.21 that is a boolean that **reflects any `Origin`** and answers `OPTIONS` preflights; it cannot be turned into an allowlist.
- CORS is not an access boundary. A script or `curl` can call the endpoint regardless. What actually gates cost is EntryPoint validation (signature, nonce, prefund) and, for sponsored operations, the paymaster's policy.
- For a hosted deployment, put a reverse proxy in front that terminates TLS and rate-limits; the PEPU-hosted endpoint is served through one. Plan for the endpoint URL to be treated as semi-public.

## Rate limits

Alto has no built-in per-client limits. Any limits on the hosted endpoint are applied at the proxy and are not a contract; do not hammer the endpoint.

## Health probe

Use the SDK probe or the MCP tool rather than hand-rolled calls:

```ts
import { probeBundler } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/aa";

const result = await probeBundler(process.env.PEPU_BUNDLER_URL ?? "http://localhost:4337");
console.log(result.ok, result.chainId, result.entryPoints, result.supportedMethods);
```

`probeBundler` calls `eth_chainId`, `eth_supportedEntryPoints` and a capability check for `eth_sendUserOperation`, `eth_estimateUserOperationGas`, `eth_getUserOperationReceipt`, `eth_getUserOperationByHash`, `pimlico_getUserOperationGasPrice` and `zd_getUserOperationGasPrice`. A method counts as supported if it answers with anything other than "method not found". Nothing is sent on chain. `ok` is true only when the chain ID is `97741` and EntryPoint v0.7 is listed. It never throws for network trouble; it returns `ok: false` with a `BUNDLER_UNREACHABLE` error. The MCP equivalent is the `pepu_bundler_health` tool, and `pepu_sponsorship_status` checks bundler and paymaster together.

## Configuration summary

The committed file is `services/bundler/alto.config.json`; secrets live only in `.env`.

| Key | Value |
|---|---|
| `entrypoints` | v0.7 and v0.6 |
| `chain-type` | `arbitrum` |
| `safe-mode` | `false` (see above) |
| `enable-cors` | `true` (reflect any origin) |
| `enable-debug-endpoints` | `false` (the `debug_bundler_*` methods are not served) |
| `dangerous-skip-user-operation-validation` | `false` |
| `legacy-transactions` | `false` (EIP-1559) |
| `is-gas-free-chain` | `false` |
| `eip-7702-support` | `true` (enabled, not exercised) |
| `refilling-wallets` | `false` (no utility wallet yet) |
| `port` | `4337` |
| `block-time` | `5000` ms |

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `eth_sendUserOperation` returns HTTP 500 mentioning `0x99410554` | `safe-mode` is on | Set `safe-mode` to `false` and restart. Alto reads its config once at startup. |
| Browser shows `Failed to fetch` on the first call, `curl` works | CORS disabled, so the `OPTIONS` preflight got a 404 | Set `enable-cors` to `true` and restart. |
| Estimation works, sending never lands | The executor EOA has no PEPU. Estimation does not need funds, sending does | Top up the executor. See [Operating the Bundler](operating.md). |
| `probeBundler` returns `ok: false` with the wrong chain | The URL points at a different network | Use a mainnet (`97741`) bundler. |
| Config change has no effect | Alto does not hot reload | Restart the process. |

## Related

- [Bundler JSON-RPC API](api.md)
- [Operating the Bundler](operating.md)
- [Paymaster Overview](../paymaster/overview.md)
- [Infrastructure Map](../overview.md)
- [Smart Accounts](../../onboarding/smart-accounts.md)

pages.title: Infrastructure Map
pages.content:
# Infrastructure Map

One page listing every endpoint and address the PEPU dev kit relies on: bundler, paymaster, EntryPoints, Kernel, Multicall3, Permit2 and the CREATE2 deployer, with hosting status. Start here to find the right detail page. For the call flow between these pieces see [Architecture: Who Calls What](../concepts/architecture.md).

> Status: contracts are **verified live** on mainnet (`pnpm --filter @pepu-chain/sdk live-check`, 2026-10-14). The hosted bundler and paymaster service are **live** and **proven**: a fresh Kernel account holding 0 PEPU sent a project-sponsored operation through both. The v2 paymaster is deployed as a canary: internally reviewed 3x, external audit pending, funded in small tranches. Running your own bundler or policy service remains possible.

## Endpoints

| Service | Variable | Hosted URL | Local default | Detail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Bundler (Alto, ERC-4337 v0.7) | `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` (browser: `NEXT_PUBLIC_PEPU_BUNDLER_URL`) | `https://bundler.pepeunchained.com` (SDK default) | `http://localhost:4337` | [Bundler Overview](bundler/overview.md), [API](bundler/api.md), [Operating](bundler/operating.md) |
| Paymaster policy service | `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` (browser: `NEXT_PUBLIC_PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL`) | Base `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com` (SDK default). The ERC-7677 URL always embeds a token: `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<token>`, so there is no tokenless default | `http://localhost:8788` | [Paymaster Overview](paymaster/overview.md) |
| RPC | `PEPU_RPC_URL` | `https://rpc-pepu-v2-mainnet-0.t.conduit.xyz` | | [Network Reference](../get-started/network-reference.md) |

The SDK resolves these in `src/endpoints.ts` (`resolvePepuEndpoints()`): explicit option, then env, then the hosted default (`PEPU_HOSTED`: `bundlerUrl`, `paymasterBaseUrl`, and `paymasterUrl: null` because the ERC-7677 URL needs a token). `isHostedSponsorshipLive()` returns true. Build the token URL with `hostedErc7677Url(token)` (`@pepu-chain/sdk/paymaster`). The `/v2` routes of the service are public (free-tier, config, SIWE login, project verify); `/v2/admin` is not exposed. Health checks: `probeBundler` and `probePaymaster` (`@pepu-chain/sdk/aa`), or the MCP tools `pepu_bundler_health`, `pepu_paymaster_health` and `pepu_sponsorship_status`. Complete list: [Endpoints](../reference/endpoints.md).

## Addresses (mainnet 97741, each verified with `eth_getCode` on 2026-10-14)

| Name | Address | Hosting and status |
|---|---|---|
| EntryPoint v0.7 | `0x0000000071727De22E5E9d8BAf0edAc6f37da032` | Deployed |
| EntryPoint v0.6 | `0x5FF137D4b0FDCD49DcA30c7CF57E578a026d2789` | Deployed |
| Kernel v3 factory | `0xaac5D4240AF87249B3f71BC8E4A2cae074A3E419` | Deployed |
| Kernel MetaFactory | `0xd703aaE79538628d27099B8c4f621bE4CCd142d5` | Deployed |
| Kernel v3.1 implementation | `0xbAC849bB641841b44E965fb01A4Bf5F074F84B4d` | Deployed |
| Kernel ECDSA validator | `0x845ADb2C711129d4f3966735eD98a9F09fC4cE57` | Deployed |
| Kernel ECDSA signer module | `0x6A6F069E2a08c2468e7724Ab3250CdBFBA14D4FF` | Deployed |
| Call policy v0.0.4 | `0x9a52283276A0ec8740DF50bF01B28A80D880eaf2` | Deployed (v0.0.5 is not) |
| Timestamp policy | `0xB9f8f524bE6EcD8C945b1b87f9ae5C192FdCE20F` | Deployed |
| Multicall3 (PEPU-specific) | `0x9CE19273Ae9c24437DFF512E8DFCAed4E4B001bd` | Deployed. Canonical address has no code |
| Permit2 (canonical) | `0x000000000022D473030F116dDEE9F6B43aC78BA3` | Deployed |
| CREATE2 deployer | `0x4e59b44847b379578588920cA78FbF26c0B4956C` | Deployed |
| Paymaster v2 (`paymaster`, `paymasterV2`) | `0xdb28528C9399C33c9A0297E8A62F39145acbC30D` | Deployed as a canary: internally reviewed 3x, external audit pending, funded in small tranches |
| Paymaster v1 | `0x2B6FED323bFA24f0475f4e1Dd3C7F6Cc1f3ae8B0` | Retired: deposit withdrawn (0), cannot sponsor. Never deposit |
| TapScore (demo) | `0x261eA5971B93237a56990206A46Bc80318e4d078` | Deployed |

Notes and sources for each are in the [Address Map](../contracts/address-map.md).

## Proven versus pending

| Capability | State |
|---|---|
| Google to wallet (Privy embedded wallet) | Proven on mainnet |
| Session keys (Privy session signers and on-chain Kernel session key) | Proven on mainnet |
| Sponsored transactions (v2 canary paymaster plus the hosted Alto bundler) | Proven on mainnet |
| All three combined | Proven live in a browser on mainnet (2026-10-14) against the hosted bundler and v2 paymaster |
| Hosted bundler and paymaster URLs | Proven |
| v2 tiered paymaster | Proven on mainnet (canary, external audit pending) |
| Rate limits and origin allowlist on the bundler | **Pending** (planned at a proxy) |

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `CONFIG_MISSING_ENV` for a bundler or paymaster URL | `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` unset and the call needs the complete ERC-7677 URL, which always embeds a token (there is no tokenless default) | Set `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` to `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<token>`, or pass `paymasterToken`. The bundler defaults to the hosted URL |
| Batched reads fail | Tooling uses the canonical Multicall3 address | Use the PEPU address |
| Policy-service call works locally, fails for others | You pointed at `http://localhost:8788` | Use `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com` |

## Related

- [Architecture: Who Calls What](../concepts/architecture.md)
- [Address Map](../contracts/address-map.md)
- [Bundler Overview](bundler/overview.md)
- [Paymaster Overview](paymaster/overview.md)
- [Sponsored Transactions](../onboarding/sponsored-transactions.md)

pages.title: Paymaster Credential Matrix
pages.content:
# Paymaster Credential Matrix

Which credential applies to which paymaster call, how to obtain it, and how to rotate it. Read this before putting any key or URL into a browser, a Privy Dashboard field or a backend.

> Status: **v2 credentials proven on mainnet** (canary, external audit pending): a project server key (`ppk_`) in the ERC-7677 URL sponsored a real operation through `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com`. **v1 credentials are history**; the v1 paymaster is retired. The ERC-7677 URL always embeds a token (`https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<token>`); there is no tokenless default. A client token (`ppt_`) works only from the project's allowed origins and is refused with `project_origin_not_allowed` when none are set. The free tier needs a verified Privy access token from PEPU's own Privy app (`context.privyAccessToken`, REST `Authorization: Bearer`); a third-party app's own Privy token is ignored for billing.

## Credential types

| Credential | Format | Who holds it | Browser-safe |
|---|---|---|---|
| Privy access token | JWT from Privy | The signed-in user | Yes |
| v1 app key | Raw key; the service stores only `sha256(key)` in `config/apps.json` | The operator and the app | The URL embedding it is a secret |
| Server key | `ppk_...`, secret | A project's backend | **No** |
| Client token | `ppt_...`, publishable | A project's frontend or Privy Dashboard | Yes, spends only from allowed origins |
| SIWE session | Opaque bearer, 1 hour | A project owner's browser | Yes |
| Admin token | `ADMIN_TOKEN` (v1), `SPONSORSHIP_ADMIN_TOKEN` (v2, 32 or more characters) | PEPU operators | **No** |
| Privy app secret | From the Privy dashboard | The developer | **No**, one call only |

`credentialKind(credential)` from `@pepu-chain/sdk/paymaster` tells `"client"` from `"server"` by prefix and never inspects more.

## Matrix by call path

| Call | v1 | v2 |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /health` | none | none |
| `GET /v2/config`, `/v2/contract`, `/v2/free-tier` | n/a | none |
| `POST /sponsor` | Privy token (`Authorization: Bearer`) **and** app key (`X-Api-Key`) | n/a |
| `POST /v2/sponsor` | n/a | `X-Api-Key` server key (any wallet) or client token (allowed `Origin`); Privy token required for the free tier |
| `pm_getPaymasterStubData` | none: the URL credential is not resolved (spec-compliant) | none: URL token only picks the sponsor id for the stub |
| `pm_getPaymasterData` | app key in the URL | `ppt_` or `ppk_` in the URL; `context.privyAccessToken` for the free tier |
| `/v2/auth/nonce`, `/v2/auth/login` | n/a | none (login is a SIWE signature) |
| `/v2/me`, `/v2/auth/logout` | n/a | SIWE session |
| `POST /v2/projects/verify` | n/a | SIWE session for `ownerAddress` plus the Privy app secret in the body |
| `POST /v2/projects/prepare` | n/a | SIWE session |
| `POST/GET /v2/projects...`, rotation, settings, usage, events, allowlist | n/a | SIWE session whose address is the **current on-chain owner** |
| `POST /admin/circuit-breaker/reset` | `X-Admin-Token` | n/a |
| `/v2/admin/*` | n/a | `X-Admin-Token`; 404 if unset, and not exposed on the hosted host (404) |

What each unlocks on the sponsorship path:

| Credential | Sponsors | Free tier | Origin check | On a leak |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Server key `ppk_` | Any wallet, from the project's budget | No (needs a Privy token) | None | Rotate at once; bounded by the project's on-chain limits |
| Client token `ppt_` | Any wallet, only from `allowedOrigins` | With a Privy token | Yes; none configured means it cannot spend the project | Rotate; spend limited to the project's allowlist and daily limits |
| v1 app key | Registered app's budget | n/a | Optional `PAYMASTER_RPC_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` (speed bump) | Operator rotates; anyone with the URL can request sponsorship under the app's caps |

## How to obtain each

| Credential | How |
|---|---|
| Privy access token | From the signed-in Privy session, for example `getAccessToken()` in the Privy client |
| v1 app key | An operator generates a raw key, runs `npm run hash-api-key -- <key>` in the policy service and stores the hash in `config/apps.json`. There is no self-serve path in v1 |
| SIWE session | `api.v2.loginWithWallet(sign, { address, domain })`, or nonce then login by hand |
| Attestation | `requestClaimAttestation` from `@pepu-chain/sdk/paymaster/server` (server or CLI only) |
| Server key and client token | `POST /v2/projects` on a claimed project (`api.v2.projects.register`), **shown once** |
| Admin token | Set in the service environment by the operator |

## Rotation

| Credential | Rotate with | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Client token | `POST /v2/projects/{id}/token/rotate` (`rotateClientToken`) | Old token stops immediately. Update the URL in the Privy Dashboard and any frontend |
| Server key | `POST /v2/projects/{id}/server-key/rotate` (`rotateServerKey`) | Old key stops immediately |
| Both, on ownership change | Automatic revocation when the on-chain owner changes (denial `project_owner_changed`) | The new owner rotates to get fresh ones |
| Lost token | `POST /v2/admin/projects/{key}/token/rotate` (admin) | Recovery |
| Suspend | `POST /v2/admin/projects/{key}/status` | Kill switch; does not touch funds |
| v1 app key | Operator replaces the hash in `apps.json` and restarts | Old URL dies |
| Privy app secret | Rotate in the Privy dashboard after verifying | The service never stored it |

## Rules

- A `ppk_` key never goes into a browser, a `NEXT_PUBLIC_` variable or a Privy Dashboard field. `buildErc7677Url` throws `CONFIG_SERVER_ONLY` for a server key in a browser.
- Origin binding is a browser guard: non-browser clients can forge `Origin`. The contract's limits are the real backstop.
- Never log or commit any of these. Only `sha256(rawKey)` goes in `apps.json`.

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `unknown_or_invalid_app_credential` | Rotated, mistyped or wrong environment | Re-copy the credential, check which service it belongs to |
| `project_origin_not_allowed` | Client token used from an unlisted origin | Add the origin with `PATCH /v2/projects/{id}/settings` |
| `free_tier_identity_required` | No Privy token with a free-tier request | Pass `Authorization: Bearer` or `context.privyAccessToken` |
| `403` on an owner route | Session address is not the on-chain owner | Sign in with the owner wallet |
| Pasted URL stopped working | The token was rotated, or a tunnel URL changed | Re-issue and update the Dashboard |

## Related

- [Paymaster Overview](overview.md)
- [REST API v1](rest-api-v1.md), [REST API v2](rest-api-v2.md)
- [ERC-7677 Methods](erc7677.md)
- [Privy Dashboard Settings](../../privy/dashboard-settings.md)

pages.title: PepuSponsoredPaymasterV7 Contract
pages.content:
# PepuSponsoredPaymasterV7 Contract

Reference for the paymaster contracts: v2 `PepuSponsoredPaymasterV7` (deployed as a canary) and v1 `PepuVerifyingPaymasterV7` (retired): functions, events, errors, roles and timelocks. Names come from the SDK's `pepuSponsoredPaymasterV2Abi` and the spec; the contract source is `services/paymaster/contracts/src`.

> Status: **v2 proven on mainnet (canary, external audit pending)** at `0xdb28528C9399C33c9A0297E8A62F39145acbC30D` (about block 10537341, verified with `eth_getCode` on 2026-10-14 through `pnpm --filter @pepu-chain/sdk live-check`): internally reviewed 3x, funded in small tranches. 195 Foundry tests (including a harness on the real EntryPoint v0.7 sources and fuzz and invariant suites), three internal reviews, no external audit. Owner `0x5966…4A1`, manager `0x063A…aBb0`; the free pool was seeded with 300 PEPU. **v1 is retired** at `0x2B6FED323bFA24f0475f4e1Dd3C7F6Cc1f3ae8B0`: its EntryPoint deposit was withdrawn (0), so it cannot sponsor anything. Never deposit to it.

## v1: PepuVerifyingPaymasterV7

A fork of Pimlico's singleton verifying paymaster with ERC-20 mode removed. Its job is narrow: check that `paymasterAndData` carries a valid ECDSA signature from an authorised signer over an approved time window, then pay gas from its EntryPoint deposit.

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Address | `0x2B6FED323bFA24f0475f4e1Dd3C7F6Cc1f3ae8B0` (retired) |
| Stake and deposit | History: it was staked (100 PEPU) and funded, and the EntryPoint deposit has since been withdrawn (0). Retired |
| Signed prefix | `paymaster(20) ‖ verificationGasLimit(16) ‖ postOpGasLimit(16) ‖ mode(1)=0x00 ‖ validUntil(6) ‖ validAfter(6)`, then the 65-byte signature |
| Hash | keccak of sender, nonce, account gas limits, preVerificationGas, gas fees, hashes of initCode, callData and the prefix, then with `chainid`, EIP-191 signed. A frozen cross-language test vector pins both sides |
| Signers | Multi-signer (`MultiSigner`): a manager can add or remove signers without a redeploy |
| Caps | **None on chain.** Every economic safeguard is in the policy service |
| Bundler gate | Not enforced |

The main risk is signer-key compromise: any signature from an authorised signer is honoured up to the deposit. The mitigation is keeping the float small and rotating signers. See [Policy, Caps and the Circuit Breaker](policy-and-caps.md).

## v2: PepuSponsoredPaymasterV7

One contract that is both paymaster and vault. All PEPU sits in its EntryPoint deposit; an internal ledger records which sponsor owns what, with `totalLiabilities` equal to the sum of ledgers and `totalLiabilities` at most the EntryPoint balance. Deployed at `0xdb28528C9399C33c9A0297E8A62F39145acbC30D` as a canary (external audit pending).

### How it validates

`paymasterData` is `mode(1)=0x02 ‖ validUntil(6) ‖ validAfter(6) ‖ sponsorId(32) ‖ signature(65)` (97 bytes signed, `sponsorId` inside the hash). `sponsorId` is `0x00..00` for the free pool or `keccak256(bytes(appId))` for a project. Validation, in order:

1. Caller is the EntryPoint. The mode byte must be exactly `0x02`, and the **bundler gate is unconditional**: `tx.origin` must be an allowlisted bundler (`address(0)` is allowlisted so estimation works).
2. Signature exactly 65 bytes, low-s, from an authorised signer, otherwise `SIG_VALIDATION_FAILED` with no state change (so stubs never revert or charge).
3. `validUntil` non-zero; paymaster post-op gas limit at least 40,000; the op's `maxFeePerGas` at most the sponsor's cap.
4. The sponsor must be claimed and not paused; for the free pool, enabled and under `freeMaxOpCost`. A **project must also have a non-zero per-wallet daily limit** (`ZeroDailyLimit` otherwise); only the free pool may run with 0 = off.
5. Every Kernel `execute` target (single `0x00` or batch `0x01`) must be on the sponsor's allowlist. Empty means nothing.
6. Daily limit (projects) and per-wallet daily limit, keyed on the signed `validAfter` day.
7. The sponsor's balance covers `maxCost`. The full `maxCost` is deducted; `postOp` refunds `maxCost - charge` to the **same** sponsor. `charge` includes a post-op overhead (20,000 gas at deploy, floor 18,000) plus the worst case of the EntryPoint's 10% unused-gas penalty, so the ledger can never be short. Both are **snapshotted into the context at validation**, so `postOp` makes no cold storage read of the overhead and an owner changing it mid-flight cannot change an in-flight op's charge (worst-case postOp 13,918 gas against the 18,000 floor).

Because the gate uses `ORIGIN`, which ERC-7562 bans, v2 is supported only behind a self-run bundler with safe mode off whose executor is allowlisted. See [Bundler Overview](../bundler/overview.md).

### Functions

| Group | Functions | Who |
|---|---|---|
| ERC-4337 | `validatePaymasterUserOp`, `postOp`, `getHash` | EntryPoint (hash view for anyone) |
| Deposits (one-way) | `depositFor(projectId)`, `fundFreePool()`, `creditSurplusToFreePool()` | **Anyone** |
| Claims | `claimProject(Claim)`, `reclaimProject(Claim)`, `executeReclaim`, `cancelReclaim`, views `claimDigest`, `domainSeparator`, `claimUsed`, `signerRemovedAt`, `pendingReclaim`, `vetoedReclaimant`, `PENDING_EXPIRY` | Claim: anyone with a signer attestation. Execute: anyone after the delay and within 30 days. Cancel: the current project owner, **once per new owner**; for a pending **first claim** of a funded, unowned project, the contract owner or manager |
| Project settings | `setTargets`, `setDailyLimit`, `setSenderDailyLimit`, `setMaxFeePerGas`, `setRequiredAccountCodehash`, `setPaused`, `proposeProjectOwner`, `acceptProjectOwnership` | The project's own owner only |
| Free pool | `setFreeTier`, `setFreeMaxFeePerGas` (owner); `pauseFreePool`, `setFreeTargets` (owner or manager) | Owner, manager |
| Governance | `proposeAdminChange`, `executeAdminChange`, `cancelAdminChange` (kind 1 signer, 2 bundler; `address(0)` allowed as a bundler only), `removeSigner`, `removeBundlers`, `setManager`, `setPostOpOverheadGas` (can only lower), `addStake` (delay at most 30 days), `unlockStake`, `withdrawStake` (stake only) | Owner, manager (stake functions and `setManager`, `setPostOpOverheadGas` are owner only) |
| Ownership | OpenZeppelin `Ownable2Step`: `transferOwnership`, `acceptOwnership`, `renounceOwnership` | Owner |
| Views | `getProject`, `getSenderSpend`, `isTargetAllowed`, `projectIdOf`, `effectiveMaxFeePerGas`, `requiredAccountCodehash`, `pendingAdminChange`, `surplus`, `totalLiabilities`, `adminChangeDelay`, `defaultMaxFeePerGas`, `postOpOverheadGas`, `maxPostOpOverheadGas`, `freeEnabled`, `freeMaxOpCost`, `manager`, `entryPoint`, `signers`, `isBundlerAllowed` | Anyone |

There is no `receive()` or plain `deposit()`, and **no withdrawal function of any kind** for ledger funds. The contract never calls `entryPoint.withdrawTo` (a test scans the bytecode for that selector). `withdrawStake` moves only the separate EntryPoint stake balance. `claimProject` sets only the owner, so the owner follows with `setTargets`, `setDailyLimit` and `setSenderDailyLimit`. A claim of a project with **no deposited funds is immediate**; the claim of a project that **already holds funds is pending** for `adminChangeDelay` (event `ProjectClaimProposed`), signer-bound, cancellable by the contract owner or manager, and finished by anyone with `executeReclaim`. `setMaxFeePerGas` and `setFreeMaxFeePerGas` cannot exceed `defaultMaxFeePerGas`; `setFreeTier` rejects a non-zero per-wallet limit below the per-op cap (`InvalidFreeTierConfig`); `proposeProjectOwner(id, address(0))` withdraws a nomination.

### Events
