Paste `paymasterUrl` into Privy's "Paymaster URL" field if you use Privy Smart Wallets. Put the server key only in your backend. Without `allowedOrigins`, the client token cannot spend the project at all (`project_origin_not_allowed`). If Privy calls the URL from its own servers and that error appears, use the server key in the dashboard URL and keep it secret. Check state any time with `api.v2.projects.get(projectId)` and `readProject`.

## 7. Plug the credential into your app and check it

| Template | Credential | Where it goes |
|---|---|---|
| `sponsored-session-app` (and any server or bot using `/combo` or `createPepuSponsoredClient`) | The server key (`ppk_`) | `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL=https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<server key>` in `.env.local`, server only. Leave `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` as `https://bundler.pepeunchained.com` |
| `sponsored-demo` (Privy Smart Wallets) | The client token (`ppt_`) | The `paymasterUrl` from step 6 in the Privy dashboard, Smart Wallets, chain 97741. Allowed origins must include your app's origin |
| A browser using `useDirectSponsoredSend` | The client token (`ppt_`) | `NEXT_PUBLIC_PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL`, with allowed origins set |

Restart the dev server, then check:

```ts
// Check that a paymaster project is ready to sponsor: reachable services, claimed, limits set, funded.
// Read-only: sends nothing and needs no secrets. See docs/infra/paymaster/v2-register-deposit-claim.md
import { checkSponsorship, getPublicClient, pepuMainnet } from "@pepu-chain/sdk";
import { computeProjectId, readProject } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/paymaster";

export async function verifyProject(appId: string) {
  const publicClient = getPublicClient(pepuMainnet);
  const report = await checkSponsorship({ publicClient });
  if (!report.available) console.log(report.reason, report.fixes);

  const state = await readProject(publicClient, computeProjectId(appId));
  console.log(state.claimed, state.limitsConfigured, state.balance); // true, true, a positive balance
  return { available: report.available, ready: state.claimed && state.limitsConfigured && state.balance > 0n };
}
```

Success looks like `claimed: true`, `limitsConfigured: true` and a positive `balance`. Then a first sponsored transaction from a fresh account holding 0 PEPU goes through: the result's `paymaster` field is the v2 contract, and your project's balance drops by the gas it paid.

## Do it with an AI agent (MCP)

The MCP server (`@pepu-chain/mcp`) never signs and never sees your Privy secret. It does the parts that are pure encoding or reading, and tells you which steps still need your wallet or your script.

1. Ask: "Using the pepu MCP tools, walk me through claiming and funding a paymaster project for Privy app `<app id>`." The agent follows the `pepu-paymaster-projects` skill.
2. `pepu_project_balance` with your `appId` shows whether the project exists, who owns it and its balance. A zero-address owner means unclaimed.
3. Run the SIWE login and the attestation (steps 2 and 3) with the recipe script: they need your wallet and your Privy secret. The agent can write and set up the script from `pepu_sdk_snippet` (`v2-deposit-and-claim`), but you export the secrets.
4. `pepu_prepare_project_tx` with `action: "claim"` and the attestation, then `"configure"` (targets, `dailyLimitPepu`, `senderDailyLimitPepu`), then `"deposit"` (`amountPepu`) returns an unsigned `{ to, data, value }` for each. You send them from the owner wallet. The tool sends nothing.
5. Register (step 6) with the script, save the keys, then ask the agent to run `pepu_sponsorship_status` and `pepu_project_balance` for the final check.

## Rotation and the re-claim timelock

| Action | How | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Rotate the client token | `api.v2.projects.rotateClientToken(projectId)` | Old token stops immediately; update the Dashboard URL |
| Rotate the server key | `api.v2.projects.rotateServerKey(projectId)` | Old key stops immediately |
| Change origins, per-user cap, `requireIdentity` | `api.v2.projects.updateSettings(projectId, ...)` | Off-chain settings |
| Lost the owner wallet | Repeat steps 3 and 4 from a new wallet: the result is `reclaimProject` | **Timelocked at least 48 hours**, announced by `ProjectReclaimProposed`, cancellable by the current owner (`encodeCancelReclaim`) **once per new owner** (a second attested re-claim by the same wallet cannot be cancelled), finished by anyone with `encodeExecuteReclaim`; lapses 30 days after it becomes executable |
| Hand over to a multisig | `encodeProposeProjectOwner`, then the new owner calls `encodeAcceptProjectOwnership` | Voluntary two-step transfer; clears any pending re-claim that the owner has not already vetoed once. A nomination can be withdrawn by proposing the zero address (prepare API) |
| Owner changed | Automatic | The previous owner's credentials are revoked (`project_owner_changed`); the new owner rotates |

Watch `ProjectReclaimProposed` (and the contract's `AdminChangeProposed`) and pause if something looks wrong. A re-claim proposed before a signer was removed never executes, even if that signer is re-added. Because ownership follows the Privy secret, rotate the secret after any recovery.

## What to expect

- Nothing is sponsored until step 5 is complete and the project has balance.
- Money leaves only as gas paid for sponsored operations.
- The policy signer is the ownership gatekeeper. A compromised signer could claim an **empty** unclaimed project immediately, and a funded one after the admin delay unless the contract owner or manager cancels it, so claim before anyone funds the project. It can never withdraw funds, because none can be withdrawn.

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `CONFIG_MISSING_ENV` about the v2 paymaster address | A chain with no deployed v2 entry (testnet) | On mainnet use the registry address; elsewhere pass one explicitly |
| `PAYMASTER_PROJECT_NOT_CLAIMED` from `depositFor` | Project unclaimed, or the app id is mistyped (case-sensitive) | Check spelling; pass `requireClaimed: false` only on purpose |
| `403` from `verify` | Wrong secret, or `newOwner` is not the signed-in address | Fix and retry |
| Claim reverts with an expired or used claim | Attestation older than an hour, or already used | Request a new one |
| All denials after a claim | Allowlist and limits not set | Run step 5 |
| `409` from `register` | Not claimed on chain yet, or already indexed | Claim first; list with `api.v2.projects.list()` |
| `401 login_failed` at sign-in | The SIWE domain is not one the service accepts | Use `paymaster.pepeunchained.com`, or read `siweDomains` from `GET /v2/config` |
| `project_origin_not_allowed` in the app | A client token (`ppt_`) with no allowed origins, or used from a server | Pass `allowedOrigins` at register or `updateSettings`, or use the server key from a backend |
| Lost the keys shown at register | They are shown once | `rotateClientToken` or `rotateServerKey`, then update the app |

## Related

- [Paymaster Overview](overview.md)
- [REST API v2](rest-api-v2.md)
- [Credential Matrix](auth.md)
- [Deposit and Claim a Paymaster Project](../../recipes/v2-deposit-and-claim.md)
- [Sponsorship Tiers](../../onboarding/sponsorship-tiers.md)
- [Quickstart: Zero to a Sponsored Transaction in 10 Minutes](../../get-started/quickstart-app.md)
- [Smart Account Paths](../../concepts/smart-account-paths.md)
- [Paymaster v2 Spec Summary](../../contracts/paymaster-v2-spec.md)

pages.title: MCP Server Overview
pages.content:
# MCP Server Overview

`@pepu-chain/mcp` is a Model Context Protocol server that gives a coding agent a way to check PEPU-specific facts and run PEPU-specific checks instead of guessing. It has 32 tools, 6 prompts and 5 resources. This page explains what it is for, what it will and will not do, and where the details live.

> Status: built and tested (version 0.2.5). The sponsorship probes target the hosted bundler and paymaster service by default. The v2 paymaster tools default to the registry's deployed canary (Proven on mainnet as a canary, external audit pending).

## What and why

Coding agents are strong at generic EVM patterns and weak at chain-specific facts. A wrong chain ID, an invented contract address, or the canonical Multicall3 address (which has no code on PEPU) are all failures an agent can produce with confidence. See [The Multicall3 Trap](../contracts/multicall3.md).

The server answers those questions from the source of truth:

- Addresses, chain facts and endpoints come from `@pepu-chain/sdk` (`getPepuAddresses`, `pepuMainnet`, `resolvePepuEndpoints`).
- Failures are explained from the SDK's shared error catalog (`explainError`).
- Env and Privy checks use the SDK's doctor (`checkPepuEnv`, `checkPrivyDashboardConfig`).
- Generated code comes from export-checked SDK snippets, so an agent wires the SDK instead of hand-rolling infrastructure.

It is not a generic Blockscout wrapper. pepuscan is a Blockscout instance, and the official Blockscout MCP server covers generic chain-data lookups well. This server adds only what is PEPU-specific or what composes several RPC and Blockscout calls into one answer. PEPU is a chain, not "an AI chain": this is tooling that helps builders, human or agent-assisted, get PEPU facts right.

## What it contains

| Part | Count | Page |
|---|---|---|
| Tools | 32 | [Tool Reference](tools.md) |
| Prompts | 6 | [Resources and Prompts](resources-and-prompts.md) |
| Resources | 5 (`pepu://chain-facts`, `pepu://addresses`, `pepu://docs/{slug}`, `pepu://skills/{name}`, `pepu://sdk/exports`) | [Resources and Prompts](resources-and-prompts.md) |

## Security model

- **No tool returns a secret.** `pepu_check_env` reports presence and length only. A canary-secret test in the package checks tool outputs for leaks. URLs that may carry a credential, such as the paymaster URL, are reduced to their host.
- **No private key, ever.** The server holds no key and has no tool that signs or sends a transaction. `pepu_prepare_project_tx` and `pepu_encode_calls` return unsigned data. A `pepu_send_transaction` tool was considered and rejected on purpose.
- **Local execution.** The server runs on your machine over stdio, started by your client. It talks to the public PEPU RPC, pepuscan's public API and, if you configure them, your bundler and paymaster. Docs, skills, template metadata and the SDK export list are bundled into the package, so those lookups make no network call.
- **File access is narrow.** Only two tools touch your filesystem, and both take absolute paths only, refuse `..`, filesystem roots and system folders, and refuse to overwrite. `pepu_generate_authorization_key` writes only `.env*` files and never returns the private key.
- **Annotations on every tool.** All four MCP hints (`readOnlyHint`, `destructiveHint`, `idempotentHint`, `openWorldHint`) are set, so a client can auto-approve reads and ask before writes.
- **Mainnet only.** Chain `97741`. Some tools accept `network: "testnet"` only to explain that it is out of scope.

## Read versus write tools

| Class | Tools |
|---|---|
| Read-only, no network | `pepu_known_gotchas`, `pepu_decode_error`, `pepu_explain_error`, `pepu_verify_contract_guide`, `pepu_list_templates`, `pepu_check_env` (reads local env files), `pepu_session_policy`, `pepu_encode_calls`, `pepu_prepare_project_tx`, `pepu_get_docs`, `pepu_sdk_snippet`, `pepu_sdk_exports` |
| Read-only, remote | `pepu_chain_info`, `pepu_health_check`, `pepu_gas_price`, `pepu_estimate_gas_cost`, `pepu_read_contract`, `pepu_check_contract_deployed`, `pepu_get_token_info`, `pepu_get_address_overview`, `pepu_get_transaction`, `pepu_search`, `pepu_smart_account_info`, `pepu_verify_contract_status`, `pepu_bundler_health`, `pepu_paymaster_health`, `pepu_sponsorship_status`, `pepu_project_balance`, `pepu_explain_tx`, `pepu_check_privy_config` |
| Write (local files only) | `pepu_scaffold_app` (creates a new project folder), `pepu_generate_authorization_key` (writes one env key) |

Neither write tool is destructive. Neither can overwrite an existing project or an existing authorization key without an explicit flag.

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| An agent still uses the canonical Multicall3 address | The server is not connected or the agent did not call it | Check the connection ([Install per Client](install.md)) and have the agent call `pepu_check_contract_deployed` or `pepu_chain_info`. |
| An agent says sponsorship works or does not work from memory | It skipped the live check | Call `pepu_sponsorship_status` and report what it says. |

## Related

- [Install per Client](install.md)
- [Tool Reference](tools.md)
- [Resources and Prompts](resources-and-prompts.md)
- [MCP Server and Skills (overview)](../agent-tooling/mcp-and-skills.md)
- [Skills Catalog](../agent-tooling/skills.md)
- [Claude Code Plugin](../agent-tooling/plugin.md)

pages.title: Install the MCP Server per Client
pages.content:
# Install the MCP Server per Client

Exact configuration for each supported client, the environment variables the server reads, and how to confirm the connection. Use this page when you want the `pepu` tools in your editor or agent.

> Status: built and tested. `@pepu-chain/mcp` runs over stdio from npm with no clone and no build. It needs no API key.

## Prerequisites

- Node.js 18 or newer. The server runs as `npx -y @pepu-chain/mcp`.
- A client that supports MCP over stdio.
- Optional: the three environment variables below. The server works without any of them.

## Environment variables the server reads

| Variable | Used by | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PEPU_RPC_URL` | every RPC-backed tool (through the SDK's `resolvePepuEndpoints`) | public Conduit RPC for chain `97741` | Use an authenticated endpoint here. A malformed value falls back to the public default. Mainnet only: the testnet RPC is fixed. |
| `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` | `pepu_bundler_health`, `pepu_sponsorship_status`, `pepu_health_check`, `pepu_explain_tx` (UserOperation hashes) | `https://bundler.pepeunchained.com` | The hosted bundler. Local default for your own service is `http://localhost:4337`. |
| `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` | `pepu_paymaster_health`, `pepu_sponsorship_status`, `pepu_health_check` | `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com` (service base) | The probes target the hosted paymaster service base. Set this to a full ERC-7677 URL (`.../v2/paymaster/<token>`) to probe a project URL; local default for your own service is `http://localhost:8788`. May embed a credential, so it is only ever reported as a host. |

One more variable exists for development of the server itself, not for normal use: `PEPU_CREATE_APP_BIN` points `pepu_scaffold_app` at a local build of the create-pepu-app CLI. See [Environment Variables](../reference/env-vars.md) for the full list across the kit.

## Claude Code

Plugin (recommended). The plugin wires the MCP server for you and adds the skills, the six slash commands and the builder subagent:

```text
/plugin marketplace add pepu-org/pepu-devkit
/plugin install pepu-devkit@pepu
```

Claude Code asks you to trust the plugin before it loads. The plugin passes `PEPU_RPC_URL`, `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` and `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` from your shell environment to the server (empty when unset). See [Claude Code Plugin](../agent-tooling/plugin.md).

Fallback, MCP server only:

```bash
claude mcp add pepu -- npx -y @pepu-chain/mcp
```

To pass environment variables with the fallback:

```bash
claude mcp add pepu -e PEPU_RPC_URL=https://<your-rpc> -- npx -y @pepu-chain/mcp
```

Scaffolded apps from [create-pepu-app](../cli/create-pepu-app.md) also offer the plugin on first open through `.claude/settings.json`. See [AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md in Templates](../agent-tooling/agents-md.md).

## Cursor

Create `.cursor/mcp.json` in the project (or `~/.cursor/mcp.json` for all projects):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "pepu": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@pepu-chain/mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

Reload Cursor, then enable `pepu` under Settings, MCP.

## VS Code

Create `.vscode/mcp.json` in the workspace. VS Code uses a top-level key named `servers`, not `mcpServers`:

```json
{
  "servers": {
    "pepu": {
      "type": "stdio",
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@pepu-chain/mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

Open the file in VS Code and use the Start action above the server entry, then use the tools in Copilot agent mode.

## Windsurf, Claude Desktop, Cline and other clients

Any client that launches a stdio MCP server accepts the same command. The usual shape is a JSON file with an `mcpServers` map:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "pepu": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@pepu-chain/mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

| Client | Where the config lives |
|---|---|
| Windsurf | `~/.codeium/windsurf/mcp_config.json` |
| Claude Desktop | `claude_desktop_config.json` (Settings, Developer, Edit Config) |
| Cline | The MCP servers panel, "Configure MCP Servers" (`cline_mcp_settings.json`) |
| Anything else | Generic stdio: command `npx`, arguments `-y @pepu-chain/mcp`, no environment variables required |

Config file locations and menu names belong to the clients and can change. If one does not match, the command and arguments above are the part that matters.

To pass environment variables, add an `env` object next to `args`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "pepu": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@pepu-chain/mcp"],
      "env": { "PEPU_RPC_URL": "https://<your-rpc>" }
    }
  }
}
```

For a global install or local development, replace the command:

```bash
npm install -g @pepu-chain/mcp          # then command: pepu-mcp
```

```json
{ "command": "node", "args": ["/absolute/path/to/packages/mcp/dist/index.js"] }
```

## Verifying the connection

1. Ask your agent: "List the tools from the pepu MCP server." You should see 32 tools whose names start with `pepu_`.
2. Ask it to call `pepu_health_check`. A healthy answer reports the mainnet RPC reachable at chain id `97741` and pepuscan reachable.
3. Ask it to call `pepu_chain_info`. It returns the verified network facts and contract table.
4. In Claude Code, `/mcp` lists the server and its connection state.

From a checkout of the repository you can also list every tool, resource and prompt over stdio with `pnpm smoke` in `packages/mcp` (run `pnpm build` first). It makes real network calls.

## What to expect

- The first launch downloads the package through `npx`, which takes a few seconds. Later launches use the cache.
- Pin a version if you need reproducibility: `npx -y @pepu-chain/mcp@0.2.5`. The plugin pins `@pepu-chain/mcp@^0.2`.
- No tool needs a private key. The server never holds one.

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| The client shows the server as failed or never connects | Node.js older than 18, or `npx` not on the client's PATH | Install Node 18+, and on Windows try the `npx.cmd` command or an absolute path to `node`. |
| Tools are missing in VS Code | The config uses `mcpServers` instead of `servers`, or lacks `"type": "stdio"` | Use the VS Code shape shown above. |
| `pepu_bundler_health` says "not configured" | The default was cleared or `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` is empty in the server's environment | Set it in the client's `env` block, or in your shell before launching the client. |
| Env vars set in your shell are ignored | The client does not pass its environment to child processes | Put the variables in the client's `env` block. |
| Stale facts or docs | An old cached package version | Run `npx -y @pepu-chain/mcp@latest`, or clear the npx cache. |

## Related

- [MCP Server Overview](index.md)
- [Tool Reference](tools.md)
- [Claude Code Plugin](../agent-tooling/plugin.md)
- [Build with an AI Coding Agent in 3 Minutes](../get-started/ai-assisted.md)

pages.title: MCP Resources and Prompts
pages.content:
# MCP Resources and Prompts

The five `pepu://` resources the server exposes and its six prompts: what each is for, its arguments, and how an agent should chain them with the tools. Read this if you attach context by hand in a client UI, or if you want to know what the prompt starters tell the agent to do.

> Status: built and tested in `@pepu-chain/mcp` 0.2.5. Resources and prompts are static text and bundled data; nothing here sends a transaction or needs a key.

## Prerequisites

- The server is installed in your client. See [Install per Client](install.md).
- A client that supports MCP resources and prompts. Not every client does: Claude Code lists prompts as slash commands and resources as `@` mentions, other clients vary. Tools work everywhere.

## Resources

Resources are read-only context that you or the agent can attach without a tool call.

| URI | Content | MIME type |
|---|---|---|
| `pepu://chain-facts` | Verified mainnet network facts (chain `97741`), a note that the testnet `97740` is out of scope, and the known gotchas list | `application/json` |
| `pepu://addresses` | Every tracked mainnet contract from the SDK registry (`getPepuAddresses`): deployed addresses with notes (including the v2 paymaster canary and the retired v1 paymaster, flagged `retired`), and pending rows with the reason | `application/json` |
| `pepu://docs/{slug}` | A page of these docs, from a snapshot bundled at build time. `{slug}` is a page path such as `onboarding/session-keys` | `text/markdown` |
| `pepu://skills/{name}` | A skill's `SKILL.md`, bundled at build time. `{name}` is a skill name such as `pepu-session-keys` | `text/markdown` |
| `pepu://sdk/exports` | Every `@pepu-chain/sdk` import path with its exports and one-line summaries, generated from the SDK build | `application/json` |

Notes:

- `pepu://docs/{slug}` and `pepu://skills/{name}` are resource templates. A client lists the available slugs and names, and the server completes partial values.
- The docs and skills snapshots are bundled when the package is built. They are as current as the installed server version. For a newer answer, update the server (`npx -y @pepu-chain/mcp` fetches the latest unless a version is pinned) or read the docs directly.
- An unknown slug or skill name returns an error that lists what is available.
- `pepu://addresses` shows `paymasterV2` (and its alias `paymaster`) at the deployed canary `0xdb28528C9399C33c9A0297E8A62F39145acbC30D`, and `paymasterV1` as retired. Do not deposit to the retired v1 paymaster. See [Address Map](../contracts/address-map.md).

The tools that mirror resources: `pepu_chain_info` and `pepu_known_gotchas` (chain facts), `pepu_get_docs` (docs), `pepu_sdk_exports` (SDK exports). Use the resource when you want to attach the whole thing; use the tool when the agent should decide.

## Prompts

A prompt returns one user message that tells the agent which tools and SDK functions to use, in order. Each ends with the same honesty reminder: sponsorship is proven on mainnet and the hosted bundler and paymaster service are live, the v2 paymaster is a canary (external audit pending), Privy session mode is off-chain with the user paying gas, Kernel session mode is on-chain, and secrets are never printed.

| Prompt | Arguments (all optional) | What it tells the agent to do |
|---|---|---|
| `new-pepu-app` | `idea`, `directory` (absolute path) | Read `pepu://chain-facts`, call `pepu_list_templates` and choose a template, call `pepu_scaffold_app`, run `pepu_check_env`, then `pepu_check_privy_config` with the dev origin and port, and use `pepu_sdk_snippet` and `pepu_sdk_exports` for extra wiring. |
| `add-google-login` | `projectDir` | Apply the `privy-provider` and `ensure-wallet-route` snippets, run `pepu_check_env` (template `consumer-app`) then `pepu_check_privy_config`, and pin Coinbase to `eoaOnly` and the embedded wallet when wagmi is used. |
| `add-session` | `mode` (`privy` or `kernel`), `contract`, `functions` (comma-separated signatures) | Explain the two trust models and confirm one, call `pepu_session_policy`, apply the session snippets (Privy mode also runs `pepu_generate_authorization_key` and asks you to register the public key), and show the consent text and trust notice. |
| `add-sponsorship` | `projectDir` | Run `pepu_sponsorship_status`, `pepu_bundler_health` and `pepu_paymaster_health`; apply `sponsored-send` (and `sponsored-send-server` for scripts); use `pepu_explain_error` on failures; do not tell you to deposit into v2. |
| `add-sponsored-session` | `contract`, `functions` | Build the Kernel scope with `pepu_session_policy`, apply `sponsored-session` and `sponsored-session-client` (the scope on server and client must match), confirm with `pepu_sponsorship_status`, size spend caps above the gas reservation (about 20.5 PEPU for a session's first operation, 6.9 later), and warn that `createMemoryStore` is dev only. |
| `debug-tx` | `hash`, `error` | With a hash: `pepu_explain_tx`. With an error: `pepu_explain_error` using the text exactly as given. Then `pepu_sponsorship_status` if sponsorship is involved, `pepu_decode_error` for custom errors, and `pepu_known_gotchas`. |

The three pillar prompts map one to one onto the proven pillars: `add-google-login` (Google to wallet), `add-session` (session keys), `add-sponsorship` (sponsored transactions), and `add-sponsored-session` is the combination. See [The Three Pillars and How They Combine](../get-started/pillars.md).

## How agents should chain them

1. Start from a prompt when one fits. It encodes the right order. In Claude Code the [plugin commands](../agent-tooling/plugin.md) wrap the same flows (`/pepu-new-app`, `/pepu-add-login`, `/pepu-add-session`, `/pepu-add-sponsorship`, `/pepu-add-sponsored-session`, `/pepu-doctor`).
2. Ground the facts first: `pepu_chain_info` or the `pepu://chain-facts` resource. Never answer chain questions from memory.
3. Pick code from `pepu_sdk_snippet` and confirm names with `pepu_sdk_exports` before writing anything by hand.
4. Verify with `pepu_check_env` and `pepu_check_privy_config`, then the project's own typecheck and build.
5. When something fails, `pepu_explain_error` with the exact text, then `pepu_known_gotchas`.

## What to expect

- Invoking a prompt produces a message, not a result. The agent then makes the tool calls itself, and you approve them according to your client's permission rules.
- The read-only tools run without prompting in most clients. The two write tools (`pepu_scaffold_app`, `pepu_generate_authorization_key`) ask first in clients that honour the annotation hints.

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| The client shows no prompts or resources | The client only supports MCP tools | Use the tools directly, or the plugin commands in Claude Code. |
| `pepu://docs/...` returns "No docs page" | The slug is not in the bundled snapshot | Read the slug list the error prints, or call `pepu_get_docs` with no arguments. |
| Resource content looks stale | The snapshot is bundled at build time | Update the server to the latest version, or pin a newer one. |

## Related

- [MCP Server Overview](index.md)
- [Tool Reference](tools.md)
- [Skills Catalog](../agent-tooling/skills.md)
- [Claude Code Plugin](../agent-tooling/plugin.md)

pages.title: MCP Tool Reference
pages.content:
# MCP Tool Reference

All 32 tools of `@pepu-chain/mcp`, derived from the tool registry in `packages/mcp/src/tools`: what each does, its inputs (from the zod schemas), what it returns, the SDK function it uses, its safety properties and an example call. Read this when you are wiring an agent to the server or when you need to know exactly what a tool will and will not do.

> Status: built and tested. The server is at version 0.2.5 and every tool runs against live mainnet RPC and pepuscan. Tools that probe the bundler or paymaster target the hosted bundler (`https://bundler.pepeunchained.com`) and the paymaster service base (`https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com`) by default; `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` and `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` override them. Tools that touch the v2 paymaster default to the registry's deployed canary `0xdb28528C9399C33c9A0297E8A62F39145acbC30D` (Proven on mainnet as a canary: internally reviewed 3x, external audit pending, funded in small tranches); an explicit `paymaster` address overrides it.

## Prerequisites

- The server is installed in your client. See [Install per Client](install.md).
- For the sponsorship probes: `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` and `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` in the server's environment. Local development defaults are `http://localhost:4337` and `http://localhost:8788`. See [Environment Variables](../reference/env-vars.md).
- Mainnet only (chain `97741`). Several tools accept `network: "testnet"` only so they can explain that the testnet is out of scope instead of failing schema validation.

## How to read this page

Every tool declares four MCP annotation hints. A client uses them to decide what to auto-approve.

| Class | `readOnlyHint` | `openWorldHint` | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| Static read | true | false | Pure data or computation. No network, no files. |
| Remote read | true | true | Reads PEPU RPC, pepuscan or a configured bundler or paymaster. Changes nothing. |
| Write | false | true | Writes a file on your machine. Never destructive, never idempotent. Only two tools are in this class. |

Conventions shared by all tools:

- `response_format` is `"concise"` (default) or `"detailed"` wherever output can be large.
- Results are JSON text. Big integers are returned as decimal strings.
- Errors are actionable: what happened, why, and the fix.
- No tool returns a secret. URLs that may carry a credential are reduced to their host. See [MCP Server Overview](index.md#security-model).

## Tool index

| Tool | Group | Class | SDK function or source |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pepu_chain_info` | Chain and lookups | Remote read | `getPepuAddresses` |
| `pepu_known_gotchas` | Chain and lookups | Static read | `PEPU_ERROR_CATALOG` |
| `pepu_health_check` | Chain and lookups | Remote read | `resolvePepuEndpoints`, `probeBundler`, `probePaymaster` |
| `pepu_gas_price` | Chain and lookups | Remote read | RPC (viem) |
| `pepu_estimate_gas_cost` | Chain and lookups | Remote read | RPC (viem) |
| `pepu_read_contract` | Chain and lookups | Remote read | RPC (viem) |
| `pepu_check_contract_deployed` | Chain and lookups | Remote read | RPC (`eth_getCode`) and the SDK registry |
| `pepu_get_token_info` | Chain and lookups | Remote read | pepuscan plus RPC cross-check |
| `pepu_get_address_overview` | Chain and lookups | Remote read | pepuscan |
| `pepu_get_transaction` | Chain and lookups | Remote read | pepuscan |
| `pepu_search` | Chain and lookups | Remote read | pepuscan |
| `pepu_smart_account_info` | Chain and lookups | Remote read | Kernel factory `getAddress` over RPC |
| `pepu_decode_error` | Chain and lookups | Static read | `explainError` |
| `pepu_verify_contract_guide` | Chain and lookups | Static read | static reference |
| `pepu_verify_contract_status` | Chain and lookups | Remote read | pepuscan |
| `pepu_bundler_health` | Probe, status, explain | Remote read | `probeBundler` (`/aa`) |
| `pepu_paymaster_health` | Probe, status, explain | Remote read | `probePaymaster` (`/aa`) |
| `pepu_sponsorship_status` | Probe, status, explain | Remote read | `checkSponsorship` |
| `pepu_project_balance` | Probe, status, explain | Remote read | `readProject`, `computeProjectId` (`/paymaster`) |
| `pepu_explain_error` | Probe, status, explain | Static read | `explainError`, `mapPaymasterReason` |
| `pepu_explain_tx` | Probe, status, explain | Remote read | `explorerLinks`, `formatPepu`, `userOpEventFromReceipt` |
| `pepu_list_templates` | Generate, scaffold, docs | Static read | `TEMPLATE_REQUIREMENTS` (`/doctor`) |
| `pepu_scaffold_app` | Generate, scaffold, docs | Write | create-pepu-app CLI, `checkPepuEnv` |
| `pepu_check_env` | Generate, scaffold, docs | Static read | `checkPepuEnv` (`/doctor`) |
| `pepu_check_privy_config` | Generate, scaffold, docs | Remote read | `checkPrivyDashboardConfig` (`/privy`) |
| `pepu_generate_authorization_key` | Generate, scaffold, docs | Write | `generatePrivyAuthorizationKey` (`/doctor`) |
| `pepu_session_policy` | Generate, scaffold, docs | Static read | `buildSessionPolicy`, `buildKernelSessionPolicies` and the `describe*` helpers |
| `pepu_encode_calls` | Generate, scaffold, docs | Static read | `encodeAggregate3`, `getMulticall3` |
| `pepu_prepare_project_tx` | Generate, scaffold, docs | Static read | the `encode*` helpers and `configureProject` (`/paymaster`) |
| `pepu_get_docs` | Generate, scaffold, docs | Static read | bundled docs snapshot |
| `pepu_sdk_snippet` | Generate, scaffold, docs | Static read | bundled, export-checked snippets |
| `pepu_sdk_exports` | Generate, scaffold, docs | Static read | bundled SDK export list |

The groups follow the registry: the original lookups first, then the SDK-backed probes and explainers, then generate, scaffold and docs.

---

## Chain facts and lookups

### `pepu_chain_info`

Verified network facts: chain ids, RPC and explorer URLs, native currency, ArbOS version, and which infrastructure contracts are deployed (Multicall3, Permit2, EntryPoint, Kernel factory, the verifying paymaster), including the sponsorship status. Call it first, before writing any PEPU chain config.

| Input | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `network` | `mainnet`, `testnet`, `both` | `both` | |
| `verify_live` | boolean | `false` | Adds a live `eth_chainId` and `eth_gasPrice` call to confirm the cached facts. |
| `response_format` | `concise`, `detailed` | `concise` | Detailed adds canonical-contract notes and the gotchas list. |

Returns network facts and the registry rows from `getPepuAddresses`. Safety: remote read. It lists the v2 paymaster canary as deployed (external audit pending) and the v1 paymaster as retired.

```json
{ "network": "mainnet", "verify_live": true }
```

### `pepu_known_gotchas`

The curated list of PEPU footguns as one flat list, with no network calls: the Multicall3 address, sponsorship status, the two-address model, Privy's server-side `eth_sendTransaction` limit on chain 97741, Privy setup traps, scope decisions and more.

| Input | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `response_format` | `concise`, `detailed` | `concise` | Detailed adds the full canonical-contract table and the SDK error catalog (`PEPU_ERROR_CATALOG`). |

Safety: static read. Call `pepu_check_contract_deployed` for a live check of one address and `pepu_explain_error` for a specific failure.

```json
{ "response_format": "detailed" }
```

### `pepu_health_check`

Is the RPC (mainnet and or testnet) and pepuscan's Blockscout API (mainnet only) reachable right now, with chain id and latest block. When a bundler or paymaster URL is configured it adds those rows. It separates "pepuscan is behind", "wrong network" and "testnet has no explorer".

| Input | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `network` | `mainnet`, `testnet`, `both` | `both` | Blockscout is only ever checked for mainnet. |
| `response_format` | `concise`, `detailed` | `concise` | Detailed adds latency and full error text. |

Safety: remote read. Use it to rule out chain-side unavailability before assuming a bug in your code.

```json
{ "network": "mainnet" }
```

### `pepu_gas_price`

The current live gas price and what it costs in PEPU for a transfer, an ERC-20 transfer, a swap and a rough contract deploy. No other inputs needed.

| Input | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `network` | `mainnet`, `testnet` | `mainnet` | RPC-direct, so testnet works. |
| `response_format` | `concise`, `detailed` | `concise` | Detailed adds the raw wei value and block number. |

Safety: remote read. The base fee is about 12,500 gwei. That is high in gwei terms and not an error. The tool never returns a USD figure.

```json
{ "response_format": "detailed" }
```

### `pepu_estimate_gas_cost`

Estimates the PEPU cost of a call (live simulation), of a contract deployment (pass init bytecode as `data` and omit `to`), or of a `gas_limit` you already know.

| Input | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `network` | `mainnet`, `testnet` | `mainnet` | |
| `to` | string | none | Recipient or contract. Omit for a deployment estimate. |
| `from` | string | none | Sender to simulate from. |
| `data` | string | `0x` | Calldata, or init bytecode for a deployment. |
| `value` | string | `0` | Wei, as a decimal string. |
| `gas_limit` | string or number | none | Skip simulation and price this gas amount. |
| `response_format` | `concise`, `detailed` | `concise` | |

Safety: remote read. No USD figure: there is no on-chain price oracle for PEPU, so bring your own price feed.

```json
{ "to": "0x261eA5971B93237a56990206A46Bc80318e4d078", "data": "0x" }
```

### `pepu_read_contract`

Calls a view or pure function over RPC, given the address, a minimal ABI fragment and the arguments. Works on testnet too.

| Input | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `address` | string | required | 0x address of the contract. |
| `abi` | array of objects | required | At least one ABI item. Only the function you call is needed. |
| `functionName` | string | required | Must match a function in `abi`. |
| `args` | array | `[]` | Positional. uint and int values may be strings or numbers. |
| `network` | `mainnet`, `testnet` | `mainnet` | |

Safety: remote read. Sends no transaction and needs no key. Use `pepu_verify_contract_status` first if you do not know the ABI.

```json
{
  "address": "0xF9Cf4A16d26979b929Be7176bAc4e7084975FCB8",
  "abi": [{ "type": "function", "name": "decimals", "stateMutability": "view", "inputs": [], "outputs": [{ "type": "uint8" }] }],
  "functionName": "decimals"
}
```

### `pepu_check_contract_deployed`

A live `eth_getCode` check by well-known name ("Multicall3", "Permit2", "EntryPoint v0.7", "Kernel Factory", "WPEPU", "TapScore") or by address. When you ask about a canonical address that has no code on PEPU, it surfaces the PEPU-specific replacement. It is the guardrail against assuming Multicall3 sits at its usual address. See [The Multicall3 Trap](../contracts/multicall3.md).

| Input | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `query` | string, min 1 char | required | Address or partial, case-insensitive name. |
| `network` | `mainnet`, `testnet` | `mainnet` | Works on both. |
| `response_format` | `concise`, `detailed` | `concise` | Detailed lists every matching known contract. |

Safety: remote read.

```json
{ "query": "multicall" }
```

### `pepu_get_token_info`

An ERC-20's name, symbol, decimals, supply and holder count from pepuscan, cross-checked against the contract over RPC, and flagged when it is WPEPU. Never returns a USD value.

| Input | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `address` | string | required | ERC-20 contract address. |
| `network` | `mainnet`, `testnet` | `mainnet` | Only mainnet works; testnet returns an explanation. |
| `response_format` | `concise`, `detailed` | `concise` | Detailed adds the raw RPC cross-check and reputation metadata. |

Safety: remote read. Use `pepu_search` first if you only have a symbol.

```json
{ "address": "0xF9Cf4A16d26979b929Be7176bAc4e7084975FCB8" }
```

### `pepu_get_address_overview`

One call for an address: native balance, contract or EOA, verification status, transaction count and token holdings.

| Input | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `address` | string | required | 40 hex characters. |
| `network` | `mainnet`, `testnet` | `mainnet` | Only mainnet works. |
| `response_format` | `concise`, `detailed` | `concise` | Concise shows the top 5 holdings; detailed up to 25 plus proxy information. |

Safety: remote read, mainnet only. Internal Blockscout ids are stripped from the output.

```json
{ "address": "0x9CE19273Ae9c24437DFF512E8DFCAed4E4B001bd" }
```

### `pepu_get_transaction`

A transaction with its decoded call when pepuscan has the ABI, and PEPU-denominated value and fee. Detailed adds the gas breakdown, nonce and Arbitrum L1 batch status. The server deliberately has no bulk transaction-history tool.

| Input | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `hash` | string | required | 64 hex characters. |
| `network` | `mainnet`, `testnet` | `mainnet` | Only mainnet works. |
| `response_format` | `concise`, `detailed` | `concise` | |

Safety: remote read, mainnet only. For an EOA versus UserOperation breakdown use `pepu_explain_tx`.

```json
{ "hash": "0x<64-hex-transaction-hash>", "response_format": "detailed" }
```

### `pepu_search`

Resolves an ambiguous string (address, transaction hash, block number, token or contract name) to an entity and points to the next tool to call.

| Input | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `query` | string, min 1 char | required | Anything you would type into an explorer search box. |
| `network` | `mainnet`, `testnet` | `mainnet` | Only mainnet works. |
| `response_format` | `concise`, `detailed` | `concise` | Top 5 versus top 20 matches. |

Safety: remote read, mainnet only.

```json
{ "query": "WPEPU" }
```

### `pepu_smart_account_info`

The counterfactual address of a ZeroDev Kernel v3 account (single EOA owner) for an owner and salt, taken from the factory's own on-chain `getAddress(bytes,bytes32)` and checked with `eth_getCode` for deployment. This is the smart account address, which is not the owner address. See [The Two-Address Model](../onboarding/two-address-model.md).

| Input | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `owner` | string | required | The EOA that controls the account. |
| `salt` | string | `"0"` | Integer string or a full 0x 32-byte value. |
| `network` | `mainnet`, `testnet` | `mainnet` | The factory exists on mainnet only. |
| `response_format` | `concise`, `detailed` | `concise` | Detailed adds the encoded init data and assumptions. |

Safety: remote read. Never deploys, never holds a key. It does not imply sponsorship works.

```json
{ "owner": "0x<owner-address>", "salt": "0" }
```

### `pepu_decode_error`

Decodes revert data into an error name and arguments: your own custom errors (pass `abi`), Solidity `Error` and `Panic`, ERC-4337 EntryPoint v0.6 and v0.7 errors with AA-code phase explanations, and a small ArbOS precompile table. The public RPC does not expose `debug_traceCall`, so this is often the only way to read a failure.

| Input | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `data` | string | required | Revert payload, 0x hex. Bare selector or selector plus args. |
| `abi` | array of objects | none | Your contract's error fragments. Checked first. |
| `response_format` | `concise`, `detailed` | `concise` | Detailed adds which table matched. |

Safety: static read. For the PEPU-specific cause and fix of any failure prefer `pepu_explain_error`; keep this tool for decoding custom errors from your own ABI.

```json
{ "data": "0x08c379a0..." }
```

### `pepu_verify_contract_guide`

The exact command to verify a contract on pepuscan: Foundry (`--verifier blockscout` with the `--verifier-url` ending in `/api`) and or the Hardhat `customChains` and `verify.blockscout` configuration.

| Input | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tool` | `foundry`, `hardhat`, `both` | `both` | |
| `network` | `mainnet`, `testnet` | `mainnet` | Only mainnet is verifiable. |
| `response_format` | `concise`, `detailed` | `concise` | Detailed adds the Hardhat config, failure modes and proxy handling. |

Safety: static read. Call it right after deploying, then `pepu_verify_contract_status` to check the result. See [Deploy and Verify a Contract](../contracts/deployment.md).

```json
{ "tool": "foundry" }
```

### `pepu_verify_contract_status`

Is this address a verified contract on pepuscan, and if so its ABI, compiler and Sourcify link. It tells an unverified contract apart from an address that is not a contract at all.

| Input | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `address` | string | required | |
| `network` | `mainnet`, `testnet` | `mainnet` | Only mainnet works. |
| `response_format` | `concise`, `detailed` | `concise` | Detailed adds the full ABI, license and proxy information. |

Safety: remote read, mainnet only.

```json
{ "address": "0x261eA5971B93237a56990206A46Bc80318e4d078" }
```

---

## Probes, status and explainers

### `pepu_bundler_health`

Probes an ERC-4337 bundler with `probeBundler` from `@pepu-chain/sdk/aa`: chain id (must be `97741`), supported EntryPoints (must include v0.7), which UserOperation methods exist, latency, and a verdict with a fix. Defaults to `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL`.

| Input | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `url` | URL string | `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` | Never echoed back, only its host. |

Safety: remote read. Sends nothing on-chain. The default is the hosted bundler; an explicitly cleared or unreachable value is reported with next steps.

```json
{}
```

### `pepu_paymaster_health`

Probes an ERC-7677 paymaster with `probePaymaster`: `GET /health`, the free-tier endpoint and a `pm_getPaymasterStubData` round trip. A JSON-RPC denial still counts as alive, because the probe has no credential. Defaults to `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL`.

| Input | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `url` | URL string | `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` | The ERC-7677 endpoint, often `https://host/paymaster/<token>`. Returns only the host. |

Safety: remote read. The URL can embed a credential and is never returned.

```json
{}
```

### `pepu_sponsorship_status`

Answers "can my app send a gas-sponsored transaction right now?" with `checkSponsorship`: resolves the URLs with `resolvePepuEndpoints`, probes both, optionally reads the paymaster's EntryPoint deposit, and returns `available`, a reason and fixes. Always run this before making any claim about sponsorship.

| Input | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bundlerUrl` | URL string | `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` | |
| `paymasterUrl` | URL string | `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` | Never echoed back. |
| `include_deposit` | boolean | `true` | Reads the paymaster's EntryPoint v0.7 deposit (the v2 canary from the registry). An empty deposit makes sponsorship unavailable. |

Returns `available`, `transport`, `reason`, `fixes`, a bundler section, a paymaster section (host, health, ERC-7677 stub result, free tier, deposit) and notes. Safety: remote read. The notes always state that the hosted bundler and paymaster service are live and that the v2 paymaster is a canary with the external audit pending. Without a token URL the paymaster service is probed at its base.

```json
{ "include_deposit": true }
```

### `pepu_project_balance`

Reads a v2 sponsorship project on-chain with `readProject`: owner, claimed, balance, spendable limits, spent today, paused and pending re-claim. The project id is `computeProjectId`, which is `keccak256(bytes(appId))` and case-sensitive.

| Input | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `appId` | string | none | Privy app id. Give `appId` or `projectId`. |
| `projectId` | string | none | 32-byte id, 0x plus 64 hex. |
| `paymaster` | string | none | Address of a v2 paymaster you have verified. Required today. |

Safety: remote read. Status: Proven on mainnet (canary, external audit pending). With no `paymaster` argument the tool reads the registry's deployed v2 canary (`0xdb28528C9399C33c9A0297E8A62F39145acbC30D`); an explicit `paymaster` overrides it, and only if neither exists does it return the computed project id and say so. Deposits are one-way and cannot be withdrawn. See [Sponsorship Tiers](../onboarding/sponsorship-tiers.md).

```json
{ "appId": "<your-privy-app-id>" }
```

### `pepu_explain_error`

Explains any PEPU failure from the SDK's shared error catalog (`explainError`): an error message or stack text, a paymaster denial reason code (mapped with `mapPaymasterReason`, for example `project_not_claimed_onchain`), or raw revert data. Returns the catalog code, cause, fix, whether a retry can help, the HTTP status the SDK route factories use and a docs link.

| Input | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `error` | string, 1 to 20,000 chars | required | Pass the text exactly as given. It is never echoed back. |

Safety: static read, pure and offline. It is the first call for any failure and a superset of `pepu_decode_error`. See [SDK Error Catalog](../sdk/errors.md).

```json
{ "error": "AA21 didn't pay prefund" }
```

### `pepu_explain_tx`

Explains a transaction or ERC-4337 bundle from the RPC alone: EOA transaction or UserOperation bundle, sender, who paid gas (the EOA, a paymaster, or the smart account's own deposit), success or revert, fee in PEPU and pepuscan links. Each `UserOperationEvent` is decoded with `userOpEventFromReceipt`. A UserOperation hash also works when `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` is set.

| Input | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `hash` | string | required | Transaction hash, or a UserOperation hash when a bundler URL is configured. |

Safety: remote read. Use `pepu_get_transaction` for pepuscan's decoded input and L1 batch status.

```json
{ "hash": "0x<64-hex-transaction-hash>" }
```

---

## Generate, scaffold and docs

### `pepu_list_templates`

Lists the create-pepu-app templates with their doctor pillars (login, wallet, session, sponsorship, gate, mint) and, separately, `features` (the CLI display tags login, session, sponsor), required and optional env vars, Privy dashboard settings (`TEMPLATE_REQUIREMENTS`), when to pick each, and the exact scaffold and run commands. Metadata comes from the bundled `templates.json`. Takes no inputs. Safety: static read. Call it before `pepu_scaffold_app`. See [Template Gallery](../templates/index.md).

```json
{}
```

### `pepu_scaffold_app`

Creates a PEPU Next.js app by running the create-pepu-app CLI with `--yes --json`. It never reimplements the CLI. Optionally writes the Privy app id and the bundler and paymaster URLs into the new `.env.local`, then reports which env vars are still missing with `checkPepuEnv`. See [create-pepu-app CLI](../cli/create-pepu-app.md).

| Input | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `template` | string | required | A name from `pepu_list_templates`. |
| `directory` | string | required | ABSOLUTE path. Must not exist or must be empty; the parent must exist. Relative paths and `..` are refused. |
| `packageManager` | `npm`, `pnpm`, `yarn`, `bun` | auto-detected | Used in the printed commands (CLI `--pm`). |
| `privyAppId` | string | none | Written as `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_APP_ID`. Public value. Format-checked. |
| `bundlerUrl` | URL string | none | Written as `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL`. Never echoed. |
| `paymasterUrl` | URL string | none | Written as `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL`. Can embed a credential. Never echoed. |
| `dry_run` | boolean | `false` | Validates and shows the command without creating anything. |

Safety: write class (not read-only, not destructive, not idempotent). It refuses a non-empty directory, so nothing is overwritten. It runs `npx -y create-pepu-app@latest` unless a local build is found, and falls back to the human-readable CLI output if an older CLI lacks `--json`. Returns the created path, top-level entries, env keys written, env still missing (key names and fixes only) and next steps.

```json
{ "template": "sponsored-session-app", "directory": "C:/projects/my-pepu-app", "dry_run": true }
```

### `pepu_check_env`

Checks a project's environment with `checkPepuEnv` and `TEMPLATE_REQUIREMENTS` from `@pepu-chain/sdk/doctor`. Reads `.env` and `.env.local` (the latter wins) or pasted text, and reports each key as ok, missing, placeholder or malformed, with whether it is a secret, its value length and the fix.

| Input | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `projectDir` | string | none | ABSOLUTE path. Give `projectDir`, `envText` or both (`envText` wins). |
| `envText` | string, max 100,000 chars | none | Pasted dotenv text. Values are never echoed. |
| `template` | string | none | Selects required and optional keys. Omit for the base Privy keys. |
| `pillars` | array of `login`, `wallet`, `session`, `sponsorship`, `gate`, `mint` | none | Extra pillars to require, for example `["sponsorship"]` adds `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` and `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL`. |

Safety: static read that reads local files. It never returns or logs a value, only presence and length. The result includes `valuesReturned: false`.

```json
{ "projectDir": "C:/projects/my-pepu-app", "template": "game-app" }
```

### `pepu_check_privy_config`

Checks the Privy dashboard settings an app needs with `checkPrivyDashboardConfig` from `@pepu-chain/sdk/privy`, using Privy's public app-config endpoint (no secret): allowed origin with the exact port, create-on-login, Google login, Smart Wallets with bundler and paymaster URLs, and session signers. Each requirement comes back `pass`, `fail` or `unknown` with a fix. `unknown` means Privy did not report it, not that it failed. The result also carries the full `PEPU_PRIVY_REQUIREMENTS` table, including env and code requirements that cannot be checked remotely.

| Input | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `appId` | string, min 1 char | required | `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_APP_ID`, a public value. |
| `origin` | URL string | none | The origin including the port, such as `http://localhost:3000`. A different dev port is the usual cause of login failure. |
| `pillars` | array of `login`, `session`, `sponsor` | all | Only report requirements that matter for these pillars. |

Safety: remote read. It needs network access to `auth.privy.io`. See [Dashboard Settings, Field by Field](../privy/dashboard-settings.md).

```json
{ "appId": "<your-privy-app-id>", "origin": "http://localhost:3000", "pillars": ["login", "session"] }
```

### `pepu_generate_authorization_key`

Generates the P-256 Privy authorization key for session signers with `generatePrivyAuthorizationKey`. The private half is written straight to the env file as `PRIVY_AUTHORIZATION_KEY` and is never returned. Only the public key and a short fingerprint come back, with the next dashboard step: register the public key as a key quorum, then set `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_KEY_QUORUM_ID`. See [Authorization Keys and Key Quorums](../privy/authorization-keys.md).

| Input | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `envFile` | string | required | ABSOLUTE path, normally `<project>/.env.local`. Created if missing; the folder must exist. Must be named `.env` or `.env.<something>`. |
| `confirm_write` | boolean | `false` | Must be `true` to generate and write. When false the tool only reports what it would do. |
| `overwrite` | boolean | `false` | Required to replace an existing non-empty key. Replacing invalidates sessions granted under the old quorum. |

Safety: write class. Refuses an existing key without `overwrite: true`, refuses to write anything but an `.env*` file, and returns `privateKeyReturned: false`.

```json
{ "envFile": "C:/projects/my-pepu-app/.env.local", "confirm_write": true }
```

### `pepu_session_policy`

Builds a scoped session policy for one contract and a list of functions. Mode `privy` uses `buildSessionPolicy` and `describeSessionScope` from `@pepu-chain/sdk/session`: an off-chain Privy policy, the user pays gas, value is always zero. Mode `kernel` uses `buildKernelSessionPolicies` and `describeKernelSessionScope` from `@pepu-chain/sdk/session/kernel`: on-chain call and timestamp policies on a Kernel account, which compose with sponsorship.

| Input | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | `privy`, `kernel` | required | |
| `contract` | string | required | The one contract the session may call. |
| `functions` | array of strings or ABI fragments, min 1 | required | Solidity signatures such as `tap()` or `transfer(address to, uint256 amount)`, or JSON ABI function fragments. |
| `minutes` | positive number | 15 | Clamped to 1 to 1440. |
| `valueLimitWei` | decimal string | `0` | Kernel mode only. Privy mode always requires zero value. |

Returns the policy, a consent summary, selectors, the trust notice (`SESSION_TRUST_NOTICE`) and a paste-ready snippet. Safety: static read, pure; nothing is signed or sent. In kernel mode the `@zerodev/*` optional peers must be installed to build the policy objects; without them the tool still describes the scope and says so. See [Session Keys](../onboarding/session-keys.md) and [Sponsored Session](../onboarding/sponsored-session.md).

```json
{ "mode": "kernel", "contract": "0x261eA5971B93237a56990206A46Bc80318e4d078", "functions": ["tap()"], "minutes": 15 }
```

### `pepu_encode_calls`

ABI-encodes contract calls with viem's `encodeFunctionData` from a signature or an ABI and optionally wraps them. `multicall3` builds one `aggregate3` call to PEPU's own Multicall3 with `encodeAggregate3` and `getMulticall3`, never the canonical `0xcA11...` address. `kernel-execute` and `userop-callData` build the Kernel v3 ERC-7579 execute calldata for a UserOperation (single or batch mode).

| Input | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `calls` | array of 1 to 50 call objects | required | See below. |
| `as` | `calldata`, `multicall3`, `kernel-execute`, `userop-callData` | `calldata` | `kernel-execute` and `userop-callData` produce the same bytes; the second name is what goes in a UserOperation. |

Each call object:

| Field | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `to` | string | required | Target contract. |
| `signature` | string | none | Solidity signature. Give `signature`, or `abi` plus `functionName`. |
| `abi` | array of objects | none | Full or single-function ABI. |
| `functionName` | string | none | Function to call in `abi`. |
| `args` | array | `[]` | In order. |
| `value` | decimal string | `0` | Wei. |
| `allowFailure` | boolean | `false` | `multicall3` only. |

Returns hex, a decoded echo and a gas hint. Safety: static read, pure; nothing is signed or sent.

```json
{
  "as": "multicall3",
  "calls": [
    { "to": "0xF9Cf4A16d26979b929Be7176bAc4e7084975FCB8", "signature": "balanceOf(address account)", "args": ["0x<holder-address>"] }
  ]
}
```

### `pepu_prepare_project_tx`

Encodes unsigned transactions for a v2 sponsorship project with the helpers in `@pepu-chain/sdk/paymaster`: `encodeDeposit` (`depositFor`), `encodeClaimProject` and `encodeReclaimProject` (from a claim attestation), `encodeExecuteReclaim`, `encodeCancelReclaim`, `configureProject` (`setTargets`, `setDailyLimit`, `setSenderDailyLimit`) and `encodeSetPaused`. Returns `{ to, data, value }` and a plain-English warning.

| Input | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `action` | `deposit`, `claim`, `reclaim`, `executeReclaim`, `cancelReclaim`, `configure`, `setPaused` | required | `claim` and `reclaim` need the attestation from `requestClaimAttestation` (server). |
| `paymaster` | string | none | The v2 contract address you have verified. Required today. |
| `appId` | string | none | Case-sensitive. Give `appId` or `projectId`. |
| `projectId` | string | none | bytes32. |
| `amountPepu` | string | none | `deposit`: decimal PEPU such as `"2.5"`. |
| `amountWei` | decimal string | none | `deposit`: wei. Give `amountPepu` or `amountWei`. |
| `attestation` | object | none | `claim` and `reclaim`: `{ appId, newOwner, nonce, deadline, signature }`, the EIP-712 `ProjectClaim` attestation. |
| `targets` | array of up to 50 strings | none | `configure`: destination contracts to sponsor. |
| `dailyLimitPepu` | string | none | `configure`: total daily budget. |
| `senderDailyLimitPepu` | string | none | `configure`: per-wallet daily budget. |
| `paused` | boolean | none | `setPaused`. |

Safety: static read. It never signs or sends. Status: Proven on mainnet (canary, external audit pending). With no `paymaster` argument it uses the registry's deployed v2 canary; an explicit verified address overrides it. Deposits are one-way, the app id is case-sensitive, and a claim sets the owner only: the owner must then call `configure` (a claim of a project that already holds funds is pending for the 48-hour admin delay and needs `executeReclaim`). See [Register, Deposit and Claim a v2 Project](../infra/paymaster/v2-register-deposit-claim.md).

```json
{ "action": "deposit", "paymaster": "0x<verified-v2-paymaster>", "appId": "<your-privy-app-id>", "amountPepu": "2.5" }
```

### `pepu_get_docs`

Reads the PEPU developer docs from a snapshot of this repository's `docs/` folder, bundled at build time (no network). `query` returns the best-matching sections with their `guide.pepeunchained.com` URL, `slug` returns a whole page, and no arguments lists every page.

| Input | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `query` | string, min 2 chars | none | A few words, for example `privy allowed origins port`. |
| `slug` | string | none | A page slug such as `onboarding/session-keys`. Long pages are truncated; then ask for a section with `query`. |

Safety: static read. The snapshot is only as new as the installed server version. Docs describe the SDK; for exact exports use `pepu_sdk_exports` and for working code `pepu_sdk_snippet`.

```json
{ "query": "sponsored session" }
```

### `pepu_sdk_snippet`

Canonical code that uses `@pepu-chain/sdk` for one task. Each snippet names its file, peer packages, env vars and caveats, and every import is checked against the SDK export list in the package's tests. Omit `task` to list them all.

| Input | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `task` | enum, optional | list all | One of the ids below. |

Snippet ids: `privy-provider`, `ensure-wallet-route`, `wagmi-privy`, `grant-session`, `session-routes`, `session-action-route`, `kernel-session-policy`, `sponsored-send`, `sponsored-send-server`, `check-sponsorship`, `sponsored-session`, `sponsored-session-client`, `multicall-read`, `permit2-permit`, `v2-deposit`.

Safety: static read. The `v2-deposit` snippet targets the v2 paymaster canary (external audit pending); keep deposits small.

```json
{ "task": "sponsored-session" }
```

### `pepu_sdk_exports`

Lists the exports of `@pepu-chain/sdk` per import path with one-line summaries, from an export list generated from the SDK build and bundled with the server. Use it to find the right function before writing code. Omit `subpath` to list the paths with export counts.

| Input | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `subpath` | string | none | `@pepu-chain/sdk/session` or just `session`. |
| `search` | string | none | Name or summary contains this text, case-insensitive. |
| `kind` | `function`, `value`, `type`, `class`, `enum` | none | Only this kind of export. |

Safety: static read. The same data is available as the `pepu://sdk/exports` resource.

```json
{ "subpath": "session/kernel", "kind": "function" }
```

---

## What to expect

- Every tool returns one JSON text block, or an actionable error with what, why and fix.
- Tools that depend on a service you have not configured say so. They do not guess and they do not invent a hosted URL.
- The two write tools (`pepu_scaffold_app`, `pepu_generate_authorization_key`) are the only ones that touch your filesystem, and both accept absolute paths only.

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| A Blockscout-backed tool says testnet is not supported | pepuscan does not index testnet `97740` | Use mainnet, or an RPC-direct tool (`pepu_read_contract`, `pepu_gas_price`, `pepu_estimate_gas_cost`, `pepu_check_contract_deployed`). |
| `pepu_bundler_health` or `pepu_paymaster_health` reports "not configured" | A default was cleared, or the URL you passed is empty | The hosted bundler and paymaster service are the defaults. Set `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` / `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` in the server env, or pass `url`. |
| `pepu_scaffold_app` refuses the directory | Not absolute, contains `..`, or exists and is not empty | Pass an absolute path to a folder that does not exist yet. |
| `pepu_generate_authorization_key` refuses | An existing key is set, or `confirm_write` is false | Pass `confirm_write: true`; add `overwrite: true` only if you mean to rotate (that invalidates existing sessions). |
| `pepu_project_balance` or `pepu_prepare_project_tx` asks for a paymaster address | The registry has no `paymasterV2` address for the chain in use | On mainnet the registry holds the canary and both tools default to it. Pass an address you have verified to override. |
| `pepu_session_policy` kernel mode warns about missing packages | The optional `@zerodev/*` peers are not installed next to the server | Install `@zerodev/sdk`, `@zerodev/permissions` and `@zerodev/ecdsa-validator`, or accept the scope description only. |
| `pepu_check_privy_config` shows `unknown` rows | Privy's public config did not report that setting | Check the dashboard by hand; `unknown` is not a failure. |

## Related

- [MCP Server Overview](index.md)
- [Install per Client](install.md)
- [Resources and Prompts](resources-and-prompts.md)
- [Skills Catalog](../agent-tooling/skills.md)
- [SDK Overview and Reference](../sdk/reference.md)

pages.title: Google Login, Session and Sponsorship End to End
pages.content:
# Google Login, Session and Sponsorship End to End The headline flow of the dev kit: the user signs in with Google, signs once to approve a limited session, and from then on every action runs with no wallet popup and no gas from the user. This page is the full walkthrough: the architecture, every step with the SDK calls and the failure modes, what the chain enforces versus what the server only checks, and the checks that catch problems before a user does. > Status: the mechanism is proven on PEPU mainnet by script. `npm run prove-session` (and the SDK's own `pnpm --filter @pepu-chain/sdk prove-session`) ran: a throwaway owner signs one grant, then a throwaway session key sends two sponsored UserOperations that deploy the account and call `tap()`. The smart account balance stayed exactly 0, `TapScore.scores(account)` read 2, and the paymaster's EntryPoint deposit dropped. A different function on the allowed contract, and an already-expired grant, were refused. Google login and the wallet pillar are proven separately. A person has also clicked through this template's browser UI end to end on mainnet (2026-10-14): Google sign-in, one Privy `eth_signTypedData_v4` signature on chain 97741, sponsored taps with no popup while the smart account stayed at 0 PEPU, and revoke. The hosted bundler (`https://bundler.pepeunchained.com`) and paymaster (`https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com`) are live and proven for project-sponsored operations; the combination itself (Google login, Kernel session key and sponsorship) is proven live in a browser on mainnet (2026-10-14) against the hosted bundler and v2 paymaster. You need a claimed and funded project; the v2 paymaster is a canary with external audit pending. ## Prerequisites - A Privy app with Google enabled, `http://localhost:3000` in Allowed origins and embedded wallets on. Smart Wallets, authorization keys and key quorums are NOT needed. See [Dashboard Settings](../privy/dashboard-settings.md). - A bundler and a paymaster for chain 97741 (EntryPoint v0.7, ERC-7677). PEPU hosts them: the bundler at `https://bundler.pepeunchained.com` (the SDK default) and the paymaster at `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/`. Treat the paymaster URL as a secret. You need your own project (claim, deposit, server key); see [Sponsorship Tiers](sponsorship-tiers.md). The free tier needs a verified Privy token from PEPU's own Privy app and is not available to third-party apps; the session routes forward the signed-in user's Privy token as ERC-7677 context, which a project ignores for billing. Local defaults for self-run services: `http://localhost:4337` and `http://localhost:8788/paymaster/`. - Your target contract on the paymaster's destination allowlist, and per-user spend caps above the first-operation reservation. - Node 18.17 or newer. `npx create-pepu-app@latest my-app --template sponsored-session-app` scaffolds everything below. ## Architecture ``` browser your server services / chain ------- ----------- ---------------- Google sign-in (Privy) embedded wallet = OWNER WalletGate ─ POST /api/wallet/ensure ─► createEnsureWalletRoute() ──► Privy (create wallet) useSponsoredSession.grant() ─ POST /api/session/prepare ───────► routes.prepare generateSessionKey() (private key stays here) expectedPermissionId(), getKernelAddress() store.set(record) ◄─ { sessionKeyAddress, validUntil, scope, kernelAddress } approveKernelSession(): owner signs ONE EIP-712 message (no gas) ─ POST /api/session/activate {approval} ─► routes.activate checkApproval(): this account, this permission id store.set({ ...record, approval }) useSponsoredSession.act() ─ POST /api/session/act ───────────► routes.act assertCallsInScope() (fail fast) loadKernelSessionAccount(approval, sessionPrivateKey) createPepuSponsoredClient() + sendSponsored() ─ bundler ─► EntryPoint v0.7 ─► Kernel account ─ paymaster pays gas call policy + timestamp policy validate ◄─ { transactionHash, userOpHash, paymaster, actualGasCostWei, explorerUrl, actions } useSponsoredSession.revoke() ─ POST /api/session/revoke ────────► routes.revoke (delete key and approval) ``` | Hop | Package and subpath | |---|---| | Provider, wallet gate, token-bearing fetch | `@pepu-chain/sdk/privy/react` | | Ensure-wallet route, `requireUser` | `@pepu-chain/sdk/privy/server` | | Five session routes | `@pepu-chain/sdk/combo` (`createSponsoredSessionRoutes`) | | Browser flow | `@pepu-chain/sdk/combo/react` (`useSponsoredSession`) | | Policies, owner approval, session account | `@pepu-chain/sdk/session/kernel` | | Kernel account and sponsored client | `@pepu-chain/sdk/aa/kernel` | | Endpoint resolution | `@pepu-chain/sdk` (`resolvePepuEndpoints`) | ## Step by step ### 1. Configure Privy and the environment ``` NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_APP_ID= PRIVY_APP_SECRET= PEPU_BUNDLER_URL=https://bundler.pepeunchained.com # server only; the SDK default, so optional PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL=https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/ # server only; a credential SESSION_DURATION_MINUTES=15 # optional; 1 to 1440 PEPU_RPC_URL= # optional authenticated RPC for server chain reads ``` Failure modes: login fails or loops (origin, including port); the page shows a setup screen listing what is missing (an env var is empty); `/api/session/*` answers `CONFIG_MISSING_ENV` (a call target or a URL is unset). Caught by: `npm run doctor`, `pepu_check_env`, `pepu_check_privy_config`. ### 2. Ensure the wallet ```tsx // app/providers.tsx ("use client") import { PepuPrivyProvider } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/privy/react"; {children} ``` ```ts // app/api/wallet/ensure/route.ts import { createEnsureWalletRoute } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/privy/server"; export const { POST } = createEnsureWalletRoute(); ``` Wrap the signed-in view in `WalletGate` from `/privy/react`. The owner of the Kernel account is the embedded wallet, so it must exist before a session can start. Failure modes: "Creating your wallet..." hangs (a custom provider is in use), ensure route 401 or 500 (secret), `WalletGate` stalled (reload). See [Social Login and Embedded Wallets](privy-embedded-wallets.md). ### 3. Define one scope and mount the routes The scope is one shared object imported by both the server routes and the browser, so the policy the user signs and the one the server issued cannot drift. ```ts // lib/scope.ts import { getContract, isDeployed, pepuMainnet } from "@pepu-chain/sdk"; import type { KernelSessionCall } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/session/kernel"; import { tapScoreAbi } from "./tapscore"; const entry = getContract(pepuMainnet.id, "tapScore"); if (!isDeployed(entry)) throw new Error("TapScore is not deployed in the SDK registry."); export const TAPSCORE_ADDRESS = entry.address; export const scope: { calls: readonly KernelSessionCall[] } = { calls: [{ target: TAPSCORE_ADDRESS, abi: tapScoreAbi, functionName: "tap" }], }; ``` ```ts // lib/session-routes.ts import "server-only"; import { createMemoryStore, createSponsoredSessionRoutes } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/combo"; import { scope, TAPSCORE_ADDRESS } from "./scope"; import { tapScoreAbi } from "./tapscore"; export const routes = createSponsoredSessionRoutes({ scope, store: createMemoryStore(), // DEV ONLY: lost on restart, holds session keys in plaintext act: { parse: () => ({}), buildCalls: () => [{ to: TAPSCORE_ADDRESS, abi: tapScoreAbi, functionName: "tap" }], }, }); ``` Each route file is a one-line mount: `app/api/session/prepare/route.ts` exports `routes.prepare.POST`, and likewise `activate` (POST), `status` (GET), `act` (POST) and `revoke` (POST). Defaults match what `useSponsoredSession` calls. Options worth knowing: `endpoints` (explicit bundler and paymaster URLs), `minutes`, `authenticate` (custom auth), `publicClient`, `privy`. Failure modes: a malformed scope throws at startup; an empty call target makes every route answer `CONFIG_MISSING_ENV` instead. ### 4. Start the session in the browser ```tsx "use client"; import { useSponsoredSession, type SponsoredActResult } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/combo/react"; import { describeKernelSessionScope } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/session/kernel"; import { scope } from "@/lib/scope"; export function SessionFlow() { const { phase, statusLoading, smartAccount, owner, expiresAt, actions, grant, act, revoke, error } = useSponsoredSession({ scope }); if (statusLoading) return

Checking session...

; if (phase === "ready" || phase === "expired") { const preview = describeKernelSessionScope({ calls: scope.calls, validUntil: Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000) + 900 }); // Render preview.calls as the consent screen, then: return ; } if (phase === "active") { return ( <> ); } return

{error?.message ?? phase}

; } ``` `grant()` runs prepare, the one owner signature and activate. `phase` is one of `signed-out`, `provisioning`, `ready`, `granting`, `active`, `expired`, `error`. `smartAccount` (the Kernel address) is a read and is known before any session exists; show it, not the owner address, as the account that transacts. Failure modes: Privy's signature prompt for `eth_signTypedData_v4` on chain 97741 does not appear or errors (not exercised by a person yet; check the Privy dashboard and the console); the scope on the browser differs from the server's (400 `SESSION_APPROVAL_MISMATCH`); the offer expired before the user approved (410 `SESSION_EXPIRED`, call grant again). ### 5. Act `act(input)` posts to the act route. The server re-checks the calls against the scope (`assertCallsInScope`, fail fast), takes a per-user lock, loads the session account, sends one UserOperation and waits up to 90 seconds for the receipt. The first action of a session also deploys the Kernel account and enables the permission on-chain, so it costs more. The result tells you who paid: `paymaster` is the sponsoring contract, and `actualGasCostWei` is a decimal string. Failure modes: | Response | Meaning | Fix | |---|---|---| | 409 `SESSION_NONE` | No live approved session | Grant again | | 403 `POLICY_UNSCOPED` | A call is outside the scope | Fix `buildCalls`, or widen the scope on purpose | | 429 "An action is already in flight" | Another act is running for this user | Retry shortly | | `PAYMASTER_*` or `AA3x` | Sponsorship denied or no deposit | See [Sponsored Transactions](sponsored-transactions.md) | | `trailing-hour spend ... would exceed cap` | Per-user caps below the reservation (about 20.5 PEPU first operation, 6.9 later) | Raise caps; `SESSION_GAS_RESERVATION_PEPU` exports the numbers | | `BUNDLER_AA_FAILED` `AA25` | Nonce conflict | Wait and retry | | `BUNDLER_UNREACHABLE` | `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` unset or down | Fix the URL; `pepu_bundler_health` | ### 6. Revoke `revoke()` deletes the server-held key and approval at once, so the app can no longer act. It does not uninstall the permission on-chain (see below). Offer it anyway, and keep sessions short. ## What is enforced on-chain and what is not | Property | Enforced by | Strength | |---|---|---| | Only the listed contracts and function selectors, value at most `valueLimit` | Call policy v0.0.4 `0x9a52283276A0ec8740DF50bF01B28A80D880eaf2`, checked in UserOperation validation | On-chain. Holds even if your server is compromised | | Valid only until `validUntil` | Timestamp policy `0xB9f8f524bE6EcD8C945b1b87f9ae5C192FdCE20F` | On-chain | | The session is the one the owner approved | The owner's EIP-712 signature and the permission id | On-chain | | `assertCallsInScope`, approval and permission-id checks in `activate` | Your server | Off-chain, fail fast only. The chain is the real enforcement | | What the paymaster pays for | Paymaster policy service and contract | Off-chain allowlist plus on-chain signature check. Limits sponsorship money, not the user's account | | Revocation | Server deletes the key | Immediate for your app. On-chain the grant lapses at expiry | | Who owns the account | Owner address from Privy's records for the verified token, never from the request | Server check | ## Production notes - **`createMemoryStore()` is dev-grade.** A restart ends every session, it does not work across serverless instances, and the session private key sits in plaintext process memory. Production implements `SessionStore` (`get`, `set`, `delete`, `tryLock`, `unlock`) on a database or KV, encrypts `sessionPrivateKey` at rest, and uses an atomic or distributed lock for `tryLock`. Nothing else in the SDK changes. - **Gas budget.** Size the paymaster's per-user hourly and daily caps and your app's daily cap above the reservation numbers. - **Never expose** `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` and `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` to the browser. These routes run them server-side. - **Not production-ready as shipped.** The template says so itself, for the store reason above. ## Verify 1. `npm run doctor` (the template's script; runs the SDK's `checkPepuEnv`; prints no values). 2. `pepu_check_privy_config` with `appId`, `origin: "http://localhost:3000"`, `pillars: ["login"]`. 3. `pepu_sponsorship_status`: `available: true`, or read the `fixes`. 4. Prove it with no browser: `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL=... PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL=... npm run prove-session`. It sends real sponsored transactions on mainnet with throwaway keys that need no balance, and checks the account balance (0) and the score (2). 5. By hand: sign in, start a session, tap, confirm both addresses show 0 PEPU, open the explorer link, tap again (cheaper, no deploy), revoke. ### Doctor checks that catch each step | Step | Check | |---|---| | Env | `env.` fails for a missing, placeholder or malformed value (Privy id shape, URL shape, `SESSION_DURATION_MINUTES` positive) | | Privy id | `privy.app-id` format check | | Chain | `chain.rpc` reports chainId 97741 | | Sponsorship | `sponsorship.bundler` and `sponsorship.paymaster` (skip when unset, fail when set but unreachable) | | Dashboard | `privy.login-methods`, `privy.login-methods.google`, `privy.allowed-origins`, `privy.embedded-wallets` when a checker is injected; see [Privy Env Vars and Verification](../privy/env-and-checks.md) | ## Related - [Sponsored Session: No Popup, No Gas](sponsored-session.md) - [Session Keys](session-keys.md) - [Sponsored Transactions](sponsored-transactions.md) - [Trust and Security Model](../concepts/trust-and-security.md) - [Architecture: Who Calls What](../concepts/architecture.md) - [Sponsored Session App](../templates/sponsored-session-app.md) - [/combo](../sdk/combo.md), [/session/kernel](../sdk/session-kernel.md) - [Recipes: Sponsored Session in One Flow](../recipes/sponsored-session.md)

pages.title: Social Login and Embedded Wallets (Privy)
pages.content:
# Social Login and Embedded Wallets (Privy) Pillar 1 of the dev kit: a user signs in with Google (or email) and gets a self-custodial Privy embedded wallet on Pepe Unchained V2, with no seed phrase and no browser extension. This page covers the experience, the architecture and trust model, the SDK code, the dashboard settings it needs, the tools that automate it and the failures you will hit.
