It is the base for sessions and sponsorship, so read it before them. > Status: proven. A real Google login on a real Privy app created an embedded wallet through the server-side ensure-wallet route on PEPU mainnet, in the `consumer-app` template and in `game-app`. Not verified: concurrent and multi-tab first login. ## Prerequisites - A Privy app with its App ID and App Secret. Create one at [dashboard.privy.io](https://dashboard.privy.io). - The settings on [Dashboard Settings, Field by Field](../privy/dashboard-settings.md): Allowed origins with the exact port, Google enabled, embedded wallets on for Ethereum. - `@pepu-chain/sdk`, `@privy-io/react-auth`, `@privy-io/node`. Add `@privy-io/wagmi`, `wagmi` and `@tanstack/react-query` if you use wagmi hooks. - No bundler, no paymaster and no gas: login and wallet creation cost nothing. ## The user experience 1. The user clicks sign in and chooses Google (or email). 2. Privy handles the OAuth flow. The user lands back in your app authenticated. 3. `WalletGate` shows "Setting up your wallet..." for a moment while your server creates the embedded wallet. 4. The app renders with an address. The user never saw a seed phrase. The wallet is an EOA. On its own it is the only address the user has. With sponsorship or Kernel sessions there is a second, smart-account address; see [The Two-Address Model](two-address-model.md). ## Architecture and trust model ``` browser your Next.js server Privy ------- ------------------- ----- PepuPrivyProvider usePrivy().login() ───────────────────────────────────────────────► Google OAuth, user created WalletGate / useEnsureWallet POST /api/wallet/ensure ─────► createEnsureWalletRoute() Authorization: Bearer verifies the token (app secret) ──► verifyAccessToken finds an existing wallet ──► users()._get else creates one, owner = user ──► wallets().create ◄──── { address, created } refreshUser() (client picks up the wallet) ``` What this guarantees, and what it does not: - **The user id comes only from the verified access token.** The route never reads it from the body or query string. - **Your server gets no signing authority.** The wallet is created with `owner: { user_id }`. Your backend can create it, and cannot sign for it. Do not add a session signer in this route. Authority is only granted later, with the user's consent, by a session grant (see [Session Keys](session-keys.md)). - **The route is idempotent.** It looks for an existing Ethereum embedded wallet first, and re-checks after a failed create, so a double submit never makes a second wallet. - **Custody is Privy's, not yours.** Privy runs two execution modes. `legacy-embedded-wallets-only` reassembles keys on the user's device. `user-controlled-server-wallets-only`, which Privy calls TEE execution, reassembles them inside a secure enclave that only Privy's infrastructure can invoke, gated by the user's session. Both are self-custodial by Privy's description; the live tests ran with TEE. You are trusting Privy's infrastructure either way. See [Trust and Security Model](../concepts/trust-and-security.md). ### Why the server creates the wallet Privy's own client-side creation depends on the dashboard's "automatically create embedded wallets on login" setting. With it off, a Google login creates a user, but nothing creates the wallet, and Privy's "Creating your wallet..." screen hangs forever. This was reproduced live. Calling `useCreateWallet()` explicitly did not help, because it still runs through the same client-side machinery. The SDK avoids all of it: `createPepuPrivyConfig` sets `createOnLogin: "off"`, and `WalletGate` calls your ensure route right after login. The `createOnLogin` value you pass is largely symbolic, because Privy resolves it from the dashboard. Leave the dashboard setting on as well; having both is fine. ## Configure the dashboard Short list, in `.env.local` and the Privy dashboard. The field-by-field table is on [Dashboard Settings](../privy/dashboard-settings.md). | Where | Setting | Value | |---|---|---| | env | `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_APP_ID` | the App ID (public) | | env | `PRIVY_APP_SECRET` | the App Secret (server only) | | dashboard | Allowed origins | `http://localhost:3000` exactly, plus your production origin | | dashboard | Login methods | Google, plus any method you list in `loginMethods` | | dashboard | Embedded wallets | on for Ethereum | | dashboard | Smart Wallets | leave off unless you use the Privy Smart Wallets transport | ## SDK code Each snippet uses exports that exist today. Add `"use client"` in files that use the React entries. ### 1. Provider With wagmi (what the templates use), `PepuPrivyWagmiProvider` mounts Privy, react-query and wagmi in the order Privy requires, and pins the embedded wallet as wagmi's active account: ```tsx // app/providers.tsx "use client"; import { PepuPrivyWagmiProvider } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/privy/wagmi"; export function Providers({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) { return ( {children} ); } ``` Without wagmi, use `PepuPrivyProvider` from `@pepu-chain/sdk/privy/react` with the same props. When `appId` is missing it renders a notice naming the env variable instead of crashing inside Privy. Both providers build their config with `createPepuPrivyConfig`: mainnet only, `createOnLogin: "off"`, and Coinbase Wallet pinned to `eoaOnly` because Coinbase Smart Wallet does not support chain 97741. ### 2. Ensure-wallet route (server) ```ts // app/api/wallet/ensure/route.ts import { createEnsureWalletRoute } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/privy/server"; export const { POST } = createEnsureWalletRoute(); ``` It reads `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_APP_ID` and `PRIVY_APP_SECRET` through the SDK's single env reader and returns `{ address, created }`. It answers with typed JSON errors: 401 for a bad token, 500 for missing config, 502 if Privy cannot be reached. ### 3. Wallet gate (browser) ```tsx import { WalletGate, useEmbeddedWallet } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/privy/react"; function Home() { return ( ); } function Account() { const { address } = useEmbeddedWallet(); return

{address}

; } ``` `WalletGate` takes render props `loading`, `error(e, retry)` and `stalled(address, reload)` for your own markup. `useEmbeddedWallet` separates the embedded wallet from any external wallet (MetaMask, Phantom) that Privy is also tracking. Gate on the embedded wallet, never on "any connected wallet". The lower-level hook is `useEnsureWallet`, which returns `{ status, address, error, retry }` with status `idle`, `checking`, `creating`, `ready`, `stalled` or `error`. ### 4. Protect an API route ```ts // app/api/me/route.ts import { requireUser } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/privy/server"; export async function GET(request: Request) { const auth = await requireUser(request); if (!auth.ok) return auth.response; return Response.json({ userId: auth.user.userId, address: auth.user.address }); } ``` And the browser side, which attaches the Privy access token for you: ```tsx import { usePepuAuthFetch } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/privy/react"; const authFetch = usePepuAuthFetch(); const me = await authFetch("/api/me").then((r) => r.json()); ``` `requireUser` never throws. It returns either `{ ok: true, user }` or a ready `Response`. Lower-level pieces are `verifyRequestUser`, `createPrivyServer`, `findEmbeddedEthereumWallet` and `readPrivyServerEnv`. ### 5. Wagmi active account Left alone, an installed extension can silently become wagmi's active account, and balances and sends then act on the wrong wallet. `PepuPrivyWagmiProvider` mounts `useActiveWalletPin` to keep the embedded wallet active. Pass `pinEmbeddedWallet={false}` only for an app that is deliberately external-wallet-first. ## MCP tools and skills that automate it | Need | Tool or skill | |---|---| | Canonical code for the provider and the route | `pepu_sdk_snippet` with `privy-provider` or `wagmi-privy`, and `ensure-wallet-route` | | Check the env keys (presence and length, never values) | `pepu_check_env` | | Check dashboard settings and get the requirement table | `pepu_check_privy_config` | | Add login to an existing app | Slash command `/pepu-add-login` | | The agent's playbook | Skill `pepu-onboarding-privy` | | Scaffold the whole app | `pepu_scaffold_app` with template `consumer-app` | See [MCP Tool Reference](../mcp/tools.md), [Skills Catalog](../agent-tooling/skills.md) and [Claude Code Plugin](../agent-tooling/plugin.md). ## The template that demonstrates it `consumer-app`: sign in, see your address and PEPU balance, send a real transaction. It states plainly that gas is not sponsored. See [Consumer App](../templates/consumer-app.md). ```bash npx create-pepu-app@latest my-app --template consumer-app ``` ## What is proven | Claim | Evidence | |---|---| | Google login creates a Privy user on a PEPU app | Run live, mainnet, real Privy app | | The server-side ensure route creates the wallet when the dashboard creation setting is off | Run live in `consumer-app` and in `game-app` (before it moved onto the SDK); the grant and taps ran on a wallet created this way | | The pin keeps the embedded wallet active when an extension is installed | A live bug reproduced without it, fixed with it | | The SDK's version of all of this against a live Privy app | Typecheck, lint, build and unit tests pass; the SDK versions of the routes were checked by tests, with the original template versions proven live | | Concurrent or multi-tab first login | **Not verified** | | The exact fields Privy's public config returns | **Unverified**: the SDK treats every field as optional and reports `unknown`, not a failure | ## Common failures | Symptom | Cause | Fix | |---|---|---| | Login fails, iframe blocked, OAuth init 403 | The page origin is not in Allowed origins. Next.js moved to port 3001 because 3000 was taken | Free port 3000, or add the exact new origin to Allowed origins | | "Creating your wallet..." never ends | A custom `PrivyProvider` is in use and the dashboard creation setting is off | Use `PepuPrivyProvider`, which turns client creation off, and `WalletGate` | | `POST /api/wallet/ensure` returns 500 | `PRIVY_APP_SECRET` is unset on the server, or the dev server was not restarted after editing `.env.local` | Set it and restart; Next.js reads `.env.local` once | | `POST /api/wallet/ensure` returns 401 for a logged-in user | The access token does not verify: wrong secret for this app, or a stale `next dev` still holds the port | Check the secret belongs to the same app as the App ID; kill the leftover process | | `WalletGate` shows "stalled" | The server confirmed the wallet but this session has not seen it yet | Reload. It is a client sync delay, not a lost wallet | | Balances or sends use the wrong address | An extension became the active account | Use `PepuPrivyWagmiProvider`, or call `useActiveWalletPin()` once near the root | | Console: "configured chains are not supported by Coinbase Smart Wallet: 97741" | The Coinbase connector is not `eoaOnly` | Use the SDK provider, which pins it | | Console: "Unable to fetch token price" | Privy has no fiat price for PEPU | Harmless | | A transfer is refused in Privy's modal though the wallet can afford it | Privy's pre-flight gas check is conservative at PEPU's roughly 12,500 gwei base fee | Cannot be fixed in your code; see [Troubleshooting](../troubleshooting.md) | Testing without a faucet: login and wallet creation need no gas. An on-chain action needs a little PEPU, because there is no testnet faucet and the kit targets mainnet, where a transaction costs a fraction of a cent. ## Related - [Dashboard Settings, Field by Field](../privy/dashboard-settings.md) - [Privy Setup Walkthrough](privy-setup.md) - [The Two-Address Model](two-address-model.md) - [Session Keys](session-keys.md) - [Sponsored Transactions](sponsored-transactions.md) - [/privy](../sdk/privy.md), [/privy/react](../sdk/privy-react.md), [/privy/wagmi](../sdk/privy-wagmi.md), [/privy/server](../sdk/privy-server.md) - [Recipes: Provision the Wallet and Pin the Active Account](../recipes/provision-and-pin-the-wallet.md)

pages.title: Privy Setup
pages.content:
# Privy Setup

This page is the short first-time walkthrough for [Privy](https://privy.io). The complete table of every dashboard field, with exact values and failure symptoms, is [Dashboard Settings, Field by Field](../privy/dashboard-settings.md); authorization keys are in [Authorization Keys and Key Quorums](../privy/authorization-keys.md); verification is in [Privy Env Vars and Verification](../privy/env-and-checks.md). This page is the setup guide for using [Privy](https://privy.io) with Pepe Unchained V2: the Dashboard settings that decide whether login works, the code configuration, and the failures you are most likely to hit. Most of it was learned the hard way during live testing on mainnet, so it is more specific than Privy's own docs.

If you used `create-pepu-app`, the code configuration is already done. The Dashboard settings below are not: they live in your Privy app, not in your repository.

## What is proven

All three onboarding pillars have been exercised live on PEPU mainnet:

| Pillar | State |
|---|---|
| Google login and an embedded wallet | Proven. You can use it today. |
| Session signers for popup-free transactions | Proven. You can use it today. See [Session Keys](session-keys.md). |
| Gas sponsorship | Proven end to end through the hosted bundler (`https://bundler.pepeunchained.com`) and paymaster (`https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com`); the v2 paymaster is a canary, external audit pending. You need a funded project. See [Sponsored Transactions](sponsored-transactions.md). |
| Kernel session plus sponsorship (the combination) | Proven live in a browser on mainnet (2026-10-14). See [End to End](google-session-sponsored.md). |

## 1. Create the app and set the environment

1. Go to [dashboard.privy.io](https://dashboard.privy.io), sign up and create an app.
2. Copy the **App ID** and the **App Secret** from the app's settings.
3. Put them in `.env.local`:

```
NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_APP_ID=your-app-id-here
PRIVY_APP_SECRET=your-app-secret-here
```

The App ID is public by design (it is bundled into client JavaScript). The App Secret is server-only: never give it a `NEXT_PUBLIC_` prefix and never commit it. The templates use it in `POST /api/wallet/ensure` to verify the caller's access token and create their embedded wallet after login.

## 2. Dashboard settings that matter

### Allowed origins must include the exact port

Privy matches the full origin: scheme, host **and port**. For local development that means:

```
http://localhost:3000
```

`http://localhost` with no port is a different origin (an unspecified `http` port means 80), so it will not match.

The trap: if port 3000 is already in use, Next.js does not stop. It silently starts on 3001 instead, and login then fails with errors that do not mention the port (the login iframe is blocked by a CSP `frame-ancestors` rule, and OAuth init returns a 403). Free port 3000 rather than working around it with `-p 3001`. If you deliberately use another port, add that exact origin to **Allowed origins** first. Add your production origin the same way before you deploy.

### Automatically create embedded wallets on login

Turn on **Automatically create embedded wallets on login** in the Dashboard. The `createOnLogin` value you pass to `<PrivyProvider>` does not override the Dashboard: the Dashboard wins.

The templates also provision the wallet server-side right after login, through their own `POST /api/wallet/ensure` route (Privy's documented "pregenerate wallets" pattern, using `@privy-io/node` and your App Secret). That is a fallback for apps where the Dashboard setting is off or Privy's client-side creation screen stalls: without it, the user would sit on "Creating your wallet..." indefinitely. It creates a wallet owned by the signed-in user only if they do not already have one, and it gives your backend no authority to sign for that wallet.

You want both: the Dashboard setting on, and the server-side fallback left in place.

### Wallet execution mode: TEE

The live tests ran with Privy's **TEE execution** mode (`user-controlled-server-wallets-only` in Privy's SDK types). Wallets are reassembled inside a secure enclave that only Privy can invoke, gated by the user's authenticated session. Neither Privy nor your server sees the full private key. The older `legacy-embedded-wallets-only` mode reassembles keys on the user's device. Both are self-custodial; the difference is the mechanism. Use TEE mode unless you have a reason not to, and know which one your app is in, because it changes how wallet creation behaves.

### Smart Wallets (required only for `sponsored-demo`)

Smart Wallets is a separate Dashboard section. It is **required** for `sponsored-demo` (Privy Smart Wallets). It is **not** required for `sponsored-session-app` or the other templates: the SDK builds the ZeroDev Kernel account itself, and leaving it enabled is harmless (users then also get a Privy smart wallet linked, which the paymaster also accepts as owned). For `sponsored-demo` it needs:

- provider **Kernel** (ZeroDev) v3.1,
- custom chain **PEPU**, chain id **97741**, RPC `https://rpc-pepu-v2-mainnet-0.t.conduit.xyz`,
- bundler URL `https://bundler.pepeunchained.com`,
- paymaster URL `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<project client token ppt_...>`.

You need a claimed and funded project first (see [Sponsorship Tiers](sponsorship-tiers.md)). Use the **client token** with your app's origins allowed, because Privy calls the URL from the browser; never use the server key (`ppk_`) there. A static URL carries no per-user token, so the free tier is not reachable here and a funded project is required. Old dashboards may still hold temporary development bundler or paymaster URLs (such as tunnels); replace them with the hosted ones. Details are on [Sponsored Transactions](sponsored-transactions.md). If Smart Wallets is off for `sponsored-demo`, the page spins forever on "Setting up your smart wallet...".

Per-template requirements, including the game template's authorization key and quorum and the paymaster credentials of each sponsored template, are in [Dashboard Settings](../privy/dashboard-settings.md#per-template-requirements).

### Coinbase smart wallet: set `eoaOnly`

Coinbase's smart wallet does not support chain 97741. If you offer external-wallet login, restrict the Coinbase connector:

```tsx
externalWallets: {
  coinbaseWallet: { config: { preference: { options: "eoaOnly" } } },
},
```

Without it, the browser console fills with "The configured chains are not supported by Coinbase Smart Wallet: 97741". `eoaOnly` keeps the Coinbase extension and mobile paths working and drops the one that cannot work here.

## 3. Code configuration

Privy does not ship PEPU as a built-in chain, so give it a chain object. With the SDK:

```tsx
import { PrivyProvider } from "@privy-io/react-auth";
import { pepuMainnet } from "@pepu-chain/sdk";

<PrivyProvider
  appId={process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_APP_ID!}
  config={{
    loginMethods: ["email", "google"],
    defaultChain: pepuMainnet,
    supportedChains: [pepuMainnet],
    externalWallets: {
      coinbaseWallet: { config: { preference: { options: "eoaOnly" } } },
    },
  }}
>
  {/* your app */}
</PrivyProvider>;
```

`loginMethods` is a starting point, not the source of truth: the methods users actually see are the intersection of this list and what is enabled in the Dashboard. Enable them in both places or Privy hides them silently. Without `@pepu-chain/sdk` (`npm i @pepu-chain/sdk`; see [Quickstart](../get-started/quickstart-app.md)), define the chain yourself with viem's `defineChain` using the values on [Network Reference](../get-started/network-reference.md).

Privy's SDK options change between versions. If something here does not match your installed version, check [docs.privy.io](https://docs.privy.io); the chain object is the stable part.

## Troubleshooting

**Login fails, the iframe is blocked, or OAuth returns 403.** Almost always the origin. Check which port your dev server actually started on, then check **Allowed origins** for that exact `scheme://host:port`.

**"Creating your wallet..." never finishes.** Check that **Automatically create embedded wallets on login** is on, that `PRIVY_APP_SECRET` is set in `.env.local`, and that the dev server was restarted afterwards: Next.js reads `.env.local` once at startup, and a stale process keeps failing no matter how correct the file is. If `POST /api/wallet/ensure` returns 401 for a logged-in user, look for a leftover `next dev` still bound to the port.

**Wallet created but `useWallets()` is empty at first.** The client picks up the server-created wallet after a user refresh. The templates call `refreshUser()` and wait a bounded time for it to appear. If you build your own flow, do the same.

**"Setting up your smart wallet..." never clears.** Smart Wallets is not enabled for chain 97741 in the Dashboard, or the bundler and paymaster URLs are missing. See [Sponsored Transactions](sponsored-transactions.md).

**Console error: "The configured chains are not supported by Coinbase Smart Wallet: 97741".** Set the Coinbase connector to `eoaOnly` as above.

**Console error: "Unable to fetch token price".** Harmless. Privy cannot fetch a fiat price for PEPU, and the message does not affect login, wallets or transactions.

**A transfer is refused in Privy's confirmation modal even though the wallet can afford it.** Privy's own pre-flight gas estimate is conservative, and PEPU's base fee is around 12,500 gwei, so the estimate can exceed the real cost by enough to block a transfer the wallet could pay for. The check happens inside Privy's modal, so you cannot fix it in your own code. This is why the `consumer-app` template has no "Max" button. If your app sends transactions itself rather than through Privy's modal, `maxSendableAmount` in [`@pepu-chain/sdk`](../sdk/core.md#gas-and-fees) sizes a transfer correctly. See also [Troubleshooting](../troubleshooting.md).

**Server-side `eth_sendTransaction` fails with "Unsupported chain with id 97741".** Expected. See [Sign with Privy, Broadcast Yourself](../recipes/sign-with-privy-broadcast-yourself.md).

**The embedded wallet's address is not the address I see on pepuscan.** If you are using sponsorship, the account that transacts is a Kernel smart account at a different address. See [The Two-Address Model](two-address-model.md).

## Next

- [Session Keys: No Popup Per Transaction](session-keys.md)
- [Sponsored Transactions](sponsored-transactions.md)
- [The Two-Address Model](two-address-model.md)

Smart Accounts
pages.content:
# Smart Accounts

Pepe Unchained V2 has an ERC-4337 foundation deployed on mainnet: both EntryPoint versions, a ZeroDev Kernel v3 smart-account factory, and a v2 sponsored paymaster contract (a canary). Smart accounts are possible here, and sponsorship is proven working on top of them through PEPU's hosted bundler (`https://bundler.pepeunchained.com`) and paymaster service (`https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com`). Keep the two claims separate: an account existing is not the same as gas being sponsored for it.

Terms used on this page: [UserOperation](../reference/glossary.md), [bundler](../reference/glossary.md), [paymaster](../reference/glossary.md), [EntryPoint](../reference/glossary.md), [Kernel](../reference/glossary.md). All are defined in the [Glossary](../reference/glossary.md). Which smart-account setup to use: [Smart Account Paths](../concepts/smart-account-paths.md).

## What is live (mainnet only)

Deployed via ZeroDev's one-click Conduit Marketplace integration, plus a project-deployed paymaster:

| Contract | Address |
|---|---|
| EntryPoint v0.6 | `0x5FF137D4b0FDCD49DcA30c7CF57E578a026d2789` |
| EntryPoint v0.7 | `0x0000000071727De22E5E9d8BAf0edAc6f37da032` |
| Kernel v3 account factory | `0xaac5D4240AF87249B3f71BC8E4A2cae074A3E419` |
| Kernel MetaFactory | `0xd703aaE79538628d27099B8c4f621bE4CCd142d5` |
| Kernel ECDSA validator | `0x845ADb2C711129d4f3966735eD98a9F09fC4cE57` |
| Sponsored paymaster v2 (canary) | `0xdb28528C9399C33c9A0297E8A62F39145acbC30D` |
| Verifying paymaster v1 (retired) | `0x2B6FED323bFA24f0475f4e1Dd3C7F6Cc1f3ae8B0` |

Both EntryPoints are at their canonical addresses and the Kernel contracts are ZeroDev's standard v3 deployment. The v2 paymaster is this project's own contract, deployed on 2026-10-14 as a canary: internally reviewed 3x, external audit pending, funded in small tranches. The v1 paymaster was funded earlier and has since been withdrawn (its EntryPoint deposit is 0), so it cannot sponsor anything; never deposit to it. See [Deployed Contracts](../contracts/deployed-contracts.md) for the full table.

None of it is deployed on testnet. Testnet is out of scope for development; see [Network Reference](../get-started/network-reference.md#testnet-out-of-scope-today).

## What you can do today

- **Deploy and control a Kernel v3 smart account.** The factory and its ECDSA validator are live, so an account owned by an embedded wallet's key can be created at its counterfactual address and used. Without a paymaster it pays its own gas, exactly like an EOA.
- **Compute an account's address ahead of time**, from the factory's own on-chain `getAddress`, with [`@pepu-chain/sdk`](../sdk/aa.md) (`getKernelAccountAddress`) or the `pepu_smart_account_info` tool in the [MCP server](../agent-tooling/mcp-and-skills.md).
- **Inspect and verify the infrastructure.** The contracts are verified on pepuscan.

A smart account is a separate address from the embedded wallet that owns it. Read [The Two-Address Model](two-address-model.md) before you build UI around one.

## Sponsorship: proven and hosted

The full account of what is proven and what is missing is on [Sponsored Transactions](sponsored-transactions.md). The short version:

- **Proven:** a zero-balance Kernel smart account sent a transaction on mainnet and the paymaster paid for it, from a real Privy login, through the hosted [Alto](https://github.com/pimlicolabs/alto) bundler and ERC-7677 policy service (a project-sponsored operation from a fresh account holding 0 PEPU, paymaster paid 5.00 PEPU including account deployment).
- **Hosted URLs:** bundler `https://bundler.pepeunchained.com`, paymaster service `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com`; the ERC-7677 URL is `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<token>`. SDKs built around "construct a UserOperation, hand it to a bundler client" (permissionless.js, ZeroDev, Pimlico) can point at the bundler. The chain's standard RPC endpoints do not implement the ERC-4337 bundler methods.
- **You must bring a project:** the free tier needs a verified Privy token from PEPU's own Privy app and is not available to third-party apps. Your app claims a project, sets targets and limits, deposits and gets a token. See [Sponsorship Tiers](sponsorship-tiers.md).

The v2 paymaster is a canary with the external audit pending: deposit small amounts.

## The manual path, and when it makes sense

`EntryPoint.handleOps()` is an ordinary public function. A determined developer can construct a UserOperation by hand, sign it with a Kernel account's owner key, and submit it in a plain transaction from any funded EOA, acting as a single-operation bundler. It is a valid use of the deployed contracts and exercises a Kernel account without a hosted bundler.

It is also low-level and easy to get wrong (UserOperation hashing, gas-limit packing and signature encoding must match the EntryPoint's expectations exactly), and the submitting EOA pays real gas, with no sponsorship shortcut. Treat it as a way to validate the infrastructure or build tooling on it, not a path for a typical app. For popup-free interaction, use [Session Keys](session-keys.md), which works on a plain embedded wallet.

## What remains

- The external audit of the v2 paymaster (the canary is internally reviewed 3x).

The contracts and the hosted services are live; the end-to-end flow has been proven.

## Related

- [Sponsored Transactions](sponsored-transactions.md)
- [The Two-Address Model](two-address-model.md)
- [Session Keys](session-keys.md)
- [Privy Setup](privy-setup.md)
- [Deployed Contracts](../contracts/deployed-contracts.md)
- [EntryPoints and Kernel](../contracts/entrypoints-and-kernel.md)
- [Sponsored Session](sponsored-session.md): Kernel session keys on this stack

pages.title: Sponsored Session: No Popup, No Gas
pages.content:
# Sponsored Session: No Popup, No Gas

The three onboarding pillars in one flow: sign in with Google, approve one scoped session, then act with no wallet popup and no gas from the user. This page is the status and template summary. The full walkthrough, with every step, its SDK calls and its failure modes, is [Google Login, Session and Sponsorship End to End](google-session-sponsored.md).

> Status: proven on PEPU mainnet by script and proven live in a browser on mainnet (2026-10-14) against the hosted bundler and v2 paymaster. The hosted bundler and paymaster are live. See the table.

Terms used on this page: [UserOperation](../reference/glossary.md), [Kernel](../reference/glossary.md), [session key](../reference/glossary.md), [paymaster](../reference/glossary.md), [project](../reference/glossary.md). All are defined in the [Glossary](../reference/glossary.md).

```bash
npx create-pepu-app@latest my-app --template sponsored-session-app
```

## Prerequisites

- A Privy app with Google on, `http://localhost:3000` in Allowed origins and embedded wallets on. No Smart Wallets setting. See [Dashboard Settings](../privy/dashboard-settings.md).
- The hosted bundler (`https://bundler.pepeunchained.com`, the SDK default) and a paymaster URL with your project's server key: `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL=https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<project server key>` (secret, server only). You need a claimed and funded project; see [Sponsorship Tiers](sponsorship-tiers.md). To run your own services instead, the local defaults are `http://localhost:4337` and `http://localhost:8788`.

## Status

| | State |
|---|---|
| Mechanism on PEPU mainnet | **Proven.** `npm run prove-session`: one owner signature, then sponsored UserOperations signed by a session key alone, from an account holding 0 PEPU. Re-proven after the move onto the SDK. |
| Scope enforced on-chain | **Proven.** A different function on the allowed contract is rejected by the account's validation; an expired grant is refused. |
| Contracts | All present on chain 97741. Nothing had to be deployed. |
| Google login and the in-browser signature | **Proven live in a browser on mainnet (2026-10-14)** in this template's UI: Google sign-in, one Privy `eth_signTypedData_v4` signature on chain 97741, sponsored taps with no popup, revoke. |
| Available to app developers | **Yes, with a project.** The hosted endpoints are live (proven). You claim and fund a project and use its server key. The free tier is not available to third-party apps. The v2 paymaster is a canary: external audit pending. |
| Production readiness | **No**: sessions are stored in server memory by default. |

## How it differs from the other two pillar pages

- [Session Keys](session-keys.md), Privy mode: Privy session signers on a plain EOA. Scope enforced by Privy's backend, and the user pays gas.
- [Sponsored Transactions](sponsored-transactions.md): gas sponsored, but the owner signs every transaction.
- **This page:** a ZeroDev Kernel permission (call policy plus timestamp policy) installed by one owner signature. A session key held by your server signs UserOperations and a paymaster pays. The limits live on-chain in the user's smart account.

Because Privy's smart-wallet client cannot install a scoped session validator, the SDK builds the Kernel account itself (Path 1, ZeroDev-native). You do not enable Smart Wallets in the Privy dashboard. See [Smart Account Paths](../concepts/smart-account-paths.md) for how this differs from Privy Smart Wallets and when to pick each.

## What it is built from

| Job | SDK |
|---|---|
| Provider, wallet gate, ensure route | `PepuPrivyProvider`, `WalletGate` (`/privy/react`), `createEnsureWalletRoute` (`/privy/server`) |
| The five routes: prepare, activate, status, act, revoke | `createSponsoredSessionRoutes`, `createMemoryStore` (`/combo`) |
| The browser flow | `useSponsoredSession` (`/combo/react`) |
| Policies, owner approval, session account | `buildKernelSessionPolicies`, `approveKernelSession`, `loadKernelSessionAccount` (`/session/kernel`) |
| Gas numbers | `SESSION_GAS_RESERVATION_PEPU` (`/session/kernel`) |

Template layout: `lib/scope.ts` defines the one scope; `lib/session-routes.ts` is `createSponsoredSessionRoutes` plus the store; `app/api/session/{prepare,activate,status,act,revoke}` are one-line mounts; `components/session-flow.tsx` is the flow on `useSponsoredSession`; `scripts/prove-session.ts` is the live proof. See [Sponsored Session App](../templates/sponsored-session-app.md).

## Trust model

- The owner key never leaves Privy and the browser. The server holds only the session key.
- A compromised server or leaked session key can do only what the permission allows until it expires.
- "Revoke" deletes the key on the server at once. It does not uninstall the permission on-chain: that is an owner-signed call to the user's own account, which a destination-allowlisted paymaster should not sponsor. The grant lapses at expiry, so keep sessions short (default 15 minutes, clamped to 24 hours).
- The default store is in memory. Production needs a real `SessionStore` with the session key encrypted at rest.
- Sponsorship is a separate trust relationship: the paymaster operator chooses what to pay for, within its caps. Size per-user caps for a session's first operation (deploy plus enable permission), which reserved about 20.5 PEPU worst case in testing, and about 6.9 PEPU for later operations.

## Contracts used

Call policy v0.0.4 (`0x9a52283276A0ec8740DF50bF01B28A80D880eaf2`), timestamp policy (`0xB9f8f524bE6EcD8C945b1b87f9ae5C192FdCE20F`) and ECDSA signer module (`0x6A6F069E2a08c2468e7724Ab3250CdBFBA14D4FF`), on top of the Kernel v3.1 factory (`0xaac5D4240AF87249B3f71BC8E4A2cae074A3E419`) and ECDSA validator (`0x845ADb2C711129d4f3966735eD98a9F09fC4cE57`). Call policy v0.0.5 is not deployed on PEPU, so v0.0.4 is pinned. See [EntryPoints and Kernel](../contracts/entrypoints-and-kernel.md) and [Deployed Contracts](../contracts/deployed-contracts.md).

## Common failures

See the per-step tables in [Google Login, Session and Sponsorship End to End](google-session-sponsored.md). The two that bite first: `SESSION_APPROVAL_MISMATCH` (browser and server use different scopes; import one shared `scope`) and `trailing-hour spend ... would exceed cap` (per-user caps below the first-operation reservation).

## Related

- [Smart Account Paths: which one to use](../concepts/smart-account-paths.md)
- [The Two-Address Model](two-address-model.md)
- [Session Keys](session-keys.md)
- [Sponsored Transactions](sponsored-transactions.md)
- [Trust and Security Model](../concepts/trust-and-security.md)

pages.title: Sponsored Transactions
pages.content:
# Sponsored Transactions

Pillar 3 of the dev kit: a user with a wallet holding zero PEPU sends a transaction and a paymaster pays the gas. This page states what is proven and what is hosted, explains the architecture and trust model, gives the SDK code for both transports, lists the Privy settings, and maps the failures. It is the base for the sponsored session in [Google Login, Session and Sponsorship End to End](google-session-sponsored.md).

> Status: proven on mainnet, hosted. The bundler (`https://bundler.pepeunchained.com`) and the paymaster service (`https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com`) are live. A project-sponsored operation from a fresh Kernel account holding 0 PEPU went through both: userOp `0x8150850431639387f95c14e2c1f7c857eb833b7b8e0826426dfcbb683d6b9907`, tx `0x6b803ad49091d6758b413065ac54d09774413b55a234d873f8e371243f4e3209`; the paymaster paid 5.00 PEPU of gas including the account deployment, and the project ledger went from 25 to 19.80 PEPU. The paymaster is the v2 `PepuSponsoredPaymasterV7` at `0xdb28528C9399C33c9A0297E8A62F39145acbC30D`, deployed as a canary: internally reviewed 3x, external audit pending, funded in small tranches. The v1 paymaster is retired. See [Sponsorship Tiers](sponsorship-tiers.md).

Terms used on this page: [UserOperation](../reference/glossary.md), [bundler](../reference/glossary.md), [paymaster](../reference/glossary.md), [EntryPoint](../reference/glossary.md), [Kernel](../reference/glossary.md), [project](../reference/glossary.md), [free tier](../reference/glossary.md). All are defined in the [Glossary](../reference/glossary.md).

Sponsorship works and the services are hosted, but it is not automatic for your app: you must bring a project (or, for PEPU's own apps, use the free tier). Do not tell users a transaction is "gasless" until you have configured and tested one. `usePepuSponsorship` and the `pepu_sponsorship_status` MCP tool answer the question live.

## Prerequisites

- Pillar 1 working ([Social Login and Embedded Wallets](privy-embedded-wallets.md)).
- A bundler for chain 97741 (ERC-4337, EntryPoint v0.7) and an ERC-7677 paymaster. PEPU hosts both (below). To run your own from `services/`, the local development defaults are `http://localhost:4337` and `http://localhost:8788`; `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` and `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` override the hosted defaults.
- A way to pay, which is the part you must configure:
  - **Free tier (PEPU's own apps only).** Needs a verified Privy access token from PEPU's own Privy app in the ERC-7677 context (`context.privyAccessToken`; REST: `Authorization: Bearer`). A third-party app's own Privy token is ignored for billing and does not unlock the free tier. The Privy Smart Wallets dashboard URL is static and cannot attach a token, so the free tier is not reachable there. Per user: 100 PEPU a day and 50 PEPU an hour; free-tier targets are TapScore only for now.
  - **Your own project (any app).** SIWE login (`/v2/auth/nonce`, `/v2/auth/login`), verify your Privy app (`POST /v2/projects/verify`, app id and secret used for one request and never stored), claim (`claimProject`; immediate if empty, pending 48 hours if already funded), set targets and limits (`setTargets`, `setDailyLimit`, `setSenderDailyLimit`), deposit (`depositFor`, one-way), register the project, then set allowed origins for the client token. Full steps: [Sponsorship Tiers](sponsorship-tiers.md).
- Your target contract on the paymaster's destination allowlist and on your registered app's allowed destinations.

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| Chain ID | `97741` |
| Bundler URL | `https://bundler.pepeunchained.com` (SDK default; `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` overrides) |
| Paymaster service | `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com` (SDK default base; `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` overrides) |
| ERC-7677 URL | `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<token>`; always embeds a token, so there is no tokenless default |
| v2 paymaster contract (canary) | `0xdb28528C9399C33c9A0297E8A62F39145acbC30D` (public, on-chain) |
| Retired v1 paymaster | `0x2B6FED323bFA24f0475f4e1Dd3C7F6Cc1f3ae8B0`: withdrawn, cannot sponsor, never deposit to it |
| EntryPoint v0.7 | `0x0000000071727De22E5E9d8BAf0edAc6f37da032` |

The SDK's single swap point for hosted URLs is `src/endpoints.ts` (`PEPU_HOSTED`): `{ bundlerUrl, paymasterBaseUrl, paymasterUrl: null }`. `resolvePepuEndpoints()` resolves, per value: explicit option, then the server env variable, then the `NEXT_PUBLIC_` variant, then the hosted default. It returns `bundlerUrl`, `paymasterBaseUrl` (the hosted base, or `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` with its `/v2/paymaster/<token>` tail stripped) and `paymasterUrl` (the complete ERC-7677 URL, or `null` when you have not supplied a token). Helpers: `hostedErc7677Url(token)` from `@pepu-chain/sdk/paymaster`, `hostedFreeTierUrl()` from `@pepu-chain/sdk`, `paymasterBaseOf(url)`, `buildErc7677Url({ baseUrl, token, version })`, and `isHostedSponsorshipLive()` (true).

## Architecture and trust model

A sponsored transaction is an ERC-4337 UserOperation. Five pieces cooperate:

1. **The user's smart account.** A ZeroDev Kernel v3.1 account owned by the embedded wallet. It is a different address from the wallet: see [The Two-Address Model](two-address-model.md).
2. **A bundler.** Accepts `eth_sendUserOperation` and gas estimation, and submits through the EntryPoint. PEPU's is a hosted Alto instance configured for Nitro's dual-fee gas (`--chain-type arbitrum`). The chain's standard RPC does not serve these methods.
3. **A paymaster contract.** Pays gas from its EntryPoint deposit after checking a signature from an authorized signer. The v2 contract holds per-project balances, daily limits and a destination allowlist on-chain; the retired v1 contract enforced no spending cap of its own.
4. **A policy service.** The off-chain ERC-7677 endpoint (`pm_getPaymasterStubData`, `pm_getPaymasterData`). It signs only if every rule passes: destination allowlist, per-user and per-app spend and count caps, and a global daily circuit breaker.
5. **The client.** Either Privy Smart Wallets or the SDK's `direct` transport.

What you trust: the paymaster operator decides what to pay for, within its caps. The destination allowlist is the real boundary: a sponsored call can only target approved contracts, so a drained budget can only pay for calls to approved contracts. The signer key is a hot wallet for the deposit, so the deposit is kept small and monitored. A paymaster URL is a credential: anyone holding it can request sponsorship as that app, within its caps. Details: [Infrastructure Map](../infra/overview.md), [Policy, Caps and the Circuit Breaker](../infra/paymaster/policy-and-caps.md), [Credential Matrix](../infra/paymaster/auth.md).

## The two transports

These are two smart-account paths: `privy-smart-wallets` is Path 2 (Privy builds the Kernel account) and `direct` is Path 1 (the SDK builds it, ZeroDev-native). [Smart Account Paths](../concepts/smart-account-paths.md) explains when to use each, what each can and cannot do, and how to migrate between them.

| | `privy-smart-wallets` (default) | `direct` |
|---|---|---|
| Who builds the smart account | Privy's smart-wallet client | The SDK, with ZeroDev (`toPepuKernelAccount`) |
| Where the URLs live | The Privy dashboard, Smart Wallets, chain 97741, provider Kernel | Your env, or options passed to the hook |
| Dashboard needs | Smart Wallets configured | Nothing beyond pillar 1 |
| Extra peers | None from ZeroDev | `@zerodev/sdk`, `@zerodev/ecdsa-validator` |
| Who signs | The owner, per transaction | The owner, per transaction (unless you use a session) |
| Credential exposure | The paymaster URL is stored in Privy's dashboard | The URL must reach the browser (`NEXT_PUBLIC_`), or you send from a server |
| Free-tier context | Not sent | The Privy access token is passed as paymaster context |
| Used by | `sponsored-demo` | `sponsored-session-app` (server side, with a session key) |

A smart-wallet page that spins forever on "Setting up your smart wallet..." means Smart Wallets is not configured for chain 97741 in the dashboard. That is not fixable in code.

## SDK code

### Browser: `useSponsoredSend`

```tsx
"use client";
import { useSponsoredSend, usePepuSmartAccount, usePepuSponsorship } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/aa/react";
import { WalletGate } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/privy/react";

function Tap() {
  const { smartAccount } = usePepuSmartAccount();      // the Kernel address, not the EOA
  const sponsorship = usePepuSponsorship();            // live probe of bundler and paymaster
  const { send, status, result, error } = useSponsoredSend({ transport: "privy-smart-wallets" });
  return (
    <button
      disabled={status === "signing" || status === "submitting"}
      onClick={() => send([{ to: tapScoreAddress, abi: tapScoreAbi, functionName: "tap" }])}
    >
      Tap from {smartAccount}
    </button>
  );
}
```

`send(calls)` takes `Call[]`, sends one UserOperation and resolves `SponsoredResult`: `userOpHash`, `transactionHash`, `success`, `paymaster`, `actualGasCostWei`, `explorerUrl`. Status is `idle`, `signing`, `submitting`, `confirmed` or `error`. One send at a time: a second call while one is in flight throws. Errors are typed: `describeUserOpFailure` turns AAxx codes and paymaster reasons into `PepuError`s with a `code` and a `hint`, with tokens and keys redacted. For `privy-smart-wallets`, wrap the app in Privy's `SmartWalletsProvider` nested inside the Privy provider (`composeProviders` from `/privy/react` builds the nesting).

For your own bundler and paymaster, use `useDirectSponsoredSend` from `@pepu-chain/sdk/aa/react-direct` (peers `@zerodev/sdk` and `@zerodev/ecdsa-validator`). Pass the URLs explicitly in browser code, because frameworks only inline literal `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_X` reads:

```tsx
import { useDirectSponsoredSend } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/aa/react-direct";

const { send } = useDirectSponsoredSend({
  bundlerUrl: process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_PEPU_BUNDLER_URL,
  paymasterUrl: process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL,
});
```

Everything with `NEXT_PUBLIC_` is visible to every visitor. A paymaster URL carries a token: a project client token (`ppt_`) is publishable but only works from its allowed origins, whereas a server key (`ppk_`) must never reach a browser. Prefer the Privy transport for browser sends, or send from a server with a session key (the combination).

### Server or script: `sendSponsored`

```ts
import { createPublicClient, http } from "viem";
import { pepuMainnet } from "@pepu-chain/sdk";
import { createPepuSponsoredClient, sendSponsored, toPepuKernelAccount } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/aa/kernel";

const publicClient = createPublicClient({ chain: pepuMainnet, transport: http() });
const account = await toPepuKernelAccount({ publicClient, owner }); // owner: a viem account or wallet client
const client = createPepuSponsoredClient({ account, paymasterToken: process.env.PEPU_PAYMASTER_TOKEN }); // server key (secret)
const r = await sendSponsored({ client, calls: [{ to, abi, functionName: "tap" }] });
console.log(r.paymaster, r.actualGasCostWei, r.explorerUrl);
```

`createPepuSponsoredClient` sends through the hosted bundler (or `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL`) with gas paid by your paymaster, and takes fees from the chain with 20% headroom. Pass a `paymasterToken` (your project's server key on a backend) and it builds `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<token>` against the hosted base; `createPepuPaymasterClient` accepts the same option, and `requirePaymasterUrl(explicit?, token?)` does the resolution. With no token and no `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` it throws a typed `CONFIG_MISSING_ENV` error rather than guessing one.

### Check availability and prove it

```ts
import { checkSponsorship } from "@pepu-chain/sdk";
import { getPaymasterDeposit } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/aa";

const s = await checkSponsorship({ publicClient });   // never throws for an unreachable service
if (!s.available) console.log(s.reason, s.fixes);
```

The proof a sponsorship really happened is not the transaction hash. It is the paymaster's EntryPoint deposit dropping (`getPaymasterDeposit` before and after) while the smart account stays at 0 PEPU. The result's `paymaster` field also names who paid.

`getSponsorshipStatus` is deprecated and always says unavailable; use `checkSponsorship`.

## Privy dashboard

Only the `privy-smart-wallets` transport needs Smart Wallets. For chain 97741, choose provider **Kernel**, enter the bundler URL `https://bundler.pepeunchained.com` and the paymaster URL `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<project token>`. Use your project's client token (`ppt_`) with your app's origins allowed, because Privy calls from the browser; never use the server key (`ppk_`) there. The dashboard URL is static and cannot attach a Privy token, so the free tier is not reachable from it. Field detail: [Dashboard Settings](../privy/dashboard-settings.md). Allowed origins and embedded wallets apply to both transports.

## Tools and template

| Need | Tool |
|---|---|
| "Can I send a sponsored transaction right now?" | `pepu_sponsorship_status` |
| Bundler or paymaster health | `pepu_bundler_health`, `pepu_paymaster_health` |
| Canonical code | `pepu_sdk_snippet` with `sponsored-send`, `sponsored-send-server`, `check-sponsorship` |
| Explain a failure | `pepu_explain_error`, `pepu_explain_tx` |
| Slash command and skill | `/pepu-add-sponsorship`, skill `pepu-sponsored-transactions` |

Template: `sponsored-demo`: sign in, get a Kernel account at 0 PEPU, click one button, watch the paymaster deposit drop. See [Sponsored Demo](../templates/sponsored-demo.md).

## What is proven

| Claim | Evidence |
|---|---|
| A zero-balance Kernel account sent a project-sponsored transaction through the hosted URLs (v2) | Proven: userOp `0x8150850431639387f95c14e2c1f7c857eb833b7b8e0826426dfcbb683d6b9907`, tx `0x6b803ad49091d6758b413065ac54d09774413b55a234d873f8e371243f4e3209`; paymaster paid 5.00 PEPU including account deployment, project ledger 25 to 19.80 PEPU |
| Earlier history (v1) | tx `0x57cf2f5a332248476d775c096b4b8339d81867c14211ed3bc4fcb1895dff0f9f`, through the hosted URLs with the v1 paymaster, which has since been withdrawn and retired |
| Sponsorship for app developers | Available through a project you claim and fund; see [Sponsorship Tiers](sponsorship-tiers.md) |
| v2 tiered paymaster | **Proven on mainnet (canary, external audit pending)**: internally reviewed 3x, funded in small tranches |
| Worst-case reservation | Measured: a first operation that deploys the account reserves about 12 PEPU at PEPU's gas price, a follow-up about 3 PEPU (2026-10-01; moves with the gas price); a session's first operation about 20.5 PEPU |

## Common failures

| `code` or symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `PAYMASTER_DESTINATION_NOT_ALLOWED` | The call targets a contract not on the allowlist | Add the contract to the global allowlist and your app's allowed destinations |
| `PAYMASTER_ORIGIN_NOT_ALLOWED` | The page origin is not allowed | Allow the exact origin, port included |
| `PAYMASTER_DENIED`, `AA32` to `AA34` | Credential or sender rejected, or the policy signer does not match the contract | Check the app key in the URL and that the account belongs to the signed-in user |
| `PAYMASTER_NO_BALANCE`, `AA31` | The project's balance (or the paymaster's EntryPoint deposit) cannot cover the operation | Deposit PEPU into the project (`depositFor`); deposits are one-way |
| `project_origin_not_allowed` | A client token (`ppt_`) was used with no allowed origins, or from another origin | Set the project's allowed origins, or use the server key (`ppk_`) from a backend |
| `PAYMASTER_CAP` | A per-op, per-user, per-app or global cap was hit | Wait for the window or raise the limits |
| `BUNDLER_AA_FAILED` (`AA25`) | Invalid nonce: another operation from this account is pending | Wait for it, then retry |
| `BUNDLER_UNREACHABLE` | The bundler URL is wrong or unreachable | Check `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` (default `https://bundler.pepeunchained.com`); run `pepu_bundler_health` |
| `trailing-hour spend ... would exceed cap` after the first action | Per-user caps are below the worst-case reservation | Size caps above the first-operation reservation |
| Browser `Failed to fetch` to the bundler | The bundler has CORS off while a browser calls it | Enable CORS and put the bundler behind a filtering proxy; see [Operating the Bundler](../infra/bundler/operating.md) |

Full catalog: [Error Reference](../reference/errors.md). Hosting, Alto settings, the ERC-7677 request shapes and the policy service are in [Infrastructure Map](../infra/overview.md), [ERC-7677 Methods](../infra/paymaster/erc7677.md) and [Bundler Overview](../infra/bundler/overview.md).

## Related

- [Smart Account Paths: which one to use](../concepts/smart-account-paths.md)
- [The Two-Address Model](two-address-model.md)
- [Smart Accounts](smart-accounts.md)
- [Sponsorship Tiers](sponsorship-tiers.md)
- [Sponsored Session](sponsored-session.md)
- [/aa](../sdk/aa.md), [/paymaster](../sdk/paymaster.md)
- [Recipes: Send a Sponsored Transaction](../recipes/sponsored-send.md)

pages.title: Sponsorship Tiers
pages.content:
# Sponsorship Tiers

This page describes the v2 tiered paymaster: a free tier funded by the chain for Privy users, and per-project deposits for everyone else. It explains how a project is claimed, funded and configured, what stops a stranger draining a budget, and what a developer must configure to use it.

> Status: proven on mainnet as a canary. The `PepuSponsoredPaymasterV7` contract is deployed on PEPU mainnet at `0xdb28528C9399C33c9A0297E8A62F39145acbC30D` (about block 10537341, 2026-10-14): deployed as a canary: internally reviewed 3x, external audit pending, funded in small tranches. A project-sponsored operation from a fresh Kernel account holding 0 PEPU went through `bundler.pepeunchained.com` and `paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<server key>` (userOp `0x8150850431639387f95c14e2c1f7c857eb833b7b8e0826426dfcbb683d6b9907`, tx `0x6b803ad49091d6758b413065ac54d09774413b55a234d873f8e371243f4e3209`); the paymaster paid 5.00 PEPU of gas including the account deployment and the project ledger went from 25 to 19.80 PEPU. Deposit small amounts until the external audit is done. The v1 paymaster is retired; see [Sponsored Transactions](sponsored-transactions.md).

## What you must configure

The free tier and the project tier are set up differently.

**The free tier (PEPU's own apps).** It needs a verified Privy access token from PEPU's own Privy app, sent in the ERC-7677 request as `context.privyAccessToken` (REST: `Authorization: Bearer`). A third-party app's own Privy token is ignored for billing and does not unlock the free tier, so the free tier is not available to third-party apps. The Privy Smart Wallets dashboard takes a static paymaster URL and cannot attach a token, so the free tier is not reachable there either. Third-party apps use a project.

**Your own project (any app).** In order:

1. Sign in with Ethereum (`/v2/auth/nonce`, `/v2/auth/login`).
2. Verify your Privy app: `POST /v2/projects/verify` with the Privy app id and secret (used for one request, never stored).
3. Claim the project (`claimProject`): immediate if the project is empty, pending 48 hours if someone already funded it.
4. Set the allowed targets and limits: `setTargets`, `setDailyLimit`, `setSenderDailyLimit`.
5. Deposit PEPU (`depositFor`). Deposits are one-way; nobody can withdraw them.
6. Register the project to get credentials: a client token (`ppt_`, publishable, works only from the allowed origins you set; with no origins, or from another origin, it is refused with `project_origin_not_allowed`) and a server key (`ppk_`, secret, for backends).
7. Set the allowed origins for the client token.

Then use `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<token>` as the ERC-7677 URL. The recipe is [Deposit and Claim a Paymaster Project](../recipes/v2-deposit-and-claim.md).

## The model

Public gas sponsorship needs an answer to "who pays". The design splits it in two:

| Tier | Funded by | Who draws on it | Bound |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Free tier** | The chain, from a "free pool" the contract owner funds (seeded with 300 PEPU) | **Users with a Privy account in PEPU's own Privy app only** (a verified Privy access token is required) | **100 PEPU per user per day and 50 PEPU per user per hour**, a 40 PEPU per-operation cap, and an on-chain per-wallet backstop. There is **no chain-wide daily ceiling**: gas funds can only pay gas, so a ceiling that limited the whole chain to a handful of heavy users was judged worse than the risk |
| **Project tier** | A project, which anyone can fund by depositing PEPU on-chain (deposits are one-way) | **Any wallet**: Privy users, non-Privy users, native or EOA wallets behind smart accounts | The project's on-chain balance, daily limit, per-wallet daily limit, destination allowlist and a cap on the gas price per operation |

For each operation the order is:

1. If the request belongs to a claimed project and that project can pay, **the project pays**.
2. Otherwise the operation falls to the **free tier**, but only if the user has a verified Privy account and still has free allowance.
3. Otherwise it is denied, with a reason for each tier tried.

The free tier **never pays for a project's non-Privy wallets**. If a project's balance runs out, those wallets are denied; they do not fall through to the chain's money. An operation is never split between tiers, and operations already approved are unaffected when a balance runs out.

The values (all configurable in the service, with the on-chain bounds in the contract):

- Free tier per user: 100 PEPU in a rolling 24 hours and 50 PEPU in a rolling hour (enforced by the service), and count caps (40 a day, 20 an hour). Free-tier targets are TapScore only for now (`0x261eA5971B93237a56990206A46Bc80318e4d078`); the manager can add more. The first operation, which deploys the user's smart account, costs about 12 PEPU worst case and normal operations about 3 PEPU.
- Maximum cost per operation: 40 PEPU.
- Project per-user cap in the service: default 200 PEPU a day, adjustable by the project up to an administrator maximum.
- Deposits cannot be withdrawn, by anyone. The timelock on the chain's signer and bundler changes is immutable and at least 48 hours; a project's defence during that window is to pause.
- Gas price cap: every sponsor has an on-chain cap on an operation's `maxFeePerGas` (a contract-wide default, 40,000 gwei in the deploy, about three times today's base fee; a project can set its own lower or higher cap, the chain sets the free pool's). The policy service also refuses operations whose gas limits or fees are out of bounds against the current base fee.
- Approval validity: 60 seconds.

## How a project uses it

Everything funds-related is a plain contract call. **Deposits need no registrar, administrator or API approval, and none of it requires the policy service.**

**Deposits are one-way.** Anyone can deposit into any project (even one nobody has claimed yet) and into the free pool. Nobody can withdraw: not the project owner, not the contract owner, not the manager. The only way PEPU leaves is as gas paid for the sponsored operations of that project or pool. A project is one Privy app, with the id `keccak256(appId)`; a stranger who funds your app's project does not harm you or your users, they only top up your gas budget. The trade-off: funds put into a project that is never claimed, or whose owner disappears, stay locked.

1. **Deposit (anyone).** `depositFor(projectId)`. Check who controls the project's settings first: `getProject(projectId)` returns the owner address, and `address(0)` means "not claimed yet" (the money is in the project's ledger but cannot be spent until someone claims it).
2. **Claim it (the app's developer).** Settings (the destination allowlist, limits, gas price cap, pause) belong to the project's owner, and ownership is proven on-chain with a signed attestation. The developer signs in with a wallet (Sign-In With Ethereum), then calls `POST /v2/projects/verify` with their Privy `appId`, Privy `appSecret` and wallet address. The service checks the secret against Privy's API and returns a short-lived, single-use attestation naming that wallet. The secret is used for one request and is never stored, logged or echoed; you can rotate it in the Privy dashboard afterwards. Submitting the attestation to the contract (`claimProject`) makes the wallet the owner immediately if the project holds no funds; if anyone has already deposited into it, the claim is pending for the contract's timelock (at least 48 hours, announced by an event, cancellable by the contract owner or manager) and anyone finishes it with `executeReclaim`, so claim before anyone funds the project. The claim sets no configuration, so nothing is sponsored yet: the owner then sets the allowlist (`setTargets`, the contracts the project will sponsor calls to; the contract rejects anything else) and the daily and per-wallet limits (`setDailyLimit`, `setSenderDailyLimit`; the contract rejects a project with no per-wallet limit). The attestation must be submitted within the hour. Use the Privy app id exactly as shown in the Privy dashboard (it is case-sensitive).
3. **Re-claim if you lose the wallet.** If a project already has an owner, a new attestation starts a re-claim (`reclaimProject`). It takes effect only after the contract's timelock (at least 48 hours), is announced by an event, and the current owner can cancel it (once per new owner: a second attested re-claim by the same wallet cannot be cancelled); a re-claim proposed before a signer was removed never executes, even if that signer is later re-added. When the owner changes, the previous owner's server key and client token stop working and the new owner issues fresh ones. For a voluntary handover to a multisig, use the two-step `proposeProjectOwner` / `acceptProjectOwnership` instead.
4. **Get credentials (convenience layer).** To have the policy service sign sponsorships, index the project. You get two credentials, each shown once:
   - a **server API key** for your backend. It works for any wallet and has no origin restriction. Never ship it to a browser.
   - a **publishable client token** (a paymaster URL, `https://<host>/v2/paymaster/<token>`, for the Privy Smart Wallets field or any ERC-7677 client). It can spend your budget **only from the origins you allow**.
5. **Manage it on-chain.** Allowlist changes, limits and pausing are transactions the owner signs. The API only encodes calldata; **funds never move through it.** Two optional per-project controls: `setMaxFeePerGas` (your own cap on the gas price per operation) and `setRequiredAccountCodehash` (only sponsor accounts whose code matches the one you pin; without it the destination allowlist is a usage policy for Kernel-shaped accounts, because a contract that mimics Kernel's `execute` selector can pass the check).
6. **Watch the contract's `AdminChangeProposed` events, and pause if you do not trust one.** The chain's operators can add a signer or a bundler, but only after the immutable timelock (at least 48 hours) following the proposal. Because deposits cannot be withdrawn, **pausing is a project's exit**: a paused project's balance cannot be spent by anyone, whatever the signer signs. Inside the same window you can also lower your gas price cap and limits. Removals of signers and bundlers are instant.

**Who can be the gatekeeper of ownership?** The policy service's signer. A compromised signer could claim a project nobody has claimed yet (at once if it is empty, after the timelock if it holds funds), or start a re-claim of an owned one, but it can never withdraw funds, because no withdrawal exists. A claim of a funded project and a re-claim are visible on-chain, take at least 48 hours, can be cancelled, and die if the signer is removed.

### What stops a stranger draining a project's budget

A project can sponsor wallets it has never seen, so identity is not the control. Authorization is:

- **Who may ask:** the secret server key (from your backend), or the client token from an allowed origin. A project with no allowed origins can only be used with its server key. Browsers enforce the origin check; a non-browser client can forge an `Origin` header, so it is a speed bump, not a wall.
- **The contract's own limits**, which hold even if the policy service or its signing key were abused: calls only to the project's allowlist, a per-wallet daily limit, a project-wide daily limit, and the project's balance.
- **The service's per-user daily cap**, and the option to require a verified Privy identity for a project that wants it.
- **Reservation caps against lock-out.** An approval that is never executed still holds budget in the service until its 60 second signature expires. Someone holding the public client token could request approvals for made-up wallets to lock honest users out, so a client token is limited to 2 unexecuted approvals per wallet, 5% of the budget per source address and 25% in total (never below two worst-case operations), plus a per-address rate limit. The server key is not limited this way. This reduces the attack rather than ruling it out: an attacker with many source addresses can still hold the client-token pool; rotate the token to cut them off.

The worst a leaked client token can spend is bounded by the project's own limits.

## Surplus and refunds

Each operation prepays its worst-case cost from the sponsor's balance and the unused part is refunded **to the exact sponsor that was charged**, in the post-operation step. A small residue is genuinely unattributable (the contract charges the post-operation overhead as a fixed gas amount, and EntryPoint's real cost differs slightly). That residue accumulates as unallocated deposit and can only be credited **to the free pool**, by anyone, above a small solvency buffer. No function sends it to the owner.

## Ownership

The deployer is the contract's owner by default. Ownership transfers in two steps (`transferOwnership` then `acceptOwnership`) and can be renounced. The owner controls the free pool's settings (its per-operation cap, gas price cap and per-wallet limit), the operational manager address, lowering the post-operation overhead, unlocking and withdrawing stake (a separate balance that is never part of any sponsor's money). Nobody, the owner included, can withdraw from the free pool or from any project, and the owner cannot touch any project's owner or settings. A separate **manager** address (the deploy script asks for one and refuses to deploy with the same key as owner and manager unless explicitly acknowledged) runs day-to-day operations: it can remove signers and bundlers instantly, pause the free tier, and propose additions, which only take effect after the timelock described above. The specification states exactly what this does and does not guarantee (a compromised signer and bundler that were already authorised can still burn each project's daily limit until the signer is removed). If the owner renounces, none of those owner powers exist any more, but claiming, depositing into and running a project, and the free tier itself, keep working. See the specification for exactly what a renounce makes impossible.

## The API

The policy service's v2 API is described in an OpenAPI document, `openapi.yaml`, in the devkit repository under `services/paymaster/policy-service/`. The v2 routes are live on the hosted service at `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com`; `/v2/admin` is not exposed publicly. In summary:

| Group | Authentication | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Public | None | `GET /v2/config`, `GET /v2/contract` (address and ABI), `GET /v2/free-tier` (pool state and allowance) |
| Auth | Sign-In With Ethereum | `GET /v2/auth/nonce`, `POST /v2/auth/login`, `POST /v2/auth/logout`, `GET /v2/me` |
| Project owner | Session bearer token; the address must equal the project's current on-chain owner | Prepare transactions (`POST /v2/projects/prepare`), verify a Privy app and get a claim attestation (`POST /v2/projects/verify`), index a project, rotate its client token or server key, set allowed origins and off-chain settings, read usage, events and allowlist |
| Administrator | A separate admin token (the routes are absent when it is unset) | Overview, free-tier-only apps, suspend or rotate an app credential, run the reconciler |
| Sponsorship | Server API key, or client token from an allowed origin. Free tier: a Privy access token | `POST /v2/sponsor`, and the ERC-7677 endpoint `POST /v2/paymaster/{token}` |

All amounts are decimal wei strings.

## Canary limits

- **External audit pending.** The contract holds third-party money in an immutable deployment. An internal AI-assisted review (`services/paymaster/audits/2026-10-internal-review.md`) found and fixed issues, but it is explicitly not an external audit. The design's own threat model lists the missing external audit as the top residual risk. Deposit small amounts, in small tranches, and do not point production traffic at it before one is done.
- **Limited mainnet exercise.** It is covered by unit, fuzz and invariant tests and has one mainnet proof (above), but has not carried production traffic. The paymaster relies on PEPU's bundler with the standard opcode ban switched off (it checks the transaction's origin), so it cannot be used through a conformant public bundler.
- **Owner and manager.** Owner `0x5966dFaB11c8AEe767e0739083417D02f4a634A1`, manager `0x063Ab6C16c38D19A4bC76E7c39A4A0A73afCaBb0`.

## The SDK and tools that map to this

All of these are in `@pepu-chain/sdk/paymaster` (isomorphic) unless marked server-only. The registry's `paymasterV2` entry (and its `paymaster` alias) points at the deployed canary, so calls default to it; pass `paymaster` explicitly to override. `createPepuPaymasterClient` and `createPepuSponsoredClient` accept `paymasterToken` and build the URL against the hosted base.

| Step | SDK | MCP tool |
|---|---|---|
| Project id | `computeProjectId(appId)`, which is `keccak256(bytes(appId))`; the app id is case-sensitive | `pepu_project_balance` returns it |
| Read a project | `readProject` (owner, claimed, balance, limits, spent today, paused, pending reclaim) | `pepu_project_balance` |
| Deposit (one-way) | `encodeDeposit`, `depositFor` | `pepu_prepare_project_tx` |
| Prove ownership (server or CLI only) | `requestClaimAttestation` from `/paymaster/server`; it sends your Privy app secret to the policy service for one request | none, by design |
| Claim | `encodeClaimProject`, `encodeClaimFromVerification`, `encodeReclaimProject` | `pepu_prepare_project_tx` |
| Configure (owner only, after the claim) | `configureProject`, `encodeSetTargets`, `encodeSetDailyLimit`, `encodeSetSenderDailyLimit`, `encodeSetPaused` | `pepu_prepare_project_tx` |
| Re-claim lifecycle | `encodeExecuteReclaim`, `encodeCancelReclaim`, `encodeProposeProjectOwner`, `encodeAcceptProjectOwnership` | `pepu_prepare_project_tx` |
| REST client | `createPaymasterApi` (defaults to the hosted base), `buildErc7677Url`, `hostedErc7677Url(token)`, `hostedFreeTierUrl()` | |
| Denial reasons | `mapPaymasterReason`, `paymasterReasonToError`, `PAYMASTER_DENIAL_REASONS` | `pepu_explain_error` |

The claim sets the owner only. After it, the owner must call `setTargets`, `setDailyLimit` and `setSenderDailyLimit` before anything is sponsored. The skill is `pepu-paymaster-projects` and the recipe is [Deposit and Claim a Paymaster Project](../recipes/v2-deposit-and-claim.md). Infra pages: [Paymaster Overview](../infra/paymaster/overview.md), [REST API v2](../infra/paymaster/rest-api-v2.md), [Register, Deposit and Claim a v2 Project](../infra/paymaster/v2-register-deposit-claim.md), [PepuSponsoredPaymasterV7 Contract](../infra/paymaster/contracts.md), [Paymaster v2 Spec Summary](../contracts/paymaster-v2-spec.md), [Audits and Verification Status](../contracts/audits.md).

## Common failures

| `code` | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `PAYMASTER_PROJECT_NOT_CLAIMED` | The project has funds but no owner yet | Claim it, then configure it |
| `PAYMASTER_PROJECT_OWNER_CHANGED` | A re-claim executed since the credential was issued | Issue fresh credentials as the new owner |
| `PAYMASTER_PROJECT_PAUSED` | The owner paused the project | Unpause it with `encodeSetPaused` |
| `PAYMASTER_NO_BALANCE` | The project balance cannot cover the operation | Deposit more PEPU; deposits cannot be withdrawn |
| `PAYMASTER_FREE_TIER_UNAVAILABLE`, `PAYMASTER_IDENTITY_REQUIRED` | The free tier needs a verified Privy access token | Send the token as paymaster context |
| `PAYMASTER_CAP`, `PAYMASTER_RATE_LIMITED` | A project, per-wallet or free-tier limit, or a rate limit | Wait for the window or raise the limit |

## Related

- [Sponsored Transactions](sponsored-transactions.md): the sponsorship flow and proofs.
- [The Two-Address Model](two-address-model.md)
- [Trust and Security Model](../concepts/trust-and-security.md)
- [/paymaster](../sdk/paymaster.md)

pages.title: The Two-Address Model
pages.content:
# The Two-Address Model

With gas sponsorship, one user has **two addresses**. This is the most common source of confusion when people first run the `sponsored-demo` template, so it is worth understanding before you build anything on smart accounts.

| | Embedded wallet (EOA) | Kernel smart account |
|---|---|---|
| What it is | A plain key-controlled account that Privy creates at login | A separate contract account, controlled by the EOA |
| Role | The **signer** (owner). It authorizes actions. | The **sender**. It transacts and holds assets. |
| Address | Its own | A different one, derived from the owner and a salt |
| Holds PEPU? | Only if you send it some | Can stay at zero: a paymaster can pay the gas |
| On pepuscan | Not the sender of the sponsored transaction | The sender of the transaction |

They are different addresses. The smart account's address will not match the embedded wallet's, and that is correct.

## What this means in practice

- **Show the smart account address** to users in any sponsored flow. That is the address that transacts, owns the tokens and receives transfers. The `sponsored-demo` template displays the Kernel address, not the EOA.
- **Never tell a user to send funds to one expecting them at the other.** PEPU sent to the EOA does not appear in the smart account, and the reverse. A sponsored smart account can legitimately hold zero PEPU; the demo shows exactly that, then proves sponsorship by watching the paymaster's own EntryPoint deposit drop.
- **Look the transaction up by the smart account address** on [pepuscan.com](https://pepuscan.com). The transaction is submitted by a bundler through the EntryPoint; the smart account is the sender, the account that acted.
- **Without sponsorship, there is only one address.** Plain embedded-wallet apps (the `consumer-app`, `token-gated-app`, `nft-mint` and `game-app` templates) use the EOA directly. Session signers also act on the plain EOA. The two-address model only applies when you use a smart account, which today means the sponsorship path.
- **The smart account is created counterfactually.** Its address can be computed before it is deployed, and the first sponsored transaction deploys it as part of the same operation.

## Where each address comes from

The embedded wallet is created by Privy at login (or server-side by the template's `POST /api/wallet/ensure` fallback). The Kernel account is built on top of that wallet in one of two ways (the two [smart account paths](../concepts/smart-account-paths.md)). With Privy Smart Wallets enabled for chain 97741 (provider Kernel), Privy's client produces the Kernel address as `account.address`. Otherwise the SDK builds it itself (`toPepuKernelAccount`, or `getKernelAddress` for a read before deployment), which is what `useDirectSponsoredSend` (`/aa/react-direct`) and the Kernel session flow (`useSponsoredSession`, `smartAccount`) do. In both, the address depends only on the owner, not on any session. `usePepuSmartAccount` (Privy Smart Wallets) and `useDirectSmartAccount` (`/aa/react-direct`) return `{ owner, smartAccount }`.

The factory, implementation and validator involved are on [Deployed Contracts](../contracts/deployed-contracts.md#erc-4337--smart-accounts-mainnet-only). If you need to compute a Kernel address for an owner yourself, `getKernelAccountAddress` in [`@pepu-chain/sdk`](../sdk/aa.md) and the `pepu_smart_account_info` tool in the [MCP server](../agent-tooling/mcp-and-skills.md) both read it from the factory's own on-chain `getAddress`.

If a user has both a Privy smart wallet and an SDK-built Kernel account, they have two smart accounts and three addresses in total; see [Mixing paths](../concepts/smart-account-paths.md#mixing-paths).

## Related

- [Smart Account Paths: plain wallet, ZeroDev-native or Privy Smart Wallets](../concepts/smart-account-paths.md)
- [Sponsored Transactions](sponsored-transactions.md)
- [Smart Accounts](smart-accounts.md)
- [Privy Setup](privy-setup.md)

pages.title: Authorization Keys and Key Quorums
pages.content:
# Authorization Keys and Key Quorums

The authorization key is the credential your server uses to ask Privy to sign for a user's wallet under a session grant. This page covers what it authorizes, how to generate it without printing the private half, how to register it, where it is read and how to rotate it. It applies to Privy session signers only; Kernel sessions use no authorization key.

> Status: proven. The generate, register, grant and sign flow ran on mainnet in `game-app`.

## Prerequisites

- Pillar 1 working. See [Social Login and Embedded Wallets](../onboarding/privy-embedded-wallets.md).
- Access to the Privy dashboard for the app.

## What it authorizes

Privy requires that a signing request for a delegated wallet be authorized by the key quorum the user granted as a signer. Your server signs each `eth_signTransaction` request with the private half (`PRIVY_AUTHORIZATION_KEY`); Privy checks it, then evaluates the policy attached to the grant. So the key is a production signing credential: anyone holding it can request transactions for any wallet that granted a signer to its quorum, bounded only by the attached policy (one contract, listed functions, zero value, expiry). Gas is not bounded. It is a server secret: never `NEXT_PUBLIC_`, never committed, never logged.

## Generate

Three ways, all producing a P-256 pair in Privy's format (base64 SPKI public, base64 PKCS8 private, no PEM headers):

| Way | How |
|---|---|
| Template script | `npm run generate-authorization-key` in `game-app` |
| SDK | `generatePrivyAuthorizationKey()` from `@pepu-chain/sdk/doctor`. Returns `{ publicKey, privateKey }`; it writes and logs nothing |
| MCP | `pepu_generate_authorization_key` with an absolute `.env.local` path and `confirm_write: true`. It writes the private half to the env file and returns only the public key and a fingerprint; it refuses to replace an existing key unless `overwrite: true` |

```ts
import { generatePrivyAuthorizationKey } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/doctor";
const { publicKey, privateKey } = await generatePrivyAuthorizationKey();
// Show publicKey. Write privateKey straight to .env.local. Never print it.
```

## Register the public key and create the quorum

Menu labels may drift.

1. Privy dashboard, Controls (Wallet infrastructure), Authorization keys, **New key**. Paste the public key.
2. Create a **key quorum** containing that key.
3. Copy the key quorum id into `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_KEY_QUORUM_ID`. It is an identifier, not a secret: Privy's own client-side `addSigners` examples pass it from browser code.

## Env vars and where they are read

| Variable | Scope | Read by |
|---|---|---|
| `PRIVY_AUTHORIZATION_KEY` | Server, secret | `privySessionSigner` and `createSessionActionRoute` (`/session/server`), through `privyEnvVar`. Never given to the Privy client; Privy takes it per request |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_KEY_QUORUM_ID` (alias `PRIVY_KEY_QUORUM_ID`) | Public | `createSessionRoutes` (grant returns it as `signerId`) |

The SDK's server entries refuse to load in a browser bundle. Check presence with `pepu_check_env` or `npm run doctor`; both report presence and length only.

## Rotation and revocation

- Rotate if the private key leaks: generate a new pair, register it, create a new quorum, update both env vars, redeploy. Sessions granted under the old quorum stop working, so users must grant again.
