- To end one user's session, the browser calls `removeSigners` (`useSessionRevoke`). After it resolves your backend can no longer sign for that wallet.
- Delete a retired key and its quorum in the dashboard.

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 401 "No valid authorization keys or user signing keys available" (`PRIVY_KEY_QUORUM_MISMATCH`) | The private key is not the half of a key in the quorum named by `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_KEY_QUORUM_ID`, or the user granted a different quorum | Realign the pair; grant again |
| `CONFIG_MISSING_ENV` naming `PRIVY_AUTHORIZATION_KEY` | Unset on the server, or the dev server was not restarted | Set it and restart |
| Grant works but signing is denied | The policy rejected the call, or it expired | See [Session Keys](../onboarding/session-keys.md) |

## Related

- [Dashboard Settings, Field by Field](dashboard-settings.md)
- [Session Keys](../onboarding/session-keys.md)
- [Trust and Security Model](../concepts/trust-and-security.md)
- [/doctor](../sdk/doctor.md)

pages.title: Dashboard Settings, Field by Field
pages.content:
# Dashboard Settings, Field by Field

Every Privy dashboard setting a PEPU app depends on, with the exact value, why it matters and the symptom when it is wrong. The rows come from `PEPU_PRIVY_REQUIREMENTS` in `@pepu-chain/sdk/privy` and from the live testing recorded in the template READMEs. If you only read one Privy page, read this one.

> Status: proven. Origins, Google login, embedded wallets, TEE mode, the authorization key and quorum, and Smart Wallets (Kernel, chain 97741) were all exercised on mainnet. Menu labels are marked where they may drift: Privy renames dashboard sections, and the SDK's table is the checklist of record. Fields Privy's public config does not expose cannot be verified automatically and show as `unknown`, not as a failure.

## Prerequisites

- A Privy app from [dashboard.privy.io](https://dashboard.privy.io).
- Which pillars you use. The last column of the table says which settings each pillar needs.

## The settings

"Menu label" is where the SDK's table says to look at the time of writing. It may drift.

| Setting | Menu label (may drift) | Exact value | Why | Failure symptom | Login | Session (Privy) | Sponsor |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| App ID | Settings, Basics | Copy to `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_APP_ID` | Public identifier, bundled into client JS | Setup screen "Missing NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_APP_ID"; `privy.app-id` doctor failure | yes | yes | yes |
| App secret | Settings, Basics | Create one; copy to `PRIVY_APP_SECRET`. Server only | The ensure route, `requireUser` and every session route verify access tokens with it | `/api/wallet/ensure` returns 500; or 401 for a valid session when the secret belongs to another app | yes | yes | yes |
| Allowed origins | Configuration, App settings | The exact origin: `http://localhost:3000`, plus each production origin | Privy matches scheme, host and port. `http://localhost` is a different origin | Login iframe blocked by CSP `frame-ancestors`, OAuth init returns 403, console error naming no port | yes | yes | yes |
| Login methods | User management, Authentication | Enable every method you list in `loginMethods` | Methods not enabled here are hidden even if listed in code | Login button shows fewer methods than the code lists | yes | | |
| Google | User management, Authentication, Socials | On | The code-side `"google"` only shows if this is on | No "Continue with Google" button | yes | | |
| Embedded wallets, Ethereum | Wallets | On for Ethereum | The embedded wallet is created here | `WalletGate` errors; ensure route 502 `WALLET_NOT_PROVISIONED` | yes | yes | yes |
| Automatically create embedded wallets on login | Wallets | Either value works. On is fine | The dashboard wins over `createOnLogin` in code. The SDK provisions server-side regardless | With it off and a custom provider, "Creating your wallet..." hangs forever | recommended | | |
| Execution mode | Wallets | The live tests used TEE (`user-controlled-server-wallets-only`) | Selects where keys are reassembled | Behavior of wallet creation changes between modes | note | | |
| Coinbase Wallet eoaOnly | Not a dashboard field: set in code | Use `PepuPrivyProvider` or `createPepuPrivyConfig`, which pin it | Coinbase Smart Wallet does not support chain 97741 | Console: "configured chains are not supported by Coinbase Smart Wallet: 97741" | yes | | |
| Authorization key | Controls (Wallet infrastructure), Authorization keys, New key | Paste the public key from `generatePrivyAuthorizationKey` | Privy checks your server's signature on each signing request | `PRIVY_KEY_QUORUM_MISMATCH` | | yes | |
| Key quorum | Same area; create a quorum that contains the key | Copy its id to `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_KEY_QUORUM_ID` | The grant names this quorum as the signer | 401 "No valid authorization keys or user signing keys available" | | yes | |
| Smart Wallets | Wallets, Smart wallets (the demo README says Settings, Wallet infrastructure, Smart wallets) | Enabled; chain `97741`; provider Kernel; bundler URL `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL`; paymaster URL `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` | Only the `privy-smart-wallets` transport reads it | Page spins on "Setting up your smart wallet..." | | | Privy transport only |

The combination (`sponsored-session-app`) needs only the Login column. It does not use Smart Wallets, authorization keys or quorums.

## Field notes

### App ID and secret

The App ID is public by design. The secret is server only: never give it a `NEXT_PUBLIC_` prefix, never commit it. Rotate it in the dashboard if it leaks; update `PRIVY_APP_SECRET` and restart. Note the v2 paymaster claim flow sends this secret to the PEPU policy service for one request, so use a dedicated app for sponsorship if you can and rotate afterwards ([Sponsorship Tiers](../onboarding/sponsorship-tiers.md)).

### Allowed origins

Include the exact origin of every environment: local, preview, production. Next.js silently moves to port 3001 when 3000 is taken, and login then fails with errors that never mention the port. Free port 3000 rather than passing `-p 3001`. If you deliberately use another port, add that exact origin first. Every template defaults to 3000, and a Privy app id is typically allow-listed for one set of origins, so do not run two templates at once. Preview deployments get their own URLs, so each preview origin needs an entry, or use one stable staging origin. The SDK check accepts a `*` entry as matching, but a wildcard is a security choice you make, not something this kit recommends.

### Google

For the default Privy-managed Google login, enabling the Socials toggle is all the proven setup. A custom Google OAuth client (your own client id, redirect URL and consent screen, test versus published) is a Privy dashboard option the kit has not exercised; if you use one, register the redirect URI the dashboard shows and publish the consent screen before real users arrive. Unverified by us.

### Embedded wallets and the creation setting

Turn embedded wallets on for Ethereum. `createPepuPrivyConfig` sets `createOnLogin: "off"` and `WalletGate` calls `createEnsureWalletRoute()` right after login; with the dashboard creation setting off, Privy's own client-side creation hangs, which was reproduced live. Having the dashboard setting on and the server route in place is fine.

### TEE execution mode

TEE (`user-controlled-server-wallets-only`) reassembles wallets inside a secure enclave that only Privy can invoke, gated by the user's session. The legacy mode reassembles on the device. The live tests ran with TEE. Whether TEE is a requirement for anything here is **unverified**; only that setting has been proven.

### Smart Wallets (Privy transport only)

Smart Wallets is Path 2 in [Smart Account Paths](../concepts/smart-account-paths.md). If you are unsure whether you need it, read that page first: most apps (anything with sessions, the free tier or a server) use Path 1 and leave this off.

**Required** for `sponsored-demo`, which uses Privy Smart Wallets. **Not required** for `sponsored-session-app` or any other template: the SDK builds the ZeroDev Kernel account itself. Leaving Smart wallets enabled is harmless there; users then also get a Privy smart wallet linked to their account, which the paymaster also accepts as owned by the user.

For `sponsored-demo` configure, under Wallets, Smart wallets (or Settings, Wallet infrastructure, Smart wallets in older layouts):

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| Provider | Kernel (ZeroDev) v3.1 |
| Custom chain | PEPU, chain id `97741`, RPC `https://rpc-pepu-v2-mainnet-0.t.conduit.xyz` |
| Bundler URL | `https://bundler.pepeunchained.com` |
| Paymaster URL | `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<project CLIENT token ppt_...>` |

Use the project **client token** (`ppt_`) and add your app's origins to the project's allowed origins, because Privy calls the URL from the browser. Never put the server key (`ppk_`) in the dashboard. The free tier cannot be used on this path: the dashboard URL is static and carries no per-user Privy token, so you need a funded project of your own (claim, set targets and limits, deposit, register). Without both URLs the page cannot sponsor anything. Old dashboards may still hold temporary development bundler or paymaster URLs (for example tunnels); replace them with the hosted ones above. See [Sponsored Transactions](../onboarding/sponsored-transactions.md).

### Paymaster credentials by template

| Template | Credential | Where | Secret? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sponsored-demo` | Project client token `ppt_` | Inside the paymaster URL in the Privy dashboard | No, but only works from the allowed origins |
| `sponsored-session-app` | Project server key `ppk_` in `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` | `.env.local`, server only | Yes |
| Others | None | | |

Sponsorship is project first, then the free tier as a fallback when the project cannot cover an operation. The free tier (100 PEPU/day and 50 PEPU/hour per user, TapScore only for now) needs the user's Privy access token from PEPU's own Privy app; the SDK combination routes forward the signed-in user's token automatically, and it is ignored for project billing unless the service can verify it.

### Per-template requirements

| Template | Env vars | Login methods in code | Smart wallets | Extra |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `consumer-app` | `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_APP_ID` (public), `PRIVY_APP_SECRET` (secret) | email, google, wallet | Off | Coinbase `eoaOnly` pinned in code |
| `token-gated-app` | same | email, google, wallet | Off | `eoaOnly` pinned |
| `nft-mint` | same | email, google, wallet | Off | `eoaOnly` pinned |
| `game-app` | same, plus `PRIVY_AUTHORIZATION_KEY` (secret), `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_KEY_QUORUM_ID` (public id) | email, google, wallet | Off | Authorization key and key quorum |
| `sponsored-demo` | same as `consumer-app` | google, email | Required (above) | Client token in the dashboard URL |
| `sponsored-session-app` | same as `consumer-app`, plus `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` (secret), `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` | google, email | Not required | Server key in env |

Every template also needs Allowed origins (exact origin with port, plus production) and embedded wallets for Ethereum with creation on login. Each template's `.env.example` carries the same checklist as comments. Find the App ID and App Secret under Settings, Basics. The authorization key pair comes from `npm run generate-authorization-key` in `game-app`; the quorum id is shown after you register the public key.

### Authorization keys, key quorums, policies and TTL

See [Authorization Keys and Key Quorums](authorization-keys.md). Policies are not dashboard fields: the SDK creates them per grant through the API. Policy and rule names must be at most 49 characters (`PRIVY_POLICY_NAME_MAX_LENGTH`); Privy's live validator says fewer than 50 although its OpenAPI spec says 50. The session TTL is `SESSION_DURATION_MINUTES` (default 15, clamped to 1 to 1440), baked into the policy's expiry condition.

### Access tokens

Nothing to configure for JWT verification. `verifyRequestUser` verifies the bearer token against Privy with your App ID and App Secret. A verification failure caused by a secret from a different app looks exactly like an expired session, so check the secret first.

## Verify

```ts
import { checkPrivyDashboardConfig } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/privy";
const r = await checkPrivyDashboardConfig({ appId, origin: "http://localhost:3000" });
```

Or the `pepu_check_privy_config` MCP tool. See [Privy Env Vars and Verification](env-and-checks.md).

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Login fails, iframe blocked, OAuth 403 | Origin or port missing | Allowed origins |
| No Google button | Google off in the dashboard | Socials, Google |
| "Creating your wallet..." forever | Custom provider with creation off | `PepuPrivyProvider`, `WalletGate` |
| 401 "No valid authorization keys..." | Quorum id and private key from different keys | Realign; users re-grant |
| "Setting up your smart wallet..." forever | Smart Wallets not set for 97741 | Add chain, Kernel, both URLs |
| Everything `unknown` in the check | Privy's public config did not report fields, or the app id is wrong | Not a failure; verify by hand |

## Related

- [Smart Account Paths: which one needs Smart Wallets](../concepts/smart-account-paths.md)
- [Privy Configuration Overview](index.md)
- [Privy Setup Walkthrough](../onboarding/privy-setup.md)
- [Authorization Keys and Key Quorums](authorization-keys.md)
- [Privy Env Vars and Verification](env-and-checks.md)

pages.title: Privy Env Vars and Verification
pages.content:
# Privy Env Vars and Verification

The Privy environment variables, and the three ways to verify a Privy setup: `checkPrivyDashboardConfig`, the `pepu_check_privy_config` MCP tool and `npm run doctor`. Use it when login, wallets or sessions fail with a config error.

> Status: proven for env checks and the doctor script. The dashboard check calls Privy's public app-config endpoint, whose response fields were not verified against a real app: every field is treated as optional and reports `unknown` when absent, never a false failure.

## Prerequisites

- `.env.local` in the project, and the Privy App ID (public).

## Env vars

| Variable | Scope | Read by | Needed for |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_APP_ID` (alias `PRIVY_APP_ID`) | Public | Provider, `createPrivyServer`, doctor | Everything |
| `PRIVY_APP_SECRET` | Server, secret | `/privy/server`, `/session/server`, `/combo` | Everything with a server route |
| `PRIVY_AUTHORIZATION_KEY` | Server, secret | `/session/server` | Privy sessions |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_KEY_QUORUM_ID` (alias `PRIVY_KEY_QUORUM_ID`) | Public | `createSessionRoutes` | Privy sessions |

The canonical names are `PRIVY_ENV`; aliases are read only when the canonical name is empty. The full cross-component list is [Environment Variables](../reference/env-vars.md).

## Run the checks

### `npm run doctor`

Every template has a `doctor` script that runs the SDK's `checkPepuEnv` against `.env.local` for that template's requirements. It prints `ok` or `FAIL` per key with a fix, never a value, and exits non-zero on failure. It checks env only, not the dashboard.

```
FAIL PRIVY_APP_SECRET - Set PRIVY_APP_SECRET in .env.local to the app secret from the Privy dashboard (server only).
```

Statuses per key: `ok`, `missing`, `placeholder` (for example `your-app-id`) and `malformed` (the Privy id must look like `c` plus 20 to 29 lowercase alphanumerics; addresses must be 20-byte hex; URLs must be http or https; `SESSION_DURATION_MINUTES` must be positive).

### The full doctor

`runDoctor` from `@pepu-chain/sdk/doctor` adds the Privy app id format, the RPC chain id (97741), bundler and paymaster reachability, and, when you inject the checker, the dashboard rows:

```ts
import { runDoctor } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/doctor";
import { privyDashboardChecker } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/privy";

const report = await runDoctor({
  env: process.env,
  template: "sponsored-session-app",
  checkPrivyDashboard: privyDashboardChecker,
});
for (const c of report.checks.filter((c) => c.status !== "pass")) console.log(c.id, c.status, c.fix);
```

Check ids: `env.<NAME>`, `privy.app-id`, `chain.rpc`, `sponsorship.bundler`, `sponsorship.paymaster`, `privy.<requirement key>`. Statuses are `pass`, `fail`, `warn` and `skip`. A bundler or paymaster URL that is unset is a skip; set but unreachable is a fail. `runDoctor` does not pass an origin, so `privy.allowed-origins` comes back a warning. Use the next two for the origin.

### `checkPrivyDashboardConfig`

```ts
import { checkPrivyDashboardConfig } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/privy";
const r = await checkPrivyDashboardConfig({ appId, origin: "http://localhost:3000" });
// r.ok is false only if a REQUIRED row definitely failed
for (const i of r.items) console.log(i.id, i.ok, i.detail, i.fix);
```

It never throws and needs no secret. Each item is `true`, `false` or `"unknown"`. Rows: `allowed-origins`, `login-methods`, `login-methods.google`, `embedded-wallets`, `smart-wallets`. Env and code rows (`app-id`, `app-secret`, `coinbase-eoa-only`, `authorization-key-quorum`) are in `PEPU_PRIVY_REQUIREMENTS` but cannot be checked remotely.

### `pepu_check_privy_config`

The MCP tool wraps the same function: inputs `appId`, optional `origin` (with port) and optional `pillars` (`login`, `session`, `sponsor`). It returns `dashboard` rows with `pass`, `fail` or `unknown` and a fix, plus `notRemotelyCheckable` rows. Needs network access to `auth.privy.io`. Pair it with `pepu_check_env`, and use `/pepu-doctor` to run both.

## Reading the output

| Result | Meaning |
|---|---|
| pass | Verified from Privy's public config |
| fail | Definitely wrong; apply the `fix` |
| unknown or warn | Privy did not report it, or the origin was not given. Not a failure; verify by hand |
| skip | Not applicable (env or code rows, or no URL configured) |

## Common failures mapped to dashboard fields

| Check failing | Dashboard field | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `allowed-origins` | Allowed origins | Add the exact origin with port |
| `login-methods` | Login methods | Enable the methods in `loginMethods` |
| `login-methods.google` | Socials, Google | Turn Google on |
| `embedded-wallets` | Embedded wallets | Turn on for Ethereum |
| `smart-wallets` | Smart Wallets | Chain 97741, Kernel, both URLs (Privy transport only) |
| `env.PRIVY_AUTHORIZATION_KEY`, quorum | Authorization keys | [Authorization Keys](authorization-keys.md) |
| `privy.app-id` format | Settings, Basics | Use the App ID, not the secret or client id |

## Related

- [Dashboard Settings, Field by Field](dashboard-settings.md)
- [Environment Variables](../reference/env-vars.md)
- [/doctor](../sdk/doctor.md), [/privy](../sdk/privy.md)
- [MCP Tool Reference](../mcp/tools.md)

pages.title: Privy Configuration Overview
pages.content:
# Privy Configuration Overview

Everything about configuring Privy for a PEPU app: which feature needs which setting, how the SDK and tools verify settings, and where each detail page lives. Start here when login, wallets, sessions or Smart Wallets misbehave.

> Status: proven on mainnet for every setting listed. Menu labels in the dashboard may drift; the SDK table `PEPU_PRIVY_REQUIREMENTS` is the checklist of record.

## Prerequisites

- A Privy app. Env: `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_APP_ID`, `PRIVY_APP_SECRET`.

## Feature to setting matrix

| Feature | Settings it needs | Page |
|---|---|---|
| Google or email login | App ID, secret, Allowed origins (with port), Login methods, Google | [Dashboard Settings](dashboard-settings.md) |
| Embedded wallet | Embedded wallets on for Ethereum; server route with the secret; Coinbase `eoaOnly` (code) | [Embedded Wallets](../onboarding/privy-embedded-wallets.md) |
| Privy session signers | Authorization key, key quorum, `PRIVY_AUTHORIZATION_KEY`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_KEY_QUORUM_ID` | [Authorization Keys](authorization-keys.md) |
| Smart Wallets (Privy sponsorship transport) | Smart Wallets: chain 97741, Kernel, bundler URL, paymaster URL | [Dashboard Settings](dashboard-settings.md) |
| Kernel session plus sponsorship (the combination) | Login settings only. No Smart Wallets, no authorization key | [End to End](../onboarding/google-session-sponsored.md) |

## How settings are verified

- `PEPU_PRIVY_REQUIREMENTS` is one data table: id, where (`dashboard`, `env` or `code`), label, required, pillars, fix and docs URL. It feeds the docs, the MCP tool, the doctor and in-app notices.
- `checkPrivyDashboardConfig` reads the public app-config endpoint and reports pass, fail or unknown for the dashboard rows.
- `pepu_check_privy_config` is that function as an MCP tool.
- `npm run doctor` checks env presence and shape.

Details: [Privy Env Vars and Verification](env-and-checks.md).

## Pages in this section

- [Privy Setup Walkthrough](../onboarding/privy-setup.md): the short first-time procedure.
- [Dashboard Settings, Field by Field](dashboard-settings.md)
- [Authorization Keys and Key Quorums](authorization-keys.md)
- [Privy Env Vars and Verification](env-and-checks.md)

## Common failures

| Symptom | Go to |
|---|---|
| Login fails or the iframe is blocked | Allowed origins in [Dashboard Settings](dashboard-settings.md) |
| "Creating your wallet..." hangs | [Embedded Wallets](../onboarding/privy-embedded-wallets.md) |
| 401 "No valid authorization keys" | [Authorization Keys](authorization-keys.md) |
| "Setting up your smart wallet..." hangs | Smart Wallets in [Dashboard Settings](dashboard-settings.md) |

## Related

- [The Three Pillars](../get-started/pillars.md)
- [/privy](../sdk/privy.md)

pages.title: Recipe: Add PEPU to a Wallet
Recipe: Batch Reads with Multicall3
pages.content:
# Recipe: Batch Reads with Multicall3

Read many values in one request. PEPU has Multicall3, but not at the canonical address, so this recipe uses the SDK to pin the right one.

> Status: proven on mainnet. PEPU's Multicall3 is `0x9CE19273Ae9c24437DFF512E8DFCAed4E4B001bd`. The canonical `0xcA11bde05977b3631167028862bE2a173976CA11` has no code on PEPU.

Read [The Multicall3 Trap](../contracts/multicall3.md) first if you have not.

## Prerequisites

`@pepu-chain/sdk` and `viem`.

## Steps

`pepuMulticall(client, calls, { allowFailure?, blockNumber? })` is viem's `multicall` pinned to PEPU's address. It goes through `getMulticall3`, which throws `MULTICALL3_CANONICAL_ADDRESS` rather than ever use the canonical one.

```ts
// Batch reads through PEPU's own Multicall3. See docs/recipes/batch-reads-with-multicall3.md
import { erc20Abi, getAddress } from "viem";
import { getPublicClient, pepuMainnet, pepuMulticall, pepuTokenList } from "@pepu-chain/sdk";

const client = getPublicClient(pepuMainnet);

export async function readTokens(holder: `0x${string}`) {
  const tokens = pepuTokenList.tokens.map((t) => getAddress(t.address));

  // pepuMulticall pins the Multicall3 address; the canonical one has no code on PEPU.
  const results = await pepuMulticall(
    client,
    tokens.flatMap(
      (address) =>
        [
          { address, abi: erc20Abi, functionName: "symbol" },
          { address, abi: erc20Abi, functionName: "balanceOf", args: [holder] },
        ] as const,
    ),
    { allowFailure: true },
  );

  return results.map((r) => (r.status === "success" ? r.result : null));
}
```

Source: `docs/snippets/multicall-batch-reads.ts`, type-checked against the SDK.

Plain viem works too, because `pepuMainnet.contracts.multicall3` already holds PEPU's address: `client.multicall({ contracts })` on a client from `getPublicClient(pepuMainnet)` batches correctly. Use `pepuMulticall` when you want the guard.

In React with wagmi see [Batch Reads with Multicall3 in React](multicall-in-react.md).

### Calling `aggregate3` yourself

For per-call failure control, `encodeAggregate3(calls)` and `decodeAggregate3Result(data)` wrap the `aggregate3` ABI. The contract is a normal Multicall3 deployment; only the address differs from other chains.

### Without the SDK

Set `contracts.multicall3` explicitly in your chain definition, with `address: "0x9CE19273Ae9c24437DFF512E8DFCAed4E4B001bd"` and `blockCreated: 10521048`. Never substitute the canonical address.

## What to expect

- One RPC round trip for all calls. Results are in order, each with a `status`.
- With `allowFailure: false` a failing call rejects the whole batch.

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Every batched call fails | Routed through the canonical address | Use `pepuMainnet` or `pepuMulticall` |
| `MULTICALL3_CANONICAL_ADDRESS` | The canonical address reached `getMulticall3` | Use the registry entry, never a literal |
| `UNKNOWN` "Multicall3 is not deployed" | A non-mainnet chain ID | Use chain 97741 |

## Related

- [The Multicall3 Trap](../contracts/multicall3.md)
- [Batch Reads with Multicall3 in React](multicall-in-react.md)
- [Gate Content by Token Balance](gate-content-by-token-balance.md)
- [Core](../sdk/core.md#multicall3-and-permit2)

pages.title: Recipe: Deploy an ERC-20
pages.content:
# Recipe: Deploy an ERC-20

A standard OpenZeppelin-based ERC-20, deployed and verified on Pepe Unchained V2 mainnet with Foundry.

> Status: proven. This is the standard Foundry flow against PEPU mainnet. It uses the Foundry toolchain, so there is no SDK code to type-check; the SDK helps after deployment. If you haven't deployed anything here yet, do [Deploy & Verify a Contract](../contracts/deployment.md) first — this recipe assumes a working Foundry project and a funded development key.

## The contract

```solidity
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
pragma solidity ^0.8.24;

import "@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/ERC20.sol";

contract MyToken is ERC20 {
    constructor(uint256 initialSupply) ERC20("My Token", "MTK") {
        _mint(msg.sender, initialSupply);
    }
}
```

Save as `src/MyToken.sol`.

## Install OpenZeppelin

```bash
forge install OpenZeppelin/openzeppelin-contracts
```

Add a remapping in `foundry.toml` if `forge install` didn't add one automatically:

```toml
remappings = ["@openzeppelin/=lib/openzeppelin-contracts/"]
```

## Deploy

Constructor takes the initial supply in the token's smallest unit (18 decimals is OpenZeppelin's ERC-20 default, so `1_000_000e18` for one million whole tokens):

```bash
forge create src/MyToken.sol:MyToken \
  --rpc-url pepu_mainnet \
  --private-key $PRIVATE_KEY \
  --broadcast \
  --constructor-args 1000000000000000000000000
```

(That's `1,000,000 * 10^18` — one million tokens at 18 decimals.)

## Verify

Same Blockscout verification pattern as any other contract on this chain, with constructor args passed through so pepuscan can reproduce the exact deployed bytecode:

```bash
forge verify-contract \
  --rpc-url https://rpc-pepu-v2-mainnet-0.t.conduit.xyz \
  --verifier blockscout \
  --verifier-url https://pepuscan.com/api \
  --constructor-args $(cast abi-encode "constructor(uint256)" 1000000000000000000000000) \
  <DEPLOYED_ADDRESS> \
  src/MyToken.sol:MyToken
```

## Add it to the wallet the deploying key belongs to (optional, for testing)

Most wallets support `wallet_watchAsset` for this:

```ts
await window.ethereum.request({
  method: "wallet_watchAsset",
  params: {
    type: "ERC20",
    options: {
      address: "0xYourTokenAddress",
      symbol: "MTK",
      decimals: 18,
    },
  },
});
```

## Things this recipe deliberately does not cover

- **Listing on PepuSwap or any DEX** — that's a liquidity/business decision, not a deployment step, and out of scope for developer docs.
- **A canonical token list entry.** `@pepu-chain/sdk`'s token list (see [`@pepu-chain/sdk` Reference](../sdk/core.md#contract-and-dex-registries)) only includes addresses that clear a high independent-verification bar. Deploying your own token doesn't add it there automatically, and it shouldn't — that list is for chain-level infrastructure tokens, not every token anyone deploys.
- **Permit2.** The canonical Permit2 is deployed on PEPU (`getPermit2()`), so a freshly deployed ERC-20 can use signature-based approvals after one ordinary `approve(permit2, amount)`. See [Sign a Permit2 Permit](permit2-permit.md).


## After deployment, with the SDK

- Link the deployment: `txUrl(pepuMainnet, hash)` and `addressUrl(pepuMainnet, address)` ([Explorer Links](explorer-links.md)).
- Read it: [Read a Contract](read-a-contract.md), and gate content on it: [Gate Content by Token Balance](gate-content-by-token-balance.md).
- For gas the user does not pay, the contract must be on the paymaster allowlist: [Send a Sponsored Transaction](sponsored-send.md).

pages.title: Recipe: Explorer Links
pages.content:
# Recipe: Explorer Links

Build pepuscan links for transactions, addresses, tokens and blocks, and link a sponsored UserOperation correctly.

> Status: proven. pepuscan is PEPU mainnet's Blockscout explorer at `https://pepuscan.com`.

## Prerequisites

`@pepu-chain/sdk` and `pepuMainnet`. No React, no network call: link building is pure.

## Steps

Use the shorthand for the resource you have: `txUrl`, `addressUrl`, `tokenUrl`, `blockUrl`, or `explorerUrl(chain, type, value)` for the generic form. For a bundle of links at once use `explorerLinks`.

A UserOperation has no page of its own on pepuscan. Link its bundle transaction (`result.transactionHash`) and its sender (the smart account address). `SponsoredResult.explorerUrl` and the combo `act` response already carry the bundle transaction URL.

```ts
// Build pepuscan links. See docs/recipes/explorer-links.md
import { addressUrl, blockUrl, explorerLinks, explorerUrl, pepuMainnet, tokenUrl, txUrl } from "@pepu-chain/sdk";
import type { SponsoredResult } from "@pepu-chain/sdk/aa";

export const single = {
  tx: (hash: string) => txUrl(pepuMainnet, hash),
  address: (a: string) => addressUrl(pepuMainnet, a),
  token: (a: string) => tokenUrl(pepuMainnet, a),
  block: (n: number) => blockUrl(pepuMainnet, n),
  generic: (hash: string) => explorerUrl(pepuMainnet, "tx", hash),
};

// A UserOperation has no page of its own on pepuscan: link its bundle transaction
// and its sender (the smart account).
export function userOpLinks(result: SponsoredResult, smartAccount: string) {
  return explorerLinks({ tx: result.transactionHash, sender: smartAccount });
}
```

Source: `docs/snippets/explorer-links.ts`, type-checked against the SDK.

## What to expect

- `txUrl(pepuMainnet, hash)` gives `https://pepuscan.com/tx/<hash>`.
- `explorerLinks({ tx, sender })` returns only the keys you passed.
- `explorerUrl` throws for a chain with no explorer (`pepuTestnet`). Wrap the call if you need a soft failure.

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `explorerUrl: no block explorer is configured` | You passed `pepuTestnet` | Use `pepuMainnet` |
| A link to `/userop/...` 404s | Blockscout on PEPU has no UserOperation page | Link the transaction and sender instead |
| Block link by hash fails | Hash passed as a number | Pass the hash as a string |

## Related

- [Core](../sdk/core.md#explorer-links)
- [Send a Sponsored Transaction](sponsored-send.md)
- [Send a Transaction](send-a-transaction.md)

pages.content:
# Changelog

Dated changes to the dev kit packages and docs, newest first. Each entry lists what a builder can now do, not the commit log. Versions are those in the repository on the date of each entry. Publishing to npm is a maintainer step (see `RELEASING.md` in the repository), so check the registry for what is published.

> Status: SDK 0.2.2, MCP 0.2.3, plugin 0.4.0 and create-pepu-app 0.1.2 are the versions on main. The three pillars and their combination are proven on mainnet (the combination live in a browser on 2026-10-14, against the hosted bundler and v2 paymaster). The hosted bundler and paymaster endpoints are live, and the v2 tiered paymaster is deployed as a canary: internally reviewed 3x, external audit pending, funded in small tranches.

## 2026-10-15: @pepu-chain/mcp 0.2.5, plugin 0.4.1

New guide: [Smart account paths](../concepts/smart-account-paths.md) explains ZeroDev-native accounts built by the SDK versus Privy Smart Wallets versus plain embedded wallets, with a decision table. The quickstart is now a 10-minute zero-to-sponsored-transaction guide, the paymaster project guide is step by step with SDK and MCP routes, and the skills link the new guide. The MCP server bundles the refreshed docs and skills.

## 2026-10-15: create-pepu-app 0.1.3, @pepu-chain/mcp 0.2.4

Every template's `.env.example` now carries the full Privy dashboard checklist (allowed origins, login methods, embedded wallets, Coinbase `eoaOnly`, Smart Wallets status, authorization keys for game-app, paymaster credentials). `docs/privy/dashboard-settings.md` gains per-template requirements and the Smart Wallets table (Kernel v3.1, chain 97741, hosted bundler, paymaster URL with a project client token). The MCP server bundles the refreshed docs.

## 2026-10-15

### Fresh-account fixes for the combination: `@pepu-chain/sdk` 0.2.2, `@pepu-chain/mcp` 0.2.3, `create-pepu-app` 0.1.2

A fresh Google account hit two failures on the live `sponsored-session-app` demo that an existing account never saw.

- **First sign-in showed a red error.** The embedded wallet exists in the browser a moment before Privy's server lists it, so `status` answered 409 `WALLET_NOT_PROVISIONED`. The combo routes now look the user up again a few times (`provisioningWait`, default 3 retries), and `status` answers `{ active: false, provisioning: true }` (a normal 200) if the wallet is still not visible. `useSponsoredSession` keeps `statusLoading` true and re-checks with backoff (0.5 s to 5 s, about 30 s), and `grantKernelSession` retries `prepare` for about 6.5 s. Neither shows an error for this state.
- **The first tap was denied.** The paymaster service only recognized Privy Smart Wallets as "the user's account", but the combo flow creates a ZeroDev Kernel v3.1 account that Privy has never seen, so the service denied the first operation with `sender_not_owned_by_token_user`, before it even chose between the project and the free tier. The service now also accepts the Kernel v3.1 account (ECDSA validator, index 0) derived from one of the token user's own Privy embedded wallets (derivation via the factory's `getAddress`, pinned by a test vector from the SDK), and still denies any other sender. This is a service-side change; no app change is needed. A new user's first operation (about 20 PEPU reserved, because it deploys the account) now falls back to the free tier when the project balance cannot cover it.
- **The error named the wrong thing.** viem reports the service's denial as the generic "Missing or invalid parameters." `describeUserOpFailure` now reads the real denial and says, for example, `Paymaster denied the operation (sender_not_owned_by_token_user): ...`, with the matching catalog code and a specific hint.

`create-pepu-app` 0.1.2 vendors the 0.2.2 SDK and scaffolds `@pepu-chain/sdk@^0.2.2`; the `sponsored-session-app` README and `.env.example` now describe the project-first, free-tier-fallback behaviour accurately. `@pepu-chain/mcp` 0.2.3 pins exactly SDK 0.2.2.

## 2026-10-14

### Combination proven live in a browser

The Google login, on-chain Kernel session key and gas sponsorship combination was run by a person in a browser on mainnet (`sponsored-session-app`, against the hosted bundler `https://bundler.pepeunchained.com` and the v2 paymaster `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com`): Google sign-in to the embedded wallet, one Privy `eth_signTypedData_v4` signature on chain 97741, sponsored taps with no popup while the smart account stayed at 0 PEPU, and revoke. The "proven by script; browser flow not yet run" label is replaced across the docs, skills, MCP text and READMEs. The MCP server text changed (known gotcha and prompt), so it ships in `@pepu-chain/mcp@0.2.2`.

### `create-pepu-app` 0.1.1

Label fix only; the `features` vocabulary (`login`, `session`, `sponsor`) and `--list --json` shape are unchanged. The picker and `--list` showed every template's `login` feature as "Google login", but `consumer-app`, `token-gated-app`, `nft-mint` and `game-app` enable email, Google and wallet sign-in, and `sponsored-demo` and `sponsored-session-app` enable Google and email. The feature is now labelled "sign-in + embedded wallet", and the `consumer-app` and `sponsored-session-app` descriptions name the methods they enable. The vendored SDK is 0.2.1 and `--sdk npm` scaffolds `@pepu-chain/sdk@^0.2.1`.

### `@pepu-chain/sdk` 0.2.1 and `@pepu-chain/mcp` 0.2.1

Patch release from the first clean-room install of the public packages. `@pepu-chain/mcp` 0.2.1 depends on exactly `@pepu-chain/sdk` 0.2.1. `create-pepu-app` stays at 0.1.0, which is awaiting npm's staged-release approval; it ships the 0.2.0-era templates and scaffolds `@pepu-chain/sdk@^0.2.1`.

- **Windows clone fixed.** `git clone` of the repository failed on Windows with "Filename too long" under the vendored Solidity libraries, which also broke `/plugin marketplace add pepu-org/pepu-devkit`. Vendored test, docs, audit, certora, mock and sample files that the build never compiles were removed; the longest tracked path went from 150 to 126 characters, and CI fails above 130 (`scripts/check-path-length.mjs`). The compiled paymaster bytecode is unchanged: the pinned creation-code hashes for v1 and v2 are identical.
- **Clear errors for missing optional peers.** Importing a peer-dependent subpath (for example `@pepu-chain/sdk/privy/react` without `react` or `@privy-io/react-auth`) now throws `PEPU_MISSING_PEER` naming the subpath and the exact `npm i` command, instead of Node's "Cannot find package 'react' imported from dist/chunk-XXXX.js". Under Node the ESM entries load through a small guard (`node` export condition only; bundlers and browsers get the plain entry); CJS entries carry the guard inline. The SDK README and [SDK Reference](../sdk/reference.md#install-peers-per-subpath) gained an Install table (subpath, peers, one-line `npm i`) and a bundle command; `create-pepu-app` remains the recommended path because it scaffolds every peer.
- **Accurate health probes.** `probeBundler` and `pepu_bundler_health` reported `eth_sendUserOperation`, `eth_estimateUserOperationGas` and `eth_getUserOperationReceipt` as unsupported on the live Alto bundler, because Alto answers bad params of a known method with code `-32601` ("Validation error: ..."). Support is now judged from the message (only "method not found" and Alto's "Invalid discriminator value" mean unsupported), the calls still use deliberately invalid params so nothing is sent on-chain, and the verdict is only healthy when the chain, EntryPoint v0.7 and the three required methods are present (`missingRequiredMethods` lists any gap). `probePaymaster` and `pepu_paymaster_health` add `erc7677: "stub-ok" | "needs-credential" | "not-responding"`; without a client token the stub check is reported as not applicable (`erc7677StubOk` is `null`) instead of `false`, and a service that does not speak ERC-7677 JSON-RPC is no longer called healthy.
- **`getPepuAddresses()` shape.** The docs and TSDoc now say plainly that it returns an array of rows (`.find((r) => r.key === "paymaster")`). New `getPepuAddressMap()` returns the same rows keyed by contract name.
- **Docs.** The root README and the CLI page describe what is on npm today and the pending CLI approval.

### Hosted endpoints live, v2 canary deployed, v1 retired

- **Hosted endpoints are live.** Bundler `https://bundler.pepeunchained.com` (the SDK default for `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL`) and paymaster service `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com` (the SDK default base for `createPaymasterApi`, the probes, `checkSponsorship` and `doctor`). The `/v2` routes are public (free-tier state, config, SIWE, projects, verify); `/v2/admin` is not exposed. The ERC-7677 URL always embeds a token, `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<token>`, so there is no tokenless default: `PEPU_HOSTED` is `{ bundlerUrl, paymasterBaseUrl, paymasterUrl: null }` and `isHostedSponsorshipLive()` returns true.
- **v2 paymaster deployed as a canary.** `PepuSponsoredPaymasterV7` is on PEPU mainnet at `0xdb28528C9399C33c9A0297E8A62F39145acbC30D` (about block 10537341): deployed as a canary: internally reviewed 3x, external audit pending, funded in small tranches. The registry keys `paymasterV2` and `paymaster` point at it. Owner `0x5966dFaB11c8AEe767e0739083417D02f4a634A1`, manager `0x063Ab6C16c38D19A4bC76E7c39A4A0A73afCaBb0`, free pool seeded with 300 PEPU. Free tier per user: 100 PEPU a day and 50 PEPU an hour; free-tier targets are TapScore only for now.
- **v1 paymaster retired.** `0x2B6FED323bFA24f0475f4e1Dd3C7F6Cc1f3ae8B0` was funded earlier and its EntryPoint deposit has been withdrawn (0), so it cannot sponsor anything. The registry entry `paymasterV1` has `retired: true`, and `getPepuAddresses` rows carry `retired`.
- **Proof.** A project-sponsored operation from a fresh Kernel account holding 0 PEPU went through the hosted bundler and `paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<server key>`: userOp `0x8150850431639387f95c14e2c1f7c857eb833b7b8e0826426dfcbb683d6b9907`, tx `0x6b803ad49091d6758b413065ac54d09774413b55a234d873f8e371243f4e3209`. The paymaster paid 5.00 PEPU of gas including account deployment; the project ledger went from 25 to 19.80 PEPU. History: tx `0x57cf2f5a332248476d775c096b4b8339d81867c14211ed3bc4fcb1895dff0f9f` went through the hosted URLs with the v1 paymaster.
- **New SDK helpers.** `PEPU_HOSTED.paymasterBaseUrl`; `resolvePepuEndpoints()` also returns `paymasterBaseUrl`; `paymasterBaseOf(url)`; `hostedErc7677Url(token)` (from `@pepu-chain/sdk/paymaster`); `hostedFreeTierUrl()` (from `@pepu-chain/sdk`); `createPepuPaymasterClient` and `createPepuSponsoredClient` accept `paymasterToken`; `requirePaymasterUrl(explicit?, token?)`; `createSponsoredSessionRoutes` accepts `endpoints.paymasterToken` and `forwardPrivyToken` (default true: forwards the request's Bearer Privy token as ERC-7677 `context.privyAccessToken`; set false for a paymaster you do not trust with it).
- **MCP.** `pepu_project_balance` and `pepu_prepare_project_tx` default to the registry's deployed v2 canary (an explicit `paymaster` overrides). `pepu_paymaster_health`, `pepu_sponsorship_status` and `pepu_health_check` probe the hosted bundler and the paymaster service base by default.
- **Token behaviour.** A project client token (`ppt_`) is publishable and works only from the project's allowed origins (otherwise `project_origin_not_allowed`); a server key (`ppk_`) is secret. The free tier needs a verified Privy token from PEPU's own Privy app; a third-party app's Privy token is ignored for billing, and the Privy Smart Wallets dashboard URL cannot attach one.
- **Docs.** The sponsorship pages, templates, recipes and style guide now describe the live endpoints; "Sponsorship Tiers (Upcoming)" is now "Sponsorship Tiers".

## 2026-10-03

### `@pepu-chain/sdk` 0.2.0

Additive release: every 0.1 export remains. See [Migration Notes](../sdk/migration.md).

**New subpaths**

| Subpath | What it gives you |
|---|---|
| `/privy`, `/privy/react`, `/privy/wagmi`, `/privy/server` | Google to wallet: typed Privy config for PEPU, `PepuPrivyProvider` and `PepuPrivyWagmiProvider`, `WalletGate`, `useEnsureWallet`, the active-wallet pin, `createEnsureWalletRoute`, `requireUser`, the Privy requirements table and dashboard checker |
| `/session`, `/session/server`, `/session/react` | Privy-mode session keys: `buildSessionPolicy`, `createSessionRoutes`, `createSessionActionRoute`, `privySessionSigner`, `signAndBroadcast`, `useSessionGrant`, `useSessionStatus`, `useSessionAct`, `useSessionRevoke` |
| `/session/kernel` | On-chain session keys with ZeroDev Kernel permissions (call policy v0.0.4 plus timestamp policy) |
| `/aa`, `/aa/kernel`, `/aa/react`, `/aa/react-direct` | Sponsored transactions: bundler and paymaster clients, the Alto-compatible fee estimator, `toPepuKernelAccount`, `createPepuSponsoredClient`, `sendSponsored`, `describeUserOpFailure`, probes, `useSponsoredSend`, `usePepuSponsorship`. `/aa/react` serves Privy Smart Wallets and never references `@zerodev/*`; the direct transport lives in `/aa/react-direct` (`useDirectSponsoredSend`, `useDirectSmartAccount`) |
| `/paymaster`, `/paymaster/server` | The policy service REST client (v1 and v2), v2 on-chain helpers (claim, configure, deposit, read), the Privy claim attestation, denial reason mapping |
| `/combo`, `/combo/react` | The combination: `createSponsoredSessionRoutes` (five routes) and `useSponsoredSession` |
| `/doctor` | `runDoctor`, `checkPepuEnv`, `TEMPLATE_REQUIREMENTS`, `generatePrivyAuthorizationKey` |
| `/server` | Kept as a stable server-only alias for the pure session policy helpers |

**New on the core entry:** the error model (`PepuError` and seven subclasses, a code catalog, `explainError`, `toPepuError`, `toErrorResponse`); endpoint resolution (`resolvePepuEndpoints`, `PEPU_ENV`, with `PEPU_HOSTED` as the single swap point for the hosted URLs); `checkSponsorship` (live bundler and paymaster probe); `pepuMulticall`, `getMulticall3` and `MULTICALL3_CANONICAL_ADDRESS` guard; `getPermit2` and Permit2 typed-data builders; `explorerLinks`; `getPepuAddresses`; `formatUnitsCompact`; `erc20Abi` and `erc721Abi`; the ERC-7677 request builders; registry entries for the Kernel implementation, signer module, call policy v0.0.4, timestamp policy, `tapScore`, `paymasterV1` and `paymasterV2` (pending at the time; deployed 2026-10-14).

**Deprecated:** `getSponsorshipStatus` and `useSponsorshipStatus`. They always report unavailable. Use `checkSponsorship` and `usePepuSponsorship`.

**Boundaries:** five server-only entries throw `CONFIG_SERVER_ONLY` in a browser bundle. `/privy/wagmi` is ESM only. Each optional peer is imported only from its own subpaths, enforced by test.

**Late additions (patch pass before this entry):** `WalletGate` `stalled` render prop, `useSessionStatus().loading`, `useSponsoredSession().statusLoading`, `SponsoredActResult`, route factories that answer `CONFIG_MISSING_ENV` at request time instead of throwing at load, the pure `session/scope` helpers that need no `@zerodev/*`, `encodeKernelExecute`, `userOpEventsFromReceipt`, and a `usePepuSmartAccount` fallback through Privy's `getClientForChain`.

**Proven live:** Google to wallet, Privy session signers, sponsored transactions (at the time, the v1 paymaster `0x2B6FED323bFA24f0475f4e1Dd3C7F6Cc1f3ae8B0`, since retired, with an Alto bundler) and the combination (on-chain Kernel session key plus sponsorship). **Not live at the time:** public bundler and paymaster URLs, and the v2 paymaster (both went live on 2026-10-14; see above).

### `@pepu-chain/mcp` 0.2.0

The MCP server was rebuilt on `@pepu-chain/sdk`. It now serves 32 tools, 6 prompts and resources, so an agent reads the same registry, error catalog and requirements table that apps import. New tools cover probing the bundler and paymaster, explaining errors and transactions, checking environment and Privy configuration, generating an authorization key, encoding calls, scaffolding, listing SDK exports and fetching docs. The health check uses the live `checkSponsorship` probe, not a hard-coded answer. See [MCP Server Overview](../mcp/index.md) and [Tool Reference](../mcp/tools.md).

### Claude Code plugin `pepu-devkit` 0.4.0

Rewritten around the SDK and the MCP server: 12 skills (including `pepu-sdk`, `pepu-session-keys`, `pepu-sponsored-session`, `pepu-sponsored-transactions`, `pepu-paymaster-projects`), 6 slash commands (`/pepu-new-app`, `/pepu-add-login`, `/pepu-add-session`, `/pepu-add-sponsorship`, `/pepu-add-sponsored-session`, `/pepu-doctor`) and a builder subagent. See [Claude Code Plugin](../agent-tooling/plugin.md) and [Skills Catalog](../agent-tooling/skills.md).

### `create-pepu-app` 0.1.0

An interactive arrow-key flow (template, project name, package manager, install, git), with a non-interactive mode for CI and agents: `--yes`, `--json` (one JSON document on stdout), `--list`, `--sdk <vendor|npm>`, `--skip-agent-files`. Six templates: `consumer-app`, `token-gated-app`, `nft-mint`, `game-app`, `sponsored-demo`, `sponsored-session-app`. Templates are built on the SDK subpaths, ship `.mcp.json`, `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`, and pre-fill environment files. See [create-pepu-app CLI](../cli/create-pepu-app.md) and [Template Gallery](../templates/index.md).

### Docs

- A page per SDK subpath, a pillar-to-subpath decision table, a server and client boundary section, and a complete export index. See [SDK Overview and Reference](../sdk/reference.md).
- Type-checked sample code under `docs/snippets`, embedded in the recipes. Fifteen recipes now use SDK functions instead of hand-rolled code, including seven new ones: grant a session, sponsored send, sponsored session, v2 deposit and claim, Permit2 permit, multicall in React and explorer links.

## Earlier

Before 0.2.0 the SDK was 0.1: chain definitions, the contract and DEX registries, ABIs, gas helpers, explorer helpers, the token list, and the `/react`, `/privy` and `/server` entries, with `getSponsorshipStatus` as an always-unavailable placeholder. There is no dated history before 2026-10-02.

## Related

- [Migration Notes](../sdk/migration.md)
- [SDK Overview and Reference](../sdk/reference.md)

pages.content:
# Endpoints

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen-docs.mjs from packages/sdk/src/endpoints.ts (PEPU_HOSTED, PEPU_ENV) and the contract registry. Do not edit by hand; run `node scripts/gen-docs.mjs`. -->

Every endpoint the dev kit talks to, in one table: the public RPC and explorer, and the bundler and paymaster. Docs elsewhere write `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` and `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` as placeholders and point here for what they mean. This page is generated from the SDK, so it cannot disagree with `resolvePepuEndpoints()`.

> Status: the hosted bundler and paymaster service are live and proven on mainnet. The SDK uses them by default (`PEPU_HOSTED`); the environment variables below override them. Bundler `https://bundler.pepeunchained.com`, paymaster service `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com`. The ERC-7677 paymaster URL always embeds a token (`https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<token>`), so it is never a default: set `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` to it. The v2 paymaster behind it is a canary: internally reviewed 3 times, external audit pending, funded in small tranches.

## Prerequisites

- Nothing for the RPC and explorer. Sponsored transactions also need a bundler and a paymaster, see [Infrastructure Map](../infra/overview.md).

## Endpoint table

| Service | Value | Environment variable | Local development default |
|---|---|---|---|
| RPC (chain `97741`) | `https://rpc-pepu-v2-mainnet-0.t.conduit.xyz` | `PEPU_RPC_URL` (browser: `NEXT_PUBLIC_PEPU_RPC_URL`) | none, use the public RPC |
| Explorer (PepuScan) | `https://pepuscan.com` | none | none |
| Explorer API (Blockscout) | `https://pepuscan.com/api` | none | none |
| Bundler (ERC-4337, EntryPoint v0.7) | `https://bundler.pepeunchained.com` | `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` (browser: `NEXT_PUBLIC_PEPU_BUNDLER_URL`) | `http://localhost:4337` |
| Paymaster service (REST API, health, free-tier state) | `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com` | base of `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` | `http://localhost:8788` |
| Paymaster ERC-7677 URL | `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<token>` | `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` (browser: `NEXT_PUBLIC_PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL`) | `http://localhost:8788/v2/paymaster/<your-token>` |

The ERC-7677 paymaster URL carries a credential in its path (`/v2/paymaster/<token>`). A project **client token** (`ppt_`) is publishable but only works from the project's allowed origins: with none set, or from another origin, the service refuses it with `project_origin_not_allowed`. A project **server key** (`ppk_`) is a secret: keep it on the server and never put it in a `NEXT_PUBLIC_` variable. The **free tier** (100 PEPU/day and 50 PEPU/hour per user, TapScore as the only target for now) needs a verified Privy access token from PEPU's own Privy app sent as `context.privyAccessToken` in the ERC-7677 request; it is not available to apps on their own Privy app. See [Credential Matrix](../infra/paymaster/auth.md).

## How the SDK resolves them

`resolvePepuEndpoints()` picks each value in this order: an explicit option, then the environment (the server variable, then the `NEXT_PUBLIC_` variable), then the hosted default in `PEPU_HOSTED`. A malformed URL throws `CONFIG_BAD_URL` naming the variable, never its value. It returns `bundlerUrl`, `paymasterUrl` (the complete ERC-7677 URL, `null` unless you configured one, because it needs a token) and `paymasterBaseUrl` (the service base: the hosted base unless `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` points elsewhere, in which case the `/v2/paymaster/<token>` tail is stripped). `createPaymasterApi`, the probes, `checkSponsorship` and `pepu doctor` default to the base; `createPepuPaymasterClient` needs the complete URL or a `paymasterToken`. `hostedErc7677Url(token)` builds `<hosted base>/v2/paymaster/<token>` and `hostedFreeTierUrl()` the public free-tier state route. `isHostedSponsorshipLive()` is `true` only when the hosted bundler and paymaster base are both set.

| Value | Explicit option | Server variable | Browser variable | Hosted default |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| RPC | `rpcUrl` | `PEPU_RPC_URL` | `NEXT_PUBLIC_PEPU_RPC_URL` | `https://rpc-pepu-v2-mainnet-0.t.conduit.xyz` |
| Bundler | `bundlerUrl` | `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` | `NEXT_PUBLIC_PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` | `https://bundler.pepeunchained.com` |
| Paymaster ERC-7677 URL | `paymasterUrl` | `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` | `NEXT_PUBLIC_PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` | none (needs your token) |
| Paymaster service base | `baseUrl` (`createPaymasterApi`) | base of `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` | base of `NEXT_PUBLIC_PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` | `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com` |

## Contract registry

Deployed addresses in the SDK registry (`getPepuAddresses()`), for quick copying. Notes, bytecode sizes and do-not-substitute warnings are on [Address Map](../contracts/address-map.md). PepuSwap's own non-canonical contracts are on [PepuSwap Addresses](../contracts/pepuswap.md).

| Key | Name | Address |
|---|---|---|
| `create2Factory` | CREATE2 Deterministic Deployer | `0x4e59b44847b379578588920cA78FbF26c0B4956C` |
| `multicall3` | Multicall3 | `0x9CE19273Ae9c24437DFF512E8DFCAed4E4B001bd` |
| `permit2` | Permit2 | `0x000000000022D473030F116dDEE9F6B43aC78BA3` |
| `entryPoint06` | ERC-4337 EntryPoint v0.6 | `0x5FF137D4b0FDCD49DcA30c7CF57E578a026d2789` |
| `entryPoint07` | ERC-4337 EntryPoint v0.7 | `0x0000000071727De22E5E9d8BAf0edAc6f37da032` |
| `kernelFactory` | Kernel v3 Account Factory | `0xaac5D4240AF87249B3f71BC8E4A2cae074A3E419` |
| `kernelMetaFactory` | Kernel MetaFactory | `0xd703aaE79538628d27099B8c4f621bE4CCd142d5` |
| `ecdsaValidator` | Kernel ECDSA Validator | `0x845ADb2C711129d4f3966735eD98a9F09fC4cE57` |
| `paymaster` | Sponsored Paymaster v2 (PepuSponsoredPaymasterV7, alias of paymasterV2) | `0xdb28528C9399C33c9A0297E8A62F39145acbC30D` |
| `kernelImplementation` | Kernel v3.1 Implementation | `0xbAC849bB641841b44E965fb01A4Bf5F074F84B4d` |
| `kernelEcdsaSignerModule` | Kernel ECDSA Signer (permission signer module) | `0x6A6F069E2a08c2468e7724Ab3250CdBFBA14D4FF` |
| `kernelCallPolicyV004` | ZeroDev Call Policy v0.0.4 | `0x9a52283276A0ec8740DF50bF01B28A80D880eaf2` |
| `kernelTimestampPolicy` | ZeroDev Timestamp Policy | `0xB9f8f524bE6EcD8C945b1b87f9ae5C192FdCE20F` |
| `tapScore` | TapScore | `0x261eA5971B93237a56990206A46Bc80318e4d078` |
| `paymasterV1` | Verifying Paymaster v1 (PepuVerifyingPaymasterV7) - RETIRED | `0x2B6FED323bFA24f0475f4e1Dd3C7F6Cc1f3ae8B0` |
| `paymasterV2` | Sponsored Paymaster v2 (PepuSponsoredPaymasterV7), canary | `0xdb28528C9399C33c9A0297E8A62F39145acbC30D` |

## Hosted-URL swap (maintainers)

The only place the hosted URLs are set is `PEPU_HOSTED` in `packages/sdk/src/endpoints.ts`. To change them: edit it, rebuild the SDK, run `node scripts/gen-docs.mjs`, run `pnpm --filter @pepu-chain/mcp snapshots`, then release the SDK and the MCP server together. See `RELEASING.md`.

## What to expect

- `pepu_health_check` and `pepu_sponsorship_status` report "not configured" for the bundler and paymaster until you set the variables or the hosted URLs exist.
- `node scripts/check-docs-parity.mjs` verifies the addresses and counts on the docs pages against the SDK registry.

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `CONFIG_BAD_URL` | A URL variable is not a valid http(s) URL | Fix the variable the message names |
| `CONFIG_MISSING_ENV` for the paymaster | No complete ERC-7677 URL: it always embeds a token, so there is no tokenless default | Set `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` to `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<token>`, or pass `paymasterToken` |
| Browser calls to the bundler fail with CORS errors | The bundler does not allow your origin | See [Operating the Bundler](../infra/bundler/operating.md) |

## Related

- [Network Reference](../get-started/network-reference.md)
- [Infrastructure Map](../infra/overview.md)
- [Environment Variables](env-vars.md)
- [Address Map](../contracts/address-map.md)
- [Error Reference](errors.md)

pages.title: Environment Variables
pages.content:
# Environment Variables

Every environment variable used by the templates, the SDK, the MCP server and the services: which component reads it, whether it is required, whether it is secret, and a placeholder. Never put real values in docs, commits or chat.

> Status: derived from `TEMPLATE_REQUIREMENTS`, `PRIVY_ENV`, `PEPU_ENV`, the templates' `.env.example` files and the services' `.env.example` files.

## Prerequisites

None. `npm run doctor` in a template checks its own variables.

## App and SDK variables

| Name | Read by | Required | Secret | Example placeholder |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_APP_ID` (alias `PRIVY_APP_ID`) | Provider, `/privy/server`, doctor | All templates | No (public) | `<privy-app-id>` |
| `PRIVY_APP_SECRET` | `/privy/server`, `/session/server`, `/combo` | All templates | **Yes** | `<privy-app-secret>` |
| `PRIVY_AUTHORIZATION_KEY` | `/session/server` | `game-app` | **Yes** | `<base64-pkcs8-private-key>` |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_KEY_QUORUM_ID` (alias `PRIVY_KEY_QUORUM_ID`) | `createSessionRoutes` | `game-app` | No | `<key-quorum-id>` |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_GAME_CONTRACT_ADDRESS` | `game-app` scope | `game-app` | No | `0x<contract>` |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_GATE_ERC20_ADDRESS` | `token-gated-app` | One of the two gate addresses | No | `0x<erc20>` |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_GATE_ERC721_ADDRESS` | `token-gated-app` | One of the two | No | `0x<erc721>` |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_NFT_CONTRACT_ADDRESS` | `nft-mint` | `nft-mint` | No | `0x<nft>` |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_PAYMASTER_CONTRACT_ADDRESS` | `sponsored-demo` (deposit proof) | Optional; defaults to the v2 canary `0xdb28528C9399C33c9A0297E8A62F39145acbC30D` | No | same |
| `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` | `resolvePepuEndpoints`, `/combo`, `/aa`, MCP, doctor | `sponsored-session-app`; any sponsorship | **Yes** (treat as a credential) | Optional; defaults to `https://bundler.pepeunchained.com` (local: `http://localhost:4337`) |
| `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` | Same | Same | **Yes** (embeds a token) | `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com/v2/paymaster/<project server key>` (local: `http://localhost:8788/paymaster/<your-app-key>`). The ERC-7677 URL always embeds a token, so there is no tokenless default; the hosted base `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com` is the default for the REST client and probes |
| `PEPU_RPC_URL` | SDK server entries, doctor, MCP | Optional; default is the public RPC | Only if it embeds a key | `<authenticated-rpc-url>` |
| `SESSION_DURATION_MINUTES` | `/session/server`, `/combo` | Optional; default 15, clamped 1 to 1440 | No | `15` |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_PEPU_BUNDLER_URL`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_PEPU_RPC_URL` | `resolvePepuEndpoints` (browser variants) | Optional | Visible to every visitor | Avoid for credentials |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_PEPU_NETWORK` | Doctor shape check only | Optional | No | `mainnet` (the only valid value) |

Precedence in `resolvePepuEndpoints`: explicit option, then the server variable, then the `NEXT_PUBLIC_` variant, then the hosted default (`PEPU_HOSTED`: the bundler `https://bundler.pepeunchained.com` and the paymaster base `https://paymaster.pepeunchained.com`; the complete ERC-7677 URL is `null` until you supply a token). The names are exported as `PEPU_ENV`, `PEPU_PUBLIC_ENV` and `PRIVY_ENV`.

## Per-template matrix

| Template | Required | Optional |
|---|---|---|
| `consumer-app` | `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_APP_ID`, `PRIVY_APP_SECRET` | none |
| `game-app` | the two above, `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_KEY_QUORUM_ID`, `PRIVY_AUTHORIZATION_KEY`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_GAME_CONTRACT_ADDRESS` | `SESSION_DURATION_MINUTES`, `PEPU_RPC_URL` |
| `token-gated-app` | the two Privy vars, plus at least one of the gate addresses | both gate addresses |
| `nft-mint` | the two Privy vars, `NEXT_PUBLIC_NFT_CONTRACT_ADDRESS` | none |
| `sponsored-demo` | the two Privy vars | `NEXT_PUBLIC_PAYMASTER_CONTRACT_ADDRESS` |
| `sponsored-session-app` | the two Privy vars, `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL`, `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` | `SESSION_DURATION_MINUTES`, `PEPU_RPC_URL` |

## MCP server

No API key. Optional: `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL`, `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` (sponsorship tools) and `PEPU_RPC_URL`. Everything else uses public PEPU RPC and pepuscan's public REST API.

## Services (operators)

| Name | Component | Secret | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ALTO_RPC_URL` | Bundler | **Yes** (embeds the RPC key) | RPC for Alto |
| `ALTO_EXECUTOR_PRIVATE_KEYS` | Bundler | **Yes** | Funded submitter key or keys |
| `PRIVY_APP_ID`, `PRIVY_APP_SECRET` | Paymaster policy service | secret: the second | Verify user tokens |
| `PAYMASTER_CONTRACT_ADDRESS`, `CHAIN_ID`, `ENTRY_POINT_ADDRESS`, `PORT`, `DB_PATH` | Policy service | No | Chain and paymaster config |
| `PAYMASTER_SIGNER_PRIVATE_KEY` | Policy service (loaded from a gitignored keys file) | **Yes** | Signs approvals |
| `USER_HOURLY_SPEND_CAP_WEI`, `USER_DAILY_SPEND_CAP_WEI`, `USER_LIFETIME_SPEND_CAP_WEI`, count caps, `GLOBAL_DAILY_SPEND_CEILING_WEI` | Policy service | No | Caps; size above the first-operation reservation |
| `ADMIN_TOKEN` | Policy service | **Yes** | Enables the circuit-breaker reset endpoint |
| `PAYMASTER_RPC_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`, `PAYMASTER_RPC_ALLOW_ACCOUNT_DEPLOYMENT` | Policy service | No | ERC-7677 endpoint controls |
| `SPONSORSHIP_V2_ENABLED` and the `SPONSORSHIP_V2_*`, `FREE_TIER_*`, `PROJECT_*`, `SPONSORSHIP_*` family | Policy service v2 (on in the hosted service; off by default in a fresh run) | `SPONSORSHIP_ADMIN_TOKEN` is secret | Tiered paymaster, deployed as a canary |

Full lists: [Operating the Bundler](../infra/bundler/operating.md), [Policy, Caps and the Circuit Breaker](../infra/paymaster/policy-and-caps.md), [Paymaster Overview](../infra/paymaster/overview.md).

## Public versus secret rules

- `NEXT_PUBLIC_` means bundled into client JavaScript. Use it only for the App ID, the quorum id and contract addresses.
- Server-only code never reads `NEXT_PUBLIC_` secrets.
- `PEPU_BUNDLER_URL` and `PEPU_PAYMASTER_URL` are credentials in practice: keep them server-side.
- Restart the dev server after editing `.env.local`; Next.js reads it once.

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `CONFIG_MISSING_ENV` | A required variable is empty | Set it, restart |
| `CONFIG_BAD_URL` | A URL variable is not http(s) | Fix the value (the message names the variable, not its value) |
| Doctor says `placeholder` | Value like `your-app-id` | Replace it |

## Related

- [Privy Env Vars and Verification](../privy/env-and-checks.md)
- [Template Gallery](../templates/index.md)
- [Error Reference](errors.md)
